Backend implementation और frontend consumption tightly coupled होंगे, लेकिन database/internal implementation expose नहीं होगी।

## Rust side का unified endpoint model

हर operation चार categories में होगा:

```text
Query        current data पढ़ना
Command      state बदलना
Stream       continuous events
LiveQuery    snapshot + automatic updates
```

हर operation metadata carry करेगा:

- Input type
- Output type
- Typed error union
- Authentication requirement
- Permission
- Organization/resource scope
- Cache identity
- Invalidation rules
- Realtime topics
- Version

Conceptually:

```text
application.get
application.rebuild
deployment.logs
monitoring.serverMetrics
```

Frontend generated registry में exact same names मिलेंगे।

## सबसे powerful concept: Live Query

सिर्फ RPC या WebSocket काफी नहीं है। हमें query और events को combine करना चाहिए:

```text
Initial database snapshot
          +
Ordered backend changes
          =
Always-current React state
```

React component केवल live query use करेगा। उसके अंदर framework:

1. Authoritative snapshot fetch करेगा
2. Matching stream subscribe करेगा
3. Events validate करेगा
4. Cache patch/invalidate करेगा
5. Disconnect पर stale mark करेगा
6. Reconnect पर replay/resync करेगा
7. Component unmount पर subscription release करेगा

यही Rustploy को truly effortless बनाएगा।

## Rust type system से TypeScript generation

Types manual नहीं होने चाहिए। Generator handle करे:

- Structs
- Enums
- Tagged unions
- Generics
- Optional vs nullable
- Timestamps
- Durations
- Pagination
- Typed IDs
- Maps/sets
- Validation constraints
- Deprecated fields
- Schema versions

लेकिन direct `Rust type → loose TypeScript interface` पर्याप्त नहीं है।

Generate करना चाहिए:

```text
TypeScript compile-time type
Runtime decoder/schema
Serializer/deserializer
React hook
Cache key factory
Mock/test fixture contract
API documentation
```

एक contract से पूरा ecosystem निकलेगा।

## Branded IDs automatically

Rust newtypes:

```text
ApplicationId
ServerId
DeploymentId
OrganizationId
```

Frontend पर generated branded types बनेंगे। इससे compile time पर `ServerId` की जगह `ApplicationId` pass नहीं हो पाएगा।

React Router params raw strings होंगे, इसलिए generated decoder उन्हें validate और brand करेगा।

## Typed errors end-to-end

Rust error enum सीधे frontend discriminated union बने:

```text
NotFound
PermissionDenied
AlreadyRunning
AgentOffline
ValidationFailed
Conflict
Internal
```

React mutation result में arbitrary exception नहीं, typed error मिलेगा।

UI exhaustive behavior define कर सकेगी:

```text
AlreadyRunning → existing deployment खोलो
AgentOffline   → setup instructions दिखाओ
PermissionDenied → control disable करो
```

Unhandled backend error variant frontend compile-time failure trigger कर सकता है।

## Transport developer से hidden होगा

हर operation के लिए best transport framework choose करे:

```text
Query       → HTTP
Command     → HTTP
Stream      → WebSocket
File upload → multipart HTTP
Download    → HTTP stream
Logs        → WebSocket/binary frames
Metrics     → compressed/batched stream
```

Frontend API समान रहे। Component को transport जानना ही नहीं चाहिए।

Future में HTTP/3, MessagePack या gRPC-Web आए, component code unchanged रह सकता है।

## Generated React layer

Generated SDK तीन levels दे:

```text
Raw typed client
Framework-independent live client
React hooks
```

Examples conceptually:

```text
api.application.get(input)
api.application.rebuild(input)

useQuery.application.get(input)
useMutation.application.rebuild()

useStream.deployment.logs(input)
useLiveQuery.application.detail(input)
```

Hooks automatically provide:

```text
data
status
error
freshness
connectionState
retry
mutate
cancel
```

## Backend-driven cache consistency

React frontend manually guess नहीं करेगा कि rebuild के बाद क्या invalidate करना है।

Backend operation metadata declare करे:

```text
application.rebuild affects:
- application detail
- active deployment
- deployment history
- project summary
```

Command complete होने पर server affected entity keys return/publish करे। Client automatically संबंधित cache patch या invalidate करे।

इससे तुम्हारा current “DB में DONE, UI में RUNNING” वाला class of bug काफी कम होगा।

## Entity revision system

हर important entity में monotonic revision होना चाहिए:

```text
Application #1 revision 84
Deployment #373 revision 12
```

हर event carry करे:

```text
previousRevision
revision
```

Client:

- Old event ignore करेगा
- Duplicate event ignore करेगा
- Revision gap detect करेगा
- Gap पर snapshot refetch करेगा

Timestamps ordering के लिए reliable नहीं हैं; revisions better हैं।

## Transaction और event consistency

सबसे important backend rule:

> Database commit के बिना कोई “successful state changed” event publish नहीं होगा।

Reliable implementation के लिए transactional outbox pattern:

```text
One DB transaction:
- Domain state update
- Deployment update
- Outbox event insert

Commit
  ↓
Publisher reads outbox
  ↓
WebSocket clients receive event
```

अगर process transaction के बाद crash हो जाए, event outbox में रहेगा और बाद में publish होगा। UI update कभी silently lost नहीं होगा।

यही real product-grade realtime consistency है।

## React state backend reality कैसे mirror करेगी

Frontend store में arbitrary component state copies avoid करेंगे।

Three layers:

```text
Server cache    authoritative remote projection
Draft state     unsaved form/editor changes
Ephemeral UI    modal, selected tab, hover
```

Resource status server cache से आएगा। Component उसे duplicate local state में नहीं रखेगा।

Unsaved visual-editor data clearly “draft” होगा, deployed backend reality से अलग।

## Authorization भी generated होगी

Frontend permissions केवल UX के लिए होंगी; security backend enforce करेगा।

Generated operation metadata UI को बता सकता है:

```text
canRun
missingPermission
disabledReason
```

लेकिन request आने पर Rust handler फिर authorization करेगा।

Subscriptions भी organization/resource ownership verify करेंगी।

## Optimistic updates safe कैसे होंगी

Framework हर mutation को optimistic नहीं बनाएगा।

Three modes:

```text
none          server confirmation तक wait
reversible    optimistic patch + rollback
commutative   immediate local merge
```

Deployment/rebuild जैसे operations `none` या server-acknowledged होंगे। Naming/tag edits reversible हो सकते हैं। Cursor/presence commutative हो सकती है।

Rust operation metadata safe mode define करेगी।

## Protocol manifest

Build के दौरान backend एक machine-readable manifest generate करे:

```text
Operations
Types
Errors
Permissions
Events
Cache dependencies
Wire formats
Versions
Deprecations
```

Frontend generator इसी manifest से SDK बनाए।

CI verify करे:

```text
Rust contract changed
→ manifest changed
→ generated SDK changed
→ TypeScript compile
→ affected React exhaustive checks
```

Stale generated client merge नहीं हो सकेगा।

## Local development experience

Developer Rust endpoint add करे और dev process automatically:

1. Rust contract rebuild करे
2. Manifest update करे
3. TypeScript SDK regenerate करे
4. React Fast Refresh trigger करे
5. Contract error IDE में दिखाए

Ideal command एक ही होगा:

```text
rustploy dev
```

यह Rust backend, generator और React dev server coordinate करेगा।

## Framework को कैसे divide करना चाहिए

Repository architecture roughly:

```text
rustploy-contract
  Rust traits, macros, IDs, error/event definitions

rustploy-codegen
  Manifest and TypeScript generation

rustploy-server
  Routing, auth, outbox, subscriptions, transport

rustploy-client
  Generated TypeScript core SDK

rustploy-react
  Hooks, cache integration, live-query support

rustploy-devtools
  Request/event/revision/cache inspector
```

Business product इनके ऊपर रहेगा।

## Devtools “X-Ray” से भी आगे

Browser devtools panel दिखाए:

- Active operations
- Query cache
- WebSocket subscriptions
- Received events
- Entity revisions
- Cache patches
- Invalidations
- Reconnect/replay
- Authorization decisions
- Runtime validation failures
- Rust trace/request ID

किसी UI badge पर click करके trace कर सको:

```text
यह RUNNING क्यों है?
→ Application revision 84
→ event #921
→ deployment transaction #373
→ backend operation application.rebuild
```

यह debugging experience बहुत powerful होगा।

## कहाँ सावधान रहना होगा

“Tightly coupled” का गलत version backend internals को frontend में leak कर देगा।

Frontend को expose करना चाहिए:

- Stable API DTOs
- Commands
- Queries
- Events
- Errors
- Permissions

Expose नहीं करना चाहिए:

- Database row structs
- SQL schema
- Internal queue structs
- Docker implementation details
- Private domain invariants

Coupling contract से होनी चाहिए, implementation से नहीं।

## सही implementation order

1. Contract crate और Rust annotations
2. Type/error/ID TypeScript generator
3. Generated HTTP client
4. React Query hooks
5. Unified typed WebSocket protocol
6. Snapshot + event live queries
7. Entity revisions
8. Transactional outbox
9. Backend-driven cache effects
10. Dev server/watch mode
11. Protocol/cache X-Ray tools
12. Framework extraction and documentation

सबसे पहले existing Rustploy application/deployment flow को reference vertical slice बनाना चाहिए। अगर उस एक flow में generated query, mutation, live logs, status reconciliation और typed errors end-to-end सही चल गए, बाकी resources उसी pattern से migrate हो सकते हैं।

Short version:

> हाँ—हम Rust function लिखकर automatically generated, runtime-validated React hooks, live queries, typed errors, permissions, cache behavior और realtime synchronization वाला अपना framework बना सकते हैं।

यह सिर्फ API client नहीं होगा; यह Rust backend और React UI के बीच पूरा product-state protocol होगा।

## Assistant

Haan bhai, ab exact samjha: tum `svelte-realtime` use nahi karna chahte. Tum Rust + React ka apna deeply integrated system banana chahte ho—backend mein function define karo aur frontend mein automatically typed hook mil jaye.

## Ideal developer experience

Rust backend mein operation define hua:

```text
application.get
application.rebuild
deployment.logs
monitoring.serverMetrics
```

Frontend mein automatically generated APIs mil jayein:

```text
useApplicationQuery(applicationId)
useRebuildApplication()
useDeploymentLogs(deploymentId)
useServerMetrics(serverId)
```

Frontend developer ko manually ye sab na karna pade:

- URL aur HTTP method likhna
- Request/response interface copy karna
- `fetch()` likhna
- WebSocket event parse karna
- Cache keys banana
- Mutation ke baad kya invalidate hoga decide karna
- Reconnect handling likhna
- `as SomeType` casting karna

## Mera recommended architecture

```text
Rust contract
    ↓
Generated manifest/schema
    ↓
Generated TypeScript SDK
    ↓
React Query hooks
    ↓
Realtime synchronization
```

Rust backend hi single source of truth hoga.

Backend ke database structs directly frontend ko expose nahi karne. Dedicated API contract types honge.

## Operations ko chaar categories mein rakho

### Query

Current data read karna:

```text
application.get
deployment.list
server.metricsHistory
```

### Command

State change karna:

```text
application.rebuild
compose.stop
notification.markRead
```

### Stream

Continuous data:

```text
deployment.logs
monitoring.liveMetrics
notifications.created
```

### Live Query

Sabse powerful feature:

```text
Initial snapshot + realtime events = always-current React state
```

Component ko sirf live query use karni pade:

```text
useLiveApplication(applicationId)
```

Framework automatically:

1. Backend se current snapshot lega.
2. Matching realtime channel subscribe karega.
3. Events se cache update karega.
4. Connection drop hone par stale mark karega.
5. Reconnect par missed events replay karega.
6. Gap mile to fresh snapshot fetch karega.

## HTTP ko हटाना नहीं चाहिए

Har cheez WebSocket RPC par daalna attractive lagega, lekin product ke liye unnecessary complexity hogi.

Meri recommendation:

```text
Initial queries       → HTTP
Commands/mutations    → HTTP
Realtime updates/logs → WebSocket
Uploads/downloads     → HTTP
```

React developer ko transport ka pata nahi chalega. Generated SDK internally decide karega.

Isse:

- Debugging easy rahegi
- Browser/proxy compatibility better hogi
- Retry semantics clear rahenge
- WebSocket unavailable hone par normal operations chal sakenge

## Real type safety mein kya generate hoga?

Sirf TypeScript interfaces nahi. Rust contract se generate karo:

- Request type
- Response type
- Runtime validator
- Typed error union
- API client
- React Query hook
- Cache key factory
- Realtime event parser
- Documentation
- Test mocks

TypeScript compile-time type safety deta hai, lekin server response runtime par validate bhi hona chahiye.

## IDs strict honi chahiye

Abhi IDs mostly numbers hongi:

```text
applicationId
serverId
deploymentId
```

Plain numbers mein frontend galti se `ServerId` ko `ApplicationId` ki jagah bhej sakta hai.

Rust newtypes aur generated branded TypeScript IDs use karo:

```text
ApplicationId
ServerId
DeploymentId
OrganizationId
```

Wire par number reh sakta hai, lekin compiler wrong ID usage rokega.

## Status ko string mat rehne do

Deployment ke liye loose model problematic hai:

```text
status
errorMessage?
finishedAt?
pid?
```

Ismein invalid combinations possible hain.

Iske badle state-wise model rakho:

```text
QueuedDeployment
RunningDeployment
CompletedDeployment
FailedDeployment
CancelledDeployment
```

Example rules:

```text
RUNNING → startedAt required
DONE    → finishedAt required
ERROR   → finishedAt + typed error required
```

React `status` check karega aur TypeScript automatically valid fields samjhega.

## Backend reality frontend tak reliably kaise पहुंचेगी?

Sabse important rule:

> Database transaction commit hone se pehle success event publish nahi hona chahiye.

Meri strong recommendation: **transactional outbox pattern**.

Ek database transaction mein:

```text
resource status update
deployment finalization
outbox event insert
```

Commit ke baad publisher event frontend ko bhejega.

Agar backend event bhejne se pehle crash ho gaya, event outbox mein safe rahega aur restart ke baad deliver hoga.

Ye tumhare recent issue ko directly address karta hai:

```text
Database mein DONE
UI mein abhi bhi RUNNING
```

## Entity revisions add karo

Application, deployment, compose jaise resources ke saath monotonically increasing revision rakho:

```text
Application #1 revision 45
Deployment #373 revision 9
```

Har event carry kare:

```text
previousRevision
revision
```

Frontend:

- Duplicate event ignore karega
- Old event ignore karega
- Revision gap detect karega
- Gap par snapshot refetch karega

Event ordering ke liye timestamp par depend mat karna.

## Cache backend-driven honi chahiye

Frontend manually ye guess na kare:

```text
Rebuild ke baad kaunsi queries invalidate hongi?
```

Command result/event bataye:

```text
Affected:
application:1
deployments:application:1
active-deployment:application:1
project-summary:3
```

Generated client automatically related React Query cache refresh/patch kare.

UI aur backend state mismatch significantly kam ho jayega.

## Typed errors bhi जरूरी hain

Backend arbitrary string error na bheje:

```text
"Something went wrong"
```

Rust error enum frontend par generated union bane:

```text
ApplicationNotFound
DeploymentAlreadyRunning
ServerOffline
PermissionDenied
ValidationFailed
```

Frontend message parse nahi karega; error code ke according behavior decide karega.

## Authentication aur permissions

Subscription room ka naam bhej dene se access nahi milna chahiye.

Backend har subscription par validate kare:

```text
User authenticated?
Organization member?
Resource same organization ka hai?
Required permission available hai?
```

Frontend ke generated hooks permission-based disabled reason dikha sakte hain, lekin security final backend hi enforce kare.

## Package structure ki suggestion

Initially project ke andar:

```text
rustploy-contract
rustploy-codegen
rustploy-realtime
rustploy-react
rustploy-devtools
```

Baad mein mature hone par generic framework packages nikale ja sakte hain.

### `rustploy-contract`

Rust operations, DTOs, IDs, errors aur event definitions.

### `rustploy-codegen`

Rust contract se TypeScript manifest/client generate karega.

### `rustploy-realtime`

WebSocket connection, subscriptions, replay aur outbox publishing.

### `rustploy-react`

React Query hooks, cache integration aur live queries.

### `rustploy-devtools`

Requests, events, cache, revisions aur reconnect inspect karne ka UI.

## Meri strongest suggestion

Pehle sirf ek complete vertical slice banao:

```text
Application detail
→ Rebuild command
→ Deployment status
→ Live build logs
→ Final application status
→ Notification
```

Is ek flow mein implement karo:

- Generated types
- Generated HTTP client
- Generated React hooks
- Typed errors
- WebSocket events
- Transactional outbox
- Revision tracking
- Cache synchronization
- Reconnect/resync

Agar ye flow reliable ho gaya, phir same infrastructure compose, database, monitoring aur notifications par apply karna easy hoga.

## Kya abhi nahi banana chahiye

Starting phase mein avoid karo:

- Generic public framework packaging
- Har command ko WebSocket RPC banana
- Redis ko mandatory banana
- Offline mutation queue
- Complex optimistic updates
- Presence/cursors
- Custom binary protocol
- Existing REST API ka full rewrite

Pehle consistency aur developer experience prove karo.

## Final recommendation

Main Rustploy ke liye ye combination choose karunga:

```text
Rust contract as source of truth
+ generated TypeScript SDK
+ React Query hooks
+ HTTP queries/commands
+ typed WebSocket events
+ Live Query abstraction
+ transactional outbox
+ entity revisions
+ runtime response validation
```

Isse Rust aur React strongly coupled honge, lekin clean contract ke through—not database internals ke through.

Long-term frontend experience kuch aisa hoga:

```text
Backend operation define karo
→ SDK automatically regenerate ho
→ React hook import karo
→ UI database-authoritative realtime state show kare
```

Ye practical bhi hai, scalable bhi, aur Rustploy ko genuinely powerful developer experience de sakta hai.

## User

ek baat batoo tume alert me table banaye ho schema bhi udpate karte rahena sare strict kyo nahi hai kj main wahi hai migration bhi matintain karna and 

## Assistant

Bilkul bhai, tum sahi keh rahe ho. Alert ke liye sirf migration/table banana enough nahi hai. **Canonical schema, Rust models, API contract aur frontend types—sabko ek saath update rehna chahiye.** Warna fresh database aur existing migrated database alag behave karenge.

Rustploy mein strict rule ye hona chahiye:

```text
Canonical DB schema
        ↓
Versioned migration
        ↓
Rust database models
        ↓
Repository/service types
        ↓
API request/response contract
        ↓
Generated frontend types
```

Har database change mein compulsory:

- Canonical schema update
- Forward-only numbered migration
- Fresh database migration test
- Existing database upgrade test
- Rust query/model update
- Nullability, defaults, foreign keys aur indexes define
- API DTO update
- Generated frontend contract update
- Backend + frontend compile/type-check

Alert system mein particularly strict cheezein:

- Alert rule aur alert event/state separate tables
- Organization/server ownership as foreign keys
- Typed states: `OK`, `FIRING`, `RESOLVED`, `NO_DATA`
- Unique constraints to prevent duplicate active alerts
- Proper timestamps and indexes
- Delete/cascade policy explicitly defined
- Rust enums and database values synchronized
- Frontend manually status strings define na kare

Migrations ke rules:

- Applied migration kabhi edit nahi hogi.
- Har schema change ki new migration बनेगी.
- Migration idempotent hone ka pretend nahi karegi; migration ledger authoritative hoga.
- Fresh DB ko migration `1 → latest` se exact canonical schema milna chahiye.
- Production data ke liye safe backfill/default strategy hogi.
- SQLx migration ledger manually mismatch nahi hona chahiye.
- CI canonical schema aur migrated schema ka drift detect karega.

Aur haan, pehle monitoring migration mein jo `duplicate server_id` issue hua tha, woh isi discipline ki कमी thi: database object मौजूद tha lekin migration ledger/schema truth synchronized nahi thi.

Aage se meri working policy ye rahegi:

> Koi table, column, enum ya relation change tab complete nahi maana jayega jab tak schema + migration + backend models + API contract + frontend generated types + migration verification sab update na hon.

Strictness ka main source Rust type system akela nahi—**poori contract chain aur CI enforcement** hai. Alert ka remaining `RESOLVED/NO_DATA` lifecycle implement karte waqt bhi schema/migration synchronization ko required part maana jayega, optional cleanup nahi.

    use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
    use std::{fmt, str::FromStr};
    
    use super::AlertParseError;
    
    #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize, poem_openapi::Enum)]
    #[serde(rename_all = "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE")]
    #[oai(rename_all = "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE")]
    pub enum AlertEventState {
        Firing,
        Resolved,
        NoData,
    }
    
    impl AlertEventState {
        pub const fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
            match self {
                Self::Firing => "FIRING",
                Self::Resolved => "RESOLVED",
                Self::NoData => "NO_DATA",
            }
        }
    }
    
    impl fmt::Display for AlertEventState {
        fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
            formatter.write_str(self.as_str())
        }
    }
    
    impl FromStr for AlertEventState {
        type Err = AlertParseError;
    
        fn from_str(value: &str) -> Result<Self, Self::Err> {
            match value.trim().to_ascii_uppercase().as_str() {
                "FIRING" => Ok(Self::Firing),
                "RESOLVED" => Ok(Self::Resolved),
                "NO_DATA" => Ok(Self::NoData),
                other => Err(AlertParseError::EventState(other.to_owned())),
            }
        }
    }

  ### 💡 Problem Kya Hai?

  • Metric ek hi hai (CPU/RAM).
  • Par Agent par bhi SQLite me INSERT + SELECT ho raha hai, aur Main Panel par bhi SQLite me INSERT + SELECT ho raha hai!
  • Dono side retention pruning loops chal rahe hain.

  ### ⚡ Solution (Ise Clean Kaise Karein?)

  • Agent side se SQLite storage HATA do! Agent direct sysinfo se measurement karke Main Panel ko push / stream kar dega.

  • Result: Agent 3MB RAM par super-fast ho jayega aur zero redundant disk writes hone lagenge!

## Assistant

Haan bhai, observation largely correct hai: abhi system mein same metrics ki two copies intentionally store ho rahi hain.

```text
Remote agent
  ├─ local SQLite persistence
  └─ HTTP push
          ↓
Main panel
  └─ panel SQLite persistence
```

Lekin ise exact “duplicate row bug” bolna thoda misleading hai. Ye same database mein duplicate insert nahi hai; do different machines/databases par same observation ki replicas hain.

## Ye kyun banaya gaya tha?

Agent ka local SQLite originally in capabilities ke liye useful tha:

- Panel temporarily offline ho tab recent history retain karna
- Local gRPC queries support karna
- Remote host par standalone monitoring/debugging
- Central panel unreachable hone par metrics completely lose na hona
- Local retention/rollups
- Network outage ke baad recovery ka possible base

README aur agent architecture mein local gRPC query server bhi hai. Isliye local store accidental code nahi tha; agent ko collector ke saath standalone monitoring node banaya gaya tha.

Problem ye hai ki current product flow mein local database ka पूरा फायदा शायद use नहीं हो रहा:

- Metrics local save hote hain
- Panel ko push bhi hote hain
- Failed HTTP push ke baad durable retry/outbox/replay apparently नहीं है
- Panel local agent history ko normally query नहीं करता
- Browser panel database/SSE se data leta hai
- Panel retention independently चलता है

Agar failed pushes automatically local DB se replay nahi ho rahe, to agent SQLite resilience nahi दे रहा—सिर्फ redundant copy बना रहा है।

## Host aur container behavior अलग check karna होगा

Host metric local save + panel push clearly दो storage paths हैं.

Container metrics ke case mein confirm करना जरूरी है कि:

- Agent हर sample local SQLite में रख रहा है,
- या सिर्फ host metrics local persist होते हैं,
- batch panel को push होता है,
- gRPC कौन-सा store query करता है।

Isliye पूरे store को remove करने से पहले local DB के consumers देखना जरूरी है.

## “Agent 3 MB RAM” expectation

SQLite हटाने से:

- Disk writes कम होंगे
- DB connection/cache memory हटेगी
- Migration startup हटेगा
- Retention task हटेगा
- Image/code complexity कम होगी

लेकिन exact 3 MB guarantee realistic नहीं है। Rust runtime, Tokio, reqwest, TLS, sysinfo, Docker/cgroup collection और buffers खुद memory use करेंगे। Improvement होगा, exact value benchmark से आएगी।

## Rustploy product के लिए मेरी recommendation

हमारा product central-panel-based है, इसलिए default architecture यह होनी चाहिए:

```text
Remote agent
  collect
  batch
  authenticate
  push
      ↓
Panel
  validate ownership
  persist
  retain
  query
  alert
  display
```

यानि **panel single source of truth**.

Agent responsibilities:

- Host metrics collect करना
- Container metrics collect करना
- Resource labels attach करना
- Short in-memory batching करना
- Retry with bounded backoff
- Authentication/identity
- Health heartbeat
- Optional logs proxy/collection

Panel responsibilities:

- Durable persistence
- History
- Retention
- Rollups
- Alerts
- Organization authorization
- Frontend queries/SSE

## SQLite remove करने का downside

Network outage के समय samples lose हो जाएंगे.

Example:

```text
Panel 30 minutes unavailable
→ agent keeps collecting
→ memory buffer भरने के बाद oldest metrics drop
→ उस duration की history missing
```

Monitoring product में ये acceptable हो सकता है अगर:

- Agent lightweight रखना priority है
- Metrics forensic/audit data नहीं हैं
- Missing interval UI में visible हो
- Agent heartbeat/stale detection मौजूद हो

Rustploy के लिए मुझे यह acceptable लगता है।

## Best middle ground

SQLite पूरी तरह हटाने के बजाय two operating modes possible हैं:

```text
Default: stateless
Optional: buffered/durable
```

लेकिन अभी product complexity देखते हुए मैं initially केवल stateless agent रखूंगा:

- Small bounded in-memory buffer
- Host metric latest sample
- Container metric limited batch queue
- Exponential backoff
- Maximum queue size/time
- Overflow पर oldest samples drop
- Dropped-sample counter logs/heartbeat में report
- Panel reconnect होने पर queued samples flush
- Agent restart पर buffer loss acceptable

इससे redundant disk writes नहीं होंगे और short panel/network outages भी tolerate होंगे।

## Local gRPC का क्या होगा?

Agent SQLite हटने पर current history gRPC methods meaningful नहीं रहेंगे।

Options:

1. gRPC remove कर दो if panel/frontend use नहीं करते.
2. gRPC केवल current in-memory snapshot return करे.
3. Panel proxy के through live logs/current metrics serve करे.

Meri recommendation:

- Historical metrics gRPC हटाओ.
- Agent health/current snapshot endpoint रख सकते हो.
- History केवल panel DB से आए.
- Container logs existing deployment/Docker SSE flow से आएं.
- Agent को second monitoring database/server मत बनाओ.

## Retention का क्या होगा?

Only panel पर:

```text
server_metrics retention
container_metrics retention
alert_events retention policy
optional rollups
```

Agent retention loop और local migration lifecycle खत्म हो जाएंगी.

## Important reliability improvement

Agent SQLite हटाकर सीधे fire-and-forget HTTP करना गलत होगा। Minimum bounded queue जरूरी है:

```text
Collect
→ enqueue in memory
→ batch push
→ success पर remove
→ failure पर backoff
→ queue full पर oldest drop + warning
```

Host और container payloads को ideally batch ingestion use करना चाहिए। अभी host metric single request है; host batch endpoint future में network efficiency improve करेगा।

## Final verdict

Ye duplication इसलिए है क्योंकि agent को originally:

> collector + local history store + gRPC query node

बनाया गया था, जबकि current Rustploy product उसे mainly:

> lightweight remote collector + panel pusher

की तरह use कर रहा है।

इसलिए architecture mismatch है, direct coding mistake नहीं। लेकिन अगर local history replay/query practically use नहीं हो रही, तो local SQLite अब unnecessary overhead है।

Meri recommendation:

> Agent को stateless, bounded-memory collector बनाओ; panel को sole durable database रखो; existing panel monitoring/SSE/log flows reuse करो; local gRPC history और agent retention हटाओ।

इससे architecture simple होगा और monitoring schema/migrations भी सिर्फ panel पर maintain करने पड़ेंगे।

## User

  ### 🏆 Final Truth & Solution

  Dokploy wala design ekdum clear hai:

  • Main Server DB Size = 0 MB (Zero metric load on main server!).
  • Remote Node = Single Storage (Remote host apna metrics khud sambhalta hai).

  Rustploy me bhi hum Main Panel DB se metrics storage hatha kar Dokploy jaisa single-storage (Pull-on-Demand) kar sakte hain!
i want asa iska plan do and itna bada likh ma diya karo and hing me short rakha karo bhai sumary kase karne wale ho

## Assistant

Haan bhai, Dokploy jaisa **remote-only metric storage + pull-on-demand** model Rustploy ke liye sahi rahega.

## Final architecture

```text
Remote Monitor
├── metrics collect
├── local SQLite mein store
├── retention manage
└── gRPC se history/live data provide

Main Panel
├── metrics store nahi karega
├── server ID se correct agent locate karega
├── gRPC se data pull karega
└── frontend ko authenticated API/SSE dega
```

## Implementation plan

1. Panel se metric persistence remove:

   - `server_metrics`
   - `container_metrics`
   - panel retention cleaner
   - metric ingestion HTTP routes

2. Agent ko single source of truth banana:

   - Host aur container metrics local SQLite mein store
   - Agent retention maintain kare
   - Proper indexes/migrations rakhe

3. gRPC contract complete karna:

   - Latest server metric
   - Host history
   - Container list/history
   - Live metric stream
   - Agent health/status

4. Panel proxy layer:

   - `server_id → monitoring agent address`
   - Organization/permission validation
   - Agent token authentication
   - Timeout, retry aur offline errors

5. Frontend same panel endpoints use karega:

   - Browser directly remote agent se connect nahi karega
   - Panel agent se data pull/proxy karega
   - Existing React monitoring UI mostly unchanged rahegi

6. Logs existing Docker/deployment SSE se hi aayenge. Monitoring system mein duplicate log storage नहीं बनाएंगे।

7. Migration:

   - Existing panel metric tables ko immediately drop nahi karenge
   - Pehle reads agent par switch
   - Verify karne ke baad new migration se panel metric tables remove
   - Existing metric data ke लिए optional cleanup/export

## Important requirement

Remote agent ko panel se reachable hona hoga:

```text
Panel → Remote Agent gRPC port
```

Token authentication, TLS/VPN aur per-server endpoint mandatory rakhenge.

## Summary

> Agent metrics collect + store karega. Panel kuch persist nahi karega. UI request aane par panel authorized gRPC call se remote agent ka data pull karke frontend ko देगा। Alerts ke liye panel periodically agent se latest metrics pull karega.

    +async fn ensure_optional_column(
    +    pool: &SqlitePool,
    +    table: &str,
    +    column: &str,
    +    sql_type: &str,
    +) -> Result<(), MonitorError> {
    +    use sqlx::Row;
    +
    +    let columns = sqlx::query(&format!("PRAGMA table_info({table})"))
    +        .fetch_all(pool)
    +        .await?;
    +    if columns
    +        .iter()
    +        .any(|row| row.get::<String, _>("name") == column)
    +    {
    +        return Ok(());
    +    }
    +    sqlx::query(&format!("ALTER TABLE {table} ADD COLUMN {column} {sql_type}"))
    +        .execute(pool)
    +        .await?;
    +    Ok(())
    +}

    Add: /run/media/das/SSD/Devloper/rustploy/src/services/monitoring/monitoring_service.rs
    use crate::{
        core::config::Config,
        db::models::{container_metrics::ContainerMetric, server_metrics::ServerMetric},
        services::remote_server::ServerService,
    };
    use auto_di::singleton;
    use std::sync::Arc;
    use tonic::{Request, metadata::MetadataValue};
    
    pub mod proto {
        tonic::include_proto!("monitoring");
    }
    
    pub struct MonitoringService {
        server_service: Arc<ServerService>,
        config: Arc<Config>,
    }
    
    #[singleton]
    impl MonitoringService {
        pub fn new(server_service: Arc<ServerService>, config: Arc<Config>) -> Self {
            Self {
                server_service,
                config,
            }
        }
    
        async fn client(
            &self,
            server_id: i64,
        ) -> Result<proto::monitoring_service_client::MonitoringServiceClient<tonic::transport::Channel>, String>
        {
            let server = self
                .server_service
                .get_by_id(server_id)
                .await
                .map_err(|_| format!("monitoring server {server_id} not found"))?;
            let host = match server.ip_address.as_str() {
                "" | "0.0.0.0" | "localhost" => "127.0.0.1",
                other => other,
            };
            proto::monitoring_service_client::MonitoringServiceClient::connect(format!(
                "http://{host}:50051"
            ))
            .await
            .map_err(|error| format!("monitoring agent {server_id} is unreachable: {error}"))
        }
    
        fn authenticated<T>(&self, message: T) -> Result<Request<T>, String> {
            let token: MetadataValue<_> = self
                .config
                .metrics_token
                .parse()
                .map_err(|_| "METRICS_TOKEN is not valid gRPC metadata".to_string())?;
            let mut request = Request::new(message);
            request.metadata_mut().insert("x-metrics-token", token);
            Ok(request)
        }
    
        pub async fn server_history(
            &self,
            server_id: i64,
            limit: i64,
        ) -> Result<Vec<ServerMetric>, String> {
            let mut client = self.client(server_id).await?;
            let request = self.authenticated(proto::GetMetricsRequest {
                server_id,
                limit: limit.clamp(1, 1000) as i32,
            })?;
            let metrics = client
                .get_server_metrics(request)
                .await
                .map_err(|error| format!("agent metric query failed: {error}"))?
                .into_inner()
                .metrics;
            Ok(metrics
                .into_iter()
                .map(|metric| ServerMetric {
                    timestamp: chrono::DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339(&metric.timestamp)
                        .ok()
                        .map(|value| value.timestamp()),
                    server_id,
                    cpu: metric.cpu,
                    cpu_model: metric.cpu_model,
                    cpu_cores: i64::from(metric.cpu_cores),
                    cpu_physical_cores: i64::from(metric.cpu_physical_cores),
                    cpu_speed: metric.cpu_speed,
                    os: metric.os,
                    distro: metric.distro,
                    kernel: metric.kernel,
                    arch: metric.arch,
                    mem_used: metric.mem_used,
                    mem_used_gb: metric.mem_used_gb,
                    mem_total: metric.mem_total,
                    uptime: metric.uptime as i64,
                    disk_used: metric.disk_used,
                    total_disk: metric.total_disk,
                    network_in: metric.network_in,
                    network_out: metric.network_out,
                })
                .collect())
        }
    
        pub async fn container_history(
            &self,
            server_id: i64,
            app_name: &str,
            limit: i64,
        ) -> Result<Vec<ContainerMetric>, String> {
            let mut client = self.client(server_id).await?;
            let request = self.authenticated(proto::GetContainerMetricsRequest {
                server_id,
                app_name: app_name.to_owned(),
                limit: limit.clamp(1, 1000) as i32,
            })?;
            let metrics = client
                .get_container_metrics(request)
                .await
                .map_err(|error| format!("agent container query failed: {error}"))?
                .into_inner()
                .metrics;
            Ok(metrics
                .into_iter()
                .map(|metric| ContainerMetric {
                    id: (metric.id > 0).then_some(metric.id),
                    timestamp: chrono::DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339(&metric.timestamp)
                        .map(|value| value.timestamp())
                        .unwrap_or_default(),
                    container_id: metric.container_id,
                    container_name: metric.name,
                    metrics_json: serde_json::json!({
                        "cpu_percent": metric.cpu_perc,
                        "memory_percent": metric.mem_perc,
                        "memory_used_mb": metric.mem_used_mb,
                        "memory_limit_mb": metric.mem_total_mb,
                        "net_rx_kbps": metric.net_in_mb * 1024.0,
                        "net_tx_kbps": metric.net_out_mb * 1024.0,
                        "block_read_mb": metric.block_read_mb,
                        "block_write_mb": metric.block_write_mb
                    })
                    .to_string(),
                    server_id,
                    application_id: (metric.application_id > 0).then_some(metric.application_id),
                    compose_id: (metric.compose_id > 0).then_some(metric.compose_id),
                })
                .collect())
        }
    
        pub async fn get_latest_metrics_per_server(&self) -> Result<Vec<ServerMetric>, String> {
            let servers = self.server_service.list().await.map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
            let mut latest = Vec::new();
            for server in servers {
                let Some(server_id) = server.id else { continue };
                match self.server_history(server_id, 1).await {
                    Ok(mut metrics) => latest.append(&mut metrics),
                    Err(error) => tracing::debug!(server_id, %error, "monitoring agent unavailable"),
                }
            }
            Ok(latest)
        }
    }

    +        let servers = self.server_service.list().await.map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
    +        let mut latest = Vec::new();

    +            let Some(server_id) = server.id else { continue };
    +            match self.container_history(server_id, "", 1000).await {
    +                Ok(metrics) => {
    +                    let mut newest = std::collections::HashMap::new();
    +                    for metric in metrics {
    +                        newest.entry(metric.container_id.clone()).or_insert(metric);
    +                    }
    +                    latest.extend(newest.into_values());
    +                }
    +                Err(error) => tracing::debug!(server_id, %error, "monitoring agent unavailable"),
    +            }
    +        }
    +        Ok(latest)
    +    }

    use auto_di::singleton;
    use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
    use tokio::sync::broadcast;
    
    #[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    pub struct ContainerMetricSseEvent {
        pub server_id: i64,
        pub application_id: i64,
        pub compose_id: i64,
        pub container_id: String,
        pub container_name: String,
        pub cpu_percent: f64,
        pub memory_used_mb: f64,
        pub memory_limit_mb: f64,
        pub net_rx_kbps: f64,
        pub net_tx_kbps: f64,
        pub timestamp: i64,
    }
    
    pub struct MonitoringSseBus {
        metrics_tx: broadcast::Sender<ContainerMetricSseEvent>,
    }
    
    #[singleton]
    impl MonitoringSseBus {
        pub fn new() -> Self {
            let (metrics_tx, _) = broadcast::channel(1000);
            Self { metrics_tx }
        }
    
        pub fn publish_container_metric(&self, event: ContainerMetricSseEvent) {
            let _ = self.metrics_tx.send(event);
        }
    
        pub fn subscribe_container_metrics(&self) -> broadcast::Receiver<ContainerMetricSseEvent> {
            self.metrics_tx.subscribe()
        }
    }

    use std::sync::Arc;
    
    use crate::services::alert::{service::EVALUATION_INTERVAL_SECS, AlertService};
    
    pub fn start(service: Arc<AlertService>) {
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            let mut ticker = tokio::time::interval(std::time::Duration::from_secs(
                EVALUATION_INTERVAL_SECS as u64,
            ));
            ticker.set_missed_tick_behavior(tokio::time::MissedTickBehavior::Skip);
    
            tracing::info!(
                interval_secs = EVALUATION_INTERVAL_SECS,
                "alert evaluation loop started"
            );
    
            loop {
                ticker.tick().await;
                match service.evaluate_once().await {
                    Ok(0) => {}
                    Ok(count) => tracing::debug!(count, "alerts dispatched"),
                    Err(error) => tracing::error!(error = %error, "alert evaluation failed"),
                }
            }
        });
    }

    use auto_di::resolve;
    
    use crate::{
        services::{
            alert::AlertService,
            notification::{
                NotificationLevel, NotificationMessage, NotificationScope, NotificationService,
                NotificationTrigger,
            },
            schedule::ScheduleRunner,
        },
        utils::builder::queue::BuilderQueue,
    };
    
    pub struct BackgroundManager;
    
    impl BackgroundManager {
        pub async fn start_all() -> Result<(), String> {
            let schedule = resolve::<ScheduleRunner>()
                .await
                .map_err(|error| format!("failed to resolve schedule runner: {error}"))?;
            schedule.start().await?;
    
            let builder = resolve::<BuilderQueue>()
                .await
                .map_err(|error| format!("failed to resolve builder queue: {error}"))?;
            builder.start().await?;
    
            let alerts = resolve::<AlertService>()
                .await
                .map_err(|error| format!("failed to resolve alert service: {error}"))?;
            super::alert::start(alerts);
    
            Self::dispatch_startup_notification().await;
            tracing::info!("all background systems started");
            Ok(())
        }
    
        async fn dispatch_startup_notification() {
            let Ok(notifications) = resolve::<NotificationService>().await else {
                tracing::warn!("startup notification service unavailable");
                return;
            };
            let message = NotificationMessage::new(
                "Rustploy Instance Started",
                "Rustploy control panel server has successfully initialized and is operational.",
            )
            .level(NotificationLevel::Info);
    
            tokio::spawn(async move {
                notifications
                    .notify(
                        NotificationScope::AllOrganizations,
                        NotificationTrigger::PanelRestart,
                        &message,
                    )
                    .await;
            });
        }
    }

Bhai current structure ka simple meaning:

```text
src/utils/background/
```

Yahan sirf long-running/background workers ka startup aur lifecycle hai.

### `manager.rs`

Central controller hai.

Ye sab workers ko start karta hai:

- schedule
- builder queue
- alerts
- startup notification

`main.rs` ko clean rakhta hai.

### `alert.rs`

Alert evaluation ka periodic worker.

Har fixed interval par:

```text
remote metrics read
→ alert rules evaluate
→ FIRING event
→ notification
```

Alert ka actual business logic yahan nahi hai; sirf background loop hai.

### `builder.rs`

Builder queue ko background mein start karta hai.

Actual build/deploy logic yahan nahi hai. Wo:

```text
utils/builder/queue/
```

mein hai.

Ye file sirf queue worker ko startup lifecycle deta hai.

### `schedule.rs`

Cron scheduler ka background startup wrapper hai.

Actual schedule logic:

```text
services/schedule/
```

mein hai.

Is file ka kaam scheduler ko central manager ke through start karna hai.

### `notification.rs`

Startup notification dispatch karta hai.

Example:

```text
Rustploy restart hua
→ organizations ko notification
```

Normal email/Discord/Telegram delivery yahan nahi hai. Wo:

```text
services/notification/
```

mein hai.

### `mod.rs`

Background modules ko register/export karta hai:

```rust
pub mod alert;
pub mod builder;
pub mod notification;
pub mod schedule;
```

### `services/alert/`

Alert ka actual domain:

- `service.rs` — alert CRUD + evaluation orchestration
- `engine.rs` — threshold/window calculation
- `rule.rs` — stored rule parsing
- `metric.rs` — CPU/memory/disk types
- `operator.rs` — `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=`, `==`
- `target.rs` — server/application/compose/database
- `event_state.rs` — `FIRING`, `RESOLVED`, `NO_DATA`
- `reading.rs` — collected metric reading
- `sample.rs` — duration/sample window
- `rule_state.rs` — enabled/disabled
- `error.rs` — invalid alert data errors

### `services/monitoring/`

Monitoring infrastructure:

- Remote agent se gRPC metrics pull
- Agent authentication
- Health/status
- Server/container metric conversion

Monitoring alert logic yahan nahi hai, kyunki monitoring data provider hai; alerting alag business feature hai.

Short mein:

```text
utils/background = worker kab aur kaise chalega
services/alert   = alert ka business logic
services/monitoring = metrics kahan se aayengi
services/notification = alert ka message kahan deliver hoga
```

Ye separation isliye hai taaki future mein naya background worker add karna ho to `utils/background/` mein entrypoint add ho, aur business logic apne domain service mein rahe.

services/notification/
```

Uske files ka meaning:

- `loader.rs` — organization ke configured channels load karta hai
- `message.rs` — title, body, fields aur severity
- `trigger.rs` — notification kis event se aayi
- `scope.rs` — kis organization/user ko bhejni hai
- `provider.rs` — Discord, Slack, Telegram jaise provider types
- `guard.rs` — duplicate/repeated notifications control
- `senders/` — har provider ka actual sender implementation
- `email.rs` — email-specific support

`background/notification.rs` normal notifications handle nahi karta. Alert, deployment aur backup notifications directly `NotificationService` use karte hain.

background/notification.rs
    panel startup par one-time asynchronous notification

services/notification/
    complete reusable notification system
```

    use serde_json::Value;
    
    /// Returns whether a webhook containing `changed_paths` should trigger a deploy.
    ///
    /// Empty watch rules mean "deploy on every matching branch". Rules accept a
    /// JSON string array (the persisted API format), newline/comma separated text,
    /// directory prefixes and `*`/`**` glob segments. A rule prefixed with `!`
    /// excludes a path after it was included by another rule.
    pub fn should_deploy(raw_rules: Option<&str>, changed_paths: &[String]) -> Result<bool, String> {
        let rules = parse_rules(raw_rules)?;
        if rules.is_empty() || changed_paths.is_empty() {
            return Ok(true);
        }
    
        Ok(changed_paths.iter().any(|path| {
            let path = normalize(path);
            let mut included = false;
            for rule in &rules {
                if matches_pattern(&rule.pattern, &path) {
                    included = !rule.exclude;
                }
            }
            included
        }))
    }
    
    #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
    struct Rule {
        pattern: String,
        exclude: bool,
    }
    
    fn parse_rules(raw: Option<&str>) -> Result<Vec<Rule>, String> {
        let Some(raw) = raw.map(str::trim).filter(|value| !value.is_empty()) else {
            return Ok(Vec::new());
        };
    
        let values = if raw.starts_with('[') {
            let value: Value = serde_json::from_str(raw)
                .map_err(|error| format!("watch_paths must be a JSON string array: {error}"))?;
            value
                .as_array()
                .ok_or_else(|| "watch_paths must be a JSON string array".to_string())?
                .iter()
                .map(|item| {
                    item.as_str()
                        .map(str::to_owned)
                        .ok_or_else(|| "watch_paths entries must be strings".to_string())
                })
                .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?
        } else {
            raw.split([',', '\n'])
                .map(str::trim)
                .filter(|value| !value.is_empty())
                .map(str::to_owned)
                .collect()
        };
    
        Ok(values
            .into_iter()
            .filter_map(|value| {
                let value = value.trim();
                let (exclude, value) = value
                    .strip_prefix('!')
                    .map_or((false, value), |value| (true, value));
                let pattern = normalize(value).trim_end_matches('/').to_owned();
                (!pattern.is_empty()).then_some(Rule { pattern, exclude })
            })
            .collect())
    }
    
    fn normalize(value: &str) -> String {
        value
            .trim()
            .trim_start_matches("./")
            .trim_start_matches('/')
            .replace('\\', "/")
    }
    
    fn matches_pattern(pattern: &str, path: &str) -> bool {
        if !pattern.contains('*') {
            return path == pattern || path.starts_with(&format!("{pattern}/"));
        }
        glob_match(pattern.as_bytes(), path.as_bytes())
    }
    
    fn glob_match(pattern: &[u8], path: &[u8]) -> bool {
        match pattern {
            [] => path.is_empty(),
            [b'*', b'*', rest @ ..] => {
                let rest = rest.strip_prefix(b"/").unwrap_or(rest);
                glob_match(rest, path)
                    || (!path.is_empty() && glob_match(pattern, &path[1..]))
            }
            [b'*', rest @ ..] => {
                glob_match(rest, path)
                    || (!path.is_empty() && path[0] != b'/' && glob_match(pattern, &path[1..]))
            }
            [head, rest @ ..] => {
                path.first() == Some(head) && glob_match(rest, &path[1..])
            }
        }
    }
    
    #[cfg(test)]
    mod tests {
        use super::*;
    
        fn paths(values: &[&str]) -> Vec<String> {
            values.iter().map(|value| (*value).to_owned()).collect()
        }
    
        #[test]
        fn empty_rules_deploy_every_change() {
            assert!(should_deploy(None, &paths(&["README.md"])).unwrap());
        }
    
        #[test]
        fn supports_json_prefix_and_glob_rules() {
            let rules = Some(r#"["apps/api", "packages/**/*.rs"]"#);
            assert!(should_deploy(rules, &paths(&["apps/api/src/main.rs"])).unwrap());
            assert!(should_deploy(rules, &paths(&["packages/core/src/lib.rs"])).unwrap());
            assert!(!should_deploy(rules, &paths(&["docs/index.md"])).unwrap());
        }
    
        #[test]
        fn later_exclusion_wins() {
            let rules = Some("apps/**,!apps/docs/**");
            assert!(!should_deploy(rules, &paths(&["apps/docs/readme.md"])).unwrap());
            assert!(should_deploy(rules, &paths(&["apps/api/main.rs"])).unwrap());
        }
    
        #[test]
        fn rejects_non_string_json_entries() {
            assert!(should_deploy(Some(r#"["src", 42]"#), &paths(&["src/main.rs"])).is_err());
        }
    }

    use serde::Deserialize;
    use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};
    use std::collections::BTreeSet;
    
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
    pub enum GitProviderKind {
        Github,
        Gitlab,
        Gitea,
        Bitbucket,
    }
    
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
    pub struct PushEvent {
        pub provider: GitProviderKind,
        pub owner: String,
        pub repository: String,
        pub branch: String,
        pub before: Option<String>,
        pub after: Option<String>,
        pub changed_paths: Vec<String>,
    }
    
    pub fn verify_hmac_sha256(secret: &[u8], body: &[u8], signature: &str) -> bool {
        let signature = signature.strip_prefix("sha256=").unwrap_or(signature);
        let Some(expected) = decode_hex(signature) else {
            return false;
        };
        constant_time_eq(&hmac_sha256(secret, body), &expected)
    }
    
    pub fn verify_token(expected: &str, received: Option<&str>) -> bool {
        received.is_some_and(|received| constant_time_eq(expected.as_bytes(), received.as_bytes()))
    }
    
    pub fn parse_push(provider: GitProviderKind, body: &[u8]) -> Result<PushEvent, String> {
        match provider {
            GitProviderKind::Github | GitProviderKind::Gitea => parse_github_like(provider, body),
            GitProviderKind::Gitlab => parse_gitlab(body),
            GitProviderKind::Bitbucket => parse_bitbucket(body),
        }
    }
    
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct GithubLikePayload {
        #[serde(rename = "ref")]
        git_ref: String,
        before: Option<String>,
        after: Option<String>,
        repository: GithubLikeRepository,
        #[serde(default)]
        commits: Vec<ChangedCommit>,
    }
    
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct GithubLikeRepository {
        name: String,
        owner: GithubLikeOwner,
    }
    
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct GithubLikeOwner {
        login: Option<String>,
        username: Option<String>,
        name: Option<String>,
    }
    
    #[derive(Deserialize, Default)]
    struct ChangedCommit {
        #[serde(default)]
        added: Vec<String>,
        #[serde(default)]
        modified: Vec<String>,
        #[serde(default)]
        removed: Vec<String>,
    }
    
    fn parse_github_like(provider: GitProviderKind, body: &[u8]) -> Result<PushEvent, String> {
        let payload: GithubLikePayload = serde_json::from_slice(body)
            .map_err(|error| format!("invalid GitHub/Gitea push payload: {error}"))?;
        let owner = payload.repository.owner.login
            .or(payload.repository.owner.username)
            .or(payload.repository.owner.name)
            .filter(|value| !value.trim().is_empty())
            .ok_or_else(|| "push payload has no repository owner".to_string())?;
        Ok(PushEvent {
            provider,
            owner,
            repository: payload.repository.name,
            branch: branch_from_ref(&payload.git_ref)?,
            before: payload.before,
            after: payload.after,
            changed_paths: collect_paths(payload.commits),
        })
    }
    
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct GitlabPayload {
        #[serde(rename = "ref")]
        git_ref: String,
        before: Option<String>,
        after: Option<String>,
        project: GitlabProject,
        #[serde(default)]
        commits: Vec<ChangedCommit>,
    }
    
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct GitlabProject {
        path: String,
        path_with_namespace: String,
    }
    
    fn parse_gitlab(body: &[u8]) -> Result<PushEvent, String> {
        let payload: GitlabPayload = serde_json::from_slice(body)
            .map_err(|error| format!("invalid GitLab push payload: {error}"))?;
        let owner = payload.project.path_with_namespace
            .rsplit_once('/')
            .map(|(owner, _)| owner.to_owned())
            .ok_or_else(|| "GitLab payload has no project namespace".to_string())?;
        Ok(PushEvent {
            provider: GitProviderKind::Gitlab,
            owner,
            repository: payload.project.path,
            branch: branch_from_ref(&payload.git_ref)?,
            before: payload.before,
            after: payload.after,
            changed_paths: collect_paths(payload.commits),
        })
    }
    
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct BitbucketPayload {
        repository: BitbucketRepository,
        push: BitbucketPush,
    }
    
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct BitbucketRepository {
        name: String,
        owner: BitbucketOwner,
    }
    
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct BitbucketOwner {
        username: Option<String>,
        nickname: Option<String>,
        display_name: Option<String>,
    }
    
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct BitbucketPush {
        changes: Vec<BitbucketChange>,
    }
    
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct BitbucketChange {
        #[serde(rename = "new")]
        new_ref: Option<BitbucketRef>,
        old: Option<BitbucketRef>,
    }
    
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct BitbucketRef {
        name: String,
        target: Option<BitbucketTarget>,
    }
    
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct BitbucketTarget { hash: String }
    
    fn parse_bitbucket(body: &[u8]) -> Result<PushEvent, String> {
        let payload: BitbucketPayload = serde_json::from_slice(body)
            .map_err(|error| format!("invalid Bitbucket push payload: {error}"))?;
        let change = payload.push.changes.into_iter().next()
            .ok_or_else(|| "Bitbucket push contains no changes".to_string())?;
        let branch = change.new_ref.as_ref().or(change.old.as_ref())
            .map(|reference| reference.name.clone())
            .ok_or_else(|| "Bitbucket push contains no branch".to_string())?;
        let owner = payload.repository.owner.username
            .or(payload.repository.owner.nickname)
            .or(payload.repository.owner.display_name)
            .ok_or_else(|| "Bitbucket payload has no repository owner".to_string())?;
        Ok(PushEvent {
            provider: GitProviderKind::Bitbucket,
            owner,
            repository: payload.repository.name,
            branch,
            before: change.old.and_then(|value| value.target).map(|target| target.hash),
            after: change.new_ref.and_then(|value| value.target).map(|target| target.hash),
            changed_paths: Vec::new(),
        })
    }
    
    fn branch_from_ref(value: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
        value.strip_prefix("refs/heads/")
            .filter(|branch| !branch.is_empty())
            .map(str::to_owned)
            .ok_or_else(|| format!("unsupported Git ref: {value}"))
    }
    
    fn collect_paths(commits: Vec<ChangedCommit>) -> Vec<String> {
        commits.into_iter()
            .flat_map(|commit| commit.added.into_iter().chain(commit.modified).chain(commit.removed))
            .collect::<BTreeSet<_>>()
            .into_iter()
            .collect()
    }
    
    fn hmac_sha256(secret: &[u8], body: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
        const BLOCK: usize = 64;
        let mut key = if secret.len() > BLOCK { Sha256::digest(secret).to_vec() } else { secret.to_vec() };
        key.resize(BLOCK, 0);
        let mut inner_pad = [0x36_u8; BLOCK];
        let mut outer_pad = [0x5c_u8; BLOCK];
        for (index, byte) in key.iter().enumerate() {
            inner_pad[index] ^= byte;
            outer_pad[index] ^= byte;
        }
        let inner = Sha256::new().chain_update(inner_pad).chain_update(body).finalize();
        Sha256::new().chain_update(outer_pad).chain_update(inner).finalize().to_vec()
    }
    
    fn decode_hex(value: &str) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
        if !value.len().is_multiple_of(2) { return None; }
        value.as_bytes().chunks_exact(2).map(|pair| {
            let high = (pair[0] as char).to_digit(16)?;
            let low = (pair[1] as char).to_digit(16)?;
            Some(((high << 4) | low) as u8)
        }).collect()
    }
    
    fn constant_time_eq(left: &[u8], right: &[u8]) -> bool {
        if left.len() != right.len() { return false; }
        left.iter().zip(right).fold(0_u8, |diff, (left, right)| diff | (left ^ right)) == 0
    }

            assert!(!verify_hmac_sha256(b"secret", b"modified", "sha256=b82fcb791acec57859b989b430a826488ce2e479fdf92326bd0a2e8375a42ba4"));
        }
    
        #[test]
        fn parses_github_push_and_deduplicates_paths() {
            let body = br#"{"ref":"refs/heads/main","before":"a","after":"b","repository":{"name":"api","owner":{"login":"acme"}},"commits":[{"added":["src/main.rs"],"modified":["src/main.rs","Cargo.toml"],"removed":[]}]}"#;
            let event = parse_push(GitProviderKind::Github, body).unwrap();
            assert_eq!(event.owner, "acme");
            assert_eq!(event.repository, "api");
            assert_eq!(event.branch, "main");
            assert_eq!(event.changed_paths, vec!["Cargo.toml", "src/main.rs"]);
        }
    
        #[test]

            let body = br#"{"ref":"refs/heads/develop","before":"a","after":"b","project":{"path":"api","path_with_namespace":"acme/platform/api"},"commits":[]}"#;
            let event = parse_push(GitProviderKind::Gitlab, body).unwrap();
            assert_eq!(event.owner, "acme/platform");
            assert_eq!(event.branch, "develop");
        }
    }

    use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};
    
    pub fn verify_hmac_sha256(secret: &[u8], body: &[u8], signature: &str) -> bool {
        let signature = signature.strip_prefix("sha256=").unwrap_or(signature);
        let Some(expected) = decode_hex(signature) else {
            return false;
        };
        constant_time_eq(&hmac_sha256(secret, body), &expected)
    }
    
    pub fn verify_token(expected: &str, received: Option<&str>) -> bool {
        received.is_some_and(|received| constant_time_eq(expected.as_bytes(), received.as_bytes()))
    }
    
    fn hmac_sha256(secret: &[u8], body: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
        const BLOCK: usize = 64;
        let mut key = if secret.len() > BLOCK {
            Sha256::digest(secret).to_vec()
        } else {
            secret.to_vec()
        };
        key.resize(BLOCK, 0);
    
        let mut inner_pad = [0x36_u8; BLOCK];
        let mut outer_pad = [0x5c_u8; BLOCK];
        for (index, byte) in key.iter().enumerate() {
            inner_pad[index] ^= byte;
            outer_pad[index] ^= byte;
        }
    
        let inner = Sha256::new()
            .chain_update(inner_pad)
            .chain_update(body)
            .finalize();
        Sha256::new()
            .chain_update(outer_pad)
            .chain_update(inner)
            .finalize()
            .to_vec()
    }
    
    fn decode_hex(value: &str) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
        if !value.len().is_multiple_of(2) {
            return None;
        }
        value
            .as_bytes()
            .chunks_exact(2)
            .map(|pair| {
                let high = (pair[0] as char).to_digit(16)?;
                let low = (pair[1] as char).to_digit(16)?;
                Some(((high << 4) | low) as u8)
            })
            .collect()
    }
    
    fn constant_time_eq(left: &[u8], right: &[u8]) -> bool {
        if left.len() != right.len() {
            return false;
        }
        left.iter()
            .zip(right)
            .fold(0_u8, |diff, (left, right)| diff | (left ^ right))
            == 0
    }

    use serde::Deserialize;
    
    use super::types::{GitProviderKind, PushEvent};
    
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct Payload {
        repository: Repository,
        push: Push,
    }
    
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct Repository {
        name: String,
        owner: Owner,
    }
    
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct Owner {
        username: Option<String>,
        nickname: Option<String>,
        display_name: Option<String>,
    }
    
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct Push {
        changes: Vec<Change>,
    }
    
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct Change {
        #[serde(rename = "new")]
        new_ref: Option<Reference>,
        old: Option<Reference>,
    }
    
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct Reference {
        name: String,
        target: Option<Target>,
    }
    
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct Target {
        hash: String,
    }
    
    pub(super) fn parse(body: &[u8]) -> Result<PushEvent, String> {
        let payload: Payload = serde_json::from_slice(body)
            .map_err(|error| format!("invalid Bitbucket push payload: {error}"))?;
        let change = payload
            .push
            .changes
            .into_iter()
            .next()
            .ok_or_else(|| "Bitbucket push contains no changes".to_string())?;
        let branch = change
            .new_ref
            .as_ref()
            .or(change.old.as_ref())
            .map(|reference| reference.name.clone())
            .ok_or_else(|| "Bitbucket push contains no branch".to_string())?;
        let owner = payload
            .repository
            .owner
            .username
            .or(payload.repository.owner.nickname)
            .or(payload.repository.owner.display_name)
            .ok_or_else(|| "Bitbucket payload has no repository owner".to_string())?;
    
        Ok(PushEvent {
            provider: GitProviderKind::Bitbucket,
            owner,
            repository: payload.repository.name,
            branch,
            before: change
                .old
                .and_then(|value| value.target)
                .map(|target| target.hash),
            after: change
                .new_ref
                .and_then(|value| value.target)
                .map(|target| target.hash),
            changed_paths: Vec::new(),
        })
    }

        git_ref: String,
        before: Option<String>,
        after: Option<String>,
        repository: Repository,

    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct Repository {
        name: String,
        owner: Owner,
    }
    
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct Owner {
        login: Option<String>,
        username: Option<String>,
        name: Option<String>,
    }
    
    pub(super) fn parse(provider: GitProviderKind, body: &[u8]) -> Result<PushEvent, String> {
        let payload: Payload = serde_json::from_slice(body)
            .map_err(|error| format!("invalid GitHub/Gitea push payload: {error}"))?;
        let owner = payload
            .repository
            .owner
            .login
            .or(payload.repository.owner.username)
            .or(payload.repository.owner.name)
            .filter(|value| !value.trim().is_empty())
            .ok_or_else(|| "push payload has no repository owner".to_string())?;
    
        Ok(PushEvent {
            provider,
            owner,
            repository: payload.repository.name,
            branch: branch_from_ref(&payload.git_ref)?,
            before: payload.before,
            after: payload.after,
            changed_paths: collect_paths(payload.commits),
        })
    }

        project: Project,

        path: String,
        path_with_namespace: String,
    }
    
    pub(super) fn parse(body: &[u8]) -> Result<PushEvent, String> {
        let payload: Payload = serde_json::from_slice(body)
            .map_err(|error| format!("invalid GitLab push payload: {error}"))?;
        let owner = payload
            .project
            .path_with_namespace
            .rsplit_once('/')
            .map(|(owner, _)| owner.to_owned())
            .ok_or_else(|| "GitLab payload has no project namespace".to_string())?;
    
        Ok(PushEvent {
            provider: GitProviderKind::Gitlab,
            owner,
            repository: payload.project.path,
            branch: branch_from_ref(&payload.git_ref)?,
            before: payload.before,
            after: payload.after,
            changed_paths: collect_paths(payload.commits),
        })
    }

    use serde::Deserialize;
    use std::collections::BTreeSet;
    
    #[derive(Deserialize, Default)]
    pub(super) struct ChangedCommit {
        #[serde(default)]
        added: Vec<String>,
        #[serde(default)]
        modified: Vec<String>,
        #[serde(default)]
        removed: Vec<String>,
    }
    
    pub(super) fn branch_from_ref(value: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
        value
            .strip_prefix("refs/heads/")
            .filter(|branch| !branch.is_empty())
            .map(str::to_owned)
            .ok_or_else(|| format!("unsupported Git ref: {value}"))
    }
    
    pub(super) fn collect_paths(commits: Vec<ChangedCommit>) -> Vec<String> {
        commits
            .into_iter()
            .flat_map(|commit| {
                commit
                    .added
                    .into_iter()
                    .chain(commit.modified)
                    .chain(commit.removed)
            })
            .collect::<BTreeSet<_>>()
            .into_iter()
            .collect()
    }

        ));
    }
    
    #[test]
    fn parses_github_push_and_deduplicates_paths() {
        let body = br#"{"ref":"refs/heads/main","before":"a","after":"b","repository":{"name":"api","owner":{"login":"acme"}},"commits":[{"added":["src/main.rs"],"modified":["src/main.rs","Cargo.toml"],"removed":[]}]}"#;
        let event = parse_push(GitProviderKind::Github, body).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(event.owner, "acme");
        assert_eq!(event.repository, "api");
        assert_eq!(event.branch, "main");
        assert_eq!(event.changed_paths, vec!["Cargo.toml", "src/main.rs"]);
    }
    
    #[test]
    fn parses_gitlab_namespace() {
        let body = br#"{"ref":"refs/heads/develop","before":"a","after":"b","project":{"path":"api","path_with_namespace":"acme/platform/api"},"commits":[]}"#;
        let event = parse_push(GitProviderKind::Gitlab, body).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(event.owner, "acme/platform");
        assert_eq!(event.branch, "develop");
    }

    use auto_route::controller;
    use axum::{
        Json,
        body::Bytes,
        extract::Path,
        http::{HeaderMap, StatusCode},
    };
    use std::sync::Arc;
    
    use crate::services::webhook::{
        GitProviderKind, WebhookCredential, WebhookCredentialStore, WebhookDispatcher, parse_push,
        verify_hmac_sha256, verify_token,
    };
    
    type ApiError = (StatusCode, String);
    
    pub struct WebhookController {
        credentials: Arc<WebhookCredentialStore>,
        dispatcher: Arc<WebhookDispatcher>,
    }
    
    #[controller("/public/webhooks")]
    impl WebhookController {
        fn new(
            credentials: Arc<WebhookCredentialStore>,
            dispatcher: Arc<WebhookDispatcher>,
        ) -> Self {
            Self {
                credentials,
                dispatcher,
            }
        }
    
        #[post("/{provider}/{provider_id}")]
        async fn receive(
            &self,
            Path((provider, provider_id)): Path<(String, i64)>,
            headers: HeaderMap,
            body: Bytes,
        ) -> Result<Json<crate::services::webhook::DispatchOutcome>, ApiError> {
            let provider = parse_provider(&provider)?;
            validate_event_header(provider, &headers)?;
            let credential = self
                .credentials
                .load(provider, provider_id)
                .await
                .map_err(|error| (StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED, error))?;
            verify_request(provider, &credential, &headers, &body)?;
            let event = parse_push(provider, &body)
                .map_err(|error| (StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, error))?;
            self.dispatcher
                .dispatch(&event)
                .await
                .map(Json)
                .map_err(|error| (StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, error))
        }
    }
    
    fn parse_provider(value: &str) -> Result<GitProviderKind, ApiError> {
        match value.to_ascii_lowercase().as_str() {
            "github" => Ok(GitProviderKind::Github),
            "gitlab" => Ok(GitProviderKind::Gitlab),
            "gitea" => Ok(GitProviderKind::Gitea),
            "bitbucket" => Ok(GitProviderKind::Bitbucket),
            _ => Err((StatusCode::NOT_FOUND, "unsupported Git provider".into())),
        }
    }
    
    fn validate_event_header(provider: GitProviderKind, headers: &HeaderMap) -> Result<(), ApiError> {
        let (name, expected) = match provider {
            GitProviderKind::Github => ("x-github-event", "push"),
            GitProviderKind::Gitlab => ("x-gitlab-event", "push hook"),
            GitProviderKind::Gitea => ("x-gitea-event", "push"),
            GitProviderKind::Bitbucket => ("x-event-key", "repo:push"),
        };
        let value = header(headers, name).unwrap_or_default().to_ascii_lowercase();
        if value != expected {
            return Err((StatusCode::ACCEPTED, format!("ignored webhook event: {value}")));
        }
        Ok(())
    }
    
    fn verify_request(
        provider: GitProviderKind,
        credential: &WebhookCredential,
        headers: &HeaderMap,
        body: &[u8],
    ) -> Result<(), ApiError> {
        let valid = match (provider, credential) {
            (GitProviderKind::Github, WebhookCredential::Hmac(secret)) => header(headers, "x-hub-signature-256")
                .is_some_and(|signature| verify_hmac_sha256(secret.as_bytes(), body, signature)),
            (GitProviderKind::Gitea, WebhookCredential::Hmac(secret)) => header(headers, "x-gitea-signature")
                .is_some_and(|signature| verify_hmac_sha256(secret.as_bytes(), body, signature)),
            (GitProviderKind::Gitlab, WebhookCredential::Token(secret)) => {
                verify_token(secret, header(headers, "x-gitlab-token"))
            }
            (GitProviderKind::Bitbucket, WebhookCredential::Token(secret)) => {
                verify_token(secret, header(headers, "x-rustploy-token"))
            }
            _ => false,
        };
        valid.then_some(()).ok_or_else(|| {
            (StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED, "invalid webhook signature or token".into())
        })
    }
    
    fn header<'a>(headers: &'a HeaderMap, name: &str) -> Option<&'a str> {
        headers.get(name)?.to_str().ok()
    }

    use auto_di::singleton;
    use sqlx::SqlitePool;
    use std::sync::Arc;
    
    use super::GitProviderKind;
    
    #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
    pub enum WebhookCredential {
        Hmac(String),
        Token(String),
    }
    
    pub struct WebhookCredentialStore {
        db: Arc<SqlitePool>,
    }
    
    #[singleton]
    impl WebhookCredentialStore {
        fn new(db: Arc<SqlitePool>) -> Self {
            Self { db }
        }
    
        pub async fn load(
            &self,
            provider: GitProviderKind,
            provider_id: i64,
        ) -> Result<WebhookCredential, String> {
            let value = match provider {
                GitProviderKind::Github => {
                    sqlx::query_scalar::<_, Option<String>>(
                        "SELECT github_webhook_secret FROM github_providers WHERE id = ?",
                    )
                    .bind(provider_id)
                    .fetch_optional(self.db.as_ref())
                    .await
                    .map_err(|error| error.to_string())?
                    .flatten()
                    .map(WebhookCredential::Hmac)
                }
                GitProviderKind::Gitlab => {
                    sqlx::query_scalar::<_, Option<String>>(
                        "SELECT secret FROM gitlab_providers WHERE id = ?",
                    )
                    .bind(provider_id)
                    .fetch_optional(self.db.as_ref())
                    .await
                    .map_err(|error| error.to_string())?
                    .flatten()
                    .map(WebhookCredential::Token)
                }
                GitProviderKind::Gitea => {
                    sqlx::query_scalar::<_, Option<String>>(
                        "SELECT client_secret FROM gitea_providers WHERE id = ?",
                    )
                    .bind(provider_id)
                    .fetch_optional(self.db.as_ref())
                    .await
                    .map_err(|error| error.to_string())?
                    .flatten()
                    .map(WebhookCredential::Hmac)
                }
                GitProviderKind::Bitbucket => {
                    sqlx::query_scalar::<_, Option<String>>(
                        "SELECT COALESCE(api_token, app_password) FROM bitbucket_providers WHERE id = ?",
                    )
                    .bind(provider_id)
                    .fetch_optional(self.db.as_ref())
                    .await
                    .map_err(|error| error.to_string())?
                    .flatten()
                    .map(WebhookCredential::Token)
                }
            };
    
            value.ok_or_else(|| "webhook provider credential is not configured".to_string())
        }
    }
