    Add: /run/media/das/SSD/Devloper/rustploy/src/utils/os/crypto/certificate.rs
    use crate::utils::exec::{CommandExecutor, ExecError, ExecResult};
    
    pub struct CertificatePairValidation { pub expires_at: i64 }
    pub struct ValidateCertificatePairBuilder<'a> { executor: &'a CommandExecutor, certificate: String, private_key: String }
    impl<'a> ValidateCertificatePairBuilder<'a> {
        pub(crate) fn new(executor: &'a CommandExecutor, certificate: String, private_key: String) -> Self { Self { executor, certificate, private_key } }
        pub async fn run(self) -> ExecResult<CertificatePairValidation> {
            if !self.certificate.contains("BEGIN CERTIFICATE") || !self.private_key.contains("PRIVATE KEY") { return Err(protocol("invalid PEM certificate or private key")); }
            let id = uuid::Uuid::new_v4().simple().to_string();
            let cert_path = format!("/tmp/rustploy-cert-{id}.pem");
            let key_path = format!("/tmp/rustploy-key-{id}.pem");
            self.executor.run_with_stdin("tee", [&cert_path], self.certificate.as_bytes()).await?;
            self.executor.run_with_stdin("tee", [&key_path], self.private_key.as_bytes()).await?;
            let cert_public = self.executor.run("openssl", ["x509", "-in", &cert_path, "-pubkey", "-noout"]).await;
            let key_public = self.executor.run("openssl", ["pkey", "-in", &key_path, "-pubout"]).await;
            let expiry = self.executor.run("openssl", ["x509", "-in", &cert_path, "-noout", "-enddate"]).await;
            let _ = self.executor.run("rm", ["-f", &cert_path, &key_path]).await;
            let cert_public = cert_public?; let key_public = key_public?; let expiry = expiry?;
            if cert_public.stdout != key_public.stdout { return Err(protocol("certificate and private key do not match")); }
            let raw = expiry.stdout_trimmed().trim_start_matches("notAfter=");
            let expires_at = chrono::NaiveDateTime::parse_from_str(raw, "%b %e %H:%M:%S %Y GMT").map(|v| v.and_utc().timestamp()).map_err(|e| protocol(&e.to_string()))?;
            if expires_at <= chrono::Utc::now().timestamp() { return Err(protocol("certificate is already expired")); }
            Ok(CertificatePairValidation { expires_at })
        }
    }
    fn protocol(message: &str) -> ExecError { ExecError::Protocol(message.to_owned()) }

    use crate::utils::exec::{CommandExecutor, ExecOutput, ExecResult};
    
    pub struct ServerDiagnosticsBuilder<'a> { executor: &'a CommandExecutor, docker: bool, firewall: bool }
    impl<'a> ServerDiagnosticsBuilder<'a> {
        pub(crate) fn new(executor: &'a CommandExecutor) -> Self { Self { executor, docker: true, firewall: true } }
        pub fn docker(mut self, enabled: bool) -> Self { self.docker = enabled; self }
        pub fn firewall(mut self, enabled: bool) -> Self { self.firewall = enabled; self }
        pub async fn run(self) -> ExecResult<ExecOutput> {
            let mut stdout = String::new(); let mut stderr = String::new();
            for (command, args) in [("uname", vec!["-a"]), ("df", vec!["-h"]), ("free", vec!["-h"])] { collect(self.executor.run(command, args).await, &mut stdout, &mut stderr); }
            if self.docker { collect(self.executor.run("docker", ["version"]).await, &mut stdout, &mut stderr); collect(self.executor.run("docker", ["info"]).await, &mut stdout, &mut stderr); }
            if self.firewall {
                if self.executor.run("command", ["-v", "ufw"]).await.is_ok() { collect(self.executor.run("ufw", ["status", "verbose"]).await, &mut stdout, &mut stderr); }
                if self.executor.run("command", ["-v", "firewall-cmd"]).await.is_ok() { collect(self.executor.run("firewall-cmd", ["--list-all"]).await, &mut stdout, &mut stderr); }
                if self.executor.run("command", ["-v", "iptables"]).await.is_ok() { collect(self.executor.run("iptables", ["-S"]).await, &mut stdout, &mut stderr); }
            }
            Ok(ExecOutput { status: crate::utils::exec::ExecExitStatus::success(), stdout, stderr })
        }
    }
    fn collect(result: ExecResult<ExecOutput>, stdout: &mut String, stderr: &mut String) { match result { Ok(output) => { stdout.push_str(&output.stdout); stdout.push('\n'); stderr.push_str(&output.stderr); }, Err(error) => { stderr.push_str(&error.to_string()); stderr.push('\n'); } } }

    use crate::utils::exec::script::IntoCommand;
    use crate::utils::exec::{CommandExecutor, ExecOutput, ExecResult};
    use crate::utils::os::escape_arg;
    
    pub struct ArchiveCreateBuilder<'a> {
        executor: &'a CommandExecutor,
        archive: String,
        entries: Vec<(Option<String>, String)>,
        ignore_failed_read: bool,
    }
    
    impl<'a> ArchiveCreateBuilder<'a> {
        pub(crate) fn new(executor: &'a CommandExecutor, archive: String) -> Self {
            Self {
                executor,
                archive,
                entries: Vec::new(),
                ignore_failed_read: false,
            }
        }
    
        pub fn entry(mut self, path: impl IntoCommand) -> Self {
            self.entries.push((None, path.build_str()));
            self
        }
    
        pub fn entry_from(mut self, base: impl IntoCommand, path: impl IntoCommand) -> Self {
            self.entries
                .push((Some(base.build_str()), path.build_str()));
            self
        }
    
        pub fn ignore_failed_read(mut self, enabled: bool) -> Self {
            self.ignore_failed_read = enabled;
            self
        }
    
        fn args(&self) -> Vec<String> {
            let mut args = vec!["-czf".into(), self.archive.clone()];
            if self.ignore_failed_read {
                args.push("--ignore-failed-read".into());
            }
            for (base, path) in &self.entries {
                if let Some(base) = base {
                    args.extend(["-C".into(), base.clone()]);
                }
                args.push(path.clone());
            }
            args
        }
    
        pub async fn run(self) -> ExecResult<ExecOutput> {
            self.executor.run("tar", self.args()).await
        }
    }
    
    impl IntoCommand for ArchiveCreateBuilder<'_> {
        fn build_str(&self) -> String {
            format!(
                "tar {}",
                self.args()
                    .iter()
                    .map(escape_arg)
                    .collect::<Vec<_>>()
                    .join(" ")
            )
        }
    }

    use crate::utils::exec::{CommandExecutor, ExecError, ExecResult};
    use crate::utils::os::OsCli;
    
    pub struct CertificatePairValidation {
        pub expires_at: i64,
    }
    
    pub struct CertificateBuilder<'a> {
        executor: &'a CommandExecutor,
        certificate: String,
    }
    
    impl<'a> CertificateBuilder<'a> {
        pub(crate) fn new(executor: &'a CommandExecutor, certificate: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
            Self {
                executor,
                certificate: certificate.into(),
            }
        }
    
        pub fn expiry(self) -> CertificateExpiryBuilder<'a> {
            CertificateExpiryBuilder {
                executor: self.executor,
                certificate: self.certificate,
            }
        }
    
        pub fn validate_with_key(
            self,
            private_key: impl Into<String>,
        ) -> CertificatePairValidationBuilder<'a> {
            CertificatePairValidationBuilder {
                executor: self.executor,
                certificate: self.certificate,
                private_key: private_key.into(),
            }
        }
    }
    
    pub struct CertificateExpiryBuilder<'a> {
        executor: &'a CommandExecutor,
        certificate: String,
    }
    
    impl CertificateExpiryBuilder<'_> {
        pub async fn run(self) -> ExecResult<i64> {
            validate_pem(&self.certificate, "BEGIN CERTIFICATE", "invalid PEM certificate")?;
            let cert_path = temporary_path("certificate");
            let os = OsCli::new(self.executor);
            os.file(&cert_path).write(&self.certificate).execute().await?;
            let result = certificate_expiry(self.executor, &cert_path).await;
            let _ = os.file(&cert_path).delete().run().await;
            result
        }
    }
    
    pub struct CertificatePairValidationBuilder<'a> {
        executor: &'a CommandExecutor,
        certificate: String,
        private_key: String,
    }
    
    impl CertificatePairValidationBuilder<'_> {
        pub async fn run(self) -> ExecResult<CertificatePairValidation> {
            validate_pem(&self.certificate, "BEGIN CERTIFICATE", "invalid PEM certificate")?;
            validate_pem(&self.private_key, "PRIVATE KEY", "invalid PEM private key")?;
    
            let cert_path = temporary_path("certificate");
            let key_path = temporary_path("private-key");
            let os = OsCli::new(self.executor);
            let result = async {
                os.file(&cert_path).write(&self.certificate).execute().await?;
                os.file(&key_path).write(&self.private_key).execute().await?;
                os.file(&key_path).chmod("0600").run().await?;
    
                let cert_public = self
                    .executor
                    .run("openssl", ["x509", "-in", &cert_path, "-pubkey", "-noout"])
                    .await?;
                let key_public = self
                    .executor
                    .run("openssl", ["pkey", "-in", &key_path, "-pubout"])
                    .await?;
                if cert_public.stdout != key_public.stdout {
                    return Err(validation_error("certificate and private key do not match"));
                }
    
                let expires_at = certificate_expiry(self.executor, &cert_path).await?;
                if expires_at <= chrono::Utc::now().timestamp() {
                    return Err(validation_error("certificate is already expired"));
                }
                Ok(CertificatePairValidation { expires_at })
            }
            .await;
    
            let _ = os.file(&cert_path).delete().run().await;
            let _ = os.file(&key_path).delete().run().await;
            result
        }
    }
    
    async fn certificate_expiry(executor: &CommandExecutor, path: &str) -> ExecResult<i64> {
        let output = executor
            .run("openssl", ["x509", "-in", path, "-noout", "-enddate"])
            .await?;
        let raw = output.stdout_trimmed().trim_start_matches("notAfter=");
        chrono::NaiveDateTime::parse_from_str(raw, "%b %e %H:%M:%S %Y GMT")
            .map(|value| value.and_utc().timestamp())
            .map_err(|error| validation_error(&format!("invalid certificate expiry: {error}")))
    }
    
    fn validate_pem(value: &str, marker: &str, message: &str) -> ExecResult<()> {
        if value.contains(marker) {
            Ok(())
        } else {
            Err(validation_error(message))
        }
    }
    
    fn temporary_path(kind: &str) -> String {
        format!(
            "/tmp/rustploy-{kind}-{}.pem",
            uuid::Uuid::new_v4().simple()
        )
    }
    
    fn validation_error(message: &str) -> ExecError {
        ExecError::CommandFailed {
            code: None,
            stderr: message.to_owned(),
        }
    }

    use crate::utils::os::escape_arg;
    
    pub struct DirCopyBuilder<'a> {
        executor: &'a CommandExecutor,
        source: String,
        target: String,
        preserve: bool,
        contents_only: bool,
    }
    
    impl<'a> DirCopyBuilder<'a> {
        pub(crate) fn new(
            executor: &'a CommandExecutor,
            source: String,
            target: impl IntoCommand,
        ) -> Self {
            Self {
                executor,
                source,
                target: target.build_str(),
                preserve: true,
                contents_only: false,
            }
        }
    
        pub fn preserve(mut self, enabled: bool) -> Self {
            self.preserve = enabled;
            self
        }
    
        pub fn contents_only(mut self, enabled: bool) -> Self {
            self.contents_only = enabled;
            self
        }
    
        fn source(&self) -> String {
            if self.contents_only {
                format!("{}/.", self.source.trim_end_matches('/'))
            } else {
                self.source.clone()
            }
        }
    
        pub async fn run(self) -> ExecResult<ExecOutput> {
            let mut args = vec![if self.preserve { "-a" } else { "-R" }.to_owned()];
            args.extend([self.source(), self.target.clone()]);
            self.executor.run("cp", args).await
        }
    }
    
    impl IntoCommand for DirCopyBuilder<'_> {
        fn build_str(&self) -> String {
            format!(
                "cp {} {} {}",
                if self.preserve { "-a" } else { "-R" },
                escape_arg(self.source()),
                escape_arg(&self.target)
            )
        }
    }

## User

what benifits i will get from dokploy and other pros and cons

## Assistant

Is typed CLI architecture se Rustploy ko Dokploy ke comparison me ye benefits milenge.

**Pros**

- Compile-time safety: `"-rf"`, `"--recursive"` ya `"tcp"` typo compile hone se pehle pakda jayega.
- Discoverable API: IDE autocomplete se `.recursive()`, `.files_only()`, `FileMode::OwnerReadWrite` jaise valid options milenge.
- Central command ownership: Docker, Git, Rclone, ZIP aur OS commands ek defined utility layer me rahenge.
- Local/remote consistency: same builder local machine aur SSH remote server dono par execute ho sakta hai.
- Safer upgrades: CLI flag change ho to ek builder update karna hoga, dozens of services nahi.
- Injection risk kam: user-provided raw flags aur arbitrary destination options execution me nahi ja sakte.
- Easier testing: command execute kiye bina generated arguments/script test kar sakte ho.
- Better reviews: service code intent batata hai, implementation flags nahi.
- Reusability: backup, deployment, setup aur schedules same typed operations reuse karenge.
- Refactoring confidence: compiler missing methods, invalid enums aur broken call-sites expose karega.
- Consistent validation: permissions, protocols, output targets aur formats ke valid states limited hain.
- API/frontend coupling better: backend enums frontend ke generated types me directly expose ho sakte hain.
- Product stability: users configuration typo karke destructive ya silently incorrect commands trigger nahi karenge.

Dokploy/TypeScript me bahut behavior runtime strings, shell commands aur validation par depend karta hai. Rustploy ka Rust type system invalid state ko runtime tak pahunchne se pehle rok sakta hai. Long-term maintainability me ye meaningful advantage hai.

**Cons**

- Initial development slower: har supported operation ke liye method/enum banana padega.
- More files and boilerplate: builder, action, enum aur tests maintain karne honge.
- New CLI feature immediately usable nahi hogi; pehle typed API add karni padegi.
- Complete external CLI coverage practical nahi hai. Product-supported subset clearly define karna hoga.
- Over-abstraction risk: har data string ko enum banana galat hoga. Paths, domains, headers aur user content generally strings/newtypes rahenge.
- Underlying CLI changes still matter: Docker, Rclone, Git versions ke behavior differences handle karne honge.
- Emergency debugging less flexible ho sakti hai because raw escape hatch intentionally unavailable hoga.
- Existing stored raw settings migrate/remove karne padenge, jaise `additional_flags`.

Best rule:

- Product behavior and switches: typed method/enum.
- Validated user data: newtype or validated DTO.
- Paths/content/secrets: structured value, raw flag nahi.
- Truly arbitrary scheduled commands: isolated explicit `UserCommandRunner`, normal `OsCli` API ka part nahi.
- Unsupported operation: pehle builder implement karo, service me temporary raw command mat likho.

Result: Dokploy ke features copy karne ke saath Rustploy ka backend structurally safer, easier to evolve, aur large-team maintenance ke liye stronger hoga.

## User

mere utils me zip naam se hai usko os ke under hona integate kya bolte ho

## Assistant

Haan, ZIP utility ko properly `os` ke andar move karna better rahega.

Recommended structure:

```text
src/utils/os/archive/
├── mod.rs
├── tar/
│   ├── builder.rs
│   ├── create.rs
│   ├── extract.rs
│   └── list.rs
└── zip/
    ├── builder.rs
    ├── create.rs
    ├── extract.rs
    ├── list.rs
    ├── sanitize.rs
    └── types.rs
```

API:

```rust
os.archive(path).tar().create()
os.archive(path).tar().extract_to(destination)

os.archive(path).zip().create()
os.archive(path).zip().extract_to(destination)
os.archive(path).zip().entry_names()
os.archive(path).zip().sanitize_to(output)
```

Current `os.zip(path)` works, but internally abhi bhi `utils::zip::ZipBuilder` ko expose karta hai. Isse ownership split rehti hai: public entry `OsCli` me hai, implementation `utils/zip` me.

Move karne ke benefits:

- TAR aur ZIP ki single ownership.
- `utils::zip` duplicate namespace remove.
- Services ko implementation type directly import nahi karna padega.
- Archive formats future me `Gzip`, `Zstd` ya `Xz` ke saath extend ho sakte hain.
- Flags/types/sanitization ek domain boundary me rahenge.
- Local aur remote execution consistently `OsCli` use karega.

Main `archive(path)` ko resource handle rakhunga aur format-specific operations uske andar organize karunga. Existing `utils::zip` ko compatibility re-export rakhna useful nahi hai unless another crate consumes it. Internal project hai to call-sites migrate karke old module completely remove karna cleaner hai.

    use crate::utils::exec::script::IntoCommand;
    use crate::utils::exec::{CommandExecutor, ExecOutput, ExecResult};
    use crate::utils::os::escape_arg;
    use super::ContainerRuntime;
    
    pub struct NvidiaConfigureBuilder<'a> { executor: &'a CommandExecutor, runtime: Option<ContainerRuntime>, config_path: Option<String>, runtime_name: Option<String>, set_as_default: bool, cdi_enabled: Option<bool> }
    impl<'a> NvidiaConfigureBuilder<'a> {
        pub(crate) fn new(executor: &'a CommandExecutor) -> Self { Self { executor, runtime: None, config_path: None, runtime_name: None, set_as_default: false, cdi_enabled: None } }
        pub fn runtime(mut self, runtime: ContainerRuntime) -> Self { self.runtime = Some(runtime); self }
        pub fn config_path(mut self, path: impl Into<String>) -> Self { self.config_path = Some(path.into()); self }
        pub fn runtime_name(mut self, name: impl Into<String>) -> Self { self.runtime_name = Some(name.into()); self }
        pub fn set_as_default(mut self) -> Self { self.set_as_default = true; self }
        pub fn enable_cdi(mut self) -> Self { self.cdi_enabled = Some(true); self }
        pub fn disable_cdi(mut self) -> Self { self.cdi_enabled = Some(false); self }
        fn args(&self) -> Vec<String> {
            let mut args = vec!["runtime".into(), "configure".into()];
            if let Some(runtime) = self.runtime { args.push(format!("--runtime={}", runtime.as_str())); }
            if let Some(path) = &self.config_path { args.push(format!("--config={path}")); }
            if let Some(name) = &self.runtime_name { args.push(format!("--nvidia-runtime-name={name}")); }
            if self.set_as_default { args.push("--set-as-default".into()); }
            if let Some(enabled) = self.cdi_enabled { args.push(format!("--cdi.enabled={enabled}")); }
            args
        }
        pub async fn run(self) -> ExecResult<ExecOutput> { self.executor.run("nvidia-ctk", self.args()).await }
    }
    impl IntoCommand for NvidiaConfigureBuilder<'_> { fn build_str(&self) -> String { format!("nvidia-ctk {}", self.args().iter().map(escape_arg).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(" ")) } }

    use crate::utils::exec::script::IntoCommand;
    use crate::utils::exec::{CommandExecutor, ExecOutput, ExecResult};
    use crate::utils::os::escape_arg;
    use super::{NvidiaQueryField, NvidiaQueryFormat};
    
    pub struct NvidiaQueryBuilder<'a> { executor: &'a CommandExecutor, fields: Vec<NvidiaQueryField>, format: NvidiaQueryFormat, header: bool, units: bool }
    impl<'a> NvidiaQueryBuilder<'a> {
        pub(crate) fn new(executor: &'a CommandExecutor) -> Self { Self { executor, fields: Vec::new(), format: NvidiaQueryFormat::Csv, header: true, units: true } }
        pub fn field(mut self, field: NvidiaQueryField) -> Self { if !self.fields.contains(&field) { self.fields.push(field); } self }
        pub fn fields(mut self, fields: impl IntoIterator<Item = NvidiaQueryField>) -> Self { for field in fields { if !self.fields.contains(&field) { self.fields.push(field); } } self }
        pub fn format(mut self, format: NvidiaQueryFormat) -> Self { self.format = format; self }
        pub fn without_header(mut self) -> Self { self.header = false; self }
        pub fn without_units(mut self) -> Self { self.units = false; self }
        fn args(&self) -> Vec<String> {
            let fields = if self.fields.is_empty() { vec![NvidiaQueryField::Name, NvidiaQueryField::DriverVersion] } else { self.fields.clone() };
            let query = fields.iter().map(|field| field.as_str()).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(",");
            let mut format = self.format.as_str().to_owned();
            if !self.header { format.push_str(",noheader"); }
            if !self.units { format.push_str(",nounits"); }
            vec![format!("--query-gpu={query}"), format!("--format={format}")]
        }
        pub async fn run(self) -> ExecResult<ExecOutput> { self.executor.run("nvidia-smi", self.args()).await }
    }
    impl IntoCommand for NvidiaQueryBuilder<'_> { fn build_str(&self) -> String { format!("nvidia-smi {}", self.args().iter().map(escape_arg).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(" ")) } }

    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
    pub enum TarCompression {
        None,
        #[default]
        Gzip,
        Bzip2,
        Xz,
        Zstd,
    }
    
    impl TarCompression {
        pub(crate) fn create_args(self) -> Vec<String> {
            match self {
                Self::None => vec!["-cf".into()],
                Self::Gzip => vec!["-czf".into()],
                Self::Bzip2 => vec!["-cjf".into()],
                Self::Xz => vec!["-cJf".into()],
                Self::Zstd => vec!["--zstd".into(), "-cf".into()],
            }
        }
    
        pub(crate) fn list_args(self) -> Vec<String> {
            match self {
                Self::None => vec!["-tf".into()],
                Self::Gzip => vec!["-tzf".into()],
                Self::Bzip2 => vec!["-tjf".into()],
                Self::Xz => vec!["-tJf".into()],
                Self::Zstd => vec!["--zstd".into(), "-tf".into()],
            }
        }
    
        pub(crate) fn extract_args(self) -> Vec<String> {
            match self {
                Self::None => vec!["-xf".into()],
                Self::Gzip => vec!["-xzf".into()],
                Self::Bzip2 => vec!["-xjf".into()],
                Self::Xz => vec!["-xJf".into()],
                Self::Zstd => vec!["--zstd".into(), "-xf".into()],
            }
        }
    }
    
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
    pub enum TarOverwritePolicy {
        Replace,
        KeepExisting,
        UnlinkFirst,
    }

    use crate::utils::exec::{CommandExecutor, ExecError};
    use std::path::PathBuf;
    
    #[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
    pub enum ZipError {
        #[error("source path not set")]
        MissingSource,
        #[error("destination path not set")]
        MissingDestination,
        #[error("execution failed: {0}")]
        Exec(#[from] ExecError),
        #[error("command failed: {0}")]
        Failed(String),
        #[error("io error: {0}")]
        Io(#[from] std::io::Error),
    }
    
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default)]
    pub enum CompressionLevel {
        Stored, // -0  no compression, fastest
        Fast,   // -1
        #[default]
        Default, // -6  zip default
        Best,   // -9  max compression
    }
    
    impl CompressionLevel {
        fn flag(&self) -> &'static str {
            match self {
                Self::Stored => "-0",
                Self::Fast => "-1",
                Self::Default => "-6",
                Self::Best => "-9",
            }
        }
    }
    
    pub struct ZipBuilder<'e> {
        executor: &'e CommandExecutor,
    
        source: Option<PathBuf>,
        destination: Option<PathBuf>,
    
        // zip options
        recurse: bool,
        junk_paths: bool,
        compression: CompressionLevel,
        excludes: Vec<String>,
    
        // unzip options
        overwrite: bool,
        list_only: bool,
        entry_names_only: bool,
        verbose_listing: bool,
        only_files: Vec<String>,
    }
    
    impl<'e> ZipBuilder<'e> {
        pub fn new(executor: &'e CommandExecutor) -> Self {
            Self {
                executor,
                source: None,
                destination: None,
                recurse: false,
                junk_paths: false,
                compression: CompressionLevel::Default,
                excludes: Vec::new(),
                overwrite: false,
                list_only: false,
                entry_names_only: false,
                verbose_listing: false,
                only_files: Vec::new(),
            }
        }
    
        pub fn source(mut self, path: impl Into<PathBuf>) -> Self {
            self.source = Some(path.into());
            self
        }
    
        pub fn destination(mut self, path: impl Into<PathBuf>) -> Self {
            self.destination = Some(path.into());
            self
        }
    
        /// `-r` recurse into directories.
        pub fn recurse(mut self) -> Self {
            self.recurse = true;
            self
        }
    
        /// `-j` strip directory paths — store filenames only.
        pub fn junk_paths(mut self) -> Self {
            self.junk_paths = true;
            self
        }
    
        /// Compression level (default: `CompressionLevel::Default`).
        pub fn compression(mut self, level: CompressionLevel) -> Self {
            self.compression = level;
            self
        }
    
        /// `-x <pattern>` exclude matching entries (works for both zip and unzip).
        pub fn exclude(mut self, pattern: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
            self.excludes.push(pattern.into());
            self
        }
    
        /// `-o` overwrite existing files without prompting.
        pub fn overwrite(mut self) -> Self {
            self.overwrite = true;
            self
        }
    
        /// `-l` list archive contents, don't extract.
        pub fn list_only(mut self) -> Self {
            self.list_only = true;
            self
        }
    
        pub fn entry_names_only(mut self) -> Self {
            self.entry_names_only = true;
            self
        }
    
        pub fn verbose_listing(mut self) -> Self {
            self.verbose_listing = true;
            self
        }
    
        /// Extract only these specific files from the archive.
        pub fn only(mut self, files: impl IntoIterator<Item = impl Into<String>>) -> Self {
            self.only_files.extend(files.into_iter().map(|f| f.into()));
            self
        }
    
        pub async fn zip(self) -> Result<(), ZipError> {
            let source = self.source.as_ref().ok_or(ZipError::MissingSource)?;
            let dest = self
                .destination
                .as_ref()
                .ok_or(ZipError::MissingDestination)?;
    
            let mut args: Vec<String> = vec!["zip".into()];
            if self.recurse {
                args.push("-r".into());
            }
            if self.junk_paths {
                args.push("-j".into());
            }
            args.push(self.compression.flag().into());
            for pat in &self.excludes {
                args.push("-x".into());
                args.push(pat.clone());
            }
            args.push(dest.to_string_lossy().into_owned());
            args.push(source.to_string_lossy().into_owned());
    
            let out = self.executor.run("zip", &args[1..]).await?;
    
            if !out.status.success() {
                return Err(ZipError::Failed(out.stderr));
            }
            Ok(())
        }
    
        pub async fn unzip(self) -> Result<(), ZipError> {
            let out = self.unzip_output().await?;
            if !out.status.success() {
                return Err(ZipError::Failed(out.stderr));
            }
            Ok(())
        }
    
        pub async fn unzip_output(self) -> Result<crate::utils::exec::ExecOutput, ZipError> {
            let source = self.source.as_ref().ok_or(ZipError::MissingSource)?;
    
            let mut args: Vec<String> = vec!["unzip".into()];
            if self.overwrite {
                args.push("-o".into());
            }
            if self.list_only {
                args.push("-l".into());
            }
            if self.entry_names_only {
                args.push("-Z1".into());
            }
            if self.verbose_listing {
                args.push("-v".into());
            }
            for pattern in &self.excludes {
                args.extend(["-x".into(), pattern.clone()]);
            }
            args.push(source.to_string_lossy().into_owned());
            args.extend(self.only_files.iter().cloned());
            if let Some(ref dest) = self.destination {
                args.push("-d".into());
                args.push(dest.to_string_lossy().into_owned());
            }
    
            self.executor
                .run("unzip", &args[1..])
                .await
                .map_err(Into::into)
        }
    
        pub async fn sanitize_to(self, output: impl Into<PathBuf>) -> Result<(), ZipError> {
            let input = self.source.as_ref().ok_or(ZipError::MissingSource)?;
            super::sanitize::sanitize_zip(input, &output.into()).await
        }
    
        pub fn to_zip_command(&self) -> Result<ZipCommand, ZipError> {
            let source = self.source.as_ref().ok_or(ZipError::MissingSource)?;
            let dest = self
                .destination
                .as_ref()
                .ok_or(ZipError::MissingDestination)?;
    
            let mut args: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
            if self.recurse {
                args.push("-r".into());
            }
            if self.junk_paths {
                args.push("-j".into());
            }
            args.push(self.compression.flag().into());
            for pat in &self.excludes {
                args.push("-x".into());
                args.push(pat.clone());
            }
            args.push(dest.to_string_lossy().into_owned());
            args.push(source.to_string_lossy().into_owned());
    
            Ok(ZipCommand { args })
        }
    
        pub fn to_unzip_command(&self) -> Result<UnzipCommand, ZipError> {
            let source = self.source.as_ref().ok_or(ZipError::MissingSource)?;
    
            let mut args: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
            if self.overwrite {
                args.push("-o".into());
            }
            if self.list_only {
                args.push("-l".into());
            }
            if self.entry_names_only {
                args.push("-Z1".into());
            }
            if self.verbose_listing {
                args.push("-v".into());
            }
            for pattern in &self.excludes {
                args.extend(["-x".into(), pattern.clone()]);
            }
            args.push(source.to_string_lossy().into_owned());
            args.extend(self.only_files.iter().cloned());
            if let Some(ref dest) = self.destination {
                args.push("-d".into());
                args.push(dest.to_string_lossy().into_owned());
            }
    
            Ok(UnzipCommand { args })
        }
    }

    mod tests {
        use super::*;
        use crate::utils::exec::pipeline::IntoCommand;
        use crate::utils::exec::{CommandExecutor, LocalExecutor};
    
        #[test]
        fn test_zip_pipeline_commands() {
            let executor = CommandExecutor::Local(LocalExecutor::new());
            let builder = ZipBuilder::new(&executor)
                .source("src")
                .destination("dest.zip")
                .recurse()
                .exclude("*.log");
    
            let zip_cmd = builder.to_zip_command().unwrap();
            assert_eq!(zip_cmd.build_str(), "zip -r -6 -x *.log dest.zip src");
    
            let unzip_builder = ZipBuilder::new(&executor)
                .source("dest.zip")
                .destination("extracted")
                .overwrite();
    
            let unzip_cmd = unzip_builder.to_unzip_command().unwrap();
            assert_eq!(unzip_cmd.build_str(), "unzip -o dest.zip -d extracted");
        }
    }

    impl<'a> ZipCreateBuilder<'a> {
        pub(crate) fn new(executor: &'a CommandExecutor, archive: PathBuf, source: PathBuf) -> Self { Self { executor, archive, source, recursive: false, path_mode: ZipPathMode::Preserve, compression: CompressionLevel::Default, excludes: Vec::new(), update: false, freshen: false, move_files: false } }
        pub fn recursive(mut self) -> Self { self.recursive = true; self }
        pub fn path_mode(mut self, mode: ZipPathMode) -> Self { self.path_mode = mode; self }

        pub fn exclude(mut self, pattern: impl Into<String>) -> Self { self.excludes.push(pattern.into()); self }
        pub fn update_existing(mut self) -> Self { self.update = true; self }
        pub fn freshen_existing(mut self) -> Self { self.freshen = true; self }
        pub fn move_files(mut self) -> Self { self.move_files = true; self }
        fn args(&self) -> Vec<String> { let mut args = Vec::new(); if self.recursive { args.push("-r".into()); } if self.path_mode == ZipPathMode::FileNamesOnly { args.push("-j".into()); } args.push(self.compression.flag().into()); if self.update { args.push("-u".into()); } if self.freshen { args.push("-f".into()); } if self.move_files { args.push("-m".into()); } for pattern in &self.excludes { args.extend(["-x".into(), pattern.clone()]); } args.push(self.archive.to_string_lossy().into_owned()); args.push(self.source.to_string_lossy().into_owned()); args }
        pub async fn run(self) -> Result<ExecOutput, ZipError> { let output = self.executor.run("zip", self.args()).await?; if output.success() { Ok(output) } else { Err(ZipError::Failed(output.stderr)) } }
    }

    use crate::utils::exec::script::IntoCommand;
    use crate::utils::exec::{CommandExecutor, ExecOutput, ExecResult};
    
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
    pub enum FirewallBackend {
        Ufw,
        Firewalld,
        Iptables,
    }
    
    impl FirewallBackend {
        pub(crate) const fn executable(self) -> &'static str {
            match self {
                Self::Ufw => "ufw",
                Self::Firewalld => "firewall-cmd",
                Self::Iptables => "iptables",
            }
        }
    
        const fn arguments(self) -> &'static [&'static str] {
            match self {
                Self::Ufw => &["status", "verbose"],
                Self::Firewalld => &["--list-all"],
                Self::Iptables => &["-S"],
            }
        }
    }
    
    pub struct FirewallInspectBuilder<'a> {
        executor: &'a CommandExecutor,
        backend: FirewallBackend,
    }
    
    impl<'a> FirewallInspectBuilder<'a> {
        pub(crate) fn new(executor: &'a CommandExecutor, backend: FirewallBackend) -> Self {
            Self { executor, backend }
        }
    
        pub async fn run(self) -> ExecResult<ExecOutput> {
            self.executor
                .run(self.backend.executable(), self.backend.arguments())
                .await
        }
    }
    
    impl IntoCommand for FirewallInspectBuilder<'_> {
        fn build_str(&self) -> String {
            std::iter::once(self.backend.executable())
                .chain(self.backend.arguments().iter().copied())
                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
                .join(" ")
        }
    }

    use crate::utils::exec::{CommandExecutor, ExecError, ExecResult};
    use crate::utils::os::OsCli;
    
    pub struct CertificatePairValidation {
        pub expires_at: i64,
    }
    
    pub struct CertificateBuilder<'a> {
        executor: &'a CommandExecutor,
        certificate: String,
    }
    
    impl<'a> CertificateBuilder<'a> {
        pub(crate) fn new(executor: &'a CommandExecutor, certificate: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
            Self {
                executor,
                certificate: certificate.into(),
            }
        }
    
        pub fn expiry(self) -> CertificateExpiryBuilder<'a> {
            CertificateExpiryBuilder {
                executor: self.executor,
                certificate: self.certificate,
            }
        }
    
        pub fn validate_with_key(
            self,
            private_key: impl Into<String>,
        ) -> CertificatePairValidationBuilder<'a> {
            CertificatePairValidationBuilder {
                executor: self.executor,
                certificate: self.certificate,
                private_key: private_key.into(),
            }
        }
    }
    
    pub struct CertificateExpiryBuilder<'a> {
        executor: &'a CommandExecutor,
        certificate: String,
    }
    
    impl CertificateExpiryBuilder<'_> {
        pub async fn run(self) -> ExecResult<i64> {
            validate_pem(
                &self.certificate,
                "BEGIN CERTIFICATE",
                "invalid PEM certificate",
            )?;
            let cert_path = temporary_path("certificate");
            let os = OsCli::new(self.executor);
            let result = async {
                os.file(&cert_path)
                    .write(&self.certificate)
                    .execute()
                    .await?;
                certificate_expiry(self.executor, &cert_path).await
            }
            .await;
            let _ = os.file(&cert_path).delete().run().await;
            result
        }
    }
    
    pub struct CertificatePairValidationBuilder<'a> {
        executor: &'a CommandExecutor,
        certificate: String,
        private_key: String,
    }
    
    impl CertificatePairValidationBuilder<'_> {
        pub async fn run(self) -> ExecResult<CertificatePairValidation> {
            validate_pem(
                &self.certificate,
                "BEGIN CERTIFICATE",
                "invalid PEM certificate",
            )?;
            validate_pem(&self.private_key, "PRIVATE KEY", "invalid PEM private key")?;
    
            let cert_path = temporary_path("certificate");
            let key_path = temporary_path("private-key");
            let os = OsCli::new(self.executor);
            let result = async {
                os.file(&cert_path)
                    .write(&self.certificate)
                    .execute()
                    .await?;
                os.file(&key_path)
                    .write(&self.private_key)
                    .execute()
                    .await?;
                os.file(&key_path)
                    .chmod(crate::utils::os::file::FileMode::OwnerReadWrite)
                    .run()
                    .await?;
    
                let cert_public = self
                    .executor
                    .run("openssl", ["x509", "-in", &cert_path, "-pubkey", "-noout"])
                    .await?;
                let key_public = self
                    .executor
                    .run("openssl", ["pkey", "-in", &key_path, "-pubout"])
                    .await?;
                if cert_public.stdout != key_public.stdout {
                    return Err(validation_error("certificate and private key do not match"));
                }
    
                let expires_at = certificate_expiry(self.executor, &cert_path).await?;
                if expires_at <= chrono::Utc::now().timestamp() {
                    return Err(validation_error("certificate is already expired"));
                }
                Ok(CertificatePairValidation { expires_at })
            }
            .await;
    
            let _ = os.file(&cert_path).delete().run().await;
            let _ = os.file(&key_path).delete().run().await;
            result
        }
    }
    
    async fn certificate_expiry(executor: &CommandExecutor, path: &str) -> ExecResult<i64> {
        let output = executor
            .run("openssl", ["x509", "-in", path, "-noout", "-enddate"])
            .await?;
        let raw = output.stdout_trimmed().trim_start_matches("notAfter=");
        chrono::NaiveDateTime::parse_from_str(raw, "%b %e %H:%M:%S %Y GMT")
            .map(|value| value.and_utc().timestamp())
            .map_err(|error| validation_error(&format!("invalid certificate expiry: {error}")))
    }
    
    fn validate_pem(value: &str, marker: &str, message: &str) -> ExecResult<()> {
        if value.contains(marker) {
            Ok(())
        } else {
            Err(validation_error(message))
        }
    }
    
    fn temporary_path(kind: &str) -> String {
        format!("/tmp/rustploy-{kind}-{}.pem", uuid::Uuid::new_v4().simple())
    }
    
    fn validation_error(message: &str) -> ExecError {
        ExecError::CommandFailed {
            code: None,
            stderr: message.to_owned(),
        }
    }

    use crate::utils::exec::{CommandExecutor, ExecResult};
    use crate::utils::os::OsCli;
    use crate::utils::os::file::FileMode;
    
    pub(crate) struct TemporaryPemFiles<'a> {
        executor: &'a CommandExecutor,
        certificate_path: String,
        private_key_path: Option<String>,
    }
    
    impl<'a> TemporaryPemFiles<'a> {
        pub(crate) async fn certificate(
            executor: &'a CommandExecutor,
            certificate: &str,
        ) -> ExecResult<Self> {
            let files = Self {
                executor,
                certificate_path: temporary_path("certificate"),
                private_key_path: None,
            };
            OsCli::new(executor)
                .file(&files.certificate_path)
                .write(certificate)
                .execute()
                .await?;
            Ok(files)
        }
    
        pub(crate) async fn pair(
            executor: &'a CommandExecutor,
            certificate: &str,
            private_key: &str,
        ) -> ExecResult<Self> {
            let mut files = Self::certificate(executor, certificate).await?;
            let key_path = temporary_path("private-key");
            let os = OsCli::new(executor);
            if let Err(error) = async {
                os.file(&key_path).write(private_key).execute().await?;
                os.file(&key_path)
                    .chmod(FileMode::OwnerReadWrite)
                    .run()
                    .await
            }
            .await
            {
                files.cleanup().await;
                let _ = os.file(&key_path).delete().run().await;
                return Err(error);
            }
            files.private_key_path = Some(key_path);
            Ok(files)
        }
    
        pub(crate) fn certificate_path(&self) -> &str {
            &self.certificate_path
        }
    
        pub(crate) fn private_key_path(&self) -> Option<&str> {
            self.private_key_path.as_deref()
        }
    
        pub(crate) async fn cleanup(&self) {
            let os = OsCli::new(self.executor);
            let _ = os.file(&self.certificate_path).delete().run().await;
            if let Some(path) = &self.private_key_path {
                let _ = os.file(path).delete().run().await;
            }
        }
    }
    
    fn temporary_path(kind: &str) -> String {
        format!("/tmp/rustploy-{kind}-{}.pem", uuid::Uuid::new_v4().simple())
    }

    use super::{
        CertificatePairValidation, PublicKeyBuilder, PublicKeySource, TemporaryPemFiles,
        certificate_expiry, validate_pem, validation_error,
    };
    use crate::utils::exec::{CommandExecutor, ExecResult};
    
    pub struct CertificatePairValidationBuilder<'a> {
        executor: &'a CommandExecutor,
        certificate: String,
        private_key: String,
    }
    
    impl<'a> CertificatePairValidationBuilder<'a> {
        pub(crate) fn new(
            executor: &'a CommandExecutor,
            certificate: String,
            private_key: String,
        ) -> Self {
            Self {
                executor,
                certificate,
                private_key,
            }
        }
    
        pub async fn run(self) -> ExecResult<CertificatePairValidation> {
            validate_pem(
                &self.certificate,
                "BEGIN CERTIFICATE",
                "invalid PEM certificate",
            )?;
            validate_pem(&self.private_key, "PRIVATE KEY", "invalid PEM private key")?;
            let files =
                TemporaryPemFiles::pair(self.executor, &self.certificate, &self.private_key).await?;
            let result = self.validate_files(&files).await;
            files.cleanup().await;
            result
        }
    
        async fn validate_files(
            &self,
            files: &TemporaryPemFiles<'_>,
        ) -> ExecResult<CertificatePairValidation> {
            let cert_public = PublicKeyBuilder::new(
                self.executor,
                PublicKeySource::Certificate,
                files.certificate_path(),
            )
            .run()
            .await?;
            let key_public = PublicKeyBuilder::new(
                self.executor,
                PublicKeySource::PrivateKey,
                files.private_key_path().expect("pair always has a private key"),
            )
            .run()
            .await?;
            if cert_public != key_public {
                return Err(validation_error("certificate and private key do not match"));
            }
            let expires_at = certificate_expiry(self.executor, files.certificate_path()).await?;
            if expires_at <= chrono::Utc::now().timestamp() {
                return Err(validation_error("certificate is already expired"));
            }
            Ok(CertificatePairValidation { expires_at })
        }
    }

abb batoo kya pros and cons

## Assistant

Is typed `OsCli` pattern ke pros aur cons:

**Pros**

- Compile-time typo protection: `runtime(ContainerRuntime::Docker)` me `"dokcer"` jaisi mistake possible nahi.
- Raw flags callers se hidden hain. `--set-as-default` ya `-Z1` yaad nahi rakhna padta.
- IDE autocomplete se available actions aur options directly milte hain.
- CLI changes ek internal builder file me update honge, saare call sites me nahi.
- Same commands services, background jobs, setup aur diagnostics me reuse honge.
- Invalid combinations builder internally prevent kar sakta hai, jaise ZIP overwrite policies.
- Testing easy hai: generated command snapshots verify ho sakte hain.
- Security improve hoti hai: arguments centrally escape hote hain aur arbitrary flag injection kam hota hai.
- Folder split se GPU, archive, firewall aur crypto independently maintainable hain.
- Local aur remote executor same typed API use kar sakte hain.
- Dokploy ke raw shell-heavy flows ke comparison me Rust compile-time guarantees zyada milengi.

**Cons**

- Initial implementation zyada hai: har action, flag aur enum ke liye code banana padega.
- CLI ka naya flag use karne ke liye pehle wrapper update karna hoga.
- Complete CLI coverage maintain karna continuous work hai.
- Over-abstraction ka risk hai. Rare one-line command ke liye bhi multiple files ban sakti hain.
- Mutually exclusive options handle na kiye gaye to typed API ke bawajood runtime-invalid command ban sakti hai.
- String values jaise paths, patterns, image names aur runtime names fully type-safe nahi ho sakte.
- External tools ke versions differ karte hain. Typed flag supported ho sakta hai, lekin old server binary usse reject kar sakti hai.
- `IntoCommand` shell rendering aur direct executor arguments dono maintain karne se duplication ho sakti hai.
- Contributors ko project-specific builder conventions pehle samajhni padengi.
- Har possible Linux distribution/tool variant cover karne se API unnecessarily large ho sakti hai.

Overall, Rustploy ke liye ye pattern suitable hai. Best balance ye rahega: commonly-used aur security-sensitive operations fully typed rakho; internal action implementation me raw flags allowed hon, lekin service/API callers tak kabhi expose na hon.

## Assistant

Haan, architecture ke hisab se `cgroup`, Docker aur Rclone ko `OsCli` ke under accessible hona chahiye, lekin existing modules ko physically move karna abhi unnecessary risk hai.

Main isko phased facade migration se fix karunga:

1. Existing `utils/docker`, `utils/rclone`, `utils/cgroup` files wahi rahenge.
2. `OsCli` me typed entry points add honge:
   - `os.docker()`
   - `os.rclone()`
   - `os.cgroup()`
3. Ye entry points existing implementations ko wrap/delegate karenge. Logic duplicate nahi hoga.
4. Services ke raw/direct usages ko small batches me `OsCli` facade par migrate karenge.
5. Har batch ke baad compile aur focused tests chalenge.
6. Jab direct imports zero ho jayenge, tab optional physical folder move:
   - `utils/os/docker/`
   - `utils/os/rclone/`
   - `utils/os/cgroup/`
7. Temporary compatibility re-exports rakhenge, isliye old imports immediately break nahi honge.
8. Final phase me deprecated paths remove honge.

Pros:

- Codebase ek saath crash nahi hoga.
- Git diff reviewable rahega.
- Existing tested implementation reuse hogi.
- Public API consistent ho jayegi.
- Rollback aur bug isolation easy rahega.

Main Docker ko fully generic OS command builder me merge nahi karunga. Docker/Rclone/Cgroup bade domains hain, isliye `OsCli` unka facade/entry point hoga, ownership unke dedicated modules me rahegi. Ye maintainability aur type safety ka better balance hai.

## User

chor do rahne do i want ki private network wala isme karna user agar ssh ke through hi chata hai to ssh wireguard or tailscale and jitne otehrprovider wirguard me hum manage karenge baki sab to user janega na

## Assistant

Samajh gaya. `cgroup`, Docker aur Rclone migration abhi chhod dete hain.

Private networking ka clean model:

- `SSH`: default direct connection. User host/IP, port aur authentication provide karega.
- `WireGuard`: Rustploy fully manage karega, including key generation, peer configuration, internal IP allocation, connectivity check, rotation and removal.
- `Tailscale`: user apna Tailnet/auth setup manage karega. Rustploy sirf provided Tailscale IP/hostname se connect aur test karega.
- Other providers such as ZeroTier, NetBird or custom VPN: user network configure karega; Rustploy ko reachable private address milega.

Server connection me typed mode hona chahiye:

```text
Direct SSH
Managed WireGuard
External Private Network
```

`External Private Network` ke andar provider metadata ho sakta hai, lekin Rustploy provider installation/configuration own nahi karega.

Important rule: WireGuard transport banega, SSH replacement nahi. Rustploy WireGuard tunnel establish karega, phir deployment, Docker aur terminal operations private WireGuard IP par SSH se chalengi.

Isse responsibility clear rahegi:

- Rustploy owns managed WireGuard lifecycle.
- User owns Tailscale aur third-party network lifecycle.
- SSH remains the actual secure command channel.
- Public IP unavailable hone par bhi remote server manage ho sakega.
- Provider-specific complexity core deployment logic me leak nahi hogi.

## Assistant

Plan ye rahega:

1. **Connection model**

`ServerConnectionMode` enum:

- `DirectSsh`
- `ManagedWireGuard`
- `ExternalPrivateNetwork`

External providers ke liye `PrivateNetworkProvider`:

- `Tailscale`
- `ZeroTier`
- `NetBird`
- `Custom`

2. **Database schema**

Server/private-network tables me:

- connection mode
- provider
- private hostname/IP
- WireGuard tunnel IP
- public key
- encrypted private key
- endpoint
- listen port
- keepalive
- tunnel status
- last handshake
- configuration version

Private keys encrypted rahengi. API response aur logs me expose nahi hongi.

3. **Folder structure**

```text
src/services/private_network/
├── mod.rs
├── service.rs
├── types.rs
├── connection.rs
├── health.rs
└── wireguard/
    ├── mod.rs
    ├── keys.rs
    ├── address_pool.rs
    ├── config.rs
    ├── install.rs
    ├── peer.rs
    ├── rotation.rs
    └── teardown.rs

src/api/
├── dto/private_network/
└── handlers/private_network/

src/db/
├── models/private_networks.rs
└── repository/private_networks.rs

src/utils/os/wireguard/
├── mod.rs
├── interface.rs
├── peer.rs
├── key.rs
└── types.rs
```

4. **Typed OS API**

Raw commands services me nahi honge:

```rust
os.wireguard()
    .interface("wg-rustploy")
    .create()
    .address(tunnel_address)
    .listen_port(port)
    .private_key(key_file)
    .run();
```

Typed enums/methods:

- interface state
- peer allowed networks
- persistent keepalive
- key generation
- config validation
- handshake/status query
- system service enable/disable

Arbitrary `.arg()` expose nahi hoga.

5. **Managed WireGuard flow**

- Server ka normal SSH connection test.
- WireGuard availability detect.
- Supported package manager se install.
- Panel aur remote peer keys generate.
- Transactional tunnel IP reserve.
- Remote configuration upload.
- Interface start and enable.
- Tunnel address par SSH test.
- Successful test ke baad server connection route switch.
- Failure par configuration rollback aur direct SSH preserve.

6. **External network flow**

Tailscale/ZeroTier/NetBird Rustploy install nahi karega:

- User provider select karega.
- Private IP/hostname enter karega.
- Rustploy SSH reachability verify karega.
- Provider command availability optional diagnostic hoga.
- Rustploy keys, membership aur provider account manage nahi karega.

7. **Connection resolver**

Saari server operations direct `server.ip` use nahi karengi. Central resolver decide karega:

```text
DirectSsh              -> public host
ManagedWireGuard       -> allocated WireGuard IP
ExternalPrivateNetwork -> user-provided private host
```

Deployment, logs, terminal, monitoring setup, backups aur Docker operations isi resolver se host lenge.

8. **API endpoints**

- network configuration get/update
- WireGuard setup
- connectivity test
- status/handshake
- key rotation
- repair/reinstall
- switch connection mode
- WireGuard teardown

Mutating actions idempotent honge aur audit events record karenge.

9. **Failure safety**

- Direct SSH immediately delete/disable nahi hoga.
- Tunnel verified hone se pehle active route switch nahi hoga.
- Unique tunnel IP database constraint.
- Setup/rotation distributed lock.
- Config backup before replacement.
- Partial setup cleanup.
- Last working connection information retained.
- Server deletion par peer/config/address cleanup.

10. **Verification**

- Address allocation and config generation unit tests.
- Typed command snapshot tests.
- Repository integration tests.
- Setup rollback tests.
- Direct → WireGuard → direct transition tests.
- External provider connection tests.
- Real Linux/Docker test using a temporary WireGuard network namespace.

Implementation order: schema and types → typed WireGuard CLI → repository/service → connection resolver → setup/rollback → API → lifecycle integration → tests.

    use auto_di::singleton;

    use crate::db::models::server_private_networks::ServerPrivateNetwork;
    
    pub struct ServerPrivateNetworkRepository {
        pool: Arc<SqlitePool>,
    }
    
    #[singleton]
    impl ServerPrivateNetworkRepository {
        pub fn new(pool: Arc<SqlitePool>) -> Self {
            Self { pool }
        }
    
        pub async fn get(&self, server_id: i64) -> sqlx::Result<Option<ServerPrivateNetwork>> {
            sqlx::query_as::<_, ServerPrivateNetwork>(
                "SELECT server_id, connection_mode, provider, private_host, tunnel_address, public_key, endpoint, listen_port, persistent_keepalive, status, last_handshake_at, config_version, created_at, updated_at FROM server_private_networks WHERE server_id = ?",
            )
            .bind(server_id)
            .fetch_optional(self.pool.as_ref())
            .await
        }
    
        #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
        pub async fn upsert(
            &self,
            server_id: i64,
            connection_mode: &str,
            provider: Option<&str>,
            private_host: Option<&str>,
            tunnel_address: Option<&str>,
            public_key: Option<&str>,
            endpoint: Option<&str>,
            listen_port: Option<i64>,
            persistent_keepalive: Option<i64>,
            status: &str,
        ) -> sqlx::Result<ServerPrivateNetwork> {
            sqlx::query(
                "INSERT INTO server_private_networks (server_id, connection_mode, provider, private_host, tunnel_address, public_key, endpoint, listen_port, persistent_keepalive, status) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?) ON CONFLICT(server_id) DO UPDATE SET connection_mode = excluded.connection_mode, provider = excluded.provider, private_host = excluded.private_host, tunnel_address = excluded.tunnel_address, public_key = excluded.public_key, endpoint = excluded.endpoint, listen_port = excluded.listen_port, persistent_keepalive = excluded.persistent_keepalive, status = excluded.status, config_version = server_private_networks.config_version + 1, updated_at = strftime('%s', 'now')",
            )
            .bind(server_id)
            .bind(connection_mode)
            .bind(provider)
            .bind(private_host)
            .bind(tunnel_address)
            .bind(public_key)
            .bind(endpoint)
            .bind(listen_port)
            .bind(persistent_keepalive)
            .bind(status)
            .execute(self.pool.as_ref())
            .await?;
            self.get(server_id).await?.ok_or(sqlx::Error::RowNotFound)
        }
    
        pub async fn disable(&self, server_id: i64) -> sqlx::Result<()> {
            sqlx::query("DELETE FROM server_private_networks WHERE server_id = ?")
                .bind(server_id)
                .execute(self.pool.as_ref())
                .await?;
            Ok(())
        }
    }

    use std::sync::Arc;
    
    use auto_di::singleton;
    
    use crate::{
        api::dto::server_management::{
            PrivateNetworkProviderDto, ServerConnectionModeDto, ServerPrivateNetworkDto,
            UpdatePrivateNetworkDto,
        },
        db::models::server_private_networks::ServerPrivateNetwork,
        repository::{ServerPrivateNetworkRepository, ServerRepository},
    };
    
    pub struct ServerPrivateNetworkService {
        servers: Arc<ServerRepository>,
        networks: Arc<ServerPrivateNetworkRepository>,
    }
    
    #[singleton]
    impl ServerPrivateNetworkService {
        fn new(
            servers: Arc<ServerRepository>,
            networks: Arc<ServerPrivateNetworkRepository>,
        ) -> Self {
            Self { servers, networks }
        }
    
        pub async fn get(&self, server_id: i64) -> sqlx::Result<Option<ServerPrivateNetworkDto>> {
            self.assert_server(server_id).await?;
            self.networks
                .get(server_id)
                .await?
                .map(map_network)
                .transpose()
        }
    
        pub async fn update(
            &self,
            server_id: i64,
            input: UpdatePrivateNetworkDto,
        ) -> sqlx::Result<ServerPrivateNetworkDto> {
            self.assert_server(server_id).await?;
            validate(&input)?;
            if input.connection_mode == ServerConnectionModeDto::DirectSsh {
                self.networks.disable(server_id).await?;
                return direct_network(server_id);
            }
            let status = match input.connection_mode {
                ServerConnectionModeDto::ManagedWireguard => "CONFIGURING",
                ServerConnectionModeDto::ExternalPrivateNetwork => "ACTIVE",
                ServerConnectionModeDto::DirectSsh => unreachable!(),
            };
            map_network(
                self.networks
                    .upsert(
                        server_id,
                        connection_mode(input.connection_mode),
                        input.provider.map(provider).as_deref(),
                        input.private_host.as_deref(),
                        input.tunnel_address.as_deref(),
                        input.public_key.as_deref(),
                        input.endpoint.as_deref(),
                        input.listen_port.map(i64::from),
                        input.persistent_keepalive.map(i64::from),
                        status,
                    )
                    .await?,
            )
        }
    
        pub async fn disable(&self, server_id: i64) -> sqlx::Result<()> {
            self.assert_server(server_id).await?;
            self.networks.disable(server_id).await
        }
    
        async fn assert_server(&self, server_id: i64) -> sqlx::Result<()> {
            self.servers
                .get_by_id(server_id)
                .await?
                .ok_or(sqlx::Error::RowNotFound)
                .map(|_| ())
        }
    }
    
    fn validate(input: &UpdatePrivateNetworkDto) -> sqlx::Result<()> {
        if input.connection_mode == ServerConnectionModeDto::DirectSsh {
            return Ok(());
        }
        let host = input
            .private_host
            .as_deref()
            .filter(|value| !value.trim().is_empty() && !value.chars().any(char::is_whitespace))
            .ok_or_else(|| sqlx::Error::Protocol("private_host is required and must not contain whitespace".into()))?;
        if host.len() > 253 {
            return Err(sqlx::Error::Protocol("private_host is too long".into()));
        }
        let provider = input
            .provider
            .ok_or_else(|| sqlx::Error::Protocol("private network provider is required".into()))?;
        match input.connection_mode {
            ServerConnectionModeDto::ManagedWireguard => {
                if provider != PrivateNetworkProviderDto::Wireguard {
                    return Err(sqlx::Error::Protocol(
                        "managed private networks require the WIREGUARD provider".into(),
                    ));
                }
                if input.tunnel_address.is_none() || input.endpoint.is_none() {
                    return Err(sqlx::Error::Protocol(
                        "managed WireGuard requires tunnel_address and endpoint".into(),
                    ));
                }
            }
            ServerConnectionModeDto::ExternalPrivateNetwork => {
                if provider == PrivateNetworkProviderDto::Wireguard {
                    return Err(sqlx::Error::Protocol(
                        "use MANAGED_WIREGUARD for the WireGuard provider".into(),
                    ));
                }
            }
            ServerConnectionModeDto::DirectSsh => {}
        }
        Ok(())
    }
    
    fn map_network(value: ServerPrivateNetwork) -> sqlx::Result<ServerPrivateNetworkDto> {
        Ok(ServerPrivateNetworkDto {
            server_id: value.server_id,
            connection_mode: parse_mode(&value.connection_mode)?,
            provider: value.provider.as_deref().map(parse_provider).transpose()?,
            private_host: value.private_host,
            tunnel_address: value.tunnel_address,
            public_key: value.public_key,
            endpoint: value.endpoint,
            listen_port: value.listen_port.map(to_u16).transpose()?,
            persistent_keepalive: value.persistent_keepalive.map(to_u16).transpose()?,
            status: value.status,
            last_handshake_at: value.last_handshake_at,
            config_version: value.config_version,
            updated_at: value.updated_at,
        })
    }
    
    fn direct_network(server_id: i64) -> sqlx::Result<ServerPrivateNetworkDto> {
        Ok(ServerPrivateNetworkDto {
            server_id,
            connection_mode: ServerConnectionModeDto::DirectSsh,
            provider: None,
            private_host: None,
            tunnel_address: None,
            public_key: None,
            endpoint: None,
            listen_port: None,
            persistent_keepalive: None,
            status: "DISABLED".into(),
            last_handshake_at: None,
            config_version: 0,
            updated_at: chrono::Utc::now().timestamp(),
        })
    }
    
    fn connection_mode(value: ServerConnectionModeDto) -> &'static str {
        match value {
            ServerConnectionModeDto::DirectSsh => "DIRECT_SSH",
            ServerConnectionModeDto::ManagedWireguard => "MANAGED_WIREGUARD",
            ServerConnectionModeDto::ExternalPrivateNetwork => "EXTERNAL_PRIVATE_NETWORK",
        }
    }
    
    fn provider(value: PrivateNetworkProviderDto) -> String {
        match value {
            PrivateNetworkProviderDto::Wireguard => "WIREGUARD",
            PrivateNetworkProviderDto::Tailscale => "TAILSCALE",
            PrivateNetworkProviderDto::Zerotier => "ZEROTIER",
            PrivateNetworkProviderDto::Netbird => "NETBIRD",
            PrivateNetworkProviderDto::Custom => "CUSTOM",
        }
        .into()
    }
    
    fn parse_mode(value: &str) -> sqlx::Result<ServerConnectionModeDto> {
        match value {
            "DIRECT_SSH" => Ok(ServerConnectionModeDto::DirectSsh),
            "MANAGED_WIREGUARD" => Ok(ServerConnectionModeDto::ManagedWireguard),
            "EXTERNAL_PRIVATE_NETWORK" => Ok(ServerConnectionModeDto::ExternalPrivateNetwork),
            _ => Err(sqlx::Error::Protocol(format!("invalid connection mode: {value}"))),
        }
    }
    
    fn parse_provider(value: &str) -> sqlx::Result<PrivateNetworkProviderDto> {
        match value {
            "WIREGUARD" => Ok(PrivateNetworkProviderDto::Wireguard),
            "TAILSCALE" => Ok(PrivateNetworkProviderDto::Tailscale),
            "ZEROTIER" => Ok(PrivateNetworkProviderDto::Zerotier),
            "NETBIRD" => Ok(PrivateNetworkProviderDto::Netbird),
            "CUSTOM" => Ok(PrivateNetworkProviderDto::Custom),
            _ => Err(sqlx::Error::Protocol(format!("invalid private network provider: {value}"))),
        }
    }
    
    fn to_u16(value: i64) -> sqlx::Result<u16> {
        u16::try_from(value).map_err(|error| sqlx::Error::Protocol(error.to_string()))
    }

    #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
    pub struct WireGuardConfig {

        pub addresses: Vec<String>,
        pub listen_port: Option<u16>,
        pub peers: Vec<WireGuardPeer>,
    }
    
    impl WireGuardConfig {
        pub fn render(&self) -> String {
            let mut output = String::from("[Interface]\n");
            output.push_str(&format!("PrivateKey = {}\n", self.private_key));
            if !self.addresses.is_empty() {
                output.push_str(&format!("Address = {}\n", self.addresses.join(", ")));
            }
            if let Some(port) = self.listen_port {
                output.push_str(&format!("ListenPort = {port}\n"));
            }
            for peer in &self.peers {
                output.push_str("\n[Peer]\n");
                output.push_str(&format!("PublicKey = {}\n", peer.public_key));
                output.push_str(&format!("AllowedIPs = {}\n", peer.allowed_ips.join(", ")));
                if let Some(endpoint) = &peer.endpoint {
                    output.push_str(&format!("Endpoint = {endpoint}\n"));
                }
                if let Some(keepalive) = peer.persistent_keepalive {
                    output.push_str(&format!("PersistentKeepalive = {keepalive}\n"));
                }
            }
            output
        }
    }

    use crate::utils::exec::{CommandExecutor, ExecOutput, ExecResult};
    use crate::utils::os::file::FileMode;
    use crate::utils::os::OsCli;
    
    use super::WireGuardConfig;
    
    pub struct WireGuardInterfaceBuilder<'a> {
        executor: &'a CommandExecutor,
        name: String,
    }
    
    impl<'a> WireGuardInterfaceBuilder<'a> {
        pub(crate) fn new(executor: &'a CommandExecutor, name: String) -> Self {
            Self { executor, name }
        }
    
        pub async fn install(self, config: &WireGuardConfig) -> ExecResult<ExecOutput> {
            validate_name(&self.name)?;
            let path = format!("/etc/wireguard/{}.conf", self.name);
            let os = OsCli::new(self.executor);
            os.dir("/etc/wireguard").create().parents(true).run().await?;
            os.file(&path).write(config.render()).execute().await?;
            os.file(&path)
                .chmod(FileMode::OwnerReadWrite)
                .run()
                .await?;
            self.executor.run("wg-quick", ["up", &self.name]).await
        }
    
        pub async fn remove(self) -> ExecResult<ExecOutput> {
            validate_name(&self.name)?;
            let _ = self.executor.run("wg-quick", ["down", &self.name]).await;
            OsCli::new(self.executor)
                .file(format!("/etc/wireguard/{}.conf", self.name))
                .delete()
                .run()
                .await
        }
    
        pub async fn latest_handshakes(self) -> ExecResult<ExecOutput> {
            validate_name(&self.name)?;
            self.executor
                .run("wg", ["show", &self.name, "latest-handshakes"])
                .await
        }
    }
    
    fn validate_name(name: &str) -> ExecResult<()> {
        if !name.is_empty()
            && name.len() <= 15
            && name
                .chars()
                .all(|value| value.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(value, '-' | '_' | '=' | '+'))
        {
            Ok(())
        } else {
            Err(crate::utils::exec::ExecError::CommandFailed {
                code: None,
                stderr: "invalid WireGuard interface name".into(),
            })
        }
    }

    +            address
    +                .parse::<ipnet::IpNet>()
    +                .map_err(|_| WireGuardConfigError::InvalidAddress(address.clone()))?;
    +        }
    +        let mut routes = HashSet::new();
    +        for peer in &self.peers {

    +                validate_endpoint(endpoint)?;
    +            }

    +                    .parse::<ipnet::IpNet>()
    +                    .map_err(|_| WireGuardConfigError::InvalidAllowedIp(allowed.clone()))?;
    +                if network.prefix_len() == 0 {
    +                    return Err(WireGuardConfigError::DefaultRouteNotAllowed);
    +                }
    +                let canonical = network.trunc().to_string();
    +                if !routes.insert(canonical.clone()) {
    +                    return Err(WireGuardConfigError::DuplicateAllowedIp(canonical));
    +                }
    +            }
    +        }

    +fn validate_key(value: &str) -> Result<(), ()> {
    +    if value.chars().any(char::is_whitespace) {
    +        return Err(());
    +    }
    +    let decoded = base64::engine::general_purpose::STANDARD
    +        .decode(value)
    +        .map_err(|_| ())?;
    +    (decoded.len() == 32).then_some(()).ok_or(())
    +}
    +
    +fn validate_endpoint(value: &str) -> Result<(), WireGuardConfigError> {
    +    if value.is_empty() || value.chars().any(char::is_whitespace) {
    +        return Err(WireGuardConfigError::InvalidEndpoint);
    +    }
    +    if value.parse::<std::net::SocketAddr>().is_ok() {
    +        return Ok(());
    +    }
    +    let (host, port) = value
    +        .rsplit_once(':')
    +        .ok_or(WireGuardConfigError::InvalidEndpoint)?;
    +    if host.is_empty()
    +        || host.len() > 253
    +        || host.starts_with('-')
    +        || host.ends_with('-')
    +        || !host
    +            .chars()
    +            .all(|ch| ch.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(ch, '.' | '-'))
    +        || port.parse::<u16>().is_err()
    +    {
    +        return Err(WireGuardConfigError::InvalidEndpoint);
    +    }
    +    Ok(())
    +}

    use std::process::Command;
    
    #[test]
    #[ignore = "requires Linux user namespaces and WireGuard kernel support"]
    fn wireguard_peers_complete_real_kernel_handshake() {
        if !cfg!(target_os = "linux") {
            return;
        }
    
        let script = r#"
    set -euo pipefail
    umask 077
    test_dir=$(mktemp -d)
    unshare --net sleep 30 & peer_a=$!
    unshare --net sleep 30 & peer_b=$!
    cleanup() {
        kill "$peer_a" "$peer_b" 2>/dev/null || true
        rm -rf "$test_dir"
    }
    trap cleanup EXIT
    
    ip link add bridge0 type bridge
    ip link set bridge0 up
    ip link add underlay-a type veth peer name peer-a
    ip link add underlay-b type veth peer name peer-b
    ip link set underlay-a master bridge0
    ip link set underlay-b master bridge0
    ip link set underlay-a up
    ip link set underlay-b up
    ip link set peer-a netns "$peer_a"
    ip link set peer-b netns "$peer_b"
    
    nsenter -t "$peer_a" -n ip link set lo up
    nsenter -t "$peer_b" -n ip link set lo up
    nsenter -t "$peer_a" -n ip link set peer-a up
    nsenter -t "$peer_b" -n ip link set peer-b up
    nsenter -t "$peer_a" -n ip address add 192.0.2.11/24 dev peer-a
    nsenter -t "$peer_b" -n ip address add 192.0.2.12/24 dev peer-b
    
    wg genkey > "$test_dir/a.key"
    wg pubkey < "$test_dir/a.key" > "$test_dir/a.pub"
    wg genkey > "$test_dir/b.key"
    wg pubkey < "$test_dir/b.key" > "$test_dir/b.pub"
    
    nsenter -t "$peer_a" -n ip link add wg-a type wireguard
    nsenter -t "$peer_b" -n ip link add wg-b type wireguard
    nsenter -t "$peer_a" -n ip address add 10.90.0.1/32 dev wg-a
    nsenter -t "$peer_b" -n ip address add 10.90.0.2/32 dev wg-b
    nsenter -t "$peer_a" -n wg set wg-a private-key "$test_dir/a.key" listen-port 52031 peer "$(cat "$test_dir/b.pub")" allowed-ips 10.90.0.2/32 endpoint 192.0.2.12:52032

4. Private DNS records automatically generate.

## User

BoringTun **WireGuard nahi hai**, balki **WireGuard protocol ka Rust implementation** hai. Cloudflare ne ise Rust me likha hai aur ye **userspace** me run karta hai. ([The Cloudflare Blog][1])

Simple comparison:

```text
WireGuard (Protocol)
        │
        ├── Linux Kernel WireGuard (C)
        ├── wireguard-go (Go)
        ├── BoringTun (Rust)
        └── GotaTun (Rust, Mullvad)
```

### Iska fayda kya hai?

Normally Linux me WireGuard kernel module use hota hai:

```text
App
 │
 ▼
Kernel WireGuard
 │
 ▼
Network
```

Lekin agar:

* Windows
* iOS
* Android
* Restricted container
* Ya kernel module install nahi kar sakte

to BoringTun use kar sakte ho.

```text
App
 │
 ▼
BoringTun (Userspace)
 │
 ▼
TUN Interface
 │
 ▼
Network
```

Ye portability ke liye bana hai. Cloudflare ise apne WARP/1.1.1.1 ecosystem me bhi use karta raha hai. ([The Cloudflare Blog][1])

### Rustploy me kaam aa sakta hai?

**Haan.**

Agar tum Rustploy me private networking banana chahte ho, to do approaches hain:

**Kernel WireGuard**

* ✅ Sabse fast
* ✅ Lowest latency
* ❌ Host par kernel support chahiye

**BoringTun**

* ✅ Pure Rust
* ✅ Embed as library
* ✅ Containers aur cross-platform me aasaan
* ❌ Kernel implementation se thoda slower ho sakta hai. ([The Cloudflare Blog][1])

### Agar tumhara goal hai:

* AWS ↔ Hostinger
* Docker Swarm
* Cross-cloud private mesh
* Rust-only implementation

to BoringTun dekhna worthwhile hai. Isse tum Rust application ke andar hi WireGuard protocol integrate kar sakte ho, instead of sirf `wg` CLI ko shell se call karne ke. Ye especially useful ho sakta hai agar tum apna network controller ya VPN management layer banana chahte ho. ([whatisgithub][2])

[1]: https://blog.cloudflare.com/boringtun-userspace-wireguard-rust/?utm_source=chatgpt.com "BoringTun, a userspace WireGuard implementation in Rust | The Cloudflare Blog"
[2]: https://whatisgithub.com/cloudflare/boringtun?utm_source=chatgpt.com "What is boringtun? — cloudflare, explained · whatisgithub"
 what you think about this pros and cons acording to you

## Assistant

BoringTun technically interesting hai, lekin Rustploy ke managed-server use case me ise primary WireGuard implementation banana abhi sahi decision nahi hoga.

**Pros**

- Rust implementation hone ki wajah se Rustploy ecosystem ke close hai.
- Kernel WireGuard unavailable ho tab userspace fallback mil sakta hai.
- Kernel module installation ki dependency kam hoti hai.
- Restricted VM/container aur cross-platform agent ke liye useful ho sakta hai.
- Protocol processing application ke control me hone se custom metrics, lifecycle aur debugging possible hai.
- `wg` CLI output parse karne ki dependency reduce ho sakti hai.
- Testing network namespaces ke bina userspace level par easier ho sakti hai.
- Future desktop/edge agent me same networking engine reuse ho sakta hai.

**Cons**

- BoringTun ko library ki tarah embed karna complete VPN product ready nahi karta.
- TUN interface ke liye generally `CAP_NET_ADMIN` aur `/dev/net/tun` phir bhi chahiye. Restricted container problem completely solve nahi hoti.
- IP allocation, routes, DNS, firewall, NAT, MTU, persistence aur peer reconciliation Rustploy ko khud manage karne padenge.
- Userspace packet processing kernel WireGuard se slower aur CPU-heavy ho sakta hai.
- Rustploy process crash/restart hua to tunnel availability application lifecycle se coupled ho jayegi.
- Privileged networking code main panel process me embed karna security blast radius badhata hai.
- BoringTun project maintenance/activity aur platform support ko production adoption se pehle carefully verify karna hoga.
- Kernel WireGuard ke operational tooling, systemd integration aur widespread debugging knowledge ka benefit kam ho jayega.
- Mobile platforms par BoringTun alone enough nahi; OS-specific VPN APIs bhi chahiye.
- Main Rustploy binary me embed karne se deployment, privileges aur failure isolation complicated hogi.

Mera recommended architecture:

```text
Rustploy controller
        |
        v
Networking backend abstraction
        |
        +-- Kernel WireGuard (default)
        +-- BoringTun sidecar/agent (fallback)
        +-- External network (Tailscale/NetBird/custom)
```

BoringTun ko main panel binary me directly embed nahi karunga. Dedicated `rustploy-network-agent` process ya sidecar better hoga:

- limited privileges
- independent restart
- version/health management
- private IPC or authenticated local gRPC
- packet engine crash se panel unaffected
- kernel aur userspace backend interchangeable

Practical priority:

1. Kernel WireGuard backend production-ready karo.
2. Private DNS, route reconciliation, key rotation aur health monitoring complete karo.
3. Backend trait stabilize karo.
4. BoringTun proof-of-concept sidecar banao.
5. Kernel support unavailable hone par only fallback select karo.

Ek important correction: BoringTun “pure Rust” hone se automatically Docker-friendly nahi ho jata. Container ko TUN device, network capabilities aur routing access ab bhi chahiye. Isliye current Docker-host-network experiment me BoringTun privileges ki core problem solve nahi karega; primarily kernel-module portability ka fallback dega.
