        sections: BTreeMap<DigSection, bool>,
    }
    
    impl<'a> DigBuilder<'a> {
        pub(super) fn new(executor: &'a CommandExecutor, name: DnsName) -> Self {
            Self::base(executor, Some(name), None)
        }
    
        pub(super) fn reverse(executor: &'a CommandExecutor, address: IpAddr) -> Self {
            Self::base(executor, None, Some(address))
        }
    
        fn base(executor: &'a CommandExecutor, name: Option<DnsName>, reverse: Option<IpAddr>) -> Self {
            Self {
                executor,
                name,
                reverse,
                server: None,
                port: DigPort::default(),
                record_type: DigRecordType::default(),
                query_class: DigQueryClass::default(),
                transport: DigTransport::default(),
                family: DigAddressFamily::default(),
                dnssec: false,
                recurse: true,
                trace: false,
                short: false,
                search: false,
                show_search: false,
                fail_on_servfail: false,
                ignore_truncation: false,
                multiline: false,
                identify: false,
                show_command: true,
                ttl: true,
                ttl_units: false,
                cookie: None,
                nsid: false,
                edns_version: None,
                edns_buffer_size: None,
                timeout: DigTimeout::default(),
                tries: DigTries::default(),
                sections: BTreeMap::new(),
            }
        }
    
        pub fn server(mut self, server: IpAddr) -> Self { self.server = Some(server); self }
        pub fn port(mut self, port: DigPort) -> Self { self.port = port; self }
        pub fn record_type(mut self, value: DigRecordType) -> Self { self.record_type = value; self }
        pub fn query_class(mut self, value: DigQueryClass) -> Self { self.query_class = value; self }
        pub fn transport(mut self, value: DigTransport) -> Self { self.transport = value; self }
        pub fn address_family(mut self, value: DigAddressFamily) -> Self { self.family = value; self }
        pub fn dnssec(mut self, enabled: bool) -> Self { self.dnssec = enabled; self }
        pub fn recurse(mut self, enabled: bool) -> Self { self.recurse = enabled; self }
        pub fn trace(mut self, enabled: bool) -> Self { self.trace = enabled; self }
        pub fn short(mut self, enabled: bool) -> Self { self.short = enabled; self }
        pub fn search(mut self, enabled: bool) -> Self { self.search = enabled; self }
        pub fn show_search(mut self, enabled: bool) -> Self { self.show_search = enabled; self }
        pub fn fail_on_servfail(mut self, enabled: bool) -> Self { self.fail_on_servfail = enabled; self }
        pub fn ignore_truncation(mut self, enabled: bool) -> Self { self.ignore_truncation = enabled; self }
        pub fn multiline(mut self, enabled: bool) -> Self { self.multiline = enabled; self }
        pub fn identify(mut self, enabled: bool) -> Self { self.identify = enabled; self }
        pub fn show_command(mut self, enabled: bool) -> Self { self.show_command = enabled; self }
        pub fn ttl(mut self, enabled: bool) -> Self { self.ttl = enabled; self }
        pub fn ttl_units(mut self, enabled: bool) -> Self { self.ttl_units = enabled; self }
        pub fn cookie(mut self, enabled: bool) -> Self { self.cookie = Some(enabled); self }
        pub fn nsid(mut self, enabled: bool) -> Self { self.nsid = enabled; self }
        pub fn edns_version(mut self, value: DigEdnsVersion) -> Self { self.edns_version = Some(value); self }
        pub fn edns_buffer_size(mut self, value: DigEdnsBufferSize) -> Self { self.edns_buffer_size = Some(value); self }
        pub fn timeout(mut self, value: DigTimeout) -> Self { self.timeout = value; self }
        pub fn tries(mut self, value: DigTries) -> Self { self.tries = value; self }
        pub fn section(mut self, section: DigSection, enabled: bool) -> Self { self.sections.insert(section, enabled); self }
        pub fn include(self, section: DigSection) -> Self { self.section(section, true) }
        pub fn exclude(self, section: DigSection) -> Self { self.section(section, false) }
    
        pub async fn execute(self) -> ExecResult<DigResponse> {
            let output = self.executor.run("dig", self.arguments()?).await?;
            Ok(DigResponse::parse(output.stdout))
        }
    
        fn arguments(&self) -> ExecResult<Vec<String>> {
            let mut args = Vec::new();
            if let Some(server) = self.server { args.push(format!("@{server}")); }
            args.push(format!("-p{}", self.port.get()));
            args.push(format!("+time={}", self.timeout.get()));
            args.push(format!("+tries={}", self.tries.get()));
            toggle(&mut args, "recurse", self.recurse);
            if self.transport == DigTransport::Tcp { args.push("+tcp".into()); }
            match self.family {
                DigAddressFamily::Any => {}
                DigAddressFamily::Ipv4 => args.push("-4".into()),
                DigAddressFamily::Ipv6 => args.push("-6".into()),
            }
            enabled(&mut args, "dnssec", self.dnssec);
            enabled(&mut args, "trace", self.trace);
            enabled(&mut args, "short", self.short);
            enabled(&mut args, "search", self.search);
            enabled(&mut args, "showsearch", self.show_search);
            enabled(&mut args, "fail", self.fail_on_servfail);
            enabled(&mut args, "ignore", self.ignore_truncation);
            enabled(&mut args, "multiline", self.multiline);
            enabled(&mut args, "identify", self.identify);
            toggle(&mut args, "cmd", self.show_command);
            toggle(&mut args, "ttlid", self.ttl);
            enabled(&mut args, "ttlunits", self.ttl_units);
            if let Some(cookie) = self.cookie { toggle(&mut args, "cookie", cookie); }
            enabled(&mut args, "nsid", self.nsid);
            if let Some(version) = self.edns_version { args.push(format!("+edns={}", version.get())); }
            if let Some(size) = self.edns_buffer_size { args.push(format!("+bufsize={}", size.get())); }
            for (section, value) in &self.sections { toggle(&mut args, section.as_str(), *value); }
            if let Some(address) = self.reverse {
                args.extend(["-x".into(), address.to_string()]);
            } else if let Some(name) = &self.name {
                args.extend([name.as_str().into(), self.record_type.as_str().into(), self.query_class.as_str().into()]);
            } else {
                return Err(command_error("dig query requires a name or reverse address"));
            }
            Ok(args)
        }
    }
    
    fn enabled(args: &mut Vec<String>, option: &str, value: bool) { if value { args.push(format!("+{option}")); } }
    fn toggle(args: &mut Vec<String>, option: &str, value: bool) { args.push(format!("+{}{option}", if value { "" } else { "no" })); }

Architected container-to-container networking via host-level WireGuard tunneling
Architected container-to-container networking via host-level WireGuard tunneling

Ahh ok, ab clear ho gaya — matlab backend aur postgres khud containers ke andar chal rahe hain, host pe directly nahi. Ye ek extra layer add karta hai. Samjhate hain:

Problem
Container ka apna isolated network namespace hota hai (Docker bridge network, jaise 172.17.0.2)
WireGuard host pe hai (10.8.0.1), container ke andar nahi
Toh container ka traffic host ke WireGuard interface tak pahunchega kaise, aur wahan se doosre host ke container tak?
Solution: Layers ka route
[Backend container]  172.17.0.2  (Server 1, Docker bridge network)
        ↓ (docker bridge → host routing)
[Server 1 host]       10.8.0.1  (WireGuard interface)
        ↓ (WireGuard encrypted tunnel)
[Server 2 host]       10.8.0.2  (WireGuard interface)
        ↓ (host → docker bridge routing)
[Postgres container]  172.18.0.2  (Server 2, Docker bridge network)
Ye kaam kaise hota hai (iptables level pe, tumhare mindset ke hisaab se):
Container → Host routing: Docker already iptables FORWARD rules use karta hai container ke traffic ko host ke through bahar bhejne ke liye (NAT/MASQUERADE). Ye already Docker khud handle karta hai jab container external IP tak pahunchne ki koshish karta hai.
Host → WireGuard routing: Tumhe host pe ek route add karna padega taaki jab bhi koi packet 10.8.0.0/24 (WireGuard subnet) ki taraf jaaye, wo wg0 interface se nikle:
   ip route add 10.8.0.0/24 dev wg0
WireGuard → Remote host container: Server 2 pe, WireGuard se aane wala traffic jab 10.8.0.2 (Server 2 ka WireGuard IP) pe aata hai, usse Postgres container (172.18.0.2:5432) tak forward karna hoga. Ye ek iptables DNAT rule se hota hai:
   iptables -t nat -A PREROUTING -i wg0 -p tcp --dport 5432 -j DNAT --to-destination 172.18.0.2:5432

(Ya phir Postgres container ko directly WireGuard interface pe expose karna hoga docker run ke -p 10.8.0.2:5432:5432 jaisa binding se.)

Naam resolution (postgres-db): Backend container ke andar /etc/hosts mein entry chahiye:
   10.8.0.2   postgres-db

(Container ka apna /etc/hosts — Docker isko mount karta hai, tum runtime pe update kar sakte ho docker exec ya bind-mount se.)

Summary — 3 cheezein chahiye per hop
Layer	Kaam	Mechanism
Container → Host	Container ka traffic host tak nikale	Docker ka default bridge + iptables (already hota hai)
Host → Host	Encrypted tunnel do servers ke beech	WireGuard
Host → Container (remote)	Incoming traffic sahi container tak pahunche	iptables DNAT rule (jo tumhe khud add karna hoga per exposed port)

Ye poora setup basically ek mini overlay network ban jaata hai — jo Docker Swarm ka overlay network built-in deta hai, wahi cheez tum manually iptables + WireGuard se replicate kar rahe ho.

Sawaal: kya tum ye per-container port ke hisaab se manually DNAT rules manage karoge (jaise Postgres ke liye 5432), ya sochte ho ki container ko seedha WireGuard interface pe hi bind kar do (bina Docker bridge ke, --network host jaisa)?

mutiple container honge to kya karna shai rahega

Weighed container networking solutions beyond basic DNAT approach
Weighed container networking solutions beyond basic DNAT approach

Bahut accha sawaal — per-container manual DNAT rules scale nahi karenge (10 containers = 10 rules manage karna, harr naye container pe update, port clashes waghera). Behtar tarika hai NAT ki jagah routing use karna — poora subnet route kar do, individual container/port level pe kuch mat karo.

Better Approach: Per-host subnet routing (NAT-free)
1. Har server ko unique container subnet do

Master jab bhi naya server register kare, usko ek alag /16 ya /24 range assign kare — koi overlap na ho:

Server 1 → containers 172.18.0.0/16
Server 2 → containers 172.19.0.0/16
Server 3 → containers 172.20.0.0/16

(Docker custom bridge network banate waqt --subnet flag se ye set hota hai)

2. WireGuard mein poora subnet allow karo (per-port nahi)

Har server ke WireGuard peer config mein, AllowedIPs mein us doosre server ka poora container subnet daal do, sirf uska WireGuard IP nahi:

# Server 1 ke wg0.conf mein Server 2 ka peer entry
[Peer]
PublicKey = <server2-key>
AllowedIPs = 10.8.0.2/32, 172.19.0.0/16   ← ye important hai
Endpoint = server2-ip:51820
3. Routing add karo (per port nahi, ek baar per server)
ip route add 172.19.0.0/16 dev wg0
Result

Ab koi DNAT rule nahi chahiye. Backend container (172.18.0.5) directly Postgres container (172.19.0.3) ko uske real container IP pe pahunch sakta hai — packet seedha route hoke WireGuard se jaayega, kyunki poora subnet hi tunnel ke through reachable hai.

Backend (172.18.0.5) → 172.19.0.3 directly
        ↓
   route table: "172.19.0.0/16 → wg0"
        ↓
   WireGuard tunnel → Server 2
        ↓
   Docker bridge pe deliver → Postgres container milta hai
Naam resolution abhi bhi wahi rahega

Backend postgres-db use karega, /etc/hosts mein entry:

172.19.0.3   postgres-db

(WireGuard IP 10.8.0.2 ki jagah ab directly container ka apna IP use hoga — cleaner hai kyunki port-specific NAT translation ki zaroorat hi khatam)

Yeh kyun better hai
Manual DNAT (pehle wala)	Subnet routing (ye wala)
Per port, per container rule	Ek baar per server (route + AllowedIPs)
Naya container = naya rule	Naya container = kuch nahi karna, subnet already covered
Port conflicts ka risk	Har container ka apna unique IP, no conflict

Master ka kaam sirf itna: naye server ko unique subnet allocate karna aur sab peers ke WireGuard config + routes ko sync/update karna jab topology change ho.

Ye basically wahi cheez hai jo Docker Swarm ka overlay network (VXLAN based) internally karta hai — bas tum ise WireGuard + plain routing se manually replicate kar rahe ho, jo tumhare "iptables jaisa direct control" wale philosophy ke saath match karta hai.

Architected custom DNS resolver leveraging SQLite for distributed updates
Architected custom DNS resolver leveraging SQLite for distributed updates

Haan bilkul — SQLite backed custom DNS resolver bana sakte ho. Docker jo embedded DNS (127.0.0.11) use karta hai, wahi concept hai bas tum apna khud banaoge. Design samjhte hain:

Architecture
Master (SQLite - source of truth)
   ↓ container create/destroy hone par
   ↓ gRPC push
   ↓
Agent (har server pe)
   ↓ apna local cache/SQLite maintain kare
   ↓
Mini DNS resolver (port 53 pe listen, per-server ya per-container-network)
   ↓
Container query karta hai "postgres-db" → resolver SQLite se lookup kare → IP return kare
Kaise kaam karega step by step
1. Master ke SQLite mein table
sql
CREATE TABLE dns_records (
    name TEXT NOT NULL,        -- "postgres-db"
    ip TEXT NOT NULL,          -- "172.19.0.3"
    server_id TEXT,            -- kis server pe hai
    updated_at INTEGER
);

Jab bhi koi container create/destroy hota hai, master ye table update karta hai (ye tumhare paas already BuilderQueue jaisa reconciliation pattern hai).

2. Agent (har server pe) apna local resolver chalata hai
Chhota Rust binary jo port 53 pe UDP listen kare (sirf us server ke docker bridge network pe, jaise Docker 127.0.0.11 karta hai)
Iske paas apna khud ka SQLite (read-only replica) ya in-memory HashMap<String, IpAddr> ho, jo master se sync hota rahe
Query aaye → HashMap/SQLite check karo → IP return karo (agar nahi mila to upstream DNS ko forward kar do, jaise Google DNS, normal internet domains ke liye)
3. Container ko is resolver ki taraf point karo
Docker container banate waqt --dns flag se container ka resolver IP set karo (jaise Docker khud 127.0.0.11 set karta hai internally):
  docker run --dns=172.18.0.1 ...

(172.18.0.1 = us server ke docker bridge gateway pe chal raha tumhara resolver)

4. Sync mechanism (master → agent)
Push based (better for real-time): Master jab bhi record change kare, connected agents ko gRPC stream se turant bhej de (tumhare paas already broadcast::Sender<DeployEvent> pattern hai — isi ko DNS events ke liye bhi use kar sakte ho)
Agent apna local SQLite/HashMap update kar le turant
Kyun ye approach sahi hai tumhare architecture ke saath
Master hi authoritative source hai (jo tumhari existing philosophy hai)
Har server ka apna local resolver hai — koi cross-server DNS query latency nahi, sab kuch local, fast
SQLite hi consistent storage hai jo tum already use kar rahe ho BuilderQueue mein — same pattern reuse ho jaayega
Crate suggestion

Poora DNS protocol khud parse karne ki zaroorat nahi — hickory-server (pehle trust-dns-server) crate use kar sakte ho jo bas ek lightweight authoritative DNS server library hai. Tum bas uske backend mein apna SQLite/HashMap plug kar doge, baaki protocol handling wo crate karega.

Ek cheez decide karni hai: agent ka local resolver poora master ka data cache karega (sab servers ke records), ya sirf apne server ke co kya lagta ye apreoach shai hoga bajaye coredns ke

## Assistant

Haan, tumhare multi-host container networking goal ke liye embedded Rust DNS resolver CoreDNS container se better fit hai—but proposed design ko thoda simplify karna chahiye.

Recommended architecture:

```text
Container
   ↓ DNS query
Local Rustploy Agent DNS
   ↓ in-memory service registry
Remote container IP
   ↓ routed Docker subnet
Host WireGuard tunnel
   ↓
Remote Docker subnet/container
```

- Har server ko unique Docker subnet mile.
- WireGuard `AllowedIPs` me remote container subnets hon.
- Har host ka agent bridge gateway IP par DNS serve kare.
- Container creation/deletion par panel authoritative DNS record update kare.
- Agents ko versioned snapshot/delta events milen.
- Agent records memory me rakhe; local SQLite ki zarurat nahi. Optional snapshot file restart recovery ke liye enough hai.
- Unknown/public domains configured upstream resolver ko forward hon.
- Container me local agent ka bridge IP `--dns` se set ho.
- Names globally scoped hon, for example:
  `postgres.production.project.rustploy.internal`
- Short name `postgres` sirf same project/environment scope me resolve ho.

CoreDNS ke comparison me benefits:

- Extra CoreDNS container/image/config lifecycle nahi.
- Rustploy agent ke andar direct integration.
- Container lifecycle ke saath instant DNS updates.
- Typed record model, health checks aur reconciliation.
- Project/environment isolation implement karna easier.
- Panel down hone par agent cache se resolution chalta rahega.

Cons:

- DNS protocol, caching, TTL, truncation, TCP/UDP, forwarding aur security maintain karna tumhari responsibility hogi.
- `hickory-server` dependency aur agent complexity badhegi.
- Wrong routing/firewall configuration me DNS resolve hoga, lekin connection fail karega.
- Split-brain/stale records avoid karne ke liye versioned synchronization required hai.

Important: per-container DNAT use mat karo. Unique per-host Docker subnets + routed WireGuard network scalable solution hai.

`dig` builder waste nahi hoga—woh embedded resolver ka actual query health check, diagnostics aur debugging ke liye use hoga.

Final suggestion: CoreDNS remove karke agent-embedded Hickory authoritative/forwarding resolver banao, master DB ko source of truth rakho, agent me in-memory versioned cache rakho. Ye Rustploy ke architecture ke liye cleaner rahega.

```text
Container A → local bridge → WireGuard → remote bridge → Container B
```

3. Agent-embedded DNS

CoreDNS container completely remove hoga.

4. DNS control-plane sync

Existing authenticated agent gRPC connection extend hogi:

- Panel agent ko complete versioned DNS snapshot push karega.
- Create/update/delete ke liye incremental changes supported honge.
- Version mismatch par agent full snapshot request/replace karega.
- Updates idempotent honge.
- Panel unavailable hone par last valid agent snapshot continue karega.

5. Proper DNS naming

Globally unique canonical names:

```text
postgres.production.my-project.rustploy.internal
api.production.my-project.rustploy.internal
```

Optional short aliases same environment scope me:

```text
postgres
api
```

Invalid names aur duplicate canonical records DB/service validation me reject honge.

6. Container integration

Application, database aur Compose builders me managed network support centralize hoga:

- Managed Docker network automatically attach hoga.
- Agent DNS bridge gateway `--dns` ke through inject hoga.
- Required search domain `--dns-search` se inject hoga.
- Container create/redeploy/restart sab same typed configuration use karenge.
- Caller raw DNS flags nahi dega.

7. Container lifecycle registry

Deployment successful hone par:

- Actual container IP inspect hoga.
- DNS record authoritative registry me upsert hoga.
- Agent snapshots reconcile honge.

Container remove/redeploy hone par:

- Old record remove/replace hoga.
- Stale records periodic reconciliation se clean honge.

8. Security and isolation

- DNS listener sirf Rustploy bridge/WireGuard addresses par bind hoga.
- Public interface par port 53 expose nahi hoga.
- Project/environment naming isolation hogi.
- WireGuard routing alone access permission nahi banega; firewall policy server/project boundaries enforce karegi.
- DNS sync existing monitoring token authentication reuse nahi karega blindly; typed agent-control authorization scope hoga.

9. Health and recovery

Health runner check karega:

- Agent DNS UDP query
- Agent DNS TCP query
- Expected container IP response
- WireGuard handshake
- Remote Docker subnet route
- Forwarding/firewall state
- Registry version drift

Failure par safe reconciliation hoga; healthy config unnecessarily restart nahi hogi.

```text
  registry.rs
  forwarding.rs
  snapshot.rs
  types.rs

src/services/server_management/private_network/

src/utils/os/

  network/

src/utils/docker/
  managed_network/
```

11. Migration and rollout

- Existing CoreDNS manager/config generation remove hoga.
- New container subnet, DNS registry and sync-version schema migration banegi.
- Existing WireGuard users ko deterministic subnet migration milegi.
- Upgrade sequence pehle agent capability verify karega, uske baad CoreDNS remove karega—DNS blackout avoid hoga.

12. Verification and commit

- DNS registry unit tests
- UDP/TCP real DNS query integration tests
- Multi-network namespace WireGuard routing test
- Container-to-container connection test

```text
rustploy panel

Remote Rustploy system agent
    ├── WireGuard

    ├── embedded DNS
    └── reconciliation

rustploy_monitor
```

Current project me separate general remote agent nahi hai. Isliye correct choices:

- `rustploy_monitor` untouched rahega.
- `rustploy_agent` WireGuard, routed Docker subnets, DNS resolver and configuration sync manage karega.

Isse benefits:

- Monitoring failure networking ko affect nahi karega.
- DNS/networking update metrics collection ko restart nahi karega.
- Permissions separate rahengi: monitor read-only, network agent privileged.
- Future server setup, backup, cleanup jaise host tasks bhi `rustploy_agent` me aa sakte hain.
- Docker socket aur `NET_ADMIN` monitoring container ko dene ki zarurat nahi padegi.

So revised decision: `rustploy_monitor` me kuch nahi daalunga. Dedicated `rustploy_agent` crate/container banega.

    use std::{collections::BTreeSet, net::IpAddr};
    
    use crate::{
        db::models::server_private_networks::{PrivateNetworkConnectionMode, ServerPrivateNetwork},
        repository::ServerPrivateNetworkRepository,
        utils::{
            docker::{
                DockerCli,
                query::{ContainerFilter, RestartPolicy},
            },
            exec::{CommandExecutor, LocalExecutor},
            os::{
                OsCli,
                dns::{DigRecordType, DigTimeout, DigTries, DnsName},
            },
            paths::rustploy_paths,
        },
    };
    
    use super::addressing::tunnel_addresses;
    
    const CONTAINER_NAME: &str = "rustploy-private-dns";
    const COREDNS_IMAGE: &str = "coredns/coredns:1.12.4";
    const CONTAINER_CONFIG_DIR: &str = "/etc/coredns";
    const CONTAINER_COREFILE: &str = "/etc/coredns/Corefile";
    
    pub(super) struct PrivateDnsManager<'a> {
        networks: &'a ServerPrivateNetworkRepository,
    }
    
    impl<'a> PrivateDnsManager<'a> {
        pub fn new(networks: &'a ServerPrivateNetworkRepository) -> Self {
            Self { networks }
        }
    
        pub async fn reconcile(&self) -> sqlx::Result<()> {
            let records = dns_records(self.networks.list_dns_enabled().await?)?;
            let docker = DockerCli::new_local();
            if records.is_empty() {
                let _ = docker.containers().rm(CONTAINER_NAME).force().run().await;
                return Ok(());
            }
    
            let paths = rustploy_paths();
            let executor = CommandExecutor::Local(LocalExecutor::new());
            let os = OsCli::new(&executor);
            os.dir(paths.private_dns())
                .create()
                .with_parents()
                .run()
                .await
                .map_err(protocol)?;
            let hosts_changed =
                write_atomic_if_changed(&os, &paths.private_dns_hosts(), &render_hosts(&records))
                    .await?;
            let corefile_changed = write_atomic_if_changed(
                &os,
                &paths.private_dns_corefile(),
                &render_corefile(&records),
            )
            .await?;
    
            let container_running = docker
                .query()
                .containers()
                .filter(ContainerFilter::name(CONTAINER_NAME))
                .exists()
                .await
                .map_err(protocol)?;
            if container_running && !hosts_changed && !corefile_changed {
                return Ok(());
            }
    
            let _ = docker.containers().rm(CONTAINER_NAME).force().run().await;
            docker
                .query()
                .create_container(COREDNS_IMAGE)
                .name(CONTAINER_NAME)
                .network("host")
                .restart(RestartPolicy::UnlessStopped)
                .bind_ro(paths.private_dns(), CONTAINER_CONFIG_DIR)
                .command(["-conf", CONTAINER_COREFILE])
                .detach()
                .run()
                .await
                .map_err(protocol)?;
            Ok(())
        }
    
        pub async fn is_running(&self) -> sqlx::Result<bool> {
            DockerCli::new_local()
                .query()
                .containers()
                .filter(ContainerFilter::name(CONTAINER_NAME))
                .exists()
                .await
                .map_err(protocol)
        }
    
        pub async fn query(
            &self,
            name: &str,
            nameserver: IpAddr,
            expected: IpAddr,
        ) -> sqlx::Result<bool> {
            let executor = CommandExecutor::Local(LocalExecutor::new());
            let response = OsCli::new(&executor)
                .dns()
                .dig(DnsName::new(name).map_err(protocol)?)
                .server(nameserver)
                .record_type(match expected {
                    IpAddr::V4(_) => DigRecordType::A,
                    IpAddr::V6(_) => DigRecordType::Aaaa,
                })
                .short(true)
                .timeout(DigTimeout::default())
                .tries(DigTries::default())
                .execute()
                .await
                .map_err(protocol)?;
            Ok(response.addresses.contains(&expected))
        }
    }
    
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
    struct DnsRecord {
        name: String,
        address: IpAddr,
        nameserver: IpAddr,
    }
    
    fn dns_records(networks: Vec<ServerPrivateNetwork>) -> sqlx::Result<Vec<DnsRecord>> {
        let mut records = Vec::new();
        for network in networks {
            if PrivateNetworkConnectionMode::try_from(network.connection_mode.as_str())?
                != PrivateNetworkConnectionMode::ManagedWireguard
            {
                continue;
            }
            let name = network.dns_name.ok_or_else(|| {
                sqlx::Error::Protocol("DNS-enabled private network has no dns_name".into())
            })?;
            let private_host = network.private_host.ok_or_else(|| {
                sqlx::Error::Protocol("DNS-enabled private network has no private_host".into())
            })?;
            let tunnel = network.tunnel_address.ok_or_else(|| {
                sqlx::Error::Protocol("DNS-enabled private network has no tunnel_address".into())
            })?;
            let (panel_address, _, _) = tunnel_addresses(&tunnel)?;
            records.push(DnsRecord {
                name,
                address: private_host.parse().map_err(|error| {
                    sqlx::Error::Protocol(format!("invalid private DNS record address: {error}"))
                })?,
                nameserver: panel_address
                    .split('/')
                    .next()
                    .unwrap_or_default()
                    .parse()
                    .map_err(|error| {
                        sqlx::Error::Protocol(format!("invalid private DNS listener: {error}"))
                    })?,
            });
        }
        Ok(records)
    }
    
    fn render_hosts(records: &[DnsRecord]) -> String {
        records
            .iter()
            .map(|record| format!("{} {}\n", record.address, record.name))
            .collect()
    }
    
    fn render_corefile(records: &[DnsRecord]) -> String {
        let listeners = records
            .iter()
            .map(|record| record.nameserver)
            .collect::<BTreeSet<_>>()
            .into_iter()
            .map(|address| address.to_string())
            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
            .join(" ");
        format!(
            ".:53 {{\n    bind {listeners}\n    hosts {CONTAINER_CONFIG_DIR}/rustploy.hosts {{\n        ttl 30\n        reload 5s\n        fallthrough\n    }}\n    forward . 1.1.1.1 1.0.0.1\n    cache 30\n    errors\n}}\n"
        )
    }
    
    async fn write_atomic_if_changed(os: &OsCli<'_>, path: &str, content: &str) -> sqlx::Result<bool> {
        if let Ok(existing) = os.file(path).read().execute().await
            && existing.stdout == content
        {
            return Ok(false);
        }
        let temporary = format!("{path}.tmp");
        os.file(&temporary)
            .write(content)
            .execute()
            .await
            .map_err(protocol)?;
        os.file(&temporary)
            .move_to(path)
            .execute()
            .await
            .map_err(protocol)?;
        Ok(true)
    }
    
    fn protocol(error: impl std::fmt::Display) -> sqlx::Error {
        sqlx::Error::Protocol(error.to_string())
    }

            let records = vec![DnsRecord {

                address: IpAddr::V4(Ipv4Addr::new(10, 91, 0, 2)),
                nameserver: IpAddr::V4(Ipv4Addr::new(10, 91, 0, 1)),
            }];
            assert_eq!(render_hosts(&records), "10.91.0.2 pi.rustploy.internal\n");
            let corefile = render_corefile(&records);
            assert!(corefile.contains("bind 10.91.0.1"));
            assert!(corefile.contains("reload 5s"));
            assert!(corefile.contains("forward . 1.1.1.1 1.0.0.1"));
        }
    }

    use std::net::IpAddr;
    
    use crate::utils::exec::{CommandExecutor, ExecResult};
    
    use super::types::{DnsSearchDomain, validate_interface};
    
    pub(super) async fn configure_split(
        executor: &CommandExecutor,
        interface: &str,
        nameserver: IpAddr,
        domain: &DnsSearchDomain,
    ) -> ExecResult<()> {
        validate_interface(interface)?;
        let nameserver = nameserver.to_string();
        if executor
            .run("resolvectl", ["dns", interface, nameserver.as_str()])
            .await
            .is_ok()
        {
            let routing_domain = domain.routing_domain();
            executor
                .run("resolvectl", ["domain", interface, routing_domain.as_str()])
                .await?;
            executor
                .run("resolvectl", ["default-route", interface, "no"])
                .await?;
            return Ok(());
        }
    
        let content = format!("nameserver {nameserver}\nsearch {}\n", domain.as_str());
        executor
            .run_with_stdin("resolvconf", ["-a", interface], content)
            .await?;
        Ok(())
    }
    
    pub(super) async fn revert(executor: &CommandExecutor, interface: &str) -> ExecResult<()> {
        validate_interface(interface)?;
        if executor
            .run("resolvectl", ["revert", interface])
            .await
            .is_ok()
        {
            return Ok(());
        }
        executor.run("resolvconf", ["-d", interface]).await?;
        Ok(())
    }

## Assistant

Bilkul. Cluster transport provider-aware hona chahiye; WireGuard hardcoded nahi.

Correct flow:

```text
Remote server setup
  → private network mode/provider read karo
  → provider ka stable private IP resolve karo
  → us IP ko Swarm advertise/data-path address banao
  → cluster join/reconcile karo
```

Provider mapping:

- Managed WireGuard → Rustploy tunnel IP
- Tailscale → Tailscale interface IP
- NetBird → NetBird interface IP
- ZeroTier → ZeroTier interface IP
- External/custom private network → user-configured private IP
- Direct SSH → validated public/private server IP fallback

Ek stable trait/boundary rahegi:

```text
PrivateTransport
  ├── address()
  ├── connectivity_check()
  ├── required_routes()
  └── health()
```

Remote-server setup service provider select karega. Swarm builder ko provider ka naam nahi pata hoga; usko sirf validated advertise/data-path address milega.

Also important:

- Tailscale selected ho to WireGuard install/configure nahi hoga.
- NetBird selected ho to NetBird ka existing network use hoga.
- Managed WireGuard selected ho tabhi Rustploy keys/routes manage karega.
- Provider change par pehle new transport health verify hoga, phir Swarm migrate hoga.
- Migration failure par old advertise path preserve/rollback hoga.
- Cluster lifecycle existing remote-server setup folder me rahega; separate cluster/private-network handlers nahi banenge.

Ye missing abstraction next implementation ka first fix hona chahiye.

    use std::{future::Future, time::Duration};
    
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
    pub(super) struct RetryPolicy {
        attempts: usize,
        initial_delay: Duration,
        max_delay: Duration,
    }
    
    impl RetryPolicy {
        pub(super) const fn network() -> Self {
            Self {
                attempts: 3,
                initial_delay: Duration::from_secs(1),
                max_delay: Duration::from_secs(4),
            }
        }
    
        #[cfg(test)]
        const fn immediate(attempts: usize) -> Self {
            Self {
                attempts,
                initial_delay: Duration::ZERO,
                max_delay: Duration::ZERO,
            }
        }
    
        pub(super) async fn run<T, E, F, Fut>(self, mut operation: F) -> Result<T, E>
        where
            F: FnMut(usize) -> Fut,
            Fut: Future<Output = Result<T, E>>,
        {
            debug_assert!(self.attempts > 0);
            let mut delay = self.initial_delay;
            for attempt in 1..=self.attempts {
                match operation(attempt).await {
                    Ok(value) => return Ok(value),
                    Err(error) if attempt == self.attempts => return Err(error),
                    Err(_) => {
                        tokio::time::sleep(delay).await;
                        delay = delay.saturating_mul(2).min(self.max_delay);
                    }
                }
            }
            unreachable!("retry policy always performs at least one attempt")
        }
    }
    
    #[cfg(test)]
    mod tests {
        use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};
    
        use super::RetryPolicy;
    
        #[tokio::test]
        async fn retries_transient_failures_until_success() {
            let attempts = AtomicUsize::new(0);
            let result = RetryPolicy::immediate(4)
                .run(|_| async {
                    let current = attempts.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst) + 1;
                    (current == 3).then_some("ready").ok_or("disconnected")
                })
                .await;
            assert_eq!(result, Ok("ready"));
            assert_eq!(attempts.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 3);
        }
    
        #[tokio::test]
        async fn returns_last_error_after_attempt_budget() {
            let attempts = AtomicUsize::new(0);
            let result: Result<(), usize> = RetryPolicy::immediate(3)
                .run(|attempt| async {
                    attempts.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
                    Err(attempt)
                })
                .await;
            assert_eq!(result, Err(3));
            assert_eq!(attempts.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 3);
        }
    }

## Assistant

Fresh code-level comparison ke baad, enterprise features exclude karke Rustploy me ye genuine missing/partial items hain. Purani list ka kaafi part ab complete ho chuka hai.

**Confirmed Missing**

1. Audit logs

Rustploy me schema/repository hai, lekin:

- Central audit API nahi
- Mutations automatically record nahi hoti
- Filtering, pagination, export, retention nahi
- Application/server/container actions ka complete audit trail nahi

Dokploy har important mutation me `audit(...)` call karta hai.

2. Organization lifecycle

Rustploy organization CRUD karta hai, lekin missing:

- Invite member
- Pending invitations list
- Resend/revoke invitation
- Accept invitation lifecycle
- Member list/remove
- Member role update
- Default/active organization switching
- Ownership transfer
- Resource-access assignment API

Schemas/repositories kuch available hain, public workflow incomplete hai.

3. Product/global settings

Rustploy me proper central settings service/API missing hai:

- Panel version/update check
- Panel upgrade/restart
- Public URL/IP settings
- Web-server settings
- Traefik environment settings
- Global build concurrency
- Global Docker cleanup policy
- Log cleanup policy
- Default timezone/retention
- Telemetry
- Infrastructure health summary

4. Docker management API

Rustploy logs, stats, terminal aur Swarm tooling deta hai, lekin general container management missing hai:

- Start/stop/restart/kill arbitrary container
- Remove arbitrary container
- Inspect full container config
- Upload/download container files
- Container mounts/networks inspection endpoints
- Container recreate/update configuration
- Images/networks/volumes list and management
- Docker disk-usage endpoint

5. Compose management

Core Compose lifecycle strong hai, lekin Dokploy comparison me missing/partial:

- Template catalogue/install/process/preview
- Converted Compose preview
- Compose randomization workflow
- Isolated-deployment action endpoint
- Deployment webhook-token rotation
- Move between environments
- Queue cleanup/history clear
- Force-kill stuck build
- Compose search
- Full service discovery/removal workflow
- Docker configs/secrets complete lifecycle

6. Application management gaps

Most important application features complete hain. Remaining:

- Application search
- Full Traefik raw/structured config read-write endpoint
- Drop/cancel individual queued deployment distinction
- Server-side deployment log query/search
- Watch-path behavior needs complete runtime verification
- Git release/tag deployment end-to-end verification

7. Template marketplace

Rustploy has AI Compose generation and local builder functionality, but no Dokploy-style:

- Template catalogue
- Categories/tags/search
- Template variables
- Generated passwords
- Template preview
- One-click installation
- Template import/export/versioning

8. Logs platform

Live logs available hain, lekin product-level logs tooling missing:

- Log download/export
- Time-range query
- Persistent log indexing
- Cross-resource search
- Retention configuration
- stdout/stderr server-side filtering everywhere
- Terminal session audit
- Terminal timeout policy
- Terminal/container file transfer

9. Server management gaps

Rustploy ka setup, audit repair, GPU, cleanup, backup, upgrade, diagnostics aur private networking strong hai. Remaining:

- Build concurrency per server
- Build-server assignment discovery
- Public IP/server-time helpers
- Server security/firewall report equivalent
- Removal dependency migration workflow
- Automatic cleanup scheduling from server policy
- Long operation lease heartbeat renewal

10. Global search and bulk operations

Missing:

- Applications/Compose/databases/servers ka global search
- Bulk start/stop/redeploy/delete
- Global deployment queue cleanup
- Cross-resource dependency view
- Consistent safe-delete diagnostics

**Partial, But Better Than Before**

11. Notifications

Provider CRUD, testing, bindings and delivery history available hain. Still check/complete karna hai:

- Failed delivery retry worker coverage
- Incident timeline
- Silence/snooze
- Backup/cleanup/restart event wiring coverage
- Delivery-to-alert correlation

12. Monitoring

Rustploy Dokploy se several areas me stronger hai: agent lifecycle, Prometheus export, retention policy, maintenance windows and alerts. Remaining:

- Alert acknowledgement
- Silence/snooze windows
- Incident lifecycle
- Monitoring-agent automatic version rollout policy
- Notification delivery correlation

13. Backups

Panel backup, Compose config backup, remote listing/download, verification, retention preview, retries and execution history implemented hain. Remaining:

- Full one-action disaster restore execution
- Restore progress stream
- Automatic integrity verification after every backup
- Scheduled panel backup lifecycle
- Traefik/certificate restoration verification

**Already Complete, Purani Missing List Se Hata Do**

- AI provider settings/models/testing/generation/log analysis/deploy
- Preview deployment lifecycle
- GitHub/GitLab/Gitea/Bitbucket providers and webhooks
- Application ports/mounts/redirects/security/patches
- Application import/export/move/token rotation/rollback APIs
- Registry discovery/tags/rotation/usage
- Schedule history/retry/missed-run/concurrency/notifications
- Certificate renewal/history
- Traefik version and middleware rendering
- DNS/domain diagnostics, CDN purge and root-network repair
- Monitoring agent reinstall/restart/export/Prometheus
- Password reset, email verification, 2FA, sessions and API tokens
- Managed WireGuard/private-network lifecycle

Highest priority ab:

1. Audit logs
2. Organization members/invitations
3. Product settings
4. Docker management
5. Compose templates and remaining lifecycle operations
6. Logs/search/export
7. Global search and bulk operations

Rustploy ka deployment/backend feature coverage ab Dokploy ke kaafi close hai. Sabse bada difference ab deployment engine nahi, balki administration, auditability, Docker operator tooling aur product-level settings hain.

    use std::sync::Arc;
    use auto_di::singleton;
    
    use crate::{
        api::dto::docker_management::{ContainerActionDto, DockerActionResponseDto, DockerPruneRequestDto, DockerPruneResponseDto},
        repository::ServerRepository,
        utils::{
            docker::{ContainerSummary, DockerCli, ImageSummary, NetworkSummary, VolumeSummary},
            exec::{CommandExecutor, LocalExecutor, RemoteExecutor, SshAuth, SshHostKey},
        },
    };
    
    pub struct DockerManagementService { servers: Arc<ServerRepository> }
    
    #[singleton]
    impl DockerManagementService {
        fn new(servers: Arc<ServerRepository>) -> Self { Self { servers } }
    
        pub async fn containers(&self, server_id: Option<i64>) -> Result<Vec<ContainerSummary>, String> {
            self.docker(server_id).await?.containers().ps().all().list().await.map_err(error)
        }
        pub async fn images(&self, server_id: Option<i64>) -> Result<Vec<ImageSummary>, String> {
            self.docker(server_id).await?.images().list().all().list().await.map_err(error)
        }
        pub async fn networks(&self, server_id: Option<i64>) -> Result<Vec<NetworkSummary>, String> {
            self.docker(server_id).await?.networks().list().list().await.map_err(error)
        }
        pub async fn volumes(&self, server_id: Option<i64>) -> Result<Vec<VolumeSummary>, String> {
            self.docker(server_id).await?.volumes().list().list().await.map_err(error)
        }
        pub async fn container_inspect(&self, server_id: Option<i64>, id: &str) -> Result<serde_json::Value, String> {
            validate_resource_name(id)?; self.docker(server_id).await?.containers().inspect_raw(id).await.map_err(error)
        }
        pub async fn image_inspect(&self, server_id: Option<i64>, id: &str) -> Result<serde_json::Value, String> {
            validate_resource_name(id)?; self.docker(server_id).await?.images().inspect_raw(id).await.map_err(error)
        }
        pub async fn network_inspect(&self, server_id: Option<i64>, id: &str) -> Result<serde_json::Value, String> {
            validate_resource_name(id)?; self.docker(server_id).await?.networks().inspect_raw(id).await.map_err(error)
        }
        pub async fn volume_inspect(&self, server_id: Option<i64>, id: &str) -> Result<serde_json::Value, String> {
            validate_resource_name(id)?; self.docker(server_id).await?.volumes().inspect_raw(id).await.map_err(error)
        }
        pub async fn container_action(&self, server_id: Option<i64>, id: &str, action: ContainerActionDto) -> Result<DockerActionResponseDto, String> {
            validate_resource_name(id)?;
            let docker = self.docker(server_id).await?;
            let containers = docker.containers();
            let output = match action {
                ContainerActionDto::Start => containers.start(id).run().await,
                ContainerActionDto::Stop => containers.stop(id).run().await,
                ContainerActionDto::Restart => containers.restart(id).run().await,
                ContainerActionDto::Kill => containers.kill(id).run().await,
                ContainerActionDto::Pause => containers.pause(id).run().await,
                ContainerActionDto::Unpause => containers.unpause(id).run().await,
            }.map_err(error)?;
            Ok(output.into())
        }
        pub async fn remove_container(&self, server_id: Option<i64>, id: &str, force: bool, volumes: bool) -> Result<DockerActionResponseDto, String> {
            validate_resource_name(id)?;
            let docker = self.docker(server_id).await?;
            let mut command = docker.containers().rm(id);
            if force { command = command.force(); }
            if volumes { command = command.volumes(); }
            command.run().await.map(Into::into).map_err(error)
        }
        pub async fn disk_usage(&self, server_id: Option<i64>) -> Result<serde_json::Value, String> {
            self.docker(server_id).await?.system_df().await.map(serde_json::Value::Object).map_err(error)
        }
        pub async fn prune(&self, server_id: Option<i64>, input: DockerPruneRequestDto) -> Result<DockerPruneResponseDto, String> {
            let docker = self.docker(server_id).await?;
            let mut operations = Vec::new();
            if input.containers { operations.push(docker.containers().prune().run().await.map_err(error)?.into()); }
            if input.images { operations.push(docker.images().prune().all().run().await.map_err(error)?.into()); }
            if input.networks { operations.push(docker.networks().prune().run().await.map_err(error)?.into()); }
            if input.volumes { operations.push(docker.volumes().prune().all().run().await.map_err(error)?.into()); }
            Ok(DockerPruneResponseDto { operations })
        }
        async fn docker(&self, server_id: Option<i64>) -> Result<DockerCli, String> {
            match server_id {
                None => Ok(DockerCli::from_executor(CommandExecutor::Local(LocalExecutor::new()))),
                Some(server_id) => {
                    let (host, port, username, private_key, public_key) = self.servers.get_direct_ssh_credentials(server_id).await.map_err(|error| error.to_string())?.ok_or_else(|| "server or SSH key not found".to_owned())?;
                    let port = u16::try_from(port).map_err(|_| "invalid SSH port".to_owned())?;
                    Ok(DockerCli::from_executor(CommandExecutor::Remote(RemoteExecutor::new(host, port, username, SshAuth::key_pair(private_key, public_key), SshHostKey::InsecureAcceptAny).with_sudo())))
                }
            }
        }
    }
    
    impl From<crate::utils::docker::DockerOutput> for DockerActionResponseDto {
        fn from(value: crate::utils::docker::DockerOutput) -> Self { Self { stdout: value.stdout, stderr: value.stderr } }
    }
    fn validate_resource_name(value: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
        if !value.is_empty() && value.len() <= 255 && value.chars().all(|character| character.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || ".:_/@+-".contains(character)) { Ok(()) } else { Err("invalid Docker resource identifier".into()) }
    }
    fn error(error: impl std::fmt::Display) -> String { error.to_string() }
    
    #[cfg(test)] mod tests {
        use super::validate_resource_name;
        #[test] fn validates_docker_resource_identifiers() {
            assert!(validate_resource_name("registry.example.com/team/app:latest").is_ok());
            assert!(validate_resource_name("container_name-1").is_ok());
            assert!(validate_resource_name("bad name").is_err());
            assert!(validate_resource_name(";shutdown").is_err());
        }
    }

    use std::sync::Arc;
    
    use auto_route::controller;
    use axum::{
        Json,
        extract::{Path, Query},
        http::StatusCode,
    };
    use serde::Deserialize;
    
    use crate::{
        api::dto::docker_management::{
            ContainerActionRequestDto, ContainerRemoveRequestDto, DockerActionResponseDto,
            DockerPruneRequestDto, DockerPruneResponseDto,
        },
        core::middleware::{
            permission::{RequirePermission, ServerCreatePermission, ServerReadPermission},
            validator::ValidatedJson,
        },
        services::docker_management::DockerManagementService,
        utils::docker::{ContainerSummary, ImageSummary, NetworkSummary, VolumeSummary},
    };
    
    type ApiError = (StatusCode, String);
    
    #[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
    struct DockerTargetQuery {
        server_id: Option<i64>,
    }
    
    pub struct DockerManagementController {
        service: Arc<DockerManagementService>,
    }
    
    #[controller("/docker")]
    impl DockerManagementController {
        fn new(service: Arc<DockerManagementService>) -> Self {
            Self { service }
        }
    
        #[get("/containers")]
        async fn containers(
            &self,
            RequirePermission(_, _): RequirePermission<ServerReadPermission>,
            Query(query): Query<DockerTargetQuery>,
        ) -> Result<Json<Vec<ContainerSummary>>, ApiError> {
            self.service
                .containers(query.server_id)
                .await
                .map(Json)
                .map_err(api_error)
        }
    
        #[get("/images")]
        async fn images(
            &self,
            RequirePermission(_, _): RequirePermission<ServerReadPermission>,
            Query(query): Query<DockerTargetQuery>,
        ) -> Result<Json<Vec<ImageSummary>>, ApiError> {
            self.service
                .images(query.server_id)
                .await
                .map(Json)
                .map_err(api_error)
        }
    
        #[get("/networks")]
        async fn networks(
            &self,
            RequirePermission(_, _): RequirePermission<ServerReadPermission>,
            Query(query): Query<DockerTargetQuery>,
        ) -> Result<Json<Vec<NetworkSummary>>, ApiError> {
            self.service
                .networks(query.server_id)
                .await
                .map(Json)
                .map_err(api_error)
        }
    
        #[get("/volumes")]

            Query(query): Query<DockerTargetQuery>,

            self.service

        #[delete("/containers/{id}")]
        async fn remove_container(

            Path(id): Path<String>,
            Query(query): Query<DockerTargetQuery>,
            ValidatedJson(body): ValidatedJson<ContainerRemoveRequestDto>,
        ) -> Result<Json<DockerActionResponseDto>, ApiError> {
            self.service
                .remove_container(query.server_id, &id, body.force, body.volumes)

        #[get("/disk-usage")]

        ) -> Result<Json<serde_json::Value>, ApiError> {
            self.service

        #[post("/prune")]
        async fn prune(

            Query(query): Query<DockerTargetQuery>,
            ValidatedJson(body): ValidatedJson<DockerPruneRequestDto>,

            self.service
                .prune(query.server_id, body)
                .await
                .map(Json)
                .map_err(api_error)
        }
    }
    
    fn api_error(error: String) -> ApiError {
        if error.starts_with("invalid") {
            (StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, error)
        } else {
            (StatusCode::BAD_GATEWAY, error)
        }
    }

Ab expressive resource pattern hai:

```rust
docker.container(id).start()
docker.container(id).restart()
docker.container(id).remove().force().volumes()
docker.container(id).inspect_typed()

docker.image(id).remove()
docker.network(name).remove()
docker.volume(name).remove()
```

Naye Docker management service aur existing setup/railpack code ko bhi isi pattern par migrate kiya. Low-level plural handles sirf collection operations ke liye hain:

```rust
docker.containers().list()
docker.images().list()
docker.networks().prune()
docker.volumes().prune()
```

Tests aur `cargo check --all-targets` pass hain. Ab isi convention me remaining implementation continue hogi.

    use std::sync::Arc;
    
    use auto_route::controller;
    use axum::{Json, extract::Path, http::StatusCode};
    
    use crate::{
        api::dto::settings::{SettingsResponseDto, UpdateSettingsDto},
        core::middleware::{
            permission::{OrgWritePermission, RequirePermission},
            validator::ValidatedJson,
        },
        services::settings::SettingsService,
    };
    
    type ApiError = (StatusCode, String);
    
    pub struct SettingsController {
        service: Arc<SettingsService>,
    }
    
    #[controller("/settings")]
    impl SettingsController {
        fn new(service: Arc<SettingsService>) -> Self { Self { service } }
    
        #[get]
        async fn get(
            &self,
            RequirePermission(_claims, _): RequirePermission<OrgWritePermission>,
        ) -> Result<Json<SettingsResponseDto>, ApiError> {
            self.service.get().await.map(Json).map_err(map_error)
        }
    
        #[put]
        async fn update(
            &self,
            RequirePermission(_claims, _): RequirePermission<OrgWritePermission>,
            ValidatedJson(body): ValidatedJson<UpdateSettingsDto>,
        ) -> Result<Json<SettingsResponseDto>, ApiError> {
            self.service.update(body).await.map(Json).map_err(map_error)
        }
    }
    
    fn map_error(error: sqlx::Error) -> ApiError {
        match error {
            sqlx::Error::Protocol(message) => (StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, message),
            other => {
                tracing::error!(error = %other, "settings operation failed");
                (StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, "settings operation failed".into())
            }
        }
    }

    use std::sync::Arc;
    
    use auto_di::singleton;
    
    use crate::{
        api::dto::settings::{SettingsResponseDto, UpdateSettingsDto},
        db::models::settings::Setting,
        repository::SettingRepository,
    };
    
    pub struct SettingsService {
        repository: Arc<SettingRepository>,
    }
    
    #[singleton]
    impl SettingsService {
        fn new(repository: Arc<SettingRepository>) -> Self {
            Self { repository }
        }
    
        pub async fn get(&self) -> sqlx::Result<SettingsResponseDto> {
            let setting = self.current().await?;
            Ok(setting.into())
        }
    
        pub async fn update(&self, input: UpdateSettingsDto) -> sqlx::Result<SettingsResponseDto> {
            let current = self.current().await?;
            let setting = Setting {
                id: current.id,
                server_ip: input.server_ip.or(current.server_ip),
                certificate_type: input.certificate_type.unwrap_or(current.certificate_type),
                custom_cert_resolver: input.custom_cert_resolver.or(current.custom_cert_resolver),
                https: input.https.map(i64::from).unwrap_or(current.https),
                host: input.host.or(current.host),
                lets_encrypt_email: input
                    .lets_encrypt_email
                    .or(current.lets_encrypt_email),
                enable_docker_cleanup: input
                    .enable_docker_cleanup
                    .map(i64::from)
                    .unwrap_or(current.enable_docker_cleanup),
                log_cleanup_cron: input.log_cleanup_cron.or(current.log_cleanup_cron),
                metrics_config: input.metrics_config.unwrap_or(current.metrics_config),
                created_at: current.created_at,
                updated_at: chrono::Utc::now().timestamp(),
            };
            self.repository
                .update(current.id.unwrap_or_default(), &setting)
                .await?;
            Ok(setting.into())
        }
    
        async fn current(&self) -> sqlx::Result<Setting> {
            if let Some(setting) = self.repository.get_all().await?.into_iter().next() {
                return Ok(setting);
            }
            let now = chrono::Utc::now().timestamp();
            let setting = Setting {
                id: None,
                server_ip: None,
                certificate_type: "NONE".into(),
                custom_cert_resolver: None,
                https: 0,
                host: None,
                lets_encrypt_email: None,
                enable_docker_cleanup: 1,
                log_cleanup_cron: Some("0 0 * * *".into()),
                metrics_config: "{}".into(),
                created_at: now,
                updated_at: now,
            };
            let id = self.repository.create(&setting).await?;
            Ok(Setting { id: Some(id), ..setting })
        }
    }
    
    impl From<Setting> for SettingsResponseDto {
        fn from(value: Setting) -> Self {
            Self {
                id: value.id.unwrap_or_default(),
                server_ip: value.server_ip,
                certificate_type: value.certificate_type,
                custom_cert_resolver: value.custom_cert_resolver,
                https: value.https != 0,
                host: value.host,
                lets_encrypt_email: value.lets_encrypt_email,
                enable_docker_cleanup: value.enable_docker_cleanup != 0,
                log_cleanup_cron: value.log_cleanup_cron,
                metrics_config: value.metrics_config,
                updated_at: value.updated_at,
            }
        }
    }

```text
services/deployment/
├── mod.rs

```

`mod.rs` sirf modules expose karega:

```rust
mod docker;

    CancelDeploymentResult,
```

```rust
pub struct DeploymentService {
    db: Arc<SqlitePool>,
    repo_deploy: Arc<DeploymentRepository>,
    repo_app: Arc<ApplicationRepository>,
}
```

`types.rs` me typed inputs/results:

```rust
pub struct DockerLogOptions {
    pub tail: usize,
    pub follow: bool,
    pub timestamps: bool,
    pub since: Option<String>,
    pub until: Option<String>,
}
```

`docker.rs` me Docker-related service methods:

```rust
impl DeploymentService {
    pub async fn stream_docker_container_logs(
        &self,
        server_id: Option<i64>,
        container: String,
        options: DockerLogOptions,
    ) -> Result<Receiver<DockerStreamEvent>> {
        // Typed Docker builder use hoga
    }
}
```

Handler ko internal files se matlab nahi hoga:

```rust
use crate::services::deployment::{
    DeploymentService,
    DockerLogOptions,
};
```

Use:

```rust
service
    .stream_docker_container_logs(
        server_id,
        container_name,
        DockerLogOptions {
            tail: 200,
            follow: true,
            timestamps: true,
            since: Some("1h".into()),
            until: None,
        },
    )
    .await?;
```

Docker command raw assemble nahi hoga:

```rust
docker
    .container(container_name)
    .logs()
    .tail(options.tail)
    .follow()
    .since("1h")
    .stream(sender)
    .await?;
```

Isse caller sirf typed values control karega. `--tail`, `--follow`, `--since` jaise actual flags builder ke andar encapsulated rahenge. Typo ya unsupported raw flag pass nahi ho sakta.

    use crate::utils::docker::{core::ArgBuilder, DockerCli, DockerOutput, DockerResult};
    
    #[derive(Clone, Copy)]
    enum CopyDirection { ToContainer, FromContainer }
    
    pub struct ContainerCopyBuilder<'a> {
        cli: &'a DockerCli,
        container: String,
        path: String,
        direction: CopyDirection,
    }
    
    impl<'a> ContainerCopyBuilder<'a> {
        pub(crate) fn upload(cli: &'a DockerCli, container: String, destination: String) -> Self {
            Self { cli, container, path: destination, direction: CopyDirection::ToContainer }

            let mut args = ArgBuilder::cmd(&["cp"]);
            match self.direction {
                CopyDirection::ToContainer => { args.push(other); args.push(format!("{}:{}", self.container, self.path)); }
                CopyDirection::FromContainer => { args.push(format!("{}:{}", self.container, self.path)); args.push(other); }
            }
            args.build()
        }

    +fn single_file_tar(filename: &str, data: &[u8]) -> DockerResult<Vec<u8>> {
    +    validate_path(filename)?;
    +    let mut archive = vec![0u8; 512];
    +    write_field(&mut archive[0..100], filename.as_bytes());
    +    write_octal(&mut archive[100..108], 0o644, 8);
    +    write_octal(&mut archive[108..116], 0, 8);
    +    write_octal(&mut archive[116..124], 0, 8);
    +    write_octal(&mut archive[124..136], data.len() as u64, 12);
    +    write_octal(&mut archive[136..148], 0, 12);
    +    archive[156] = b'0';
    +    archive[257..263].copy_from_slice(b"ustar\0");
    +    archive[263..265].copy_from_slice(b"00");
    +    archive[148..156].fill(b' ');
    +    let checksum: u32 = archive.iter().map(|byte| *byte as u32).sum();
    +    write_octal(&mut archive[148..156], checksum as u64, 8);
    +    archive.extend_from_slice(data);
    +    archive.resize((archive.len() + 511) / 512 * 512, 0);
    +    archive.extend_from_slice(&[0u8; 1024]);
    +    Ok(archive)
    +}
    +
    +fn extract_single_tar_file(archive: &[u8]) -> DockerResult<Vec<u8>> {
    +    if archive.len() < 512 || archive[257..263] != *b"ustar\0" {
    +        return Err(crate::utils::docker::DockerError::CommandFailed("docker returned invalid tar archive".into()));
    +    }
    +    let size = parse_octal(&archive[124..136])? as usize;
    +    let end = 512usize.checked_add(size).ok_or_else(|| crate::utils::docker::DockerError::CommandFailed("archive too large".into()))?;
    +    if end > archive.len() { return Err(crate::utils::docker::DockerError::CommandFailed("truncated tar archive".into())); }
    +    Ok(archive[512..end].to_vec())
     }
     
    +fn validate_path(path: &str) -> DockerResult<()> {
    +    if path.is_empty() || path.contains('\0') || path.contains("..") || path.starts_with('/') {
    +        return Err(crate::utils::docker::DockerError::CommandFailed("invalid transfer path".into()));
    +    }
    +    Ok(())
    +}

    +fn write_field(field: &mut [u8], value: &[u8]) { let len = value.len().min(field.len()); field[..len].copy_from_slice(&value[..len]); }

    use std::sync::Arc;
    
    use crate::services::deployment::DeploymentService;
    
    pub fn start(service: Arc<DeploymentService>) {
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            let mut ticker = tokio::time::interval(std::time::Duration::from_secs(24 * 60 * 60));
            ticker.set_missed_tick_behavior(tokio::time::MissedTickBehavior::Skip);
            loop {
                ticker.tick().await;
                let cutoff = chrono::Utc::now().timestamp() - 30 * 24 * 60 * 60;
                match service.cleanup_logs_before(cutoff).await {
                    Ok(0) => {}
                    Ok(removed) => tracing::info!(removed, "expired deployment logs removed"),
                    Err(error) => tracing::error!(error = %error, "deployment log cleanup failed"),
                }
            }
        });
    }

    use std::sync::Arc;
    
    use crate::services::backup::PanelBackupService;
    
    pub fn start(service: Arc<PanelBackupService>) {
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            let mut ticker = tokio::time::interval(std::time::Duration::from_secs(24 * 60 * 60));
            ticker.set_missed_tick_behavior(tokio::time::MissedTickBehavior::Skip);
            ticker.tick().await;
            loop {
                ticker.tick().await;
                match service.create().await {
                    Ok(backup) => tracing::info!(path = %backup.path, checksum = %backup.checksum_sha256, "scheduled verified panel backup completed"),
                    Err(error) => tracing::error!(error = %error, "scheduled panel backup failed"),
                }
            }
        });
    }

    use std::sync::Arc;
    
    use auto_di::singleton;
    use sqlx::SqlitePool;
    
    use super::{GlobalResourceDto, GlobalSearchOptions};
    
    pub struct GlobalOperationsService { db: Arc<SqlitePool> }
    
    #[singleton]
    impl GlobalOperationsService {
        fn new(db: Arc<SqlitePool>) -> Self { Self { db } }
    
        pub async fn search(&self, options: GlobalSearchOptions) -> sqlx::Result<Vec<GlobalResourceDto>> {
            let pattern = format!("%{}%", options.query.trim());
            let rows = sqlx::query!(r#"
                SELECT resource_type, id, name, status FROM (
                    SELECT 'APPLICATION' resource_type, CAST(id AS TEXT) id, name, app_status status FROM applications
                    UNION ALL SELECT 'COMPOSE', CAST(id AS TEXT), name, compose_status FROM compose_projects
                    UNION ALL SELECT 'SERVER', CAST(id AS TEXT), name, server_status FROM servers
                    UNION ALL SELECT 'PROJECT', CAST(id AS TEXT), name, NULL FROM projects
                    UNION ALL SELECT 'ENVIRONMENT', CAST(id AS TEXT), name, NULL FROM environments
                    UNION ALL SELECT 'POSTGRES', CAST(id AS TEXT), name, database_status FROM postgres_dbs
                    UNION ALL SELECT 'MYSQL', CAST(id AS TEXT), name, database_status FROM mysql_dbs
                    UNION ALL SELECT 'MARIADB', CAST(id AS TEXT), name, database_status FROM mariadb_dbs
                    UNION ALL SELECT 'MONGO', CAST(id AS TEXT), name, database_status FROM mongo_dbs
                    UNION ALL SELECT 'REDIS', CAST(id AS TEXT), name, database_status FROM redis_dbs
                    UNION ALL SELECT 'LIBSQL', CAST(id AS TEXT), name, database_status FROM libsql_dbs
                ) resources WHERE name LIKE ? COLLATE NOCASE ORDER BY name LIMIT ?
            "#, pattern, options.limit).fetch_all(self.db.as_ref()).await?;
            Ok(rows.into_iter().map(|row| GlobalResourceDto { resource_type: row.resource_type.unwrap_or_default(), id: row.id.unwrap_or_default(), name: row.name, status: row.status }).collect())
        }
    
        pub async fn cleanup_deployment_queue(&self) -> sqlx::Result<u64> {
            let result = sqlx::query!("UPDATE deployments SET status = 'CANCELLED', state = 'CANCELLED', finished_at = strftime('%s', 'now'), last_state_at = strftime('%s', 'now') WHERE status = 'QUEUED'").execute(self.db.as_ref()).await?;
            Ok(result.rows_affected())
        }
    }

    Add: /run/media/das/SSD/Devloper/rustploy/src/utils/background/policy.rs
    pub fn cron_due(expression: &str, now: chrono::DateTime<chrono::Utc>) -> bool {
        use chrono::{Datelike, Timelike};
        let fields = expression.split_whitespace().collect::<Vec<_>>();
        fields.len() == 5
            && matches_field(fields[0], now.minute())
            && matches_field(fields[1], now.hour())
            && matches_field(fields[2], now.day())
            && matches_field(fields[3], now.month())
            && matches_field(fields[4], now.weekday().num_days_from_sunday())
    }
    
    fn matches_field(field: &str, value: u32) -> bool {
        field.split(',').any(|item| {
            if item == "*" { true }
            else if let Some(step) = item.strip_prefix("*/").and_then(|v| v.parse::<u32>().ok()) { step > 0 && value % step == 0 }
            else { item.parse::<u32>().ok() == Some(value) }
        })
    }

    +    let paths = crate::utils::paths::rustploy_paths();
    +    let marker = format!("{}/backups/panel-restore.pending.json", paths.base);
    +    let Ok(bytes) = tokio::fs::read(&marker).await else { return };
    +    let Ok(value) = serde_json::from_slice::<serde_json::Value>(&bytes) else { return };
    +    let Some(restore_id) = value.get("restore_id").and_then(|value| value.as_str()) else { return };
    +    let directory = format!("{}/backups/restore-history", paths.base);
    +    let _ = tokio::fs::create_dir_all(&directory).await;
    +    let record = serde_json::json!({ "restore_id": restore_id, "status": "FAILED", "message": error, "updated_at": chrono::Utc::now().timestamp() });
    +    if let Ok(body) = serde_json::to_vec_pretty(&record) { let _ = tokio::fs::write(format!("{directory}/{restore_id}.json"), body).await; }

    +    pub async fn stage_rollback(&self, recovery_database: &str) -> sqlx::Result<StagePanelRestoreDto> {
    +        let paths = rustploy_paths();
    +        let database = Path::new(recovery_database);
    +        let allowed_parent = Path::new(&paths.base);
    +        if !database.is_absolute() || !database.starts_with(allowed_parent) || !database.file_name().is_some_and(|name| name.to_string_lossy().contains(".pre-restore-")) {
    +            return Err(sqlx::Error::Protocol("recovery database must be a Rustploy pre-restore snapshot".into()));
    +        }
    +        let bytes = tokio::fs::read(database).await.map_err(io_error)?;
    +        let restore_id = uuid::Uuid::new_v4().simple().to_string();
    +        let staging = format!("{}/backups/restore-staging/{restore_id}", paths.base);
    +        tokio::fs::create_dir_all(&staging).await.map_err(io_error)?;
    +        tokio::fs::write(format!("{staging}/db.sqlite3"), &bytes).await.map_err(io_error)?;
    +        let checksum = format!("{:x}", Sha256::digest(&bytes));
    +        let marker = format!("{}/backups/panel-restore.pending.json", paths.base);
    +        tokio::fs::write(&marker, serde_json::to_vec_pretty(&serde_json::json!({ "restore_id": restore_id.clone(), "staging": staging, "checksum_sha256": checksum, "created_at": chrono::Utc::now().timestamp(), "kind": "ROLLBACK" })).map_err(|error| sqlx::Error::Protocol(error.to_string()))?).await.map_err(io_error)?;
    +        Ok(StagePanelRestoreDto { restore_id, checksum_sha256: checksum, restart_required: true, pending_marker: marker })
    +    }
     }

    use auto_di::singleton;
    use sqlx::SqlitePool;
    use std::sync::Arc;
    
    #[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, serde::Serialize, poem_openapi::Object)]
    pub struct ResourceDependencyCounts {
        pub active_deployments: i64,
        pub deployments: i64,
        pub domains: i64,
        pub mounts: i64,
        pub patches: i64,
        pub schedules: i64,
        pub backups: i64,
        pub enabled_backups: i64,
        pub preview_deployments: i64,
        pub middleware: i64,
        pub ports: i64,
        pub redirects: i64,
        pub security_rules: i64,
    }
    
    impl ResourceDependencyCounts {
        pub fn blocks_delete(&self) -> bool {
            self.active_deployments > 0 || self.enabled_backups > 0
        }
    }
    
    #[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, serde::Serialize, poem_openapi::Object)]
    pub struct CertificateDependencyCounts {
        pub renewals: i64,
        pub running_renewals: i64,
    }
    
    #[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, serde::Serialize, poem_openapi::Object)]
    pub struct NetworkDependencyCounts {
        pub applications: i64,
        pub compose_services: i64,
        pub databases: i64,
    }
    
    impl NetworkDependencyCounts {
        pub fn total(&self) -> i64 {
            self.applications + self.compose_services + self.databases
        }
    }
    
    pub struct ResourceDependencyRepository {
        pool: Arc<SqlitePool>,
    }
    
    #[singleton]
    impl ResourceDependencyRepository {
        pub fn new(pool: Arc<SqlitePool>) -> Self {
            Self { pool }
        }
    
        pub async fn application(&self, id: i64) -> sqlx::Result<ResourceDependencyCounts> {
            let row = sqlx::query!(
                r#"SELECT
                    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM deployments WHERE application_id = ? AND status IN ('QUEUED', 'RUNNING')) AS "active_deployments!: i64",
                    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM deployments WHERE application_id = ?) AS "deployments!: i64",
                    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM domains WHERE application_id = ?) AS "domains!: i64",
                    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM mounts WHERE application_id = ?) AS "mounts!: i64",
                    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM patches WHERE application_id = ?) AS "patches!: i64",
                    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM schedules WHERE application_id = ?) AS "schedules!: i64",
                    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM volume_backups WHERE application_id = ?) AS "backups!: i64",
                    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM volume_backups WHERE application_id = ? AND enabled = 1) AS "enabled_backups!: i64",
                    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM preview_deployments WHERE base_application_id = ? OR preview_application_id = ?) AS "preview_deployments!: i64",
                    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM application_middlewares WHERE application_id = ?) AS "middleware!: i64",
                    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ports WHERE application_id = ?) AS "ports!: i64",
                    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM redirects WHERE application_id = ?) AS "redirects!: i64",
                    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM security WHERE application_id = ?) AS "security_rules!: i64""#,
                id, id, id, id, id, id, id, id, id, id, id, id, id, id
            )
            .fetch_one(self.pool.as_ref())
            .await?;
            Ok(ResourceDependencyCounts {
                active_deployments: row.active_deployments,
                deployments: row.deployments,
                domains: row.domains,
                mounts: row.mounts,
                patches: row.patches,
                schedules: row.schedules,
                backups: row.backups,
                enabled_backups: row.enabled_backups,
                preview_deployments: row.preview_deployments,
                middleware: row.middleware,
                ports: row.ports,
                redirects: row.redirects,
                security_rules: row.security_rules,
            })
        }
    
        pub async fn compose(&self, id: i64) -> sqlx::Result<ResourceDependencyCounts> {
            let row = sqlx::query!(
                r#"SELECT
                    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM deployments WHERE compose_id = ? AND status IN ('QUEUED', 'RUNNING')) AS "active_deployments!: i64",
                    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM deployments WHERE compose_id = ?) AS "deployments!: i64",
                    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM domains WHERE compose_id = ?) AS "domains!: i64",
                    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM mounts WHERE compose_id = ?) AS "mounts!: i64",
                    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM patches WHERE compose_id = ?) AS "patches!: i64",
                    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM schedules WHERE compose_id = ?) AS "schedules!: i64",
                    ((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM backups WHERE compose_id = ?) + (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM volume_backups WHERE compose_id = ?)) AS "backups!: i64",
                    ((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM backups WHERE compose_id = ? AND enabled = 1) + (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM volume_backups WHERE compose_id = ? AND enabled = 1)) AS "enabled_backups!: i64""#,
                id, id, id, id, id, id, id, id, id, id
            )
            .fetch_one(self.pool.as_ref())
            .await?;
            Ok(ResourceDependencyCounts {
                active_deployments: row.active_deployments,
                deployments: row.deployments,
                domains: row.domains,
                mounts: row.mounts,
                patches: row.patches,
                schedules: row.schedules,
                backups: row.backups,
                enabled_backups: row.enabled_backups,
                ..Default::default()
            })
        }
    
        pub async fn certificate(&self, id: i64) -> sqlx::Result<CertificateDependencyCounts> {
            let row = sqlx::query!(
                r#"SELECT COUNT(*) AS "renewals!: i64",
                    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'RUNNING') AS "running_renewals!: i64"
                   FROM certificate_renewals WHERE certificate_id = ?"#,
                id
            )
            .fetch_one(self.pool.as_ref())
            .await?;
            Ok(CertificateDependencyCounts {
                renewals: row.renewals,
                running_renewals: row.running_renewals,
            })
        }
    
        pub async fn database_network(&self, id: i64) -> sqlx::Result<NetworkDependencyCounts> {
            let key = id.to_string();
            let applications = sqlx::query_scalar!(
                r#"SELECT COUNT(*) AS "count!: i64" FROM applications, json_each(applications.network_ids) WHERE json_each.value = ?"#,
                key
            ).fetch_one(self.pool.as_ref()).await?;
            let compose_services = sqlx::query_scalar!(
                r#"SELECT COUNT(*) AS "count!: i64" FROM compose_projects, json_each(compose_projects.service_networks) WHERE json_each.value LIKE '%' || ? || '%'"#,
                key
            ).fetch_one(self.pool.as_ref()).await?;
            let databases = sqlx::query_scalar!(
                r#"SELECT
                    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM postgres_dbs, json_each(postgres_dbs.network_ids) WHERE json_each.value = ?) +
                    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM mysql_dbs, json_each(mysql_dbs.network_ids) WHERE json_each.value = ?) +
                    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM mariadb_dbs, json_each(mariadb_dbs.network_ids) WHERE json_each.value = ?) +
                    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM mongo_dbs, json_each(mongo_dbs.network_ids) WHERE json_each.value = ?) +
                    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM redis_dbs, json_each(redis_dbs.network_ids) WHERE json_each.value = ?) +
                    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM libsql_dbs, json_each(libsql_dbs.network_ids) WHERE json_each.value = ?) AS "count!: i64""#,
                key, key, key, key, key, key
            ).fetch_one(self.pool.as_ref()).await?;
            Ok(NetworkDependencyCounts { applications, compose_services, databases })
        }
    }
