    use axum::extract::Multipart;
    
    use super::{ApplicationRecord, ApplicationService};
    use crate::{
        core::cache::CacheKey,
        repository::ServerRepository,
        utils::{
            exec::{CommandExecutor, LocalExecutor},
            paths::rustploy_paths,
            remote_transfer::upload_via_rclone,
            upload::{MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES, extract_zip, sanitize_zip, stream_multipart_file},
        },
    };
    
    impl ApplicationService {
        pub async fn upload_drop_source(
            &self,
            id: i64,
            multipart: Multipart,
        ) -> Result<ApplicationRecord, String> {
            let application = self
                .repo_app
                .get_by_id(id)
                .await
                .map_err(|error| format!("database error: {error}"))?
                .ok_or_else(|| "application not found".to_owned())?;
    
            let upload = tempfile::NamedTempFile::new()
                .map_err(|error| format!("failed to create upload file: {error}"))?;
            let clean = tempfile::NamedTempFile::new()
                .map_err(|error| format!("failed to create sanitized archive: {error}"))?;
            let uploaded = stream_multipart_file(multipart, "file", upload.path(), MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES).await?;
            if !uploaded.filename.to_ascii_lowercase().ends_with(".zip") {
                return Err("application source upload must be a .zip archive".into());
            }
            sanitize_zip(upload.path(), clean.path()).await?;
    
            let destination = rustploy_paths().application_code(&application.app_name);
            match application.server_id {
                None => {
                    extract_zip(
                        &CommandExecutor::Local(LocalExecutor::new()),
                        clean.path(),
                        &destination,
                    )
                    .await?;
                }
                Some(server_id) => {
                    let servers = auto_di::resolve::<ServerRepository>()
                        .await
                        .map_err(|error| format!("failed to resolve server repository: {error}"))?;
                    let remote_archive = format!(
                        "/tmp/rustploy-application-upload-{}.zip",
                        uuid::Uuid::new_v4()
                    );
                    let remote = upload_via_rclone(
                        servers.as_ref(),
                        server_id,
                        clean.path(),
                        &remote_archive,
                    )
                    .await?;
                    let executor = CommandExecutor::Remote(remote);
                    let result = extract_zip(&executor, &remote_archive, &destination).await;
                    let _ = crate::utils::os::OsCli::new(&executor)
                        .file(&remote_archive)
                        .delete()
                        .run()
                        .await;
                    result?;
                }
            }
    
            self.repo_app
                .set_drop_source(
                    id,
                    application.drop_build_path.unwrap_or_else(|| "/".into()),
                )
                .await
                .map_err(|error| format!("failed to update application source: {error}"))?;
            self.cache.invalidate(&CacheKey::Application(id)).await;
            self.get_by_id(id)
                .await
                .map_err(|error| format!("failed to reload application: {error}"))
        }
    }

Upload system properly fix kar diya.

- Application archive now actually uploads through `FormData`.
- Multipart chunks directly temporary disk file me stream hote hain.
- 100 MiB limit streaming ke waqt enforce hoti hai.
- ZIP sanitize hone ke baad hi extract hota hai.
- Remote application upload uses rclone SFTP.
- DB source state successful extraction ke baad hi update hoti hai.
- Build path same atomic multipart request me jata hai.
- Container upload no longer loads full file into RAM.
- Local container: temp file → typed `container().upload().from_host()`.
- Remote container: temp file → rclone → remote temp file → typed Docker copy.
- Local/remote temporary files automatically cleanup hote hain.
- Old in-memory TAR upload implementation remove kar diya.
- Original uploaded filename container ke andar preserve hota hai.

- `cargo check -p rustploy --all-targets` passed

- `git diff --check` passed

    use std::{io::Write, path::Path};
    
    use crate::{
        repository::ServerRepository,
        utils::{
            exec::{CommandExecutor, LocalExecutor, RemoteExecutor, SshAuth, SshHostKey},
            rclone::{builder::RcloneBuilder, command::RcloneCommand, target::RcloneTarget},
        },
    };
    
    pub async fn upload_via_rclone(
        servers: &ServerRepository,
        server_id: i64,
        local_path: &Path,
        remote_path: &str,
    ) -> Result<RemoteExecutor, String> {
        let (host, port, username, private_key, public_key) = servers
            .get_direct_ssh_credentials(server_id)
            .await
            .map_err(|error| format!("failed to load remote credentials: {error}"))?
            .ok_or_else(|| "server or SSH key not found".to_owned())?;
        let port = u16::try_from(port).map_err(|_| "invalid SSH port".to_owned())?;
    
        let mut key = tempfile::NamedTempFile::new()
            .map_err(|error| format!("failed to create temporary SSH key: {error}"))?;
        key.write_all(private_key.as_bytes())
            .map_err(|error| format!("failed to write temporary SSH key: {error}"))?;
        key.flush()
            .map_err(|error| format!("failed to flush temporary SSH key: {error}"))?;
        #[cfg(unix)]
        {
            use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;
            std::fs::set_permissions(key.path(), std::fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o600))
                .map_err(|error| format!("failed to protect temporary SSH key: {error}"))?;
        }
    
        RcloneBuilder::new(RcloneCommand::Copyto)
            .source(RcloneTarget::Local {
                path: local_path.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
            })
            .destination(RcloneTarget::Sftp {
                host: host.clone(),
                port: Some(port),
                user: username.clone(),
                pass: None,
                key_file: Some(key.path().to_string_lossy().into_owned()),
                key_use_agent: false,
                path: remote_path.to_owned(),
            })
            .execute(&CommandExecutor::Local(LocalExecutor::new()))
            .await
            .map_err(|error| format!("rclone SFTP upload failed: {error}"))?;
    
        Ok(RemoteExecutor::new(
            host,
            port,
            username,
            SshAuth::key_pair(private_key, public_key),
            SshHostKey::InsecureAcceptAny,
        )
        .with_sudo())
    }

    use std::{collections::HashMap, path::Path};
    
    use axum::extract::Multipart;
    use tokio::io::AsyncWriteExt;
    
    use crate::utils::{
        exec::{CommandExecutor, LocalExecutor},
        os::OsCli,
    };
    
    pub const MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES: u64 = 100 * 1024 * 1024;
    
    #[derive(Debug)]
    pub struct MultipartFile {
        pub filename: String,
        pub fields: HashMap<String, String>,
        pub bytes_written: u64,
    }
    
    pub async fn stream_multipart_file(
        mut multipart: Multipart,
        file_field: &str,
        destination: &Path,
        limit: u64,
    ) -> Result<MultipartFile, String> {
        let mut output = tokio::fs::File::create(destination)
            .await
            .map_err(|error| format!("failed to create temporary upload: {error}"))?;
        let mut filename = None;
        let mut fields = HashMap::new();
        let mut bytes_written = 0u64;
    
        while let Some(mut field) = multipart
            .next_field()
            .await
            .map_err(|error| format!("invalid multipart upload: {error}"))?
        {
            let Some(name) = field.name().map(str::to_owned) else {
                continue;
            };
            if name == file_field {
                if filename.is_some() {
                    return Err("only one file may be uploaded".into());
                }
                filename = Some(sanitize_filename(
                    field.file_name().unwrap_or("upload.bin"),
                )?);
                while let Some(chunk) = field
                    .chunk()
                    .await
                    .map_err(|error| format!("failed to read upload: {error}"))?
                {
                    bytes_written = bytes_written
                        .checked_add(chunk.len() as u64)
                        .ok_or_else(|| "upload size overflow".to_owned())?;
                    if bytes_written > limit {
                        return Err(format!("file exceeds {} MiB limit", limit / 1024 / 1024));
                    }
                    output
                        .write_all(&chunk)
                        .await
                        .map_err(|error| format!("failed to store upload: {error}"))?;
                }
            } else {
                let value = field
                    .text()
                    .await
                    .map_err(|error| format!("invalid multipart field {name}: {error}"))?;
                fields.insert(name, value);
            }
        }
    
        output
            .flush()
            .await
            .map_err(|error| format!("failed to flush upload: {error}"))?;
        let filename = filename.ok_or_else(|| format!("{file_field} is required"))?;

        }

            || filename.len() > 255
            || filename.contains(['\0', '\r', '\n'])
            || filename == "."
            || filename == ".."
        {
            return Err("invalid upload filename".into());
        }

            .sanitize()
            .to(output)

            .overwrite()
            .run()

    use std::{collections::HashMap, path::Path};
    
    use axum::extract::Multipart;
    use tokio::io::AsyncWriteExt;
    
    pub const MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES: u64 = 100 * 1024 * 1024;
    
    #[derive(Debug)]
    pub struct MultipartFile {
        pub filename: String,
        pub fields: HashMap<String, String>,
        pub bytes_written: u64,
    }
    
    pub async fn stream_multipart_file(
        mut multipart: Multipart,
        file_field: &str,
        destination: &Path,
        limit: u64,
    ) -> Result<MultipartFile, String> {
        let mut output = tokio::fs::File::create(destination)
            .await
            .map_err(|error| format!("failed to create temporary upload: {error}"))?;
        let mut filename = None;
        let mut fields = HashMap::new();
        let mut bytes_written = 0u64;
    
        while let Some(mut field) = multipart
            .next_field()
            .await
            .map_err(|error| format!("invalid multipart upload: {error}"))?
        {
            let Some(name) = field.name().map(str::to_owned) else {
                continue;
            };
            if name == file_field {
                if filename.is_some() {
                    return Err("only one file may be uploaded".into());
                }
                filename = Some(sanitize_filename(
                    field.file_name().unwrap_or("upload.bin"),
                )?);
                while let Some(chunk) = field
                    .chunk()
                    .await
                    .map_err(|error| format!("failed to read upload: {error}"))?
                {
                    bytes_written = bytes_written
                        .checked_add(chunk.len() as u64)
                        .ok_or_else(|| "upload size overflow".to_owned())?;
                    if bytes_written > limit {
                        return Err(format!("file exceeds {} MiB limit", limit / 1024 / 1024));
                    }
                    output
                        .write_all(&chunk)
                        .await
                        .map_err(|error| format!("failed to store upload: {error}"))?;
                }
            } else {
                let value = field
                    .text()
                    .await
                    .map_err(|error| format!("invalid multipart field {name}: {error}"))?;
                fields.insert(name, value);
            }
        }
    
        output
            .flush()
            .await
            .map_err(|error| format!("failed to flush upload: {error}"))?;
        let filename = filename.ok_or_else(|| format!("{file_field} is required"))?;
        if bytes_written == 0 {
            return Err("uploaded file is empty".into());
        }
        Ok(MultipartFile {
            filename,
            fields,
            bytes_written,
        })
    }
    
    fn sanitize_filename(value: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
        let filename = value.rsplit(['/', '\\']).next().unwrap_or_default().trim();
        if filename.is_empty()
            || filename.len() > 255
            || filename.contains(['\0', '\r', '\n'])
            || filename == "."
            || filename == ".."
        {
            return Err("invalid upload filename".into());
        }
        Ok(filename.to_owned())
    }

    use std::{io::Write, path::Path};
    
    use crate::{
        repository::ServerRepository,
        utils::{
            exec::{CommandExecutor, LocalExecutor, RemoteExecutor, SshAuth, SshHostKey},
            rclone::{builder::RcloneBuilder, command::RcloneCommand, target::RcloneTarget},
        },
    };
    
    pub async fn upload_via_rclone(
        servers: &ServerRepository,
        server_id: i64,
        local_path: &Path,
        remote_path: &str,
    ) -> Result<RemoteExecutor, String> {
        let (host, port, username, private_key, public_key) = servers
            .get_direct_ssh_credentials(server_id)
            .await
            .map_err(|error| format!("failed to load remote credentials: {error}"))?
            .ok_or_else(|| "server or SSH key not found".to_owned())?;
        let port = u16::try_from(port).map_err(|_| "invalid SSH port".to_owned())?;
    
        let mut key = tempfile::NamedTempFile::new()
            .map_err(|error| format!("failed to create temporary SSH key: {error}"))?;
        key.write_all(private_key.as_bytes())
            .map_err(|error| format!("failed to write temporary SSH key: {error}"))?;
        key.flush()
            .map_err(|error| format!("failed to flush temporary SSH key: {error}"))?;
        #[cfg(unix)]
        {
            use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;
            std::fs::set_permissions(key.path(), std::fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o600))
                .map_err(|error| format!("failed to protect temporary SSH key: {error}"))?;
        }
    
        RcloneBuilder::new(RcloneCommand::Copyto)
            .source(RcloneTarget::Local {
                path: local_path.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
            })
            .destination(RcloneTarget::Sftp {
                host: host.clone(),
                port: Some(port),
                user: username.clone(),
                pass: None,
                key_file: Some(key.path().to_string_lossy().into_owned()),
                key_use_agent: false,
                path: remote_path.to_owned(),
            })
            .execute(&CommandExecutor::Local(LocalExecutor::new()))
            .await
            .map_err(|error| format!("rclone SFTP upload failed: {error}"))?;
    
        Ok(RemoteExecutor::new(
            host,
            port,
            username,
            SshAuth::key_pair(private_key, public_key),
            SshHostKey::InsecureAcceptAny,
        )
        .with_sudo())
    }

    import {getApiBaseUrl} from '#/api/client';
    
    import type {PrivateNetworkConfig, UpdatePrivateNetworkInput} from './types';
    
    function authHeaders(json = false): HeadersInit {
    	const sessionRaw = localStorage.getItem('rustploy-auth-session');
    	let token = '';
    	try {
    		token = sessionRaw ? JSON.parse(sessionRaw)?.tokens?.access_token || '' : '';
    	} catch {
    		// Invalid sessions are handled by the global authentication flow.
    	}
    	return {
    		Accept: 'application/json',
    		...(json ? {'Content-Type': 'application/json'} : {}),
    		...(token ? {Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`} : {}),
    	};
    }
    
    async function request<T>(path: string, init?: RequestInit): Promise<T> {
    	const response = await fetch(`${getApiBaseUrl()}${path}`, init);
    	if (!response.ok) {
    		const message = await response.text();
    		throw new Error(message || `Request failed (${response.status})`);
    	}
    	if (response.status === 204) return undefined as T;
    	return response.json() as Promise<T>;
    }
    
    const pathFor = (serverId: number, action = '') => `/servers/${serverId}/private-network${action}`;
    
    export const privateNetworkApi = {
    	get: (serverId: number) =>
    		request<PrivateNetworkConfig | null>(pathFor(serverId), {headers: authHeaders()}),
    	update: (serverId: number, input: UpdatePrivateNetworkInput) =>
    		request<PrivateNetworkConfig>(pathFor(serverId), {
    			method: 'PUT',
    			headers: authHeaders(true),
    			body: JSON.stringify(input),
    		}),
    	setup: (serverId: number) =>
    		request<PrivateNetworkConfig>(pathFor(serverId, '/setup'), {method: 'POST', headers: authHeaders()}),
    	health: (serverId: number) =>
    		request<{status: string; error: string | null}>(pathFor(serverId, '/health'), {headers: authHeaders()}),
    	repair: (serverId: number) =>
    		request<PrivateNetworkConfig>(pathFor(serverId, '/repair'), {method: 'POST', headers: authHeaders()}),
    	rotateKeys: (serverId: number) =>
    		request<PrivateNetworkConfig>(pathFor(serverId, '/rotate-keys'), {method: 'POST', headers: authHeaders()}),
    	teardown: (serverId: number) =>
    		request<void>(pathFor(serverId, '/teardown'), {method: 'POST', headers: authHeaders()}),
    };

    interface PrivateNetworkModalProps {

    function remoteHostFromTunnel(cidr: string): string | null {
    	const [address, prefix] = cidr.trim().split('/');
    	const octets = address?.split('.').map(Number);
    	if (prefix !== '24' || octets?.length !== 4 || octets.some(value => !Number.isInteger(value) || value < 0 || value > 255)) return null;
    	return `${octets[0]}.${octets[1]}.${octets[2]}.2`;
    }
    
    export function PrivateNetworkModal({open, server, onClose}: PrivateNetworkModalProps) {
    	const [mode, setMode] = useState<ConnectionMode>('DIRECT_SSH');
    	const [provider, setProvider] = useState<PrivateNetworkProvider>('TAILSCALE');
    	const [privateHost, setPrivateHost] = useState('');
    	const [tunnelAddress, setTunnelAddress] = useState('10.77.1.0/24');
    	const [endpoint, setEndpoint] = useState('');

    	const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false);
    	const [action, setAction] = useState('');
    
    	const managedHost = useMemo(() => remoteHostFromTunnel(tunnelAddress), [tunnelAddress]);
    
    	useEffect(() => {
    		if (!open || !server) return;

  Bhai, Root Cause mil gaya aur Fix 100% implement kar diya gaya hai! ⚡
  ──────
  ### 🔍 Root Cause Explanation:

  Galti 2 jagaha par ho rahi thi:

  1. IdentitiesOnly=no:
      • Pehle SSH key authentication me IdentitiesOnly=no set tha. Iska matlab SSH pehle isolated key-agent check karta tha, aur agar wo galat ya invalid tha, toh wo Silent Mode me apne host machine ke default
      keys (~/.ssh/id_rsa / system SSH agent) ko trial me le leta tha. Agar aapke computer me koi SSH key setup thi jo us remote server par match kar gayi, toh SSH connection 200 OK return kar deta tha!
  2. SSH Connection Socket Multiplexing (ControlMaster):
      • Test connection pehle se persistent Open SSH Socket /tmp/rustploy-ssh-* ko reuse kar raha tha. Is wajah se purani valid session ki socket file dwara request bypass ho rahi thi aur Naya Invalid Key test
      hi nahi ho raha tha!

  ──────
  ### 🛠️ Fix Implemented:

  1. IdentitiesOnly=yes Enforced (builder.rs):
      • Ab SSH STRICTLY ONLY wahi key check karega jo aapne Rustploy GUI/API me choose ki hai. Host machine ki fallback keys ko complete block kar diya gaya hai.
  2. Multiplexing Disabled During Test Connection (exec_remote.rs & controller.rs):
      • test-direct-connection par .with_multiplexing(false) lagaya gaya hai. Ab har test connection fresh and direct SSH handshake perform karega with ZERO socket reuse!


  Background me cargo check --workspace verification run ho raha hai! 🚀

  ──────
  ### 📜 Git History Trace & Root Cause:

  1. Pehle (Before pure-Rust ssh-agent commit e453bbe):
      • Pehle SSH key ko temp file -i /tmp/id_key bana kar pass kiya jata tha aur IdentitiesOnly=yes set tha. Tab tak bilkul sahi kaam kar raha tha aur wrong key reject ho rahi thi.
  2. Refactoring Commit e453bbe ("pure-Rust SSH keypair & agent management"):
      • Code refactor karke RAM-based isolated ssh-agent support add kiya gaya (taki disk par private key write na ho).
      • Lekin in-memory agent session set karte waqt SshBuilder me line 446 par:

  • IdentitiesOnly ko wapas yes set kar diya gaya hai (builder.rs).

      trial me le leta tha!
      • Is wajah se aapka local machine SSH key remote server par authenticated hone ki wajah se test connection 200 OK pass kar deta tha!

  • Test connection me with_multiplexing(false) enforce kar diya gaya hai (controller.rs).

- `IdentitiesOnly=no`
- Only isolated `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`
- `PreferredAuthentications=publickey`

## User

why this process is very slow jabki ram me hai chize

## Assistant

Slow isliye hai kyunki private key RAM me hone ka matlab poora SSH process fast hona nahi hota.

Current flow har connection par:

1. Naya `ssh-agent` process start hota hai.
2. Private key ko `ssh-add` ke stdin se parse/load kiya jata hai.
3. Agent socket create hota hai.
4. Fresh SSH TCP connection hota hai.
5. Host-key verification hoti hai.
6. Public-key challenge/response hota hai.
7. Test connection me multiplexing intentionally disabled hai, isliye existing SSH session reuse nahi hota.
8. Remote command `true` execute karke response wait hota hai.

Network handshake usually main delay hai; RAM/disk write nahi. `mlock` bhi negligible time leta hai.

Security ke liye test connection deliberately fresh rakha hai, isliye ~500 ms–2 sec normal hai. Repeated deployment commands me multiplexing enabled reh sakta hai, so woh faster honge.

Agar test UX faster chahiye, safe optimization:

- Agent ko per-request ke bajay short-lived server/session scope me reuse karna.
- SSH connection pool reuse karna.
- Test timeout 8–15 sec rakhna.
- Health check ke liye existing connection reuse karna.
- Wrong-key validation ke liye sirf explicit “Verify credentials” action par fresh handshake karna.

Important: agent RAM me hone ke bawajood remote server tak encrypted network round-trip unavoidable hai.

- Config apply/setup stage pass hua ✅

Lekin WireGuard topology me remote server ke peer config ka endpoint Rustploy panel ka public IP/domain hona chahiye, remote server ka nahi.

Correct flow:

```text
Panel public IP:51820  ← endpoint
Remote server private tunnel IP: 10.77.14.2
Panel tunnel IP: 10.77.14.1
```

UI me `Endpoint` field me panel ka externally reachable public IP/domain dalo:

```text
<PANEL_PUBLIC_IP>:51820
```

- Panel par UDP `51820` open ho
- Panel WireGuard interface allowed ho
- Remote server outbound UDP allowed ho
- Remote server ka SSH `10.77.14.2:22` par listen/reachable ho

Rustploy normal user ke under run ho raha hai. Managed WireGuard ko local panel par ye privileged operations chahiye:

- WireGuard interface create/delete

Poora Rustploy `sudo` se chalana correct solution nahi hai. Proper solution narrowly scoped privileged helper hai:

```text
Rustploy normal user

rustploy-network-helper (root)
        ↓
wg / wg-quick / ip / protected config writes
```

Abhi remote side ko baar-baar debug karna useful nahi; remote setup key stage pass kar raha hai. Local privileged helper ke bina tunnel complete nahi ho sakta.

Next correct implementation:

2. Strictly allowed WireGuard operations only.

4. Explicit re-setup background repair ko supersede kare.
5. Raw generated private keys ko logs me print hone se rokna.

Ye UI issue nahi, local privilege architecture issue hai.

    import type {ConnectionMode} from './types';
    
    interface PrivateNetworkForm {
    	mode: ConnectionMode;
    	managedHost: string | null;
    	endpoint: string;
    	listenPort: string;
    	privateHost: string;
    }
    
    export function validatePrivateNetworkForm(form: PrivateNetworkForm): string | null {
    	if (form.mode === 'MANAGED_WIREGUARD' && !form.managedHost) {
    		return 'Use a valid /24 IPv4 tunnel network, for example 10.77.2.0/24';
    	}
    	if (form.mode === 'MANAGED_WIREGUARD' && !form.endpoint.trim()) {
    		return 'Panel public endpoint is required, for example panel.example.com:51820';
    	}
    	if (form.mode === 'MANAGED_WIREGUARD' && !form.endpoint.trim().includes(':')) {
    		return 'Panel public endpoint must include the WireGuard UDP port';
    	}
    	if (
    		form.mode === 'MANAGED_WIREGUARD' &&
    		Number(form.endpoint.trim().split(':').at(-1)) !== Number(form.listenPort)
    	) {
    		return 'Panel endpoint port must match the WireGuard listen port';
    	}
    	if (form.mode === 'EXTERNAL_PRIVATE_NETWORK' && !form.privateHost.trim()) {
    		return 'Private IP or hostname is required for an existing VPN';
    	}
    	return null;
    }

## Assistant

Haan, project ko modular crates me split karna sahi rahega. Isse compile scope chhota hoga, tests isolated honge, aur app/server/agent ke responsibilities clear rahenge.

Proposed structure:

```text
rustploy/
├── Cargo.toml                 # workspace only
├── crates/
│   ├── app/                   # shared domain/application layer
│   ├── server/                # Rustploy API + orchestration
│   ├── agent/                 # remote monitoring/deployment agent
│   ├── global/                # shared types, errors, config, traits
│   ├── os/                    # typed OS/CLI builders
│   └── test-support/          # fixtures, fake executors, test helpers
├── web/
│   └── rustploy_react/
└── db/
    └── migrations/
```

**1. `global` crate**

Pure shared code only:

- DTOs and API contracts
- Enums
- IDs and typed newtypes
- Error contracts
- Event definitions
- Pagination/filter types
- Configuration primitives
- Serialization helpers
- Shared traits

Rules:

- No database connection
- No Axum
- No Docker shell commands
- No UI logic
- Minimal dependencies

This crate should compile fastest and be usable by every other crate.

```text
global/
├── src/
│   ├── ids/
│   ├── enums/
│   ├── errors/
│   ├── events/
│   ├── contracts/
│   ├── config/
│   └── lib.rs
```

**2. `app` crate**

Application/domain layer:

- Application use-cases
- Deployment orchestration
- Compose orchestration
- Notification workflows
- Backup workflows
- Schedule workflows
- Private-network domain logic
- Repository traits
- Service traits
- Transaction boundaries

`app` database implementation ya HTTP framework par directly depend nahi karega. Repository interfaces yaha define hongi.

```text
app/
├── src/
│   ├── application/
│   ├── compose/
│   ├── deployment/
│   ├── private_network/
│   ├── backup/
│   ├── notification/
│   ├── schedule/
│   ├── server/
│   ├── ports/
│   ├── domains/
│   ├── repositories/
│   ├── services/
│   └── lib.rs
```

Example dependency direction:

```text
app → global
app → os traits/contracts only
```

`app` ko directly `server` ya `agent` par depend nahi karna chahiye.

**3. `server` crate**

Main Rustploy backend:

- Axum/Poem routes
- Authentication middleware
- Permissions
- SQLx repositories
- SQLite/Postgres connection
- Migration startup
- Background managers
- App use-case wiring
- Remote server connection management
- API error mapping
- WebSocket/Socket.IO handling

```text
server/
├── src/
│   ├── api/
│   │   ├── routes/
│   │   ├── handlers/
│   │   ├── dto/
│   │   └── middleware/
│   ├── db/
│   │   ├── connection/
│   │   ├── repositories/
│   │   └── models/
│   ├── runtime/
│   │   ├── bootstrap/
│   │   ├── background/
│   │   └── scheduler/
│   ├── adapters/
│   │   ├── docker/
│   │   ├── ssh/
│   │   ├── traefik/
│   │   └── notifications/
│   ├── composition/
│   └── main.rs
```

Dependency direction:

```text
server → app
server → global
server → os
server → database/framework crates
```

SQL queries sirf `server` ke repository modules me rahengi. `app` raw SQL nahi dekhega.

**4. `agent` crate**

Remote agent ko independent binary/crate rakhenge:

- Host/container metrics
- gRPC server
- Remote command execution
- Agent configuration
- Agent health
- Agent update lifecycle
- Local agent persistence, agar required ho

```text
agent/
├── src/
│   ├── grpc/
│   ├── metrics/
│   ├── containers/
│   ├── host/
│   ├── runtime/
│   ├── config/
│   └── main.rs
```

Dependency direction:

```text
agent → global
agent → os
```

Agent ko `server` par depend nahi karna chahiye. Server-agent communication shared contracts ya generated proto se hoga.

Monitoring ko server crate me duplicate nahi rakhenge. Agent measurements collect karega; server ingestion/orchestration karega.

**5. `os` crate**

Current typed OS builders yahi rahenge:

- SSH builder
- Docker builder
- WireGuard builder
- Rclone builder
- Filesystem builder
- Package manager
- System/network/process helpers
- Local/remote executors

```text
os/
├── src/
│   ├── exec/

│   ├── docker/
│   ├── wireguard/
│   ├── rclone/
│   ├── filesystem/
│   ├── package/
│   ├── network/
│   └── lib.rs
```

`os` ko business logic nahi pata hona chahiye. Ye sirf typed command execution provide karega.

**6. `test-support` crate**

Repeated test setup alag crate me:

- Fake repository
- Fake executor
- Fake SSH server
- Fake Docker client
- SQLite temporary database
- API test application
- Event recorder
- Fixture builders

```text
test-support/
├── src/
│   ├── database.rs
│   ├── repositories.rs
│   ├── executors.rs
│   ├── fixtures.rs
│   └── lib.rs
```

Isse integration tests me har baar full backend bootstrap nahi karna padega.

**Workspace dependencies**

Root `Cargo.toml` sirf workspace manage karega:

```text
global
app
server
agent
os
test-support
```

Dependencies ko workspace-level versions me centralize karenge:

- `tokio`
- `serde`
- `thiserror`
- `sqlx`
- `tracing`
- `async-trait`
- `uuid`
- `chrono`

Har crate sirf required dependencies lega. Example:

```text
global: serde, thiserror
app: global, async-trait
os: tokio, tracing, typed builders
agent: global, os, tonic
server: app, global, os, axum, sqlx
test-support: app, server, tempfile, test dependencies
```

**Build fast karne ke rules**

- `global` ko dependency-light rakhenge.
- `app` me framework dependencies nahi.
- `server` ke heavy dependencies ko baaki crates me leak nahi karenge.
- `sqlx` macros sirf server repository crate me.
- `agent` ko server compile changes se independent rakhenge.
- `cargo check -p agent` server ke bina chalega.
- `cargo test -p app` database/server startup ke bina chalega.
- `cargo test -p os` typed command builders ke liye isolated hoga.
- `cargo test -p server` API/database integration tests ke liye hoga.
- `cargo build -p agent` sirf agent binary rebuild karega.

Useful commands:

```bash
cargo check -p global
cargo check -p app
cargo check -p os
cargo check -p agent
cargo check -p server

cargo test -p app
cargo test -p os
cargo test -p agent
cargo test -p server
```

**Migration strategy**

Big-bang refactor nahi karenge. Order:

1. Workspace crates define karna.
2. `global` me shared enums/contracts move karna.
3. `os` ko independent compile/test crate banana.
4. `app` me service/domain logic move karna.
5. `server` me API/DB/adapters isolate karna.
6. Existing agent ko independent `agent` crate banana.
7. Test-support crate add karna.
8. Old `src/` modules ko gradually remove karna.
9. Dependency cycle check karna.
10. Full workspace build/test run karna.

Final dependency graph:

```text
                 ┌──────────┐
                 │  global  │
                 └────┬─────┘
                      │
          ┌───────────┼───────────┐
          ▼           ▼           ▼
       ┌─────┐     ┌─────┐    ┌────────┐
       │  os │     │ app │    │ agent │
       └──┬──┘     └──┬──┘    └───┬────┘
          │           │           │
          └───────────┴──────┬────┘
                              ▼
                         ┌────────┐
                         │ server │
                         └────────┘
```

Important rule:

```text
global → app/os/agent → server
```

Reverse dependency nahi hogi. `server` ka code `agent` ke andar nahi jayega, aur `app` me SQL/HTTP/shell command nahi likhe jayenge.

- command/query traits
- common error types
- transaction interfaces
- event dispatcher traits
- authorization context
- repository traits
- service contracts

`app-core` kisi feature crate par depend nahi karega.

**Feature crates**

Har feature ko apna complete vertical slice milega:

```text
app-private-network/
├── commands/
│   ├── configure.rs
│   ├── setup.rs
│   ├── repair.rs
│   ├── re_setup.rs
│   ├── teardown.rs
│   └── rotate_keys.rs
├── queries/
│   ├── get.rs
│   ├── health.rs
│   └── status.rs
├── domain/
│   ├── config.rs
│   ├── state.rs
│   ├── validation.rs
│   └── lifecycle.rs
├── ports/
│   ├── repository.rs
│   ├── network_backend.rs
│   └── executor.rs
├── events/
│   └── private_network_events.rs
└── lib.rs
```

Same pattern:

```text
app-deployment/
├── commands/
├── queries/
├── domain/
├── ports/
├── policies/
├── events/
└── lib.rs
```

```text
app-backup/
├── commands/
├── queries/
├── domain/
├── retention/
├── restore/
├── ports/
├── events/
└── lib.rs
```

**Har feature ka fixed pattern**

Har feature me same layers honge:

```text
commands/
queries/
domain/
ports/
policies/
events/
lib.rs
```

Responsibilities:

- `commands/`: state change
- `queries/`: read-only operations
- `domain/`: business rules and validation
- `ports/`: traits/interfaces
- `policies/`: permission, retry, retention, placement rules
- `events/`: domain events
- `lib.rs`: public exports only

Example:

```text
app-private-network
        │
        ├── ConfigurePrivateNetwork
        ├── SetupPrivateNetwork
        ├── RepairPrivateNetwork
        ├── ReSetupPrivateNetwork
        ├── TeardownPrivateNetwork
        └── RotateKeys
```

Har command ka:

- typed input
- validator
- authorization requirement
- repository interaction
- event emission
- typed output

hoga.

**Repository placement**

Repository implementation `server` me rahegi:

```text
app-private-network/
└── ports/repository.rs

server/
└── adapters/database/private_network_repository.rs
```

`app-private-network` sirf trait define karega:

```text
PrivateNetworkRepository
PrivateNetworkHealthRepository
PrivateNetworkOperationRepository
```

SQL sirf `server` adapter me hoga.

**OS/backend placement**

WireGuard implementation `os` me:

```text
os/
└── wireguard/
```

Application-level orchestration `app-private-network` me:

```text
app-private-network/
└── ports/network_backend.rs
```

Server wiring:

```text
server/
└── adapters/private_network/kernel_wireguard.rs
```

Isse app ko `wg`, `sudo`, `ssh`, ya shell commands ka knowledge nahi hoga.

**Cross-feature communication**

Features directly ek-dusre ke internal modules access nahi karenge.

Galat:

```text
app-deployment → app-private-network/src/domain/internal.rs
```

Sahi:

```text
app-deployment → app-core event/port
app-private-network → app-core event/port
```

Example events:

```text
ServerCreated
PrivateNetworkReady
DeploymentStarted
DeploymentFailed
BackupCompleted
NotificationRequested
```

**App facade**

Root `app` crate sirf public use-cases export karega:

```text
app/
└── lib.rs
```

Facade ka kaam:

- feature services register karna
- command handlers expose karna
- event bus connect karna
- dependency graph assemble karna

Business logic `app/lib.rs` me nahi hogi.

**Dependency graph**

```text
app-core
   │
   ├── app-application
   ├── app-compose
   ├── app-deployment
   ├── app-server
   ├── app-private-network
   ├── app-backup
   ├── app-notification
   ├── app-schedule
   ├── app-database
   ├── app-registry
   └── app-certificate
          │
          ▼
         app
          │
          ▼
       server
```

Feature crates ek-dusre par direct depend nahi karenge jab tak genuine shared contract na ho.

**Testing isolation**

```bash
cargo test -p app-core
cargo test -p app-private-network
cargo test -p app-deployment
cargo test -p app-backup
cargo test -p app-notification
cargo test -p app
cargo test -p server
```

Test levels:

```text
domain tests      → no database, no network
command tests     → fake repositories
integration tests → test database
server tests      → real HTTP/API wiring
e2e tests         → browser + running backend
```

**Build optimization**

- `app-private-network` change hone par `app-backup` rebuild nahi hoga.
- `server` ke SQLx macros app feature crates ko slow nahi karenge.
- `global` minimal dependency crate rahega.
- `os` independent compile hoga.
- Agent changes server/app rebuild trigger nahi karenge.
- Feature-specific integration tests parallel chalenge.

Final rule:

```text
app = facade
app-core = shared contracts
app-feature = one bounded context
server = adapters + HTTP + DB
os = typed system operations
agent = independent remote process
```

Is structure me app maintainable, testable aur future me enterprise-scale features ke liye extendable rahega, bina ek huge service file ya ek giant `app` module banaye.

## Important Reality

Abhi current project:

```text
root src = main backend
crates/os = reusable OS library
agent = separate agent
crates/auto = internal macros
crates/sh_macros = shell macros
web = frontend
```

Abhi `crates/app`, `crates/server`, aur `crates/global` actual separate crates ke form me nahi hain. Unhe future me introduce kiya ja sakta hai, lekin current structure ko todkar sudden migration nahi karna chahiye.

Tumhare project ke rules ke hisaab se best next structure:

```text
src/
├── api/
├── core/
├── db/
├── services/
├── utils/
└── websocket/

crates/
├── os/
├── sh_macros/
└── auto/
```

Aur future me:

```text
crates/
├── app/
├── server/
├── global/
├── agent/
├── os/
├── sh_macros/
└── auto/
```

Migration gradual honi chahiye:

1. Shared enums/contracts ko `global` me move karna.
2. Business workflows ko `app` me move karna.
3. API/DB/adapters ko `server` me move karna.
4. Existing `agent` ko independent rakhna.
5. `os` ko independent typed command crate rakhna.
6. Har move ke baad crate-specific tests chalana.

Iska matlab ye nahi ki har chhoti file ka separate crate banega. Crate boundaries bade ownership boundaries ke liye hongi; folders feature ke andar maintainability ke liye honge.

## Folder ka simple meaning

```text
global/
```

Shared types only:

- enums
- IDs
- errors
- events
- contracts

```text

```

OS aur CLI builders:

- SSH
- Docker
- WireGuard
- rclone
- filesystem
- packages
- network

```text
app/
```

Actual business logic:

- deployment
- compose
- backup
- private network
- notifications
- schedules
- databases

```text
server/
```

Main panel runtime:

- HTTP API
- database implementation
- middleware
- background workers
- WebSocket
- adapters

```text
agent/
```

Remote machine ka agent:

- metrics
- Docker stats
- gRPC
- health
- upgrades

```text
test-support/
```

Common testing tools:

- fake repository
- fake executor
- temporary database
- fixtures
- fake agent

```text
infra/
```

Deployment/system files:

- systemd
- NixOS
- Docker
- WireGuard
- Traefik

```text
docs/
```

Architecture aur operational documentation.

```text
scripts/
```

Development/release/migration helper scripts.

## Feature ke andar standard structure

Har bade feature ka pattern same hoga:

```text
feature/
├── commands/
├── queries/
├── domain/
├── validation/
├── lifecycle/
├── policies/
├── ports/
├── events/
└── mod.rs
```

Example:

```text
private_network/
├── commands/
│   ├── setup.rs
│   ├── re_setup.rs
│   ├── repair.rs

├── queries/

└── mod.rs
```

## Dependency direction

```text
global
  ↓
os ───────────────┐
  ↓               │
app ──────────────┤
  ↓               │
server ───────────┘

agent → global + os
web → server API contracts
```

Rules:

```text
global kisi feature ko import nahi karega
os business logic nahi jaanta
app raw SQL nahi likhega
app raw shell command nahi likhega
server business decision nahi lega
agent server ke internal modules import nahi karega
repository sirf database handle karega
```

Ye final target structure hai. Current code ko ek baar me isme move nahi karna chahiye. Pehle existing root `src/services` ko `crates/app` me move karenge, `src/api` aur `src/db` ko `crates/server` me, shared DTO/enums ko `crates/global` me, aur `crates/os`/`agent` already mostly separate hain.

## User

soch kar batoo kay me overthink kar raha hu

## Assistant

Haan, thoda overthink ho raha hai—especially final structure me.

Tumhare project ke size aur current stage ke liye har feature ko separate crate, aur har feature ke andar `commands/queries/domain/policies/ports/events` banana unnecessary complexity create karega.

Practical structure ye rakho:

```text
crates/
├── global/
├── os/
├── app/
├── server/
├── agent/
└── test-support/
```

Bas itne crates enough hain.

`app` ke andar feature folders:

```text
app/src/
├── application/
├── compose/
├── deployment/
├── private_network/
├── backup/
├── notification/
├── schedule/
├── database/
├── registry/
└── lib.rs
```

Feature ke andar bhi initially simple structure:

```text
private_network/
├── service.rs
├── validation.rs
├── lifecycle.rs
├── ports.rs
└── mod.rs
```

Har chhoti cheez ke liye ye mat banao:

```text
commands/
queries/
policies/
events/
ports/
domain/
```

Ye tab banana jab actual complexity aaye. Private Network jaise complex feature me useful hai, lekin simple feature ke liye overkill hai.

Meri recommendation:

```text
global = shared types/contracts
os = typed system commands
app = business workflows
server = API + DB + adapters
agent = remote process
test-support = shared tests
```

Aur app ke andar:

```text
feature/
├── service.rs
├── repository.rs
├── validation.rs
├── lifecycle.rs
└── mod.rs
```

Important point: fast build sirf folders banane se nahi hota. Build fast hota hai:

- heavy dependencies isolate karne se
- SQLx macros server tak limit karne se
- agent ko independent rakhne se
- tests ko crate-specific chalane se
- unnecessary cross-crate dependencies avoid karne se

So final answer: architecture modular rakho, lekin micro-modular nahi. Tumhare liye 5-6 crates + feature folders best balance hain. 30 crates aur har feature ke 8 subfolders abhi overengineering hoga.

## User

tum jo bol rahe ho kya isko karne se fyda hoga

## Assistant

Haan, fayda hoga—but tabhi jab modularity controlled rahe.

Tumhare project me ye 5 crates useful hain:

```text
global
os
app
server
agent
```

### Real benefits

- `agent` change hone par full backend rebuild nahi hoga.
- `os` ke builders independent test honge.
- `server` me API/DB code isolated rahega.
- `app` me business logic clean rahega.
- `global` shared types ka single source of truth hoga.
- Feature-specific tests faster chalenge.
- Circular dependencies avoid hongi.
- Future contributors ko responsibility clear milegi.
- Private Network, Deployment, Backup jaise features ek-dusre me mix nahi honge.

### Current project ke liye best split

```text
global
  shared enums, IDs, contracts

os
  SSH, Docker, WireGuard, rclone, filesystem

app
  deployment, compose, backup, notification, private-network logic

server
  HTTP API, database, repositories, adapters, background runtime

agent
  remote monitoring agent
```

### Kya fayda nahi dega

Agar hum:

- har feature ko separate crate bana dein
- har file ke liye `commands`, `queries`, `events`, `policies` bana dein
- same types multiple crates me duplicate kar dein
- unnecessary trait layers add kar dein
- simple feature ko 15 files me tod dein

to build aur maintenance dono difficult ho jayenge.

### Best approach

Pehle existing code ko carefully move karo:

```text
src/services  → crates/app
src/api       → crates/server
src/db        → crates/server
shared DTOs   → crates/global
crates/os     → existing independent crate
agent         → existing independent crate
```

Phir har feature ko folders se modular rakho. Separate crate tabhi banao jab:

- independent binary ho
- dependency heavy ho
- independently test/release karna ho
- ownership clearly alag ho

Tumhare case me modularization useful hai, bas over-modularization nahi. Fast build, better testing aur maintainability ke liye controlled 5-crate architecture best rahega.

    use super::PrivateNetworkError;
    
    pub fn interface_name(server_id: i64) -> String {
        let encoded = format!("{:x}", server_id.unsigned_abs());
        let suffix = if encoded.len() > 11 { &encoded[encoded.len() - 11..] } else { &encoded };
        format!("rpwg{suffix}")
    }
    
    pub fn tunnel_addresses(cidr: &str) -> Result<(String, String, String), PrivateNetworkError> {
        let network: ipnet::Ipv4Net = cidr
            .parse()
            .map_err(|error| PrivateNetworkError::Operation(format!("invalid IPv4 tunnel network: {error}")))?;
        if network.prefix_len() > 30 {
            return Err(PrivateNetworkError::Operation(
                "WireGuard tunnel network must contain at least two host addresses".into(),
            ));
        }
        let base = u32::from(network.network());
        let panel = std::net::Ipv4Addr::from(base + 1);
        let remote = std::net::Ipv4Addr::from(base + 2);
        Ok((
            format!("{panel}/{}", network.prefix_len()),
            format!("{remote}/{}", network.prefix_len()),
            remote.to_string(),
        ))
    }
    
    pub fn panel_host(cidr: &str) -> Result<String, PrivateNetworkError> {
        tunnel_addresses(cidr).map(|(panel, _, _)| format!("{}/32", panel.split('/').next().unwrap_or_default()))
    }
    
    #[cfg(test)]
    mod tests {
        use super::{interface_name, tunnel_addresses};

            assert_eq!(tunnel_addresses("10.77.8.0/24").unwrap().1, "10.77.8.2/24");
            assert!(interface_name(i64::MAX).len() <= 15);
            assert!(tunnel_addresses("10.77.8.0/31").is_err());
        }
    }

    use super::{addressing::tunnel_addresses, ConnectionMode, PrivateNetworkError, PrivateNetworkInput, PrivateNetworkProvider};
    
    pub fn validate(input: &PrivateNetworkInput) -> Result<(), PrivateNetworkError> {
        if input.connection_mode == ConnectionMode::DirectSsh {
            return Ok(());
        }
        let host = input.private_host.as_deref().filter(|value| {
            !value.trim().is_empty() && !value.chars().any(char::is_whitespace) && value.len() <= 253
        });
        if host.is_none() {
            return Err(error("private_host is required and must not contain whitespace"));
        }
        validate_dns(input.dns_name.as_deref())?;
        validate_routes(&input.routes, input.tunnel_address.as_deref())?;
        match input.connection_mode {
            ConnectionMode::ManagedWireguard => {
                if input.provider != Some(PrivateNetworkProvider::Wireguard) {
                    return Err(error("managed private networks require the WIREGUARD provider"));
                }
                let cidr = input.tunnel_address.as_deref().ok_or_else(|| error("managed WireGuard requires tunnel_address"))?;
                let endpoint = input.endpoint.as_deref().ok_or_else(|| error("managed WireGuard requires endpoint"))?;
                let (_, _, expected_host) = tunnel_addresses(cidr)?;
                if input.private_host.as_deref() != Some(expected_host.as_str()) {
                    return Err(error(format!("private_host must be {expected_host} for tunnel {cidr}")));
                }
                let port = endpoint.rsplit_once(':').and_then(|(_, port)| port.parse::<u16>().ok());
                if port.is_none() || port != input.listen_port {
                    return Err(error("endpoint port must match listen_port"));
                }
            }
            ConnectionMode::ExternalPrivateNetwork if input.provider == Some(PrivateNetworkProvider::Wireguard) => {
                return Err(error("use MANAGED_WIREGUARD for the WireGuard provider"));
            }
            ConnectionMode::ExternalPrivateNetwork | ConnectionMode::DirectSsh => {}
        }
        Ok(())
    }
    
    fn validate_dns(value: Option<&str>) -> Result<(), PrivateNetworkError> {
        let Some(value) = value else { return Ok(()) };
        if value.len() > 253 || !value.to_ascii_lowercase().ends_with(".rustploy.internal") {
            return Err(error("private DNS name must end with .rustploy.internal"));
        }
        Ok(())
    }
    
    fn validate_routes(routes: &[String], tunnel: Option<&str>) -> Result<(), PrivateNetworkError> {
        let tunnel = tunnel.map(|value| value.parse::<ipnet::IpNet>()).transpose().map_err(|_| error("invalid tunnel route"))?;
        let mut parsed = std::collections::BTreeSet::new();
        for route in routes {
            let route = route.parse::<ipnet::IpNet>().map_err(|_| error("invalid private route"))?;
            if route.prefix_len() == 0 || Some(route) == tunnel || !parsed.insert(route) {
                return Err(error("invalid or duplicate private route"));
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }
    
    fn error(message: impl Into<String>) -> PrivateNetworkError {
        PrivateNetworkError::Operation(message.into())
    }
    
    #[cfg(test)]
    mod tests {
        use super::*;
    
        fn managed() -> PrivateNetworkInput {
            PrivateNetworkInput {
                connection_mode: ConnectionMode::ManagedWireguard,
                provider: Some(PrivateNetworkProvider::Wireguard),
                private_host: Some("10.77.2.2".into()),
                tunnel_address: Some("10.77.2.0/24".into()),
                endpoint: Some("panel.example.com:51820".into()),
                listen_port: Some(51820),
                dns_name: None,
                routes: vec![],
            }
        }
    
        #[test]
        fn validates_managed_configuration() { assert!(validate(&managed()).is_ok()); }
    
        #[test]
        fn rejects_endpoint_mismatch() {
            let mut input = managed();
            input.endpoint = Some("panel.example.com:51821".into());
            assert!(validate(&input).is_err());
        }
    }

    pub(super) fn validate(input: &UpdatePrivateNetworkDto) -> sqlx::Result<()> {

        };

            PrivateNetworkProviderDto::Zerotier => rustploy_app::private_network::PrivateNetworkProvider::Zerotier,
            PrivateNetworkProviderDto::Netbird => rustploy_app::private_network::PrivateNetworkProvider::Netbird,
            PrivateNetworkProviderDto::Custom => rustploy_app::private_network::PrivateNetworkProvider::Custom,
        });
        rustploy_app::private_network::validate(&rustploy_app::private_network::PrivateNetworkInput {

            tunnel_address: input.tunnel_address.clone(),
            endpoint: input.endpoint.clone(),
            listen_port: input.listen_port,
            dns_name: input.dns_name.clone(),
            routes: input.routes.clone(),
        })

    }

## Assistant

Short answer: conceptually haan, lekin implementation same nahi hai.

Tumhare Rustploy mein AI provider ka structure already reasonably separated hai:

- `src/utils/ai/provider.rs` — provider detection/config
- `src/utils/ai/client.rs` — HTTP/API communication
- `src/services/ai/service.rs` — business logic, DB, deployment orchestration
- `src/services/ai/types.rs` — request/response/domain types
- `src/services/ai/validation.rs` — validation
- `src/services/ai/prompts.rs` — prompts
- `src/api/handlers/ai.rs` — HTTP layer

Dokploy mein bhi similar separation hai:

- `packages/server/src/utils/ai/select-ai-provider.ts` — provider selection
- `packages/server/src/services/ai.ts` — AI business logic
- `apps/dokploy/server/api/routers/ai.ts` — API/router layer
- UI mein provider configuration alag components mein hai

Main difference:

- Dokploy provider SDKs use karta hai: OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenAI-compatible.
- Tumhara implementation raw `reqwest` HTTP client se provider-specific payload/response parse karta hai.
- Tumhare `AiService` mein provider handling ke saath deployment/compose/domain operations bhi tightly coupled hain.
- Dokploy ka provider selection ek dedicated factory-style function mein centralized hai.

    use serde::Deserialize;
    
    use super::types::{GitProviderKind, PullRequestEvent};
    
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct RepositoryOwner {
        login: Option<String>,
        username: Option<String>,
        nickname: Option<String>,
    }
    
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct Repository {
        name: String,
        owner: RepositoryOwner,
    }
    
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct GithubRepo {
        name: String,
        owner: RepositoryOwner,
    }
    
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct GithubRef {
        #[serde(rename = "ref")]
        branch: String,
        sha: Option<String>,
        repo: Option<GithubRepo>,
    }
    
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct GithubPullRequest {
        head: GithubRef,
        base: GithubRef,
        user: RepositoryOwner,
    }
    
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct GithubPayload {
        action: Option<String>,
        number: i64,
        repository: Repository,
        pull_request: GithubPullRequest,
    }
    
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct GitlabProject {
        path: String,
        path_with_namespace: String,
    }
    
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct GitlabUser {
        username: Option<String>,
    }
    
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct GitlabCommit {
        id: String,
    }
    
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct GitlabAttributes {
        iid: i64,
        action: Option<String>,
        state: Option<String>,
        source_branch: String,
        target_branch: String,
        last_commit: Option<GitlabCommit>,
    }
    
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct GitlabPayload {
        project: GitlabProject,
        source: Option<GitlabProject>,
        user: Option<GitlabUser>,
        object_attributes: GitlabAttributes,
    }
    
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct BitbucketBranch {
        name: String,
    }
    
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct BitbucketCommit {
        hash: String,
    }
    
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct BitbucketRepo {
        name: String,
        full_name: Option<String>,
    }
    
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct BitbucketSide {
        branch: BitbucketBranch,
        commit: Option<BitbucketCommit>,
        repository: Option<BitbucketRepo>,
    }
    
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct BitbucketPullRequest {
        id: i64,
        source: BitbucketSide,
        destination: BitbucketSide,
        author: RepositoryOwner,
    }
    
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct BitbucketPayload {
        repository: Repository,
        pullrequest: BitbucketPullRequest,
    }
    
    pub(super) fn parse(
        provider: GitProviderKind,
        event_name: &str,
        body: &[u8],
    ) -> Result<PullRequestEvent, String> {
        match provider {
            GitProviderKind::Github | GitProviderKind::Gitea => github_like(provider, body),
            GitProviderKind::Gitlab => gitlab(body),
            GitProviderKind::Bitbucket => bitbucket(event_name, body),
        }
    }
    
    fn github_like(provider: GitProviderKind, body: &[u8]) -> Result<PullRequestEvent, String> {
        let payload: GithubPayload = decode(body)?;
        Ok(PullRequestEvent {
            provider,
            owner: owner_name(&payload.repository.owner).ok_or("repository owner is missing")?,
            repository: payload.repository.name,
            number: payload.number.to_string(),
            action: payload.action.unwrap_or_else(|| "updated".into()),
            source_branch: payload.pull_request.head.branch,
            source_owner: payload
                .pull_request
                .head
                .repo
                .as_ref()
                .and_then(|repo| owner_name(&repo.owner)),
            source_repository: payload.pull_request.head.repo.map(|repo| repo.name),
            target_branch: payload.pull_request.base.branch,
            commit: payload.pull_request.head.sha,
            author: owner_name(&payload.pull_request.user),
        })
    }
    
    fn gitlab(body: &[u8]) -> Result<PullRequestEvent, String> {
        let payload: GitlabPayload = decode(body)?;
        let owner = namespace(&payload.project.path_with_namespace)
            .ok_or("project namespace is missing")?;
        Ok(PullRequestEvent {
            provider: GitProviderKind::Gitlab,
            owner,
            repository: payload.project.path,
            number: payload.object_attributes.iid.to_string(),
            action: payload
                .object_attributes
                .action
                .or(payload.object_attributes.state)
                .unwrap_or_else(|| "update".into()),
            source_branch: payload.object_attributes.source_branch,
            source_owner: payload
                .source
                .as_ref()
                .and_then(|source| namespace(&source.path_with_namespace)),
            source_repository: payload.source.map(|source| source.path),
            target_branch: payload.object_attributes.target_branch,
            commit: payload.object_attributes.last_commit.map(|commit| commit.id),
            author: payload.user.and_then(|user| user.username),
        })
    }
    
    fn bitbucket(event_name: &str, body: &[u8]) -> Result<PullRequestEvent, String> {
        let payload: BitbucketPayload = decode(body)?;
        let pull = payload.pullrequest;
        Ok(PullRequestEvent {
            provider: GitProviderKind::Bitbucket,
            owner: owner_name(&payload.repository.owner).ok_or("repository owner is missing")?,
            repository: payload.repository.name,
            number: pull.id.to_string(),
            action: event_name
                .strip_prefix("pullrequest:")
                .unwrap_or("updated")
                .to_owned(),
            source_branch: pull.source.branch.name,
            source_owner: pull
                .source
                .repository
                .as_ref()
                .and_then(|repo| repo.full_name.as_deref())
                .and_then(namespace),
            source_repository: pull.source.repository.map(|repo| repo.name),
            target_branch: pull.destination.branch.name,
            commit: pull.source.commit.map(|commit| commit.hash),
            author: owner_name(&pull.author),
        })
    }
    
    fn decode<T: for<'de> Deserialize<'de>>(body: &[u8]) -> Result<T, String> {
        serde_json::from_slice(body)
            .map_err(|error| format!("invalid pull request payload: {error}"))
    }
    
    fn owner_name(owner: &RepositoryOwner) -> Option<String> {
        owner
            .login
            .clone()
            .or_else(|| owner.username.clone())
            .or_else(|| owner.nickname.clone())
    }
    
    fn namespace(name: &str) -> Option<String> {
        name.rsplit_once('/').map(|(owner, _)| owner.to_owned())
    }

## Assistant

Tumhara deployment queue Redis/RabbitMQ nahi hai. SQLite-backed durable queue hai, aur `Notify + Semaphore` dispatcher ko wake/concurrency control dete hain.

Flow:

```text
Deploy request
    ↓
deployments table me status = QUEUED
    ↓
BuilderQueue.notify()
    ↓
Dispatcher SQLite se QUEUED rows query karta hai
    ↓
Server-wise semaphore slot leta hai
    ↓
Atomic UPDATE ... RETURNING se job claim
    ↓
status = RUNNING
    ↓
App / Compose / Database builder execute
    ↓
DONE / ERROR / CANCELLED
```

Queue ka actual source of truth `deployments` table hai. Memory me jobs store nahi hote, isliye panel restart ke baad records lose nahi hote.

Queue insert

Application deployment roughly is query se enqueue hota hai:

```sql
INSERT INTO deployments (
    title,
```

```rust
queue.notify();
```

Dispatcher ko batata hai ki new work available hai.

Worker jobs kaise query karta hai

```sql
SELECT id, server_id
FROM deployments

```

Matlab primarily FIFO hai:

1. Purana `created_at`
2. Same timestamp ho to smaller `id`
