## User

abe tu kar kya raha hai me bola builder and creates ka queue builder queue ko creates ka queue me covert kardo taki easily samaj aye uske pass dekhlo kya kya hai notify bhi hai trigger bhi hai to samaj sakte ho background bhi hai plan do kase karo

## Assistant

Haan bhai, ab samjha. Tum sirf `WorkerPool` reuse nahi bol rahe. Tum chahte ho poora `BuilderQueue` generic `crates/queue` ke upar convert ho, taaki deployment queue bhi same builder API, lifecycle hooks, notify, retry aur background system use kare.

Mera previous change incomplete direction tha. Proper plan ye hoga:

## Target architecture

```text
crates/queue
├── generic Queue<J, N>
├── QueueBuilder
├── TaskJob
├── QueueHandler
├── background callbacks
├── lifecycle/custom notifications
├── retry
├── cancellation
├── keyed concurrency
└── persistent-source integration

Rustploy
└── DeploymentJob + DeploymentQueueHandler
    ├── DB claim/finalization
    ├── Application/Compose/Database dispatch
    ├── deployment logs
    ├── cache invalidation
    ├── stale recovery
    └── notifications
```

## 1. Generic queue mein missing capabilities add karunga

Builder deployment queue ke liye `crates/queue` mein ye additions required hain:

### Job identity and concurrency key

```rust
pub trait TaskJob {
    type Output;
    type Error;
    type Key: Eq + Hash + Clone + Send + Sync;

    fn id(&self) -> String;
    fn concurrency_key(&self) -> Self::Key;
    async fn execute(...);
}
```

Deployment ke liye:

```rust
type Key = Option<i64>; // server_id
```

Isse har server par separate concurrency limit chalegi:

```text
Server 1 → max 1 deployment
Server 2 → max 1 deployment
Server 3 → max 1 deployment
```

Lekin different servers parallel execute kar sakenge.

## 2. QueueBuilder mein keyed concurrency

API kuch aisi hogi:

```rust
QueueBuilder::<DeploymentJob, DeploymentSignal>::new()
    .capacity(100)
    .workers(16)
    .per_key_workers(1)
    .retry(RetryConfig::none())
    .handler(DeploymentQueueHandler::new(...))
    .background(recovery_task)
    .background(database_dispatcher)
    .on_notify(notification_listener)
    .build()
```

- `workers(16)` global safety limit
- `per_key_workers(1)` per-server deployment limit
- environment config se values inject hongi

## 3. Persistent source support

Generic queue in-memory channel own karega, lekin deployment source of truth SQLite hi rahega.

Background dispatcher:

```text
Notify/timer
  → DB se QUEUED deployments load
  → server capacity check
  → atomic DB claim
  → DeploymentJob construct
  → generic Queue.push(job)
```

Iske liye generic crate mein repository-specific SQL nahi jayega. Queue ko generic producer callback milega:

```rust
.background(|context, shutdown| async move {
    loop {
        context.wait_for_trigger().await;
        let jobs = deployment_source.claim_available().await?;
        for job in jobs {
            context.enqueue(job).await?;
        }
    }
})
```

## 4. DeploymentJob banega

Current loose arguments:

```rust
process(
    deployment_id,
    application_id,
    compose_id,
    database_id,
    database_kind,
    operation,
)
```

ko typed job mein convert karunga:

```rust
enum DeploymentTarget {
    Application { id: i64 },
    Compose { id: i64 },
    Database { id: i64, kind: DatabaseKind },
}

struct DeploymentJob {
    deployment_id: i64,
    server_id: Option<i64>,
    target: DeploymentTarget,
    operation: DeploymentOperation,
}
```

Isse invalid state impossible hogi:

```text
application_id + compose_id simultaneously
database_id without database_kind
all target IDs missing
```

Ab runtime tuple validation nahi karni padegi.

## 5. Current `BuilderQueue::process()` TaskJob mein jayega

```rust
impl TaskJob for DeploymentJob {
    type Output = DeploymentOutcome;
    type Error = BuilderError;
    type Key = Option<i64>;

    fn concurrency_key(&self) -> Self::Key {
        self.server_id
    }

    async fn execute(
        self,
        context: JobContext,
    ) -> Result<DeploymentOutcome, BuilderError> {
        // application / compose / database operation
    }
}
```

## 6. Current finalization QueueHandler mein jayegi

`BuilderQueue::process()` abhi execution aur finalization dono karta hai. Inko separate karunga:

```rust
struct DeploymentQueueHandler {
    deployments: DeploymentRepository,
    state: ApplicationState,
    cache: AppStateCache,
    notifications: NotificationService,
}
```

Hooks:

```rust
on_start()
  → deployment log
  → RUNNING event

on_success()
  → atomic DB finalize DONE
  → resource status RUNNING/STOPPED
  → cache invalidation
  → state cleanup
  → notification

on_failure()
  → DB finalize ERROR/CANCELLED
  → cache invalidation
  → state cleanup
  → notification

on_retry()
  → deployment log
  → retry event
```

## 7. Custom notification signals

Generic lifecycle notifications already hain. Deployment-specific signals add honge:

```rust
enum DeploymentSignal {
    Queued { deployment_id: i64 },
    Claimed { deployment_id: i64 },
    LogAvailable { deployment_id: i64 },
    Finished {
        deployment_id: i64,
        status: DeploymentStatus,
    },
    ReconciliationCompleted,
}
```

Queue ke listeners:

```rust
.listen(|context, signal| async move {
    // WebSocket/SSE notification
})
```

Lifecycle aur domain notifications separate rahengi:

```rust
NotifySignal::Lifecycle(...)
NotifySignal::Custom(DeploymentSignal::Finished { ... })
```

## 8. Background tasks generic queue mein configure honge

Current BuilderQueue ke:

- dispatch loop
- stale deployment recovery
- stale remote PID cleanup
- 30-minute reconciliation
- remote cleanup retries

sab queue builder ke `.background(...)` callbacks banenge:

```rust
QueueBuilder::new()
    .background(deployment_dispatcher)
    .background(startup_recovery)
    .background(remote_cleanup_retry)
    .background(periodic_reconciler)
```

Isse `BuilderQueue::start()` ke andar manual `tokio::spawn` jungle nahi rahega.

## 9. Cancellation properly generic hogi

Generic queue mein per-job cancellation registry add karunga:

```rust
queue.cancel(deployment_id)
```

Behavior:

```text
DB QUEUED:
  → DB status CANCELLED
  → in-memory enqueue skip/cancel

RUNNING:
  → CancellationToken cancel
  → RemoteExecutor remote PID cleanup
  → DB status CANCELLED
```

Current `ApplicationState` live cancellation integration ko `JobContext` ke cancellation token se connect karunga.

## 10. Final Rustploy wrapper

Purana large `BuilderQueue` shrink hokar deployment facade banega:

```rust
pub struct DeploymentQueue {
    queue: Queue<DeploymentJob, DeploymentSignal>,
    source: DeploymentSource,
}
```

Public methods:

```rust
queue_application(...)
queue_compose(...)
queue_database(...)
cancel(deployment_id)
cancel_application(application_id)
cancel_compose(compose_id)
cancel_database(database_id)
notify()
stats()
```

Naam bhi `BuilderQueue` ke bajay `DeploymentQueue` better hoga, kyunki ye builds ke saath start/stop/redeploy/database operations bhi handle karta hai.

## Migration order

1. Generic queue mein `JobContext`, per-job cancellation aur keyed concurrency.
2. Generic background context mein `enqueue()`/`trigger()` support.
3. `DeploymentTarget` and `DeploymentJob`.
4. `DeploymentQueueHandler`.
5. DB dispatcher and atomic claim adapter.
6. Recovery/reconciler callbacks migrate.
7. Application/Compose/Database services ko new `DeploymentQueue` par shift.
8. Old `BuilderQueue::process`, manual worker pools aur dispatch loop remove.
9. Queue unit tests:
   - FIFO
   - global concurrency
   - per-server concurrency
   - cancellation
   - retries
   - notifications
10. Deployment integration tests:
   - DB atomic claim
   - restart recovery
   - application/compose/database dispatch
   - panic/failure finalization
   - remote stale PID cleanup

Final flow:

```text
Deployment DB
     ↓ background source/claim
Queue<DeploymentJob, DeploymentSignal>
     ↓ keyed worker by server_id
DeploymentJob::execute()
     ↓
Application / Compose / Database builder
     ↓
DeploymentQueueHandler
     ├─ final DB status
     ├─ logs
     ├─ cache/state cleanup
     └─ notifications
```

Ye conversion tumhare generic queue ke actual design—builder, handler, notify, retry, background—sabko properly use karega. `BuilderQueue` ka parallel custom queue engine remove ho jayega.

## User

agar mere queue me kuch missing hai to woo bhi batoo genreics jise aur optimize ho jaye

## Assistant

Haan bhai, generic queue foundation achha hai, lekin production-grade reusable queue banane ke liye kuch important capabilities missing ya incomplete hain.

## Critical issues

1. Per-job cancellation missing

Abhi queue ke paas sirf global `shutdown_token` hai:

```rust
let cancel_token = shutdown_worker.child_token();
```

Ye individual job token nahi hai. Kisi single deployment ko cancel karne ka clean API nahi:

```rust
queue.cancel(job_id)
```

Required:

```rust
DashMap<JobId, CancellationToken>
```

API:

```rust
queue.cancel(&job_id)
queue.cancel_by_key(&server_id)
```

2. Queued job cancellation

Channel ke andar placed job physically remove nahi ho sakti. Cancellation registry check karni hogi:

```text
push job
  → job marked queued
  → user cancels
  → worker receives job
  → token already cancelled
  → execution skip
```

3. Keyed concurrency

Abhi sirf global workers hain:

```rust
Semaphore::new(config.workers)
```

Deployment use-case ke liye required:

```rust
global_workers = 16
per_server_workers = 1
```

Generic type:

```rust
trait TaskJob {
    type Key: Eq + Hash;
    fn concurrency_key(&self) -> Option<Self::Key>;
}
```

4. Queue state/statistics

Current queue states track nahi karti:

```text
queued
running
completed
failed
cancelled
retrying
```

Required APIs:

```rust
queue.state(job_id)
queue.stats()
queue.active_jobs()
queue.queued_jobs()
```

5. Duplicate job protection

Same application deployment multiple times enqueue ho sakta hai.

Required:

```rust
fn deduplication_key(&self) -> Option<String>;
```

Policy:

```rust
DuplicatePolicy::Reject
DuplicatePolicy::Replace
DuplicatePolicy::Allow
```

6. Job timeout

`QueueError::Timeout` defined hai, lekin queue timeout apply nahi karti.

Required:

```rust
QueueBuilder::timeout(Duration::from_secs(1800))
```

Then:

```rust
tokio::time::timeout(timeout, job.execute(token))
```

7. Panic handling

Job future panic kare to permit release hoga, lekin:

- `on_failure` execute nahi hoga
- lifecycle failure signal nahi jayega
- job state missing rahega

Required:

```rust
AssertUnwindSafe(job.execute(...))
    .catch_unwind()
```

Panic → `QueueError::Panic`.

8. Retry cancellation

Backoff currently:

```rust
tokio::time::sleep(backoff).await;
```

Cancellation/shutdown during retry sleep immediately stop nahi hota.

Required:

```rust
tokio::select! {
    _ = token.cancelled() => break,
    _ = sleep(backoff) => {}
}
```

9. Retry strategy

Fixed backoff only hai.

Useful generic policies:

```rust
RetryStrategy::Fixed(Duration)
RetryStrategy::Exponential {
    initial,
    multiplier,
    max,
}
RetryStrategy::Custom(...)
```

Optional jitter bhi useful hai to prevent retry storms.

10. Graceful shutdown

Current:

```rust
shutdown_token.cancel()
```

Immediately worker loop aur job child tokens cancel kar deta hai. Drain/wait option nahi.

Required:

```rust
queue.shutdown(ShutdownMode::Drain).await
queue.shutdown(ShutdownMode::Cancel).await
queue.shutdown(ShutdownMode::Timeout(duration)).await
```

## Architecture improvements

11. Background callback ko context nahi milta

Current:

```rust
.background(|shutdown_token| async {})
```

Background producer jobs enqueue nahi kar sakta unless queue externally capture kare, jo construction cycle banata hai.

Better:

```rust
.background(|context| async move {
    context.enqueue(job).await?;
    context.wait_for_trigger().await;
})
```

`BackgroundContext`:

```rust
pub struct BackgroundContext<J, N> {
    shutdown: CancellationToken,
    sender: QueueSender<J>,
    notifier: Notifier<N>,
    trigger: Trigger,
}
```

12. Trigger/Notify distinction

Current `NotifySignal` notifications ke liye hai. Dispatcher ko jagane ke liye separate trigger primitive chahiye:

```rust
queue.trigger()
context.wait_for_trigger()
```

`Notify` event consumer ke liye hai; `Trigger` producer/dispatcher wakeup ke liye.

13. Persistence adapter

Generic queue ko SQL knowledge nahi chahiye, lekin persistent integration contract useful hoga:

```rust
trait JobSource<J> {
    async fn recover(&self) -> Result<Vec<J>, Error>;
    async fn claim(&self, limit: usize) -> Result<Vec<J>, Error>;
}
```

Optional hooks:

```rust
trait JobStore<J> {
    async fn on_queued(...)
    async fn on_started(...)
    async fn on_completed(...)
    async fn on_failed(...)
}
```

Deployment queue repository adapter implement karega.

14. Typed job ID

Currently:

```rust
fn id(&self) -> String;
```

Har operation string allocate karta hai aur collisions possible hain.

Better:

```rust
trait TaskJob {
    type Id: Eq + Hash + Clone + Display;
    fn id(&self) -> Self::Id;
}
```

15. Typed errors without requiring Clone

Current:

```rust
type Error: Display + Clone
```

Most real errors naturally `Clone` nahi hote—`sqlx::Error`, `io::Error`, `BuilderError`.

Queue callback presently only converted string error needs. Remove `Clone`:

```rust
type Error: Display + Send + Sync + 'static;
```

16. Output also unnecessarily Clone

Current:

```rust
type Output: Clone
```

Large outputs copy karne pad sakte hain. Callbacks references receive karte hain, so `Clone` unnecessary hai.

17. Notification backpressure

Current `send_notify()` har signal par `tokio::spawn` karta hai:

```rust
tokio::spawn(async move {
    tx.send(signal).await;
});
```

Heavy job burst mein hundreds of tasks spawn ho sakte hain and FIFO ordering theoretically scheduler-dependent ho sakti hai.

Better:

```rust
async fn notify(...)
fn try_notify(...)
```

Internal worker direct `await tx.send()` kare. External sync API only `try_send`.

18. Blocking `std::sync::RwLock`

Async queue mein listener list ke liye:

```rust
std::sync::RwLock
```

Critical section small hai, but poison behavior unnecessary hai. Better:

```rust
tokio::sync::RwLock
```

Ya listeners build-time immutable rakho; runtime listener registration required nahi ho to lock completely remove.

19. Completed job memory cleanup

Job registry add karne ke baad terminal jobs forever map mein nahi rehne chahiye.

Required:

```rust
history_capacity
history_ttl
cleanup_interval
```

20. Fairness

Per-key queues ke bina one server ke 100 jobs global FIFO ko occupy karke other servers ko delay kar sakte hain.

For deployments better:

```text
server A queue ─┐
server B queue ─┼→ round-robin/fair scheduler
server C queue ─┘
```

Generic queue mein optional:

```rust
SchedulingPolicy::Fifo
SchedulingPolicy::FairByKey
SchedulingPolicy::Priority
```

## Useful advanced capabilities

21. Priority jobs

```rust
fn priority(&self) -> i32;
```

Manual deployment schedule backup se higher priority ho sakta hai.

22. Delayed scheduling

```rust
queue.push_at(job, Instant)
queue.push_after(job, Duration)
```

Retry and cron integration easier ho jayega.

23. Rate limiting

Concurrency limit aur rate limit different hain:

```rust
10 concurrent jobs
but only 100 API calls/minute
```

Optional keyed/global token bucket useful hoga.

24. Progress events

Lifecycle events coarse hain. Long builds ko generic progress send karna chahiye:

```rust
context.progress(DeploymentProgress {
    stage: Build,
    percent: 45,
})
```

25. Health/introspection

```rust
queue.health()
queue.is_accepting()
queue.worker_count()
queue.oldest_queued_age()
queue.last_completed_at()
```

Monitoring endpoint ke liye useful.

## Recommended implementation priority

Immediately BuilderQueue conversion se pehle:

1. Typed Job ID
2. Per-job cancellation
3. Keyed concurrency
4. Duplicate policy
5. Timeout
6. Panic handling
7. Cancellation-aware retry
8. Async/ordered notifications
9. Background context with enqueue/trigger
10. Graceful shutdown

Second phase:

11. State/stats
12. Persistent source/store traits
13. Fair-by-key scheduling
14. Retry strategies
15. History cleanup
16. Priority/delayed jobs
17. Progress/health API

In changes ke baad generic queue genuinely reusable hogi:

```text
DeploymentQueue
BackupQueue
NotificationQueue
AIQueue
MaintenanceQueue
```

Aur BuilderQueue ka separate execution engine safely remove kiya ja sakega.

## Assistant

Generic queue ke core features ab implement ho gaye: typed IDs/keys, per-key concurrency, duplicate policy, timeout, panic isolation, cancellation-aware execution/retry, queue stats, enqueue/trigger context. Deployment task ab typed target validate karta hai aur server-key scheduling use karta hai. Ab formatting aur full checks chala raha hoon; jo compile/test issue milega wahi final cleanup hoga.

## Assistant

Generic queue architecture complete kar diya hai.

Main changes:

- `TaskJob` ab typed hai:
  - typed `Id`
  - typed `Key`
  - optional concurrency key
  - optional deduplication key
  - optional timeout
  - `JobContext` ke through cancellation
- Generic queue mein add hua:
  - per-key concurrency, jaise `server_id`
  - duplicate policies: `Reject`, `Replace`, `Allow`
  - job cancellation registry
  - queued/running cancellation handling
  - timeout support
  - panic isolation via `catch_unwind`
  - cancellation-aware retry delay
  - fixed/exponential retry configuration
  - queue stats: queued, running, completed, failed, cancelled
  - background context se `enqueue`, `trigger`, `wait_for_trigger`
  - notification handling
- `DeploymentTask` ab loose invalid optional IDs ke bajaye typed target validate karta hai:
  - `Application`
  - `Compose`
  - `Database`
- Deployment jobs server key ke basis par schedule hote hain.
- Queue full hone par registration cleanup bhi add kiya.
- Existing callback API preserve rakhi hai, isliye current developers ko unnecessary migration nahi karni padegi.

Verification successful:

- `cargo fmt --all`
- `cargo check -p queue`
- `cargo check -p rustploy`
- `git diff --check`
- Queue tests: all passed

Important boundary same rakhi hai: generic queue crate scheduling/execution handle karta hai, deployment ka SQLite claim/finalization/repository logic Rustploy adapter ke andar hi hai. SQL generic crate mein nahi gaya.

Ab BuilderQueue mein:

- stale remote cleanup managed background runner se hota hai
- deployment dispatcher managed background runner se hota hai

- shutdown cancellation token ke through controlled hai

- generic lifecycle/scheduling logic `crates/queue` mein hai

Generic queue mein background API ab context-based hai:

```rust
.background(|ctx| async move {
    loop {
        tokio::select! {
            _ = ctx.shutdown_token().cancelled() => break,
            _ = ctx.wait_for_trigger() => {
                // enqueue or reconcile
            }
        }
    }
})
```

  - `DEPLOYMENT_DISPATCH_BATCH_SIZE`
  - default `100`

- Reconciler startup fix:
  - start hote hi unnecessary duplicate scan nahi karega
  - pehla reconciliation actual 30-minute interval ke baad hoga
- Cancellation logic common helper mein consolidate ki:

  - compose

- Background task lifecycle managed aur shutdown-aware hai.

## Assistant

`QueueHandler` mein `on_task` add kar diya:

```rust
async fn on_task(
    &self,
    job: J,
    context: JobContext<J::Id>,
) -> Result<J::Output, QueueError>
```

Default implementation:

```rust
job.execute(context).await
```

Isliye existing queues break nahi hongi.

BuilderQueue override:

```rust
async fn on_task(
    &self,
    job: DeploymentTask,
    context: JobContext<i64>,
) -> Result<String, QueueError> {
    if context.is_cancelled() {
        return Err(QueueError::Cancelled);
    }

    self.process(...).await;
    Ok(...)
}
```

Ab complete lifecycle ek jagah implement ho sakta hai:

```text
on_start
   ↓
on_task
   ↓
on_retry
   ↓
on_success / on_failure
   ↓
on_notify
```

## Assistant

Ab architecture simple kar diya:

```text
BuilderQueue
    └── Queue<DeploymentTask, DeploymentSignal>
            └── QueueHandler implementation
```

BuilderQueue se ye custom systems hata diye:

- manual `WorkerPool`
- manual `DashMap` server pools
- manual `Notify`
- manual dispatch loop
- `BackgroundRunner`
- deployment-side `tokio::spawn`
- duplicate concurrency management

Ab responsibilities:

- `on_task`
  - application/compose/database execution
- `background_with_context`
  - startup recovery
  - DB deployment claim
  - `ctx.enqueue(job)`
  - 30-minute reconciliation
  - shutdown handling
- `on_start`
  - lifecycle logging
- `on_retry`
  - retry logging
- `on_success`
  - success signal
- `on_failure`
  - cancelled/error signal
- `on_notify`
  - lifecycle/custom signals
- `notify()`
  - generic queue ka `trigger()`

Per-server concurrency ab generic queue ke:

```rust
.keyed_concurrency(per_server_limit)
```

se handle hoti hai.

Background enqueue bhi canonical queue admission path se hota hai, isliye:

- deduplication
- cancellation registration
- stats
- capacity
- lifecycle notification

bypass nahi honge.

Verification:

- `cargo check -p rustploy` passed
- queue tests passed
- `git diff --check` passed

  ──────
  ## 2. Direct Shorthands: toggle:signal, show:signal, hide:signal

  Raw JavaScript expressions (data-on:click="$isOpen = !$isOpen") likhne ke bajaye direct attributes:

   Purana Datastar Syntax                                                                              | Naya Ultra-Clean Shorthand                                                                          | Kya Karega?
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   data-on:click="$is_open = !$is_open"                                                                | toggle:is_open                                                                                      | Click karne par is_open true/false toggle karega
   data-show="$is_open"                                                                                | show:is_open                                                                                        | Agar is_open == true hai to element dikhayega
   data-show="!$is_open"                                                                               | hide:is_open                                                                                        | Agar is_open == true hai to element chupayega

  ### Example:

    html! {
        <div signals={ is_open: false }>
            // 1. One-word toggle button!
            <button toggle:is_open>"Toggle Modal"</button>
    
            // 2. One-word show/hide!
            <div show:is_open class="modal">
                <p>"Modal is Open!"</p>
                <button toggle:is_open>"Close"</button>
            </div>
        </div>
    }
  ──────
  ## 3. Auto-Declared Signals for bind:field (Zero Setup!)

  Jab aap kisi input par bind:search="" likhte ho, to aapko parent par signals={ search: "" } likhne ki bhi zarurat nahi hai!

  Macro automatically dekhega ki bind:search used hai aur parent tag par $search signal automatic declare kar dega!

    // Aapko parent par signals declare nahi karna padega!
    html! {
        <div>
            // Macro automatically 'search' signal create kar dega!
            <input bind:search="" placeholder="Search..." />
    
            // Direct signal text display
            <p>"Search query: " {show_text:search}</p>
        </div>
    }

    // ✅ AFTER (Ultra Clean & Intuitive):
    html! {
        <div signals={ is_open: false }>

▾ Thought for 5s, 524 tokens
  Considering Template Rendering
  
  I'm now grappling with how `.await` functions within templates. The core question is: if I introduce `.await`, what specific output should the template render? I'm trying to identify the best way to handle asynchronous operations within the template context and what the template needs to represent that
  state.
  Yeh ek bohot zaroori aur sharp question hai! 👌

  Jab hum template mein {fetch_user_profile(user_id).await} likhte hain, to function kya return karega aur template usko kaise render karega?

  Iske 3 sabse clean tarike hain:
  ──────
   1. Option A: Function returns Markup (Recommended & Most Idiomatic) 

  Async function ek complete HTML snippet (Markup) return karta hai. Jab .await khatam hota hai, to wahi HTML direct DOM me patch ho jata hai:

    // Async function returns Markup
    async fn render_user_profile(user_id: &str, db: &SqlitePool) -> Markup {
        let user = sqlx::query_as!(User, "SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?", user_id)
            .fetch_one(db)
            .await
            .unwrap();
    
        // HTML fragment return karta hai
        html! {
            <div class="profile-card">
                <h2>{&user.name}</h2>
                <p>{&user.email}</p>
            </div>
        }
    }
    
    // Template usage:
    html! {
        <div>
            // Direct Markup insert ho jaayega jab async complete hoga!
            {render_user_profile(user_id, &pool).await.onloading(html! {
                <div>"Loading profile..."</div>
            })}
        </div>
    }
  ──────
   2. Option B: Function returns Struct + Inline Render Block (|data|) 

  Agar async function sirf raw Data Struct (e.g., User) return karta hai, to template me inline closure |user| de sakte hain:

    // Async function returns raw Data Struct (User)
    async fn get_user(user_id: &str, db: &SqlitePool) -> User {
        sqlx::query_as!(User, "SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?", user_id)
            .fetch_one(db)
            .await
            .unwrap()
    }
    
    // Template usage:
    html! {
        <div>
            // `|user|` block batata hai ki Struct ko kaise render karna hai
            {get_user(user_id, &pool).await.onloading(html! { "Loading..." }) |user| {
                <div class="profile-card">
                    <h2>{&user.name}</h2>
                    <p>{&user.email}</p>
                </div>
            }}
        </div>
    }
  ──────
   3. Option C: Function returns Primitive Types (String, i32, f64) 

  Agar async function single value (e.g., total count, total price, formatted string) return karta hai:

    async fn get_online_user_count(db: &SqlitePool) -> usize {
        // Returns count
        42 
    }
    
    // Template usage:
    html! {
        <p>
            "Online Users: "
            {get_online_user_count(&pool).await.onloading("...")}
        </p>
    }
  ──────
   🎯 Summary Table 

   What Async Function Returns                                                                         | Template Usage                                                                                      | How It Renders
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   Markup (HTML)                                                                                       | {render_profile(id).await}                                                                          | Returned HTML fragment patches directly
   Struct (Data Model)                                                                                 | {get_user(id).await |user| { <h2>{user.name}</h2> }}                                                | Inline block renders the fetched struct
   Primitive (String/Int)                                                                              | {get_count().await}                                                                                 | Returned text/number escapes & patches directly

  Option A (Markup return) sabse clean hai, aur Option B (Struct |data|) sabse flexible hai! 🚀

  Evaluating Syntax Choices
  
  I'm currently dissecting the provided syntax for rendering a profile card, seeking improvements. The core challenge is achieving a more elegant and readable expression. I'm focusing on the `onloading` function, aiming to streamline how the loading state is handled within the JSX structure. My goal is a
  syntax that is less verbose, and more intutive, given the context.
  YES! 100%! Yeh syntax kafi cluttered ho gaya tha!

  .await.onloading(html! { ... }) |user| { ... } mein ek saath bohot saare punctuation marks, method chains, aur nested braces aane se readability kharab ho rahi hai.

  Iska SABSE CLEAN & BEAUTIFUL solution hai: @async directive inside html! macro!
  ──────
   🎨 Alternative 1: @async Directive (Clean & Readable) 

  Trailing closure aur .onloading chain ke bajaye, macro ke andar direct @async aur @loading block:

    // ❌ PEHLE (Cluttered):
    {get_user(user_id, &pool).await.onloading(html! { "Loading..." }) |user| {
        <div class="profile-card">
            <h2>{&user.name}</h2>
            <p>{&user.email}</p>
        </div>
    }}
    
    // ✅ AB (Super Clean & Readable):
    @async get_user(user_id, &pool) |user| {
        <div class="profile-card">
            <h2>{&user.name}</h2>
            <p>{&user.email}</p>
        </div>
    } @loading {
        <div class="skeleton">"Loading..."</div>
    }
  ──────
  ## ⚡ Agar @loading custom nahi dena ho (Default Loading Skeleton):

  Agar aap @loading block nahi likhoge, to system automatically default skeleton / spinner render kar dega:

    @async get_user(user_id, &pool) |user| {

    }
  ──────

  Agar aapko @loading mein sirf ek chota string/HTML Dena hai:

        <div class="profile-card">
            <h2>{&user.name}</h2>
        </div>

  ──────
   📊 Comparison Table 

    // 1. Full Custom Loading UI:
    html! {
        @async get_user(id, &pool) |user| {
            <h2>{&user.name}</h2>
        } @loading {
            <div class="spinner">"Fetching Data..."</div>
        }
    }
    
    // 2. Short String Loading UI:
    html! {
        @async get_user(id, &pool) |user| {

    }
    
    // 3. Default System Loading UI:
    html! {
        @async get_user(id, &pool) |user| {
            <h2>{&user.name}</h2>
        }

  ### Why @async Directive Is 10x Better:

  1. No .await needed: @async keyword se macro ko pehle hi pata hai ye async hai.

  3. Crystal Clear Structure: Success View (|user| { ... }) aur Loading View (@loading { ... }) alag-alag, saaf dikhte hain!

  ──────
   👑 Master Feature List: Rust + Datastar Framework 
  ──────
  ## 1️⃣ Async Loading & Suspense (Option<T> Pattern)

  • Syntax: {get_user(id, &pool).await |user| { @if let Some(u) = user { ... } @else { ... } }}
  • How It Works:
      • Initial page render par user = None hota hai ➔ Instantly <div class="skeleton"> loading UI serve hota hai.
      • Background mein async .await finish hote hi ➔ user = Some(u) branch ka SSE patch browser mein stream ho jata hai.
      • Zero macro keywords, pure Rust Option<T>!

  ──────
  ## 2️⃣ 100% Invisible SQLite Reactivity (sqlite3_update_hook)

  • Developer Writes: Standard sqlx::query!("UPDATE applications SET status = 'running' WHERE id = 'app-1'").
  • System Engine:
      • SQLite native C-engine hook change detect karta hai.
      • Zero manual wrapper functions, zero event emitters in handlers.
      • Pure Raw SQL ➔ Instant Auto-Patch!

  ──────
  ## 3️⃣ Single SSE Connection Pipeline (NO Component Endpoints)

  • Architecture:
      • Har component ke liye alag HTTP routes/endpoints NAHI banenge.
      • Per browser tab SIRF 1 SSE Pipe (GET /sse) open hoga.
      • Saare component patches (SQL changes, async loads) usi single pipe se stream honge.

  ──────
  ## 4️⃣ Zero-Path Action Binding (on:click={Self::action})

  • Syntax: <button on:click={Self::restart}>"Restart"</button>
  • How It Works:
      • Macro compile-time par automatically expand karke data-on:click="@post('/controller/restart')" bana deta hai.
      • Hardcoded URL path strings likhne ki tension khatam!

  ──────
  ## 5️⃣ Ultra-Clean Client Signals & Shorthands

  • signals={ is_open: false, count: 0 } ➔ Raw JSON string ke jagah clean Rust key-value syntax.
  • toggle:is_open ➔ 0ms Client-side toggle (modals, dropdowns, tabs ke liye — zero server hit).
  • show:is_open / hide:is_open ➔ One-word conditional visibility.
  • bind:field ➔ 2-way form input binding.
  ──────
  ## 6️⃣ Nested Isolated Component Patching

  • Architecture:
      • Nested components ko unique IDs milti hain (#comp-Name-id).
      • Deepest level par data badalne par SIRF exact nested component re-render aur patch hota hai — parent aur sibling components untouched rehte hain (0 CPU waste).

  ──────
  ## 7️⃣ Ephemeral Streaming Pipes (Logs & Metrics)

  • Architecture:
      • Docker logs, pty-process terminal, aur CPU/RAM metrics direct Tokio Stream ➔ SSE pipe stream hote hain.
      • Database ya RAM mein log history store karne ki zarurat nahi.
      • User tab close karte hi memory instantly release ho jati hai.

  ──────
  ## 8️⃣ Maud-Style High-Performance Core Engine (html-rt & html-macro)

  • Architecture:
      • Ultra-fast Markup (PreEscaped<String>).
      • Render trait + itoa fast integer formatting.
      • Direct Axum IntoResponse integration (Html() wrapper ki zarurat nahi).
      • Full HTML syntax + @if, @for, @while, @match logic.

> agar reactive hoga wo too woo to loop me chalega na na re

▾ Thought for 5s, 575 tokens
  Considering Reactivity Loops
  
  I'm grappling with a fundamental reactivity concern, sparked by a crucial question. The core issue is the potential for an infinite loop if a reactive element triggers its own re-evaluation. I need to figure out how to manage reactivity to avoid endless iterations.
  BOHOT ZABARDAST QUESTION! 🎯

  Aapka doubt bilkul sahi hai: "Kahin aisa toh nahi hoga ki DB change hua ➔ re-render hua ➔ fir se change hua ➔ aur INFINITE LOOP mein phas gaya?"

  Aaiye dekhte hain ki Infinite Loop KYUN NAHI HOGA (3 Metal-Solid Guarantees):
  ──────
  ## 🛡️ Guarantee 1: SQLite Hook Only Fires on WRITE (UPDATE, INSERT, DELETE)

  SQLite ka native sqlite3_update_hook sirf aur sirf Write queries पर chalta hai:

    SELECT Query (Read)   ──► ❌ SQLite Hook Fire NAHI Hota!
    INSERT Query (Write)  ──► ✅ SQLite Hook Fire Hota hai (1 Baar)
    UPDATE Query (Write)  ──► ✅ SQLite Hook Fire Hota hai (1 Baar)
    DELETE Query (Write)  ──► ✅ SQLite Hook Fire Hota hai (1 Baar)

  Chain kahan rukti hai:

  1. Aapne Action mein UPDATE chalaya (1 Write) ➔ Hook fire hua (1 Baar).
  2. Framework ne Data Re-Fetch karne ke liye SELECT query chalayi (Read).
  3. SELECT query se Hook FIRE NAHI HOTA.
  4. Loop wahi ruk gaya! (Zero Infinite Loop!)
  ──────
  ## 🛡️ Guarantee 2: Render Function me Write Query Forbidden (Immutable &)

  Rust ki type-system guarantee:

  • HTML render(&self) functions hamesha Immutable (&) hote hain.
  • Aap render function ke andar UPDATE ya INSERT query chala hi nahi sakte!
  • Write queries sirf explicit Actions (jaise post handlers) mein chalti hain.
  ──────
  ## 🛡️ Guarantee 3: HTML Diffing / Deduplication (Same HTML = No Patch)

  Agar background mein koi update hua lekin HTML output mein koi badlaav nahi aaya (same HTML generated):

  • Framework patch ko browser mein bhejega hi nahi!
  ──────
  ## 🔄 Complete Single-Loop Cycle (Visual)

    [ User Clicks "Restart" ]
               │
               ▼
    [ Action Handler Runs 1 UPDATE Query ]  ◄── (Write Mutation)
               │
               ▼ (SQLite C-Hook Fires ONCE)
               │
    [ Framework Runs 1 SELECT Query ]      ◄── (Read Only — Hook STOPPED here!)
               │
               ▼
    [ HTML Rendered & SSE Patched ONCE ]
               │
               ▼
         [ CYCLE STOPS ]

  Result: Exactly 1 Event ➔ Exactly 1 Patch ➔ Loop Finished! No Infinite Loop Ever! 🚀⚡

  information should be available - maybe through the route attribute itself or some kind of registry lookup.
  
  The cleanest approach is probably to have the route macro generate a path lookup function that the html macro can call at runtime, mapping the method name to its full path. Or even simpler - leverage the inventory system that's already collecting routes to build a path lookup table that resolves

### ast.rs: AttrKind enum add karo

```rust
pub enum AttrKind {
    Normal,             // class="foo"   (existing)

    On {                // on:click={Self::restart}
        event: String,
        method: Expr,
    },
    Bind(String),       // bind:username  → data-bind:username
    Toggle(String),     // toggle:is_open → data-on:click="$s=!$s"
    Show(String),       // show:is_open   → data-show="$s"
    Hide(String),       // hide:is_open   → data-show="!$s"
    Signals(Vec<(String, Expr)>), // signals={k:v} → data-signals="{...}"
}
```

### Parser logic (ast.rs):

```
Attr parse mein prefix check:
  "on:"     → On { event, method }
  "bind:"   → Bind(field)
  "toggle:" → Toggle(signal)
  "show:"   → Show(signal)
  "hide:"   → Hide(signal)
  "signals" → Signals(pairs)
  else      → Normal (existing)
```

### Code generation (generate.rs):

```rust
AttrKind::On { event, method } =>
    // data-on:click="@post('{Self::__PATH_restart}')"
    push_raw(format!("data-on:{}=\"@post('\"", event))
    + emit method as runtime string expr
    + push_raw("')\"")

AttrKind::Bind(field) =>
    push_raw(format!("data-bind:{}", field))

AttrKind::Toggle(s) =>
    push_raw(format!("data-on:click=\"${s} = !${s}\""))

AttrKind::Show(s) =>
    push_raw(format!("data-show=\"${}\"", s))

AttrKind::Hide(s) =>
    push_raw(format!("data-show=\"!${}\"", s))

AttrKind::Signals(pairs) =>
    // compile-time JSON: data-signals="{is_open:false,count:0}"
```

## Step 4: Async Suspense

### 4A. ast.rs mein naya Node:

```rust
pub enum Node {
    // ...existing...
    AsyncExpr(AsyncExprNode),  // NEW
}

pub struct AsyncExprNode {
    pub call: Expr,     // get_app(&id, &pool)  — bina .await
    pub arg: syn::Pat,  // |app|
    pub body: Nodes,    // { @if let Some(a) = app {...} @else {...} }
}
```

### 4B. Parser:

```
{expr} dekho:
  expr mein .await hai + uske baad |pat| { ... } hai?
    → AsyncExprNode
  warna
    → Normal Expr (existing)
```

### 4C. Code generation:

```rust
Node::AsyncExpr(node) => {
    let slot_id = next_slot_id(); // unique per call site
    let arg = &node.arg;
    let call = &node.call;
    let body = generate_nodes(node.body);

    quote! {
        // 1. Slot wrapper
        out.push_str(&format!("<div id=\"{}\">", #slot_id));

        // 2. Initial render: None → @else (skeleton)
        { let #arg: Option<_> = None; #body }

        out.push_str("</div>");

        // 3. Background task: actual .await
        let __slot = #slot_id;
        let __tx = __sse_tx.clone();
        ::tokio::spawn(async move {
            let __res = (#call).await;
            let #arg = Some(__res);
            let mut __out = String::new();
            #body  // Some branch → real HTML
            __tx.send((__slot, __out)).ok();
        });
    }
}
```

### 4D. Per-Request SSE (auto, no global)

auto_route_macros: jab `Markup` return type handler mein AsyncExpr ho:

```rust
// Developer likhta hai:
async fn page(&self, ...) -> Markup { html! { ... } }

// Macro automatically generate karta hai:
async fn page(&self, ...) -> impl IntoResponse {
    let (tx, rx) = tokio::sync::mpsc::channel(16);
    let __sse_tx = tx;

    // html! runs → initial skeleton HTML + tasks spawn
    let initial = html! { ... };

    // SSE: first full page, then patches as tasks finish
    sse_stream_response(initial, rx)
}
```

Developer ko pata hi nahi chalta — sirf `-> Markup` likhta hai.

> are reactivnes kase handle karege for app me bhi if some(app) asa kar sakte hai na under me

▾ Thought for 10s
  The user is asking about reactivity - how will the `@if let Some(app)` and `@for app in` patterns handle reactivity when the underlying data changes?
  
  The question is: when SQLite data changes, how does the framework know to re-run these async functions and patch the UI?
  
  Let me think about this:
  
  1. When `get_app(&id, &pool).await` is called in the template, it queries the DB
  2. If the DB row changes, the framework needs to re-run the query and patch the UI
  3. But how does the framework know WHICH function to re-run and WHICH part of the UI to patch?
  
  The answer lies in the slot ID system:
  - When the macro encounters `.await` in an `@if let Some(app) = get_app(&id).await` block, it wraps the entire conditional in a slot div with a unique ID
  - It also tracks which database tables and rows this query touches through SQLite hooks
  - When that data changes, the framework re-runs the async function and patches just that slot with the new result
  - So if the data loads asynchronously, the `@else` branch renders first, then once the query completes, it switches to the `@if` branch in the same slot
  - For lists, the same mechanism applies: the slot gets patched with the full list when data arrives, and re-patched again if new items are added to the database
  - The key is that the same slot location handles both the initial async load and any subsequent database changes, making reactivity automatic without explicit subscriptions

  For `@if let Some(x) = expr.await`, I need to detect the `.await` keyword, wrap the entire conditional block in a slot div, render the else branch initially, spawn an async task, and then patch the slot with the result once it resolves. Similarly, for `@for item in expr.await`, I'll wrap the loop in a
  slot, start with an empty render, spawn the task, and patch with the rendered items when complete. When the loop items themselves are `Option<T>`, each `None` displays a skeleton while each `Some(item)` shows the actual content, with the nested `@if let Some` handling the conditional display.
  
  The key insight is that the user probably just wants clean syntax—the implementation can be straightforward. When `get_apps()` returns `Vec<Option<App>>` and we call `.await` on it, the framework detects that `.await` keyword, wraps everything in a slot, and patches it once the future resolves. The
  progressive streaming aspect where items load individually is just normal Rust pattern matching, no special macro handling required.

### 1. Single Async Item
```rust
@if let Some(app) = get_app(&id, &pool).await {
    <h2>{&app.name}</h2>
    <span>{&app.status}</span>
} @else {
    <div class="skeleton">"Loading..."</div>
}
```
- `None` = abhi load ho raha hai → `@else` dikhta hai
- `Some(app)` = ready → `@if` branch patch hota hai

```rust
}
```

- `None` items = skeleton, `Some` items = real card

```rust
// auto_route handler wrap hota hai:
async fn page(&self, ...) -> impl IntoResponse {
    let (tx, rx) = tokio::sync::mpsc::channel(16);
    let __sse_tx = tx;

    // html! runs:
    //   1. Initial HTML generate (skeletons/empty)
    //   2. Async tasks spawn (using __sse_tx)
    let initial_html = html! { ... };

    // SSE stream:
    //   Event 1: full initial page HTML
    //   Event 2+: slot patches as tasks complete
    sse_page_response(initial_html, rx).await
}
// Developer -> Markup likhta hai, framework -> SSE mein convert karta hai
```

**Changes needed to ast.rs:**

1. Extend the `Attr` struct to support new shorthand attribute types. Currently attrs are parsed generically as `AttrName` + `AttrValue`. We need to add a new enum `AttrKind` that captures these special cases during parsing:

```rust
pub enum AttrKind {
    Normal { name: AttrName, value: AttrValue },  // existing attrs
    On { event: String, method: syn::Expr },       // on:click={Self::restart}
    Bind(String),                                   // bind:username
    Toggle(String),                                // toggle:is_open
    Show(String),                                  // show:is_open  
    Hide(String),                                  // hide:is_open
    Signals(Vec<(String, syn::Expr)>),             // signals={k: v, k2: v2}
}
```

The `Attr` struct should use `AttrKind` instead of separate name/value:
```rust
pub struct Attr {
    pub kind: AttrKind,
}
```

Parsing rules:
- If attr name starts with `on:` → parse as `On { event: "click", method: expr }`
  - e.g. `on:click={Self::restart}` → On { event: "click", method: Self::restart }
  - e.g. `on:keydown.enter={Self::submit}` → On { event: "keydown.enter", method: Self::submit }
- If attr name is exactly `bind:fieldname` → `Bind("fieldname")`
- If attr name is exactly `toggle:signalname` → `Toggle("signalname")`
- If attr name is exactly `show:signalname` → `Show("signalname")`
- If attr name is exactly `hide:signalname` → `Hide("signalname")`
- If attr name is exactly `signals` → parse `={k: expr, k2: expr2}` as `Signals(vec![("k", expr), ("k2", expr2)])`
- Everything else → `Normal { name, value }`

For `Signals` parsing, the value looks like `={is_open: false, count: 0}` - it's a brace-delimited list of `ident: expr` pairs separated by commas.

**Changes needed to generate.rs:**

Update `gen_attr` to handle the new `AttrKind` variants:

```rust
AttrKind::Normal { name, value } => // existing logic

AttrKind::On { event, method } => {
    // Generates: data-on:click="@post({method})"
    // method is a Rust expr (Self::restart) that should evaluate to a path string
    // at runtime via Self::__PATH_restart const
    b.flush();
    b.tokens.extend(quote! {
        #out.push_str(&format!("data-on:{}=\"@post('\"", #event_str));
        #out.push_str(&#method); // Self::__PATH_restart
        #out.push_str("')\"");
    });
}

AttrKind::Bind(field) => {
    b.push_raw(&format!(" data-bind:{}", field));
}

AttrKind::Toggle(signal) => {
    b.push_raw(&format!(" data-on:click=\"${s} = !${s}\"", s = signal));
}

AttrKind::Show(signal) => {
    b.push_raw(&format!(" data-show=\"${}\"", signal));
}

AttrKind::Hide(signal) => {
    b.push_raw(&format!(" data-show=\"!${}\"", signal));
}

AttrKind::Signals(pairs) => {
    // Generate data-signals="{is_open:false,count:0}" at compile time
    // Each expr must be a literal or simple value for compile-time generation
    // Use quote to generate runtime format string
    // Example output: data-signals="{\"is_open\":false,\"count\":0}"
}
```

**Important notes:**
- For `On`, the `method` expr (e.g. `Self::restart`) will evaluate to a `&str` path constant that will be added to the controller impl by auto_route_macros as `pub const __PATH_restart: &'static str = "/apps/restart"`
- The generated code for `On` should be: `format!("data-on:{}=\"@post('{}')\"" , event, Self::__PATH_restart)` where the method expr IS `Self::__PATH_restart`
- Keep all existing functionality intact - only ADD new attr kinds
- Make sure the build compiles with `cargo build -p html-macro` in /run/media/das/SSD/Devloper/rustploy

## What to implement:

We want to support this syntax in html! templates:

```rust
// Single async item:
@if let Some(app) = get_app(&id, &pool).await {
    <h2>{&app.name}</h2>
} @else {
    <div class="skeleton">"Loading..."</div>
}

// Async list with per-item Option:
@for app in get_apps(&pool).await {
    @if let Some(a) = app {
        <div>{&a.name}</div>
    } @else {
        <div class="skeleton"></div>
    }
}
```

The macro needs to detect when `.await` is used in `@if let Some(x) = expr.await` or `@for x in expr.await` and generate code that:
1. Wraps the block in `<div id="__slot_N">` where N is a counter
2. Does an initial render with `None` (for @if) or empty Vec (for @for)
3. Spawns a tokio task that does the actual `.await` call
4. Sends the result via `__sse_tx` channel

## Implementation Plan:

### ast.rs changes:

Add `is_async: bool` field to `IfNode` and `ForNode`:

```rust
pub struct IfNode {
    pub cond: Expr,
    pub then_nodes: Nodes,
    pub else_nodes: Option<ElseBranch>,
    pub is_async: bool,  // true when cond contains .await
}

pub struct ForNode {
    pub pat: syn::Pat,
    pub expr: Expr,
    pub body: Nodes,
    pub is_async: bool,  // true when expr ends with .await
}
```

For detection:
- In `IfNode::parse`: after parsing `cond`, check if the expression contains `.await`. You can do this by converting to string with `quote!(#cond).to_string().contains(".await")` or by walking the Expr.
  - Simple approach: after parsing cond as `Expr`, check if `matches!(cond, Expr::Await(_))` — but in `@if let Some(x) = expr.await`, the let pattern means it's parsed as a whole let expression. The key insight: if we check the tokens for `.await`, we can set is_async.
  - Simplest working approach: Check `quote::quote!(#cond).to_string().contains(".await")` and set `is_async = true`.
- In `ForNode::parse`: after parsing `expr`, check `quote::quote!(#expr).to_string().contains(".await")` and if so, strip the `.await` from the expr and set `is_async = true`.

For the ForNode async case, the expr should be stored WITHOUT the .await so we can call it ourselves in the generated code.

Actually the SIMPLEST approach: Don't modify ast.rs IfNode/ForNode structs at all. Instead in the parser for IfNode, check if cond contains await AFTER parsing. Same for ForNode.

But to actually strip `.await` from ForNode's expr, we need to detect it. Here's the key:

For `@for app in get_apps(&pool).await`:
- `expr` will be parsed as an `Expr::Await` wrapping `get_apps(&pool)`  
- We can check: `if let Expr::Await(await_expr) = &expr { is_async = true; inner_expr = *await_expr.base.clone(); }`

For `@if let Some(app) = get_app(&id).await`:
- The condition is `let Some(app) = get_app(&id).await`
- Parsed as `Expr::Let` with init being `Expr::Await`
- Check: if cond is Expr::Let and its expr is Expr::Await

### generate.rs changes:

Add a thread-local counter for unique slot IDs:

```rust
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU32, Ordering};
static SLOT_COUNTER: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(0);
```

For `IfNode { is_async: true }`:
```rust
let slot_n = SLOT_COUNTER.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
let slot_id = format!("__slot_{}", slot_n);

// Initial render: replace .await expr with None
// For @if let Some(x) = expr.await { body } @else { else_body }
// Generate:
quote! {
    // Wrap in slot div
    #out.push_str(&format!("<div id=\"{}\">", #slot_id));
    
    // Initial: use None so @else (skeleton) renders
    {
        // Temporarily pass None to satisfy the pattern match
        let __init: Option<_> = None;
        // We need to render the @else branch initially
        // Simplest: render the else branch directly
        #else_branch_tokens
    }
    
    #out.push_str("</div>");
    
    // Spawn async task
    {
        let __slot = #slot_id.to_string();
        let __tx = __sse_tx.clone();
        ::tokio::spawn(async move {
            // Run the actual async call (without .await - we await it here)
            let __result = #async_expr .await;  // the inner expr without .await
            // Render with Some(result)
            let mut __patch_buf = ::std::string::String::new();
            let __patch_out = &mut __patch_buf;
            // Here we need to render the @if body with __result
            // This is where it gets tricky...
        });
    }
}
```

Actually, this is complex because inside the tokio::spawn we need to re-render the template with the actual value. The key insight is:

For `@if let Some(app) = get_app().await { <h2>{&app.name}</h2> } @else { <div>"Loading"</div> }` we generate:

```rust
// 1. Initial render - @else branch (loading skeleton)
#out.push_str(&format!("<div id=\"{}\">", slot_id));
// render @else body
#out.push_str("</div>");

// 2. Async task
let __slot = slot_id;
let __tx = __sse_tx.clone();
tokio::spawn(async move {
    let Some(app) = get_app().await else { return; }; // or handle None differently
    let mut __out = String::new();
    // render @if body with real `app`
    html_rt::macro_private::render_to!(&app.name, &mut __out);
    // etc...
    __tx.send((__slot, __out)).ok();
});
```

The challenge: how to call the body code generator twice (once for else/loading, once for the real data).

Simplest approach that works: generate the body tokens twice. The `gen_nodes` function can be called multiple times to produce the same token stream.

## Concrete Implementation:

Here's the exact code to generate for `@if let Some(x) = expr.await { then } @else { else_body }`:

```rust
// In generate.rs, gen_control_flow for IfNode { is_async: true }:

fn gen_if_async(node: IfNode, b: &mut Builder, out: &Ident) {
    // node.cond is like: `let Some(app) = get_app(&id, &pool).await`
    // We need:
    //   - inner_expr: `get_app(&id, &pool)` (without .await)
    //   - pat: `Some(app)` 
    //   - then_nodes: the body
    //   - else_nodes: the loading skeleton
    
    // Extract inner expr and pattern from the Expr::Let(Expr::Await(...))
    let slot_n = SLOT_COUNTER.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
    let slot_id_str = format!("__slot_{}", slot_n);
    
    // Parse: cond is Expr::Let { pat, expr: Expr::Await { base } }
    let (pat, inner_expr) = extract_let_await(&node.cond);
    
    // Generate loading HTML tokens (else branch)
    let mut else_b = Builder::new(out.clone());
    if let Some(else_nodes) = node.else_nodes { gen_else_branch(else_nodes, &mut else_b, out); }
    let else_tokens = else_b.finish();
    
    // Generate then HTML tokens (real data branch)
    let mut then_b = Builder::new(out.clone());
    gen_nodes(node.then_nodes, &mut then_b, out);
    let then_tokens = then_b.finish();
    
    b.flush();
    b.tokens.extend(quote! {
        // Initial render: slot wrapper + skeleton
        #out.push_str(&::std::format!("<div id=\"{}\">", #slot_id_str));
        { #else_tokens }
        #out.push_str("</div>");
        
        // Async task: real data
        {
            let __slot_id = #slot_id_str;
            let __tx = __sse_tx.clone();
            ::tokio::spawn(async move {
                if let Some(#pat) = (#inner_expr).await {
                    let mut __out = ::std::string::String::new();
                    { 
                        let #out = &mut __out;
                        #then_tokens
                    }
                    let _ = __tx.send((__slot_id.to_string(), __out)).await;
                }
            });
        }
    });
}
```

## Key helper function needed:

```rust
// Extract (pattern, inner_expr) from `let Some(x) = expr.await`
fn extract_let_await(cond: &Expr) -> (syn::Pat, Expr) {
    if let Expr::Let(let_expr) = cond {
        if let Expr::Await(await_expr) = &*let_expr.expr {
            return ((*let_expr.pat).clone(), (*await_expr.base).clone());
        }
    }
    panic!("async @if must be: @if let Some(x) = expr.await");
}
```

For `@for x in expr.await { body }` where body contains `@if let Some(a) = x { ... } @else { ... }`:

Here the `expr` is `Expr::Await`, so:
```rust
fn gen_for_async(node: ForNode, b: &mut Builder, out: &Ident) {
    let slot_n = SLOT_COUNTER.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
    let slot_id_str = format!("__slot_{}", slot_n);
    
    // inner_expr = the expr without .await
    let inner_expr = if let Expr::Await(a) = &node.expr { *a.base.clone() } else { node.expr.clone() };
    let pat = &node.pat;
    
    let mut body_b = Builder::new(out.clone());
    gen_nodes(node.body, &mut body_b, out);
    let body_tokens = body_b.finish();
    
    b.flush();
    b.tokens.extend(quote! {
        #out.push_str(&::std::format!("<div id=\"{}\">", #slot_id_str));
        // Initially empty
        #out.push_str("</div>");
        
        {
            let __slot_id = #slot_id_str;
            let __tx = __sse_tx.clone();
            ::tokio::spawn(async move {
                let __items = (#inner_expr).await;
                let mut __out = ::std::string::String::new();
                for #pat in __items {
                    let #out = &mut __out;
                    #body_tokens
                }
                let _ = __tx.send((__slot_id.to_string(), __out)).await;
            });
        }
    });
}
```

## Important notes:

1. The `__sse_tx` variable is expected to be in scope when the html! macro is called. It's provided by the framework (auto_route wraps the handler). For now, use `tokio::sync::mpsc::Sender<(String, String)>` type.

2. The `#out` ident represents the `String` being built. In the async task, we create a new `String` called `__out` and use a reference to it.

3. Use `std::sync::atomic::AtomicU32` for SLOT_COUNTER with `Ordering::Relaxed`.

4. The `__tx.send()` should be `__tx.blocking_send()` or `__tx.try_send()` since we're in an async context - use `.await` on the send since we're inside `tokio::spawn(async move {...})`.

Wait - mpsc::Sender::send() is async in tokio. Use `let _ = __tx.send(...).await;`

  Error "the binding is already a mutable borrow" — yeh message tab aata hai jab &mut X ko dobara &mut se borrow karo. The hint "try removing &mut here" points to the outer html! block's let mut __html_out.

  Root cause: lib.rs mein let mut __html_out = String::with_capacity(...). Jab tokio::spawn(async move {...}) mein __html_out ko capture karne ki koshish hoti hai (because out Ident is __html_out), it tries to move the outer mutable binding into the async block — lekin yeh already borrowed hai by the code
  before.

  Actual Fix: gen_for_async mein the outer out push calls run BEFORE tokio::spawn. The problem is that __html_out is being captured in the tokio::spawn async block by the body_tokens — body_tokens uses __task_out (which is &mut __patch), but somewhere the __html_out is also referenced.

  Let me look at exactly what body_tokens generates for <li>{&item}</li>:

  This will generate: __task_out.push_str("<li>"); render_to!(&(item), &mut __task_out); __task_out.push_str("</li>");

  Wait — render_to!(&(item), &mut __task_out) — this uses &mut __task_out — but __task_out is already &mut String. So &mut __task_out would be &mut &mut String!

  That's the bug! In Builder::flush() and Node::Expr generation, we do render_to!(&(expr), &mut #out) — where #out is __task_out. But __task_out is &mut String, so &mut __task_out becomes &mut &mut String — double mutable reference, not &mut String.

  Fix: Change the generation so inside async blocks, __task_out is used directly as &mut String, and we call render_to! with it directly (not &mut __task_out). OR — simpler — use String directly instead of &mut String:

> Yehi wo asli gap tha jo maine bhi flag kiya tha — `commit_hook` sirf "kuch commit hua" batata hai, "kya" nahi. Uska jawab hai **`preupdate_hook`**, jo sqlx me bhi available hai (feature flag ke peeche).
  
  ## `preupdate_hook` — table, operation, aur old/new values, sab milta hai
  
  ```toml
  # Cargo.toml
  sqlx = { version = "...", features = ["sqlite", "sqlite-preupdate-hook"] }
  ```
  
  ```rust
  use sqlx::sqlite::PreupdateHookResult; // sqlx ka wrapper type
  
  let pool = SqlitePoolOptions::new()
      .after_connect(move |conn, _meta| {
          let bus = bus_for_hook.clone();
          Box::pin(async move {
              let mut handle = conn.lock_handle().await?;
              handle.set_preupdate_hook(move |result: PreupdateHookResult| {
                  // ab pata chal jayega:
                  let table = result.table;        // "applications"
                  let op = result.operation;        // Insert / Update / Delete
                  let rowid = result.rowid;         // konsi row
  
                  // agar Update/Delete hai, purani values mil sakti hain:
                  // result.get_old_column_value(idx) via sqlite3_preupdate_old
                  // Update/Insert ke liye nayi values:
                  // result.get_new_column_value(idx) via sqlite3_preupdate_new
  
                  bus.notify(ChangeEvent { table: table.to_string(), rowid, op });
              });
              Ok(())
          })
      })
      .connect("sqlite://rustploy.db").await?;
  ```
  
  Ab tumhare `ChangeEvent` me **table naam** hoga, isliye Step 3 (`render_and_diff`) me tum sirf **relevant subscriptions** ko dobara chalao, sabko nahi:
  
  ```rust
  loop {
      let event = rx.recv().await.unwrap();
      for sub in subs.iter_mut() {
          if sub.table == event.table {   // ← sirf relevant query re-run hogi
              // re-query, diff, patch
          }
      }
  }
  ```
  
  ## Teen cheezein dhyan me rakhna (yeh real caveats hain, chhupane wali nahi)
  
  1. **Yeh feature relatively naya hai sqlx me** — `sqlite-preupdate-hook` flag alag se enable karna padta hai kyunki default off hai.
  
  2. **Bundled vs system SQLite ka masla** — agar tum `sqlite-unbundled` (system ki SQLite lib) use kar rahe ho, aur woh `SQLITE_ENABLE_PREUPDATE_HOOK` compile-flag ke saath nahi bani, to **linker error** aayega. Solution: sqlx ka default **bundled** SQLite hi use karo (jo already isse enable karke compile
  woh buffer flush karke SSE bhejoge — isse partial/uncommitted changes kabhi UI tak nahi pahunchenge agar beech me rollback ho jaye.
  hoti hai) — tumhare case me chalega kyunki tum ek single self-contained binary ship kar rahe ho, unbundled system-lib pe depend hone ki zarurat hi nahi.
  
  3. **Yeh `commit_hook` ko replace nahi karta, saath chalega** — `preupdate_hook` "kya badla" batata hai (per-row, transaction commit se pehle), `commit_hook` "transaction commit ho gaya" batata hai. Practically tum `preupdate_hook` se changes collect karoge (ek buffer me), aur jab `commit_hook` fire ho tab
  
  **Toh final answer tumhare sawal ka:** `preupdate_hook` se "table + operation + rowid + old/new column values" milta hai, `commit_hook` se "ab bhejna safe hai" wala signal milta hai — dono ko saath use karo, tabhi tumhe "kya hua, kaunsi table, kya value badli" ka poora, reliable picture milega bina
  manually `bus.notify()` line likhe har jagah. i am planing this for sqlite reactive what you think how we can build this for sqlite and for loop me easily manage kar payenge

▾ Thought Process
  Analyzing the Core Concept
  
  I'm now diving into the user's architectural design for a SQLite Reactive Engine, leveraging `preupdate_hook` and `commit_hook` within `sqlx`. The core concept, and the user's initial discovery, centers around the limitations of just the `commit_hook`. I'm going to determine what insights and novel design
  elements are being presented.
  
  
  Evaluating the Proposed Architecture
  
  I'm now focusing on the user's reactive system design using SQLite hooks. The `preupdate_hook` combined with the `commit_hook` are interesting because they provide exact change metadata. The proposal smartly leverages the `preupdate_hook` for real-time data collection within a transaction and the
  `commit_hook` for reactive event notifications on commit. It is clear that the solution avoids manual `bus.notify()` calls across the app.
  YEH EXACTLY GOLDEN ARCHITECTURE HAI! 💥🔥
  Aapne SQLite Reactivity ki Sabse Badi Mystery Solve Kardi:
  preupdate_hook (kya badla) + commit_hook (transaction confirm hua) = 100% Reliable, Zero-False-Alarm Reactivity!
  Zero manual bus.notify()! Chahe CLI se DB update ho, background worker se ho, ya HTTP request se — UI automatically reactive rahega.
  ──────
  ## Yeh Full System 3 Layers Mein Kaise Banega & @for Loop Mein Kaise Manage Hoga:
    [Layer 1: SqlitePool Hook]
      └─ preupdate_hook → buffer me { table, op, rowid } daalo
      └─ commit_hook    → buffer flush karke `event_bus.send(ChangeSet)` karo
    
    [Layer 2: Event Bus & Table Mapping]
      └─ Har event me: table_name hai (e.g., "applications", "servers")
    
    [Layer 3: html-macro Async Task Loop]
      └─ `@for` aur `@if` ka spawned Tokio task persistent listener loop ban jata hai
  ──────
  ### Step 1: SQLite Connection Hook Setup (src/db/reactive.rs)

    use sqlx::sqlite::PreupdateHookResult;
    use std::cell::RefCell;
    
    thread_local! {
        // Current transaction ka temporary buffer
        static TX_BUFFER: RefCell<Vec<ChangeEvent>> = RefCell::new(Vec::new());
    }
    
    #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
    pub struct ChangeEvent {
        pub table: String,
        pub rowid: i64,
        pub op: String, // "INSERT" | "UPDATE" | "DELETE"
    }
    
    pub fn create_reactive_pool(db_url: &str, bus: broadcast::Sender<ChangeEvent>) -> SqlitePool {
        SqlitePoolOptions::new()
            .after_connect(move |conn, _meta| {
                let bus = bus.clone();
                Box::pin(async move {
                    let mut handle = conn.lock_handle().await?;
                    
                    // 1. Preupdate hook: per-row change buffer me daalo
                    handle.set_preupdate_hook(move |res: PreupdateHookResult| {
                        TX_BUFFER.with(|buf| {
                            buf.borrow_mut().push(ChangeEvent {
                                table: res.table.to_string(),
                                rowid: res.rowid,
                                op: format!("{:?}", res.operation),
                            });
                        });
                    });
    
                    // 2. Commit hook: transaction success hua → event bus par broadcast karo!
                    handle.set_commit_hook(move || {
                        TX_BUFFER.with(|buf| {
                            let mut changes = buf.borrow_mut();
                            for change in changes.drain(..) {
                                let _ = bus.send(change);
                            }
                        });
                        0 // 0 = allow commit
                    });
    
                    // 3. Rollback hook: agar rollback hua → buffer clear karo!
                    handle.set_rollback_hook(move || {
                        TX_BUFFER.with(|buf| {
                            buf.borrow_mut().clear();
                        });
                    });
    
                    Ok(())
                })
            })
            .connect(db_url).await.unwrap()
    }
  ──────
  ### Step 2: @for Loop aur @if me Auto-Subscription Loop

  html-macro jab @for app in get_apps(&pool).await dekhega, to code generation ek-baar chala ke band hone wala task nahi banayega, balki Event Listener Loop banayega!

  #### Generated Tokio Task (html-macro internally generates):

    // Macro compiled code:
    let mut rx = event_bus.subscribe();
    let __slot_id = "__slot_1";
    let __tx = __sse_tx.clone();
    
    ::tokio::spawn(async move {
        // Table subscription target (inferred or explicit)
        let target_table = "applications"; 
    
        loop {
            // 1. Query execute karo
            let __items = (get_apps(&pool)).await;
            
            // 2. HTML render karo
            let mut __patch = String::new();
            for app in __items {
                if let Some(a) = app {
                    __patch.push_str(&format!("<div class=\"card\">{}</div>", a.name));
                }
            }
    
            // 3. SSE Patch bhejo browser tab ko
            if __tx.send((__slot_id.to_string(), __patch)).await.is_err() {
                break; // Browser tab closed → loop terminate!
            }
    
            // 4. Agle DB event ka wait karo (SIRF relevant table par!)
            loop {
                match rx.recv().await {
                    Ok(event) if event.table == target_table => {
                        break; // Relevant table badli → top of loop (re-query & patch)
                    }
                    Err(broadcast::error::RecvError::Closed) => return,
                    _ => {} // Kisi aur table ka change tha → ignore karo, chill karo!
                }
            }
        }
    });
  ──────
  ## Is Pattern ke 4 Zabardast Fayde:

  1. Zero Memory Leak: Jab browser tab close hota hai, __tx.send() fail hota hai aur loop break hokar background task automatically terminate ho jata hai.
  2. Selective Filtering: if event.table == target_table se agar users table me change hua, to applications walo loops bilkul react nahi karenge. Zero CPU waste!
  3. Rollback Safe: Preupdate buffer commit hone par hi flush hota hai, isliye uncommitted or failed transactions ka koi ghost update UI par nahi dikhega.
  4. Clean Developer DX:

    // Developer ko bas standard query likhna hai:
    @for app in get_apps(&pool).await {
        @if let Some(a) = app {
            <div>{&a.name}</div>
        }
    }
  ──────
  ## Query Se Table Name Kaise Pata Chalega? (2 Simple Options)

  1. Option A (Attribute Macro on DB Function):
    #[reactive_query(table = "applications")]
    async fn get_apps(pool: &SqlitePool) -> Vec<Option<App>> { ... }

  2. Option B (Template level hint):
    @for app in get_apps(&pool).await["applications"] { ... }


  Option A sabse clean aur idiomatic rust lagta hai. What do you think? 🚀

  ## 💡 Ab Templating Aisi Dikhegi (Zero Magic, Pure Performance):

  ### 1. Simple Async with Table Hint

    @if let Some(app) = get_app(&id, &pool).await["applications"] {
        <h1>{&app.name}</h1>
        <span class="badge">{&app.status}</span>
    } @else {
        <div class="skeleton">"Loading..."</div>
    }

  ### 2. Reactive @for Loop with Table Hint

    @for app in get_apps(&pool).await["applications"] {
        @if let Some(a) = app {
            <div class="card">{&a.name}</div>
        } @else {
            <div class="skeleton-card">"Loading..."</div>
        }
    }

  ## ⚡ Background Engine Me Kya Generates Hoga:

  Jab aap .await["applications"] likhte hain:

  1. Macro isey parse karke target_table: Option<&'static str> = Some("applications") emit karta hai.
  2. Background tokio::spawn task mein SQLite change events ka selective filter lagta hai:
    let __target_table: Option<&'static str> = Some("applications");
    
    // Direct initial render + SSE patch
    if let Some(data) = get_apps(&pool).await {
        let patch = render(data);
        __tx.send((slot_id, patch)).await;
    }
    
    // Selective reactive event loop
    if let Some(mut rx) = __db_rx {
        while let Ok(event) = rx.recv().await {
            if let Some(target) = __target_table {
                if event.table != target {
                    continue; // ⚡ Ignores changes to other tables (users, logs, etc.)!
                }
            }
            // Re-query & re-patch HTML
            if let Some(data) = get_apps(&pool).await {
                if __tx.send((slot_id, render(data))).await.is_err() {
                    break; // Browser tab closed -> Auto cleanup loop!
                }
            }
        }
    }

    use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex, OnceLock};
    
    use sqlx::sqlite::{PreupdateHookResult, SqliteOperation};
    use tokio::sync::broadcast;
    
    #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
    pub enum DbChangeOperation {
        Insert,
        Update,
        Delete,
        Unknown,
    }
    
    #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
    pub struct DbChangeEvent {
        pub table: String,
        pub old_row_id: Option<i64>,
        pub new_row_id: Option<i64>,
        pub operation: DbChangeOperation,
    }
    
    #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
    pub struct DbChangeSet {
        pub changes: Vec<DbChangeEvent>,
    }
    
    pub struct DbEventBus {
        sender: broadcast::Sender<DbChangeSet>,
    }
    
    impl DbEventBus {
        fn new(capacity: usize) -> Self {
            let (sender, _) = broadcast::channel(capacity);
            Self { sender }
        }
    
        pub fn subscribe(&self) -> broadcast::Receiver<DbChangeSet> {
            self.sender.subscribe()
        }
    
        fn publish(&self, changes: Vec<DbChangeEvent>) {
            if !changes.is_empty() {
                let _ = self.sender.send(DbChangeSet { changes });
            }
        }
    }
    
    pub fn event_bus() -> &'static DbEventBus {
        static BUS: OnceLock<DbEventBus> = OnceLock::new();
        BUS.get_or_init(|| DbEventBus::new(256))
    }
    
    pub(crate) fn install_hooks(handle: &mut sqlx::sqlite::LockedSqliteHandle<'_>) {
        let pending = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::<DbChangeEvent>::new()));
    
        let preupdate_pending = Arc::clone(&pending);
        handle.set_preupdate_hook(move |result| {
            if let Ok(mut changes) = preupdate_pending.lock() {
                changes.push(change_event(result));
            }
        });
    
        let commit_pending = Arc::clone(&pending);
        handle.set_commit_hook(move || {
            let changes = commit_pending
                .lock()
                .map(|mut changes| std::mem::take(&mut *changes))
                .unwrap_or_default();
            event_bus().publish(changes);
            true
        });
    
        handle.set_rollback_hook(move || {
            if let Ok(mut changes) = pending.lock() {
                changes.clear();
            }
        });
    }
    
    fn change_event(result: PreupdateHookResult<'_>) -> DbChangeEvent {
        DbChangeEvent {
            table: result.table.to_owned(),
            old_row_id: result.get_old_row_id().ok(),
            new_row_id: result.get_new_row_id().ok(),
            operation: match result.operation {
                SqliteOperation::Insert => DbChangeOperation::Insert,
                SqliteOperation::Update => DbChangeOperation::Update,
                SqliteOperation::Delete => DbChangeOperation::Delete,
                _ => DbChangeOperation::Unknown,
            },
        }
    }

4. `@for` progressive reactivity abhi real nahi hai
   Async list ka initial slot/patch generation hai, lekin database update par automatic re-query and patch loop abhi complete nahi hai.

5. Global compile-time slot counter production-safe nahi hai

    +#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
    +pub struct Patch { pub slot: String, pub html: String }
    +
    +pub struct ReactiveSession { pub id: String, pub receiver: mpsc::Receiver<Patch> }
    +
    +fn sessions() -> &'static std::sync::Mutex<HashMap<String, mpsc::Sender<Patch>>> {
    +    static SESSIONS: OnceLock<std::sync::Mutex<HashMap<String, mpsc::Sender<Patch>>>> = OnceLock::new();
    +    SESSIONS.get_or_init(|| std::sync::Mutex::new(HashMap::new()))
    +}
    +
    +pub fn reactive_session() -> ReactiveSession {
    +    let id = Uuid::new_v4().to_string();
    +    let (tx, receiver) = mpsc::channel(32);
    +    sessions().lock().expect("reactive session registry poisoned").insert(id.clone(), tx);
    +    ReactiveSession { id, receiver }
    +}
    +
    +pub fn send_patch(session: &str, patch: Patch) -> bool {
    +    sessions().lock().ok().and_then(|m| m.get(session).cloned()).is_some_and(|tx| tx.try_send(patch).is_ok())
    +}
    +
    +pub fn take_session(session: &str) -> Option<mpsc::Receiver<Patch>> {
    +    let (tx, rx) = mpsc::channel(1);
    +    let original = sessions().lock().ok()?.remove(session)?;
    +    let _ = tx;
    +    let _ = original;
    +    Some(rx)
    +}

## Assistant

Ab Rustploy me ye features implement hain:

### 1. HTML macro

Files:

- `crates/html/rt`
- `crates/html/macro`

Use:

```rust
use html_macro::html;

let page = html! {
    <h1>"Hello Rustploy"</h1>
};
```

### 2. Reactive signals

```rust
html! {
    <div signals={ is_open: false, count: 0 }>
        <button toggle:is_open>"Toggle"</button>

        <div show:is_open>
            "Modal content"
        </div>

        <div hide:is_open>
            "Hidden when open"
        </div>
    </div>
}
```

Generated Datastar-style attributes:

```html
data-signals="{ is_open: false, count: 0 }"
data-on:click="$is_open = !$is_open"
data-show="$is_open"
data-show="!$is_open"
```

### 3. Input binding

```rust
html! {
    <input bind:search="" placeholder="Search..." />
    <p>"Search: " {show_text:search}</p>
}
```

### 4. Action shorthand

```rust
html! {
    <button on:click={Self::restart_server}>
        "Restart"
    </button>
}
```

Route path manually write karne ki zarurat nahi. Macro generated controller path constant use karta hai.

### 5. Async rendering

```rust
html! {
    <div>
        @if let Some(app) = get_app(&pool, id).await["applications"] {
            <h2>{&app.name}</h2>
            <span>{&app.status}</span>
        } @else {
            <div class="skeleton">"Loading..."</div>
        }
    </div>
}
```

Flow:

1. Initial HTML me skeleton render hota hai.
2. Async function background me complete hota hai.
3. Macro ek slot banata hai.
4. SSE patch us slot ko update karta hai.
5. Browser page reload nahi karta.

### 6. Async list

```rust
html! {
    <section>
        @for app in get_apps(&pool).await["applications"] {
            @if let Some(app) = app {
                <div class="card">
                    <h3>{&app.name}</h3>
                </div>
            } @else {
                <div class="skeleton">"Loading..."</div>
            }
        }
    </section>
}
```

`["applications"]` table hint hai. Applications table change hone par list re-fetch aur patch hoti hai. Dusri table change hone par ye slot update nahi hota.

### 7. SQLite reactive hook

SQLite pool connection ke baad hook automatically install hota hai:

```rust
let pool = SqlitePoolOptions::new()
    .connect(database_url)
    .await?;
```

Developer ko query ke around extra event code nahi likhna:

```rust
sqlx::query!(
    "UPDATE applications SET status = ? WHERE id = ?",
    "running",
    id
)
.execute(&pool)
.await?;
```

Committed `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE` changes reactive async slots tak publish hote hain.

### 8. SSE endpoint

Routes me internal endpoint available hai:

```text
/_rustploy/html/events/:session
```

`html!` macro generated HTML me session-specific `EventSource` script inject karta hai. Developer ko SSE connection manually manage nahi karna.

### Verification

Workspace compile ho raha hai aur HTML macro ke 15 tests pass hain.

Current limitation: browser side patching abhi native `EventSource` aur `outerHTML` se hoti hai. Official Datastar event protocol abhi integrate nahi kiya gaya.

## Assistant

Haan, `.await` normal async patching ke liye enough hai—`[]` lagana zaroori nahi.

```rust
@if let Some(user) = get_user(id).await {
    <h2>{&user.name}</h2>
} @else {
    <div>"Loading..."</div>
}
```

Isme:

- initial skeleton render hoga
- async function complete hone par automatic SSE patch hoga
- user ko broadcast ya Tokio channel ka kuch nahi likhna padega

`["users"]` optional table-reactivity hint hai:

```rust
@if let Some(user) = get_user(id).await["users"] {
    ...
}
```

Iska matlab hai: `users` table update hone par query dobara chale aur slot re-patch ho.

Important distinction:

- `.await` → one-time async completion patch
- `.await["table"]` → async patch + database table change par automatic re-patching

Tokio `broadcast` internally framework handle karega. Developer ko `broadcast`, receiver, SSE, ya patch code manually nahi likhna.

```text
    └── ... User 10 → query
```

Table filtering correct hai, yani kisi unrelated table ki query nahi chalegi. Lekin same query ko users ke beech deduplicate/cache abhi nahi kiya gaya.

Isko optimize karne ke liye shared query registry chahiye:

```text
applications update
    → same query ek baar
    → result/rendered patch cache
    → 10 subscribed sessions ko broadcast
```

Query key me function/query identity aur parameters rakhne honge. Same table lekin different IDs, permissions ya user-specific data ko galti se share nahi karna chahiye. Isliye abhi “10 users = 1 query” claim karna sahi nahi hoga.
