Bilkul, ye important optimization hai. Dhyan rahega:

- Same reactive query ke liye ek shared watcher/query task hoga.
- DB table update par query sirf ek baar chalegi.
- Uska rendered patch multiple subscribed sessions ko broadcast hoga.
- User-specific query parameters/permissions alag hone par sharing nahi hogi.
- Last subscriber disconnect hone par shared watcher cleanup hoga.

Current code abhi per-session re-query karta hai; isliye ise “already optimized” nahi maanenge. Is optimization ko next implementation step me include karna hoga.

    # Rustploy reactive Todo test
    
    Run from the repository root:
    
    ```bash
    nix develop -c cargo run -p rustploy-todo-test
    ```
    
    Open `http://127.0.0.1:3100` in two browser tabs. Adding, toggling, or deleting a
    todo publishes a `todos` table change and both tabs re-run their reactive slot.
    
    The test database is `crates/todo-test/todo-test.sqlite3` and is ignored by the
    repository's `*.sqlite3` rule.
    Add: /run/media/das/SSD/Devloper/rustploy/crates/todo-test/src/main.rs
    use std::{convert::Infallible, str::FromStr, time::Duration};
    
    use axum::{
        Form, Router,
        extract::{Path, State},
        http::StatusCode,
        response::{IntoResponse, Response, Sse, sse::Event},
        routing::{get, post},
    };
    use html_macro::html;
    use html_rt::Markup;
    use serde::Deserialize;
    use sqlx::{FromRow, SqlitePool, sqlite::{SqliteConnectOptions, SqlitePoolOptions}};
    
    #[derive(Clone)]
    struct AppState {
        pool: SqlitePool,
    }
    
    #[derive(FromRow)]
    struct Todo {
        id: i64,
        title: String,
        done: bool,
    }
    
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct NewTodo {
        title: String,
    }
    
    #[tokio::main]
    async fn main() {
        let database_url = std::env::var("TODO_DATABASE_URL")
            .unwrap_or_else(|_| "sqlite://crates/todo-test/todo-test.sqlite3".into());
        let options = SqliteConnectOptions::from_str(&database_url)
            .expect("invalid TODO_DATABASE_URL")
            .create_if_missing(true);
        let pool = SqlitePoolOptions::new()
            .max_connections(5)
            .connect_with(options)
            .await
            .expect("failed to open todo database");
    
        sqlx::query(
            "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS todos (\
             id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,\
             title TEXT NOT NULL,\
             done INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0)",
        )
        .execute(&pool)
        .await
        .expect("failed to create todos table");
    
        let app = Router::new()
            .route("/", get(index))
            .route("/todos", post(create_todo))
            .route("/todos/{id}/toggle", post(toggle_todo))
            .route("/todos/{id}/delete", post(delete_todo))
            .route("/_rustploy/html/events/{session}", get(html_events))
            .with_state(AppState { pool });
    
        let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:3100")
            .await
            .expect("failed to bind port 3100");
        println!("Todo test app: http://127.0.0.1:3100");
        axum::serve(listener, app).await.expect("server failed");
    }
    
    async fn index(State(state): State<AppState>) -> Markup {
        let pool = state.pool.clone();
        html! {
            <!DOCTYPE html>
            <html>
                <head>
                    <meta charset="utf-8" />
                    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
                    <title>"Rustploy reactive Todo test"</title>
                    <style>{r#"
                        body{font-family:system-ui;max-width:700px;margin:3rem auto;padding:0 1rem}
                        form,.todo{display:flex;gap:.6rem;margin:.7rem 0}.todo span{flex:1}
                        .done{text-decoration:line-through;opacity:.55}button,input{padding:.65rem}
                    "#}</style>
                </head>
                <body>
                    <h1>"Reactive Todo"</h1>
                    <p>"Do browser tabs kholo. Ek tab me change karo; todos slot dono tabs me patch hoga."</p>
                    <form method="post" action="/todos">
                        <input name="title" required placeholder="New todo" />
                        <button type="submit">"Add"</button>
                    </form>
    
                    @for todo in load_todos(pool.clone()).await["todos"] {
                        <div class="todo">
                            @if todo.done {
                                <span class="done">{&todo.title}</span>
                            } @else {
                                <span>{&todo.title}</span>
                            }
                            <form method="post" action={format!("/todos/{}/toggle", todo.id)}>
                                <button type="submit">"Toggle"</button>
                            </form>
                            <form method="post" action={format!("/todos/{}/delete", todo.id)}>
                                <button type="submit">"Delete"</button>
                            </form>
                        </div>
                    }
                </body>
            </html>
        }
    }
    
    async fn load_todos(pool: SqlitePool) -> Vec<Todo> {
        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(350)).await;
        sqlx::query_as::<_, Todo>("SELECT id, title, done FROM todos ORDER BY id DESC")
            .fetch_all(&pool)
            .await
            .unwrap_or_default()
    }
    
    async fn create_todo(State(state): State<AppState>, Form(todo): Form<NewTodo>) -> impl IntoResponse {
        if !todo.title.trim().is_empty() {
            let _ = sqlx::query("INSERT INTO todos(title) VALUES (?)")
                .bind(todo.title.trim())
                .execute(&state.pool)
                .await;
            html_rt::publish_table_changes(vec!["todos".into()]);
        }
        redirect_home()
    }
    
    async fn toggle_todo(State(state): State<AppState>, Path(id): Path<i64>) -> impl IntoResponse {
        let _ = sqlx::query("UPDATE todos SET done = NOT done WHERE id = ?")
            .bind(id)
            .execute(&state.pool)
            .await;
        html_rt::publish_table_changes(vec!["todos".into()]);
        redirect_home()
    }
    
    async fn delete_todo(State(state): State<AppState>, Path(id): Path<i64>) -> impl IntoResponse {
        let _ = sqlx::query("DELETE FROM todos WHERE id = ?")
            .bind(id)
            .execute(&state.pool)
            .await;
        html_rt::publish_table_changes(vec!["todos".into()]);
        redirect_home()
    }
    
    fn redirect_home() -> impl IntoResponse {
        (StatusCode::SEE_OTHER, [(axum::http::header::LOCATION, "/")])
    }
    
    async fn html_events(Path(session): Path<String>) -> Response {
        let Some(receiver) = html_rt::take_session(&session) else {
            return StatusCode::NOT_FOUND.into_response();
        };
        let stream = futures::stream::unfold(receiver, |mut receiver| async move {
            receiver.recv().await.map(|patch| {
                let payload = serde_json::json!({"slot": patch.slot, "html": patch.html});
                (Ok::<Event, Infallible>(Event::default().data(payload.to_string())), receiver)
            })
        });
        Sse::new(stream).into_response()
    }

    async fn main() {

            .await

    async fn init_database() -> SqlitePool {
        let database_url = std::env::var("TODO_DATABASE_URL")
            .unwrap_or_else(|_| "sqlite://crates/todo-test/todo-test.sqlite3".into());
        let options = SqliteConnectOptions::from_str(&database_url)
            .expect("invalid TODO_DATABASE_URL")
            .create_if_missing(true);
        let pool = SqlitePoolOptions::new()
            .max_connections(5)
            .after_connect(|connection, _| {
                Box::pin(async move {
                    let mut handle = connection.lock_handle().await?;
                    install_reactive_hooks(&mut handle);
                    Ok(())
                })
            })
            .connect_with(options)
            .await
            .expect("failed to open todo database");
    
        sqlx::query(
            "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS todos (\
             id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,\
             title TEXT NOT NULL,\
             done INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0)",
        )
        .execute(&pool)
        .await
        .expect("failed to create todos table");
        pool
    }
    
    fn install_reactive_hooks(handle: &mut sqlx::sqlite::LockedSqliteHandle<'_>) {
        let pending = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::<String>::new()));
        let writes = Arc::clone(&pending);
        handle.set_preupdate_hook(move |change| {
            if let Ok(mut tables) = writes.lock() {
                tables.push(change.table.to_owned());
            }
        });
        let commits = Arc::clone(&pending);
        handle.set_commit_hook(move || {
            if let Ok(mut tables) = commits.lock() {
                tables.sort_unstable();
                tables.dedup();
                html_rt::publish_table_changes(std::mem::take(&mut *tables));
            }
            true
        });
        handle.set_rollback_hook(move || {
            if let Ok(mut tables) = pending.lock() {
                tables.clear();
            }
        });
    }
    
    async fn load_todos(pool: SqlitePool) -> Vec<Todo> {
        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(350)).await;
        sqlx::query_as::<_, Todo>("SELECT id, title, done FROM todos ORDER BY id DESC")
            .fetch_all(&pool)
            .await
            .unwrap_or_default()
    }
    
    fn redirect_page() -> impl IntoResponse {
        (
            StatusCode::SEE_OTHER,
            [(axum::http::header::LOCATION, "/todo")],
        )
    }
    
    #[get("/_rustploy/html/events/{session}")]
    async fn html_events(Path(session): Path<String>) -> Response {
        let Some(receiver) = html_rt::take_session(&session) else {
            return StatusCode::NOT_FOUND.into_response();
        };
        let stream = futures::stream::unfold(receiver, |mut receiver| async move {
            receiver.recv().await.map(|patch| {
                let payload = serde_json::json!({"slot": patch.slot, "html": patch.html});
                (
                    Ok::<Event, Infallible>(Event::default().data(payload.to_string())),
                    receiver,
                )
            })
        });
        Sse::new(stream).into_response()
    }

    use std::{str::FromStr, sync::{Arc, Mutex}};
    use sqlx::{SqlitePool, sqlite::{SqliteConnectOptions, SqlitePoolOptions}};
    
    pub async fn connect() -> SqlitePool {
        let url = std::env::var("TODO_DATABASE_URL")
            .unwrap_or_else(|_| "sqlite://crates/todo-test/todo-test.sqlite3".into());
        let options = SqliteConnectOptions::from_str(&url)
            .expect("invalid TODO_DATABASE_URL")
            .create_if_missing(true);
        let pool = SqlitePoolOptions::new()
            .max_connections(5)
            .after_connect(|connection, _| Box::pin(async move {
                let mut handle = connection.lock_handle().await?;
                install_hooks(&mut handle);
                Ok(())
            }))
            .connect_with(options).await.expect("failed to open todo database");
        sqlx::query("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS todos (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, title TEXT NOT NULL, done INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0)")
            .execute(&pool).await.expect("failed to create todos table");
        pool
    }
    
    fn install_hooks(handle: &mut sqlx::sqlite::LockedSqliteHandle<'_>) {
        let pending = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::<String>::new()));
        let writes = Arc::clone(&pending);
        handle.set_preupdate_hook(move |change| {
            if let Ok(mut tables) = writes.lock() { tables.push(change.table.to_owned()); }
        });
        let commits = Arc::clone(&pending);
        handle.set_commit_hook(move || {
            if let Ok(mut tables) = commits.lock() {
                tables.sort_unstable(); tables.dedup();
                html_rt::publish_table_changes(std::mem::take(&mut *tables));
            }
            true
        });
        handle.set_rollback_hook(move || {
            if let Ok(mut tables) = pending.lock() { tables.clear(); }
        });
    }

    use std::convert::Infallible;
    use axum::{extract::Path, response::{IntoResponse, Response, Sse, sse::Event}, http::StatusCode};
    
    #[auto_route::get("/_rustploy/html/events/{session}")]
    pub async fn events(Path(session): Path<String>) -> Response {
        let Some(receiver) = html_rt::take_session(&session) else { return StatusCode::NOT_FOUND.into_response(); };
        let stream = futures::stream::unfold(receiver, |mut receiver| async move {
            receiver.recv().await.map(|patch| {
                let data = serde_json::json!({"slot": patch.slot, "html": patch.html});
                (Ok::<Event, Infallible>(Event::default().data(data.to_string())), receiver)
            })
        });
        Sse::new(stream).into_response()
    }

## User

## Assistant

Kaafi optimize kar sakte hain. Abhi syntax clean hai, lekin runtime architecture me kuch important improvements baaki hain.

Sabse useful optimizations:

1. Shared query deduplication

Abhi 10 browser sessions same query listen karenge to table update par query 10 baar chal sakti hai.

Desired:

```text
same query + same parameters
        ↓
query only once
        ↓
result broadcast to 10 sessions
```

Query key:

```rust
QueryKey {
    function: "load_todos",
    arguments: hash(...),
    table: "todos",
}
```

2. No-page-reload actions

Abhi HTML forms redirect ke through current tab reload karte hain. Better syntax:

```rust
<button on:click={Self::toggle(todo.id)}>
    "Toggle"
</button>
```

Mutation complete hogi, SQLite hook fire hoga aur reactive list patch ho jayegi—redirect/page reload nahi.

Create:

```rust
<input bind:title="" />
<button on:click={Self::create($title)}>"Add"</button>
```

3. Automatic table detection

Abhi:

```rust
load_todos(pool).await["todos"]
```

Future syntax:

```rust
load_todos(pool).await
```

SQL/query metadata se framework automatically `todos` subscription detect kare.

4. Session cleanup

Agar generated page ka SSE connection kabhi open nahi hua, session registry me receiver reh sakta hai. Iske liye:

- session TTL
- disconnected-session cleanup
- last subscriber par watcher cancellation

add karna chahiye.

5. Patch deduplication

Re-query ke baad HTML same nikla to patch send nahi karna:

```text
new_html_hash == previous_html_hash
    → skip SSE patch
```

6. Update coalescing

Ek transaction me 100 rows update hon:

```text
100 SQLite events
    → one table notification
    → one query
    → one patch
```

Commit hook table names deduplicate karta hai, lekin rapid separate commits ke liye 10–30ms debounce useful hoga.

7. Official Datastar patch events

Abhi native:

```javascript
EventSource + outerHTML
```

Use ho raha hai. Better:

```text
event: datastar-patch-elements
```

Isse custom injected JavaScript kam hoga aur Datastar officially DOM merging handle karega.

Priority order:

```text
shared query dedup
→ no-reload function actions
→ session cleanup
→ patch hash dedup
→ official Datastar events
→ automatic table inference
```

Sabse pehle shared query dedup aur no-reload actions karne chahiye; performance aur developer experience me sabse bada improvement wahi dega.

## User

ye flicker kyo nahi hua jara bata sakte ho tum

## Assistant

Flicker isliye nahi hua kyunki navbar click par browser ne naya document load nahi kiya.

Normal navigation me:

```text
click link
→ current document destroy
→ browser blank/white state
→ CSS aur JS dobara load
→ new HTML render
```

Is process ke beech visible flicker aa sakta hai.

Ab hamara flow:

```text
click link
→ event.preventDefault()
→ background fetch("/todo/about")
→ response HTML parse
→ sirf #app element replace
→ history.pushState() se URL update
```

Core code:

```javascript
event.preventDefault();

const response = await fetch(link.href);
const nextDocument = new DOMParser().parseFromString(
    await response.text(),
    "text/html",
);

const nextApp = nextDocument.querySelector("#app");

document.querySelector("#app").replaceWith(nextApp);
history.pushState({}, "", link.href);
```

Isme `<body>` aur poora browser document destroy nahi hota. Tailwind aur existing JavaScript loaded rehte hain. Sirf content container replace hota hai, isliye white flash nahi aata.

Lekin current implementation basic prototype hai:

- Back button par abhi `location.reload()` hota hai, wahan flicker aa sakta hai.
- Previous page ka SSE connection cleanup/reconnection properly manage nahi ho raha.
- Fast repeated clicks aur failed requests ka handling nahi hai.
- New page ke scripts automatically execute nahi honge.
- Official Datastar navigation/patch event use nahi ho raha.

Production version me navigation ko runtime feature banana chahiye, Todo page ke inline script me nahi.

## User

htmx realtime handle kar satak hai na chizo kuske pas bhi hai na jara batoo kay diff ayea dono ke bitch me

## Assistant

Haan, HTMX realtime handle kar sakta hai. Uske paas SSE aur WebSocket extensions hain. Lekin HTMX aur Datastar ka primary design thoda different hai.

| Feature | HTMX | Datastar / Rustploy approach |
|---|---|---|
| Normal request | Request karke HTML swap | Action request + SSE patch |
| Navigation | `hx-get` + `hx-target` | SSE/element patch navigation |
| Realtime | SSE extension separately | SSE core architecture |
| Client state | Limited; Alpine.js often added | Built-in signals |
| DB reactivity | Developer ko event trigger karna hoga | SQLite hook automatic trigger kar sakta hai |
| Long-running stream | Possible | Naturally designed for streaming |
| Multiple patches | SSE events se possible | Ek action ke response me continuous patches |
| Loading state | `hx-indicator` | Signals/async slot |
| Optimistic UI | Extra JavaScript | Signals ke through easier |

HTMX navigation:

```html
<a
    hx-get="/about"
    hx-target="#app"
    hx-push-url="true"
>
    About
</a>
```

Isme:

1. HTMX background me `/about` request karega.
2. Response HTML receive karega.
3. `#app` replace karega.
4. URL update karega.
5. Full page reload nahi hoga.

Ye wahi behavior hai jo humne custom JavaScript se banaya. HTMX me pehle se available hai.

HTMX realtime example:

```html
<div
    hx-ext="sse"
    sse-connect="/events"
    sse-swap="todos"
>
    Todo list
</div>
```

Server event:

```text
event: todos
data: <div>Updated todos...</div>
```

Event milne par HTMX element swap kar dega.

Datastar style:

```html
<button data-on:click="@post('/todos/1/toggle')">
    Toggle
</button>
```

Server ek SSE stream se patches bhej sakta hai:

```text
event: datastar-patch-elements
data: elements <div id="todos">...</div>
```

Main difference:

```text
HTMX:
request → response HTML → target swap

Datastar:
action → SSE stream → signals/element patches
```

HTMX realtime kar sakta hai, lekin realtime uska optional extension hai. Datastar me SSE streaming aur signals central concepts hain.

Rustploy ke liye Datastar approach useful hai kyunki hamara desired flow hai:

```text
SQLite commit
→ table event
→ reactive query
→ SSE patch
→ exact component update
```

HTMX use karte to bhi backend ka SQLite hook, query subscription aur event bus hume banana padta. HTMX mainly browser-side swap simplify karta; automatic database reactivity nahi deta.

Practical decision:

- Simple CRUD, forms aur navigation chahiye: HTMX bahut mature aur easy hai.
- Signals, streaming, live metrics, logs aur server-driven reactivity chahiye: Datastar better fit hai.
- Rustploy ko dono simultaneously use nahi karne chahiye; overlapping attributes aur request handling unnecessary complexity create karegi.

Hamare use case me Datastar fit better hai, lekin navigation aur patch protocol ko custom JavaScript ke bajaye official Datastar mechanism par shift karna chahiye.

Haan—current custom navigation JavaScript ke comparison me HTMX + official extensions zyada maintainable hoga.

HTMX already handle karta hai:

- Partial page navigation
- Targeted element swapping
- Browser history
- Form submission
- Loading indicators
- Request cancellation
- SSE extension
- WebSocket extension
- Error handling
- CSS transitions

Navbar directly:

```rust
<input
    type="checkbox"
    hx-post={self.toggle(todo.id)}
    hx-swap="none"
/>
```

SQLite hook event ke baad SSE:

```html
<div
    id="todos"
    hx-ext="sse"
    sse-connect="/events"
    sse-swap="todos"
>
```

Flow:

```text
HTMX action
→ SQLite mutation
→ commit hook
→ reactive query
→ SSE event
→ HTMX exact component swap
```

Lekin HTMX automatic DB reactivity provide nahi karta. Ye Rustploy ka kaam rahega:

- SQLite hooks
- Table subscriptions
- Query deduplication
- Re-query
- HTML rendering
- SSE event broadcasting

HTMX browser-side plumbing replace karega.

Main trade-off:

| Requirement | Better choice |
|---|---|
| Forms/navigation maintainability | HTMX |
| Mature partial swaps/history | HTMX |
| Client-side signals | Datastar |
| Streaming-first architecture | Datastar |
| Lowest custom JavaScript | HTMX |
| Toggle/show/bind reactive state | Datastar |
| Existing ecosystem/documentation | HTMX |

Rustploy ke liye practical maintainable architecture:

```text
Rustploy backend reactivity
+ HTMX navigation/forms
+ HTMX SSE extension
```

Phir macro clean syntax ko HTMX me compile kare:

```rust
<a nav={self.about}>"About"</a>
<button post={self.delete(todo.id)}>"Delete"</button>

```

Generated output:

```html
hx-get
hx-post
hx-target
hx-push-url
hx-ext="sse"
```

Meri recommendation: agar primary goal maintainability, CRUD, navigation aur server-rendered realtime hai, HTMX use karo. Datastar signals tab rakho jab genuinely heavy client state—modal, tabs, filters, optimistic UI—chahiye. Dono ko poori tarah mix karna avoid karna chahiye.

Datastar:

HTMX successfully handle kar sakta hai:

- Component-level swaps

Datastar ki additional strength signals hain:

```text
$is_open
$search
$count
```

Aur server SSE se signals bhi patch ho sakte hain. HTMX me similar client state ke liye often Alpine.js ya small JavaScript add kiya jata hai.

Rustploy ke current Todo/realtime requirements ke liye HTMX fully capable hai:

```text
SQLite commit
→ Rust event bus
→ one SSE connection
→ HTMX named event
→ exact todo component swap
```

Is use case me Datastar technically required nahi hai. HTMX zyada mature aur maintainable choice ho sakta hai. Datastar tab materially better hoga jab server-driven signals aur fine-grained client state central requirement ho.

## Assistant

HTMX migration branch ready:

```text
feature/htmx-realtime
```

Abhi sirf branch switch hua hai; existing implementation untouched hai.

Implementation order:

1. HTMX assets add karna

```html
<script src="https://unpkg.com/htmx.org"></script>
<script src="https://unpkg.com/htmx-ext-sse"></script>
```

2. Macro syntax mapping

Developer syntax:

```rust
<button post={self.toggle(todo.id)}>
    "Toggle"
</button>
```

Generated:

```html
<button
    hx-post="/todo/42/toggle"
    hx-swap="none">
    Toggle
</button>
```

Navigation:

```rust
<a nav={self.about}>"About"</a>
```

Generated:

```html
<a
    hx-get="/todo/about"
    hx-target="#app"
    hx-push-url="true">
    About
</a>
```

3. Custom JavaScript remove karna

- `NAV_SCRIPT` remove
- custom `fetch + DOMParser` navigation remove
- Datastar client script remove

4. SSE response HTMX format me convert karna

Current:

```text
data: {"slot":"...","html":"..."}
```

New:

```text
event: todos
data: <div id="todos">...</div>
```

5. Async slot output

Generated wrapper:

```html
<div
    id="todos"
    hx-ext="sse"
    sse-connect="/_rustploy/html/events/session"
    sse-swap="todos">
    Loading...
</div>
```

6. SQLite reactive flow same rahega

```text
SQLite commit
→ preupdate/commit hook
→ table event
→ query rerun
→ HTMX SSE event
→ exact target swap
```

7. Todo app migration

- Native HTMX navigation
- `hx-post` actions
- `hx-target`
- `hx-swap`
- HTMX SSE todo list
- No manual redirect for toggle/create/delete

8. Verification

```bash
cargo test -p html-macro --tests
cargo check -p rustploy-todo-test
cargo check --workspace
just todo-dev
```

```text
.idea/rustploy.iml
.direnv/flake-profile
src/services/alert/event_state.rs
```

Implementation isi `feature/htmx-realtime` branch par hogi.

HTMX ke paas navbar ke liye sabse useful feature `hx-boost` hai.

Parent par ek baar:

```rust
<body
    hx-boost="true"
    hx-target="#app"
    hx-select="#app"
    hx-swap="outerHTML"
    hx-push-url="true"
>
```

Uske baad navbar links bilkul normal:

```rust
<nav>
    <a href={self.page}>"Home"</a>
    <a href={self.about}>"About"</a>
</nav>
```

Har link par ye sab repeat nahi karna:

```html
hx-get
hx-target
hx-select
hx-swap
hx-push-url
```

HTMX parent se automatically handle karega:

```text
normal link click
→ background GET
→ response se #app select
→ current #app replace
→ URL/history update
→ no full-page reload
```

Form bhi `hx-boost` se enhance ho sakta hai:

```rust
<form method="post" action={self.create}>
```

Lekin reactive mutation me hum explicitly `post={self.create}` rakh sakte hain, kyunki usme `hx-swap="none"` chahiye.

HTMX ke relevant features:

- `hx-boost`: normal links/forms ko AJAX navigation banata hai.
- `hx-target`: response kahan render hoga.
- `hx-select`: response se kaunsa element lena hai.
- `hx-swap`: element kaise replace hoga.
- `hx-push-url`: browser URL/history update.
- History cache: Back/Forward navigation handle karta hai.
- `hx-indicator`: request ke time loader.
- `transition:true`: View Transition animation.
- `hx-preserve`: kisi element ko swaps ke beech preserve karna.
- SSE extension: realtime server events.

HTMX automatic active navbar class nahi deta. Active link ke liye server current path dekhega ya `aria-current="page"` generate karega.

Best Todo structure:

```rust
<body
    hx-boost="true"
    hx-target="#app"
    hx-select="#app"
    hx-swap="outerHTML"
    hx-push-url="true"
>
    <div id="app">
        {self.navbar()}
        // page content
    </div>
</body>
```

Navbar:

```rust
            <a href={self.page}>"Home"</a>

        </nav>
    }
}
```

Is approach me `nav={...}` shorthand ki bhi zarurat nahi rahegi; normal `href={self.page}` enough hoga.

## User

why i choose datastar and why i choose htmx diff why not for both of them

## Assistant

Dono server-driven HTML frameworks hain, lekin unka focus different hai.

| Requirement | HTMX | Datastar |
|---|---|---|
| Forms and CRUD | Excellent | Excellent |
| Page navigation | Mature and simple | Possible, less central |
| Partial HTML replacement | Core feature | Core feature |
| Browser history | Built-in | More manual/framework-driven |
| Realtime SSE | Extension | Core design |
| Multiple streaming patches | Possible | Natural |
| Client-side state/signals | Minimal | Built-in |
| Optimistic UI | Extra JS/Alpine often needed | Signals ke saath natural |
| Ecosystem | Large and mature | Smaller and newer |
| Learning/debugging | Easier | More reactive concepts |
| Custom backend engine | Less required | Streaming engine important |

### HTMX kyun choose karein?

Jab application primarily ye ho:

```text
form submit
→ server response
→ HTML swap
```

Examples:

- Admin panels
- CRUD applications
- Dashboards
- Settings pages
- Search/filter
- Pagination
- Normal multi-page navigation

HTMX syntax:

```html
<button
    hx-post="/todos/1/toggle"
    hx-target="#todos">
    Toggle
</button>
```

HTMX browser navigation, form encoding, history, targeting aur swapping mature tarike se handle karta hai.

### Datastar kyun choose karein?

Jab application primarily ye ho:

```text
long-running SSE stream
→ signals and HTML continuously update
```

Examples:

- Live deployment logs
- Build progress
- Container metrics
- Realtime monitoring
- Collaborative state
- Optimistic interfaces
- Server-controlled client signals

Datastar syntax:

```html
<div data-signals="{ count: 0 }">
    <button data-on:click="$count++">Increment</button>
</div>
```

Server signal patches bhi bhej sakta hai:

```text
$count = 42
$status = "running"
```

### Dono ek saath kyun nahi?

Technically use kar sakte ho, lekin same element par dono ko mix karna risky hai:

```html
<button
    hx-post="/toggle"
    data-on:click="@post('/toggle')">
```

Ek click par:

- HTMX request bhejega
- Datastar bhi request bhej sakta hai
- Duplicate mutation ho sakti hai
- Dono DOM swap karne ki koshish karenge
- SSE connections duplicate ho sakte hain
- Loading/error state inconsistent ho sakta hai

Dono libraries overlap karti hain:

```text
requests
DOM patching
SSE
form handling
events
```

Isliye poori application me dono simultaneously use karna usually unnecessary complexity hai.

### Kya limited hybrid possible hai?

Haan, strict ownership boundaries ke saath:

```text
HTMX:
- navigation
- forms
- CRUD
- page swaps

Datastar:
- isolated live terminal
- metrics widget
- streaming deployment component
```

Example:

```text
Page shell → HTMX owns
Live logs component → Datastar owns
```

Lekin components nested nahi hone chahiye aur dono ko same DOM region patch nahi karna chahiye.

### Rustploy ke liye choice

Rustploy ke features do categories me hain:

```text
CRUD/navigation:
applications, settings, users, forms
→ HTMX better

Realtime:
logs, metrics, deployment progress, DB-reactive components
→ Datastar better
```

Phir bhi framework ko maintainable rakhne ke liye main ek primary library choose karunga.

- Simplicity, maturity aur normal web patterns priority hain → HTMX
- Realtime streaming, signals aur server-driven reactive UI product ka core hai → Datastar

Rustploy me live logs, metrics aur deployments important hain, lekin majority UI CRUD/navigation bhi hai. Practical choice HTMX primary rakhna hai because SSE se realtime requirements bhi handle ho jayengi. Datastar tab choose karna better hota agar signals-based client state Rustploy ka central programming model hota.

    +
    +    #[tokio::test]
    +    async fn committed_write_is_visible_before_reactive_notification() {
    +        let mut connection = SqliteConnection::connect("sqlite::memory:").await.unwrap();
    +        sqlx::query(
    +            "CREATE TABLE todos (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT NOT NULL, done INTEGER NOT NULL)",
    +        )
    +        .execute(&mut connection)
    +        .await
    +        .unwrap();
    +
    +        {
    +            let mut handle = connection.lock_handle().await.unwrap();
    +            install_hooks(&mut handle);
    +        }
    +
    +        let mut changes = html_rt::subscribe_table_changes();
    +        sqlx::query("INSERT INTO todos (id, title, done) VALUES (1, 'test', 0)")
    +            .execute(&mut connection)
    +            .await
    +            .unwrap();
    +
    +        let tables = tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(1), changes.recv())
    +            .await
    +            .expect("reactive notification timed out")
    +            .expect("reactive channel closed");
    +        assert!(tables.iter().any(|table| table == "todos"));
    +
    +        let done: i64 = sqlx::query_scalar("SELECT done FROM todos WHERE id = 1")
    +            .fetch_one(&mut connection)
    +            .await
    +            .unwrap();
    +        assert_eq!(done, 0);
    +    }

## Assistant

Toggle issue solve ho gaya.

Root cause:

- `sqlx::set_commit_hook` mein `false` ka matlab rollback hota hai.
- Code `false` return kar raha tha, isliye toggle/update commit hi nahi ho raha tha.
- SQLite worker thread se direct `tokio::spawn` karne par reactor panic aa raha tha.

Fix:

- Commit hook ab `true` return karta hai.
- Tokio runtime handle pehle capture hota hai.
- Reactive notification actual commit visible hone ke baad publish hoti hai.
- Production DB aur Todo test DB dono update kiye.
- Regression test add kiya.

Verification:

- Todo test compile passed.
- Rustploy compile passed.
- HTML macro ke saare 15 tests passed.
- SQLite commit/reactive notification test passed.
- Commit: `733a445e fix: publish sqlite changes after successful commit`

## User

can we do with this from react no datastore no htmx koi asa rasta bana sakte hai

## Assistant

Haan, bilkul. Datastar/HTMX ke bina React-jaisa system bana sakte hain.

Best architecture:

- Rust `html!` macro initial HTML render karega.
- Har reactive block ko unique `data-slot` milega.
- Browser mein apna tiny `rustploy.js` runtime hoga.
- Runtime ek SSE connection open karega.
- Async `.await` complete hone par server sirf us slot ka HTML patch bhejega.
- `on:click`, `toggle`, `bind`, filters plain JS runtime handle karega.
- Full page kabhi re-render nahi hoga.
- SQLite change ke baad sirf affected component update hoga.

Example developer syntax same rahega:

```rust
html! {
    <button on:click={self.toggle(todo.id)}>
        "Toggle"
    }

    @for todo in self.load_todos().await["todos"] {
        <TodoCard todo={todo} />
    }
}
```

Browser side sirf custom runtime:

```js
const source = new EventSource("/_rustploy/events");

source.onmessage = event => {
  const patch = JSON.parse(event.data);
  document.querySelector(
    `[data-slot="${patch.slot}"]`
  ).outerHTML = patch.html;
};
```

React ka alternative Rust side par Leptos/Dioxus bhi hai, lekin woh hydration, WASM bundle aur client-side component model laayega. Aapke current Rust HTML macro ke liye custom lightweight runtime zyada suitable hai—React jaisa behavior, React ka heavy bundle nahi.

## User

not jasa react ke sath hi i want compile time safety easy to use like heaven asa

## Assistant

Haan—React ke saath hi “heaven-level” DX bana sakte hain. Best solution hoga:

```text
Rust controller macros
        ↓ compile-time generation
Typed TypeScript client + React hooks
        ↓
React UI
```

Rust backend:

```rust
#[controller]
impl TodoController {
    #[query(reactive = "todos")]
    async fn todos(&self) -> Vec<Todo> {
        // query
    }

    #[action]
    async fn toggle(&self, id: TodoId) {
        // update
    }

    #[action]
    async fn create(&self, input: NewTodo) {
        // insert
    }
}
```

Macro automatically TypeScript hooks generate karega:

```tsx
function TodoPage() {
  const todos = useQuery(TodoController.todos);

  return (
    <>
      {todos.map(todo => (
        <TodoRow
          key={todo.id}
          todo={todo}
          onToggle={() => TodoController.toggle(todo.id)}
        />
      ))}
    </>
  );
}
```

Developer ko ye sab nahi likhna padega:

```tsx
fetch("/todo/12/toggle")
axios.post(...)
useEffect(...)
new EventSource(...)
queryClient.invalidateQueries(...)
```

Generated client internally handle karega:

- Typed function calls
- Rust → TypeScript generated types
- Routes
- Serialization
- Loading/error state
- SSE subscription
- Reactive SQLite updates
- React cache update
- Reconnection
- Component cleanup

Example “heaven” hook:

```tsx
const todos = TodoController.todos.use({
  loading: <TodoSkeleton />,
  error: <TodoError />,
});
```

Action:

```tsx
<input
  type="checkbox"
  checked={todo.done}
  onChange={() => TodoController.toggle(todo.id)}
/>
```

Create:

```tsx
TodoController.create({
  title,
});
```

Agar wrong argument diya:

```tsx
TodoController.toggle("wrong");
```

TypeScript compile-time error dega, kyunki Rust ka `TodoId` generated TypeScript type se linked hoga.

Reactive flow:

```text
React calls TodoController.toggle(id)
                 ↓
Rust action executes SQL
                 ↓
SQLite hook detects "todos"
                 ↓
SSE sends typed update
                 ↓
Generated React store updates
                 ↓
Only subscribed components re-render
```

Is approach mein:

- React rahega
- Datastar nahi
- HTMX nahi
- Manual endpoint nahi
- Manual `fetch` nahi
- Full-page render nahi
- Compile-time typed arguments/returns
- React ka normal ecosystem available

Ek limitation: Rust compiler directly `.tsx` verify nahi karega. Rust macros TypeScript contracts generate karenge, aur TypeScript compiler frontend usage verify karega. End-to-end compile-time safety ke liye ye React ke saath sabse practical architecture hai.

## User

are yaha jase hai direct sala database se hi listen kar liye hai

## Assistant

Haan, wahi architecture React ke saath bhi rahega. React database ko directly access nahi karega; Rustploy ka SQLite hook database ko directly listen karega aur React automatically updated data receive karega.

Rust:

```rust
#[reactive_query(table = "todos")]
async fn todos(&self) -> Vec<Todo> {
    sqlx::query_as("SELECT * FROM todos ORDER BY id DESC")
        .fetch_all(&self.pool)
        .await
        .unwrap()
}
```

React:

```tsx
function TodoPage() {
  const todos = useRustploy(TodoController.todos);

  return todos.map(todo => (
    <TodoItem
      todo={todo}
      onToggle={() => TodoController.toggle(todo.id)}
    />
  ));
}
```

Internal flow:

```text
SQLite UPDATE
    ↓
sqlite preupdate/commit hook
    ↓
Rustploy sees "todos" changed
    ↓
Registered todos() query runs
    ↓
Typed result SSE se browser ko milta hai
    ↓
React store update
    ↓
Only TodoPage/TodoItem re-render
```

Developer ko kuch manually listen nahi karna:

```tsx
// Nahi chahiye
new EventSource(...)
useEffect(...)
fetch(...)
invalidateQueries(...)
setInterval(...)
```

Parameterized query bhi possible:

```rust
#[reactive_query(table = "todos")]
async fn todos_for_user(&self, user_id: UserId) -> Vec<Todo> {
    // ...
}
```

```tsx
const todos = useRustploy(
  TodoController.todosForUser(user.id)
);
```

Optimization bhi waise hi hogi:

```text
10 users same todos query listen kar rahe hain
              ↓
SQLite event sirf ek baar
              ↓
Identical query key sirf ek baar execute
              ↓
Result sab 10 subscribers ko broadcast
```

Different parameters honge to alag query keys:

```text
todosForUser(1) → one shared query
todosForUser(2) → another shared query
```

Actions normal typed function calls lagenge:

```tsx
await TodoController.toggle(todo.id);
await TodoController.create({ title });
```

Isliye final system hoga: React UI + TypeScript compile safety + Rust actions + direct SQLite hooks + automatic reactive query cache. Datastar aur HTMX dono ki zarurat nahi.

## User

aur koi best way

## Assistant

Aapke use-case ke liye isse better practical architecture hoga:

## Rustploy Live Queries + React Store

React ko HTML patch mat bhejo. Server typed data patches bheje aur React apna DOM manage kare.

Rust:

```rust
#[live_query]
async fn todos(&self) -> Live<Vec<Todo>> {
    sqlx::query_as("SELECT * FROM todos ORDER BY id DESC")
        .fetch_all(&self.pool)
        .await?
}
```

Macro SQL se tables automatically identify kare:

```text
SELECT ... FROM todos
                ↑
dependency = "todos"
```

React:

```tsx
const todos = Todo.todos.use();
```

Actions:

```tsx
Todo.toggle(todo.id);
Todo.create({ title });
```

Generated TypeScript API:

```ts
Todo.todos.use(): LiveResult<Todo[]>
Todo.toggle(id: number): Promise<void>
Todo.create(input: NewTodo): Promise<void>
```

## Internal design

```text
SQLite hook
    ↓
Table "todos" changed
    ↓
Rustploy Query Registry
    ↓
Only dependent live queries execute
    ↓
Result cache/diff
    ↓
One SSE/WebSocket connection
    ↓
React external store
    ↓
Only subscribed components render
```

React integration ke liye `useSyncExternalStore` best rahega:

```tsx
function useLiveQuery<T>(query: LiveQuery<T>): T {
  return useSyncExternalStore(
    query.subscribe,
    query.getSnapshot,
    query.getServerSnapshot,
  );
}
```

Yeh React ka official external reactive-store mechanism hai. Isme manual `useEffect`, loading race ya duplicate subscriptions nahi honge.

## Important optimization

Same query ko 10 users listen kar rahe hain:

```text
SQLite event: 1
Query execution: 1
Cached result: 1
Broadcast subscribers: 10
```

Parameterized query:

```tsx
Todo.byUser.use(userId);
```

Server query key:

```text
Todo.byUser(userId=42)
```

Same parameters wale subscribers query result share karenge.

## Data diff bhejna

Har update par complete array bhejna zaroori nahi:

```json
{
  "query": "Todo.todos",
  "operation": "update",
  "key": 12,
  "value": {
    "id": 12,
    "done": true
  }
}
```

React store sirf todo `12` update karega. Proper keys/memoization ke saath sirf corresponding `TodoItem` render hoga.

## Alternatives

- GraphQL subscriptions: standard hai, lekin schema/resolvers/subscription boilerplate zyada.
- TanStack Query + SSE invalidation: implement karna easy, lekin har client refetch kar sakta hai.
- ElectricSQL/PowerSync: powerful local-first sync, lekin Rustploy SQLite server use-case ke liye heavy.
- Leptos/Dioxus: Rust compile safety strongest, lekin React nahi rahega.

Meri recommendation: custom Rustploy Live Query compiler + generated TypeScript client + React `useSyncExternalStore` + single SSE/WebSocket connection. Yeh React-native bhi hai, compile-safe bhi, aur direct SQLite reactivity bhi preserve karta hai.

## User

kike sath jana chaiye tumhare hisab se

## User

kike sath jana chaiye tumhare hisab se you have 3 optin react,htmx,datastar which you should prefer

## Assistant

Mere hisaab se Rustploy ko **React ke saath jaana chahiye**.

Priority:

1. React
2. Datastar
3. HTMX

React best kyun hai:

- Typed generated client bana sakte hain.
- Actions normal function calls jaise lagenge:

```tsx
Todo.create({ title });
Todo.toggle(todo.id);
```

- Reactive SQLite queries clean hooks banengi:

```tsx
const todos = Todo.todos.use();
```

- `useSyncExternalStore` se React-native realtime updates milenge.
- Server identical queries deduplicate kar sakta hai: 10 listeners, 1 query execution.
- Components, forms, dialogs, tables aur ecosystem mature hain.
- HTML string patching aur manually executed scripts ki problems nahi hongi.
- Sirf subscribed components re-render honge.

Final developer experience:

```rust
#[live_query]
async fn todos(&self) -> Vec<Todo> {
    // SQL query
}

#[action]
async fn toggle(&self, id: i64) {
    // SQL update
}
```

```tsx
function TodoPage() {
  const todos = Todo.todos.use();

  return todos.map(todo => (
    <TodoRow
      key={todo.id}
      todo={todo}
      onToggle={() => Todo.toggle(todo.id)}
    />
  ));
}
```

Datastar second choice hai. Server-rendered apps aur minimal JavaScript ke liye achha hai, lekin complex application UI mein signals, SSE HTML patches aur client state coordination framework-specific hoti jayegi.

HTMX third choice hai. CRUD/admin panels ke liye reliable hai, lekin database-driven continuous reactivity aur compile-time typed function calls ke liye extra custom extensions aur conventions chahiye.

Final recommendation: **Rustploy Live Queries + generated TypeScript client + React + `useSyncExternalStore` + single SSE connection**. SQLite reactivity Rust side par rahegi; React sirf typed data consume karega.

## Assistant

Haan, aapka desired model clear hai:

- Rust server initial data dega.
- Server-side event se updated data dega.
- React browser mein us data ko render karega.
- React ko direct database access nahi hoga.
- Developer normal typed Rust function call karega.

Recommended syntax:

Rust side:

```rust
#[live_query(table = "todos")]
async fn todos(&self) -> Vec<Todo> {
    sqlx::query_as!(
        Todo,
        "SELECT id, title, done FROM todos ORDER BY id DESC"
    )
    .fetch_all(&self.pool)
    .await
}

#[action]
async fn toggle(&self, id: i64) {
    sqlx::query!("UPDATE todos SET done = NOT done WHERE id = ?", id)
        .execute(&self.pool)
        .await
        .unwrap();
}
```

React page:

```tsx
import { Todo } from "@rustploy/generated";

export default function TodoPage() {
  const todos = Todo.todos.use({
    loading: <TodoSkeleton />,
    error: <ErrorMessage />,
  });

  return (
    <main>
      <TodoForm />

      <section>
        {todos.map(todo => (
          <TodoRow
            key={todo.id}
            todo={todo}
            onToggle={() => Todo.toggle(todo.id)}
          />
        ))}
      </section>
    </main>
  );
}
```

Component:

```tsx
function TodoRow({
  todo,
  onToggle,
}: {
  todo: Todo;
  onToggle: () => void;
}) {
  return (
    <label className="flex gap-2">
      <input
        type="checkbox"
        checked={todo.done}
        onChange={onToggle}
      />

      <span className={todo.done ? "line-through" : ""}>
        {todo.title}
      </span>
    </label>
  );
}
```

Create action:

```tsx
function TodoForm() {
  const [title, setTitle] = useState("");

  async function submit(event: React.FormEvent) {
    event.preventDefault();

    await Todo.create({ title });
    setTitle("");
  }

  return (
    <form onSubmit={submit}>
      <input
        value={title}
        onChange={event => setTitle(event.target.value)}
      />
      <button type="submit">Add</button>
    </form>
  );
}
```

Internal flow:

```text
Initial GET /todo
        ↓
Rust renders React page shell + initial todos
        ↓
React hydrates with initial data
        ↓
One SSE connection opens
        ↓
SQLite todos table changes
        ↓
Rust runs todos() again
        ↓
SSE sends new typed JSON
        ↓
React external store updates
        ↓
Only TodoPage subscribers re-render
```

SSE payload example:

```json
{
  "query": "Todo.todos",
  "data": [
    { "id": 1, "title": "Learn Rust", "done": true },
    { "id": 2, "title": "Build UI", "done": false }
  ]
}
```

React side generated hook internally kuch aisa karega:

```tsx
const todos = useSyncExternalStore(
  Todo.todos.subscribe,
  Todo.todos.getSnapshot,
  Todo.todos.getServerSnapshot
);
```

Developer ko ye manually nahi likhna padega.

Agar full list nahi bhejna ho, server diff bhi bhej sakta hai:

```json
{
  "query": "Todo.todos",
  "operation": "update",
  "key": 1,
  "data": {
    "done": true
  }
}
```

Meri recommendation: initial page ke liye SSR data + hydration, realtime ke liye SSE JSON patches, aur React ke liye generated `use()` hooks. Isme server authoritative rahega aur React sirf rendering layer.

## Assistant

Aur sochne ke baad ek important improvement: `Todo.todos.use()` bhi thoda generated-library jaisa lagta hai. Rustploy ka developer experience React/TanStack ke natural syntax ke kareeb hona chahiye, lekin endpoints, query keys aur invalidation completely automatic honi chahiye.

Mera preferred final syntax:

Rust backend:

```rust
#[controller("/todos")]
impl TodoController {
    #[live]
    async fn list(&self) -> Vec<Todo> {
        sqlx::query_as!(
            Todo,
            "SELECT id, title, done FROM todos ORDER BY id DESC"
        )
        .fetch_all(&self.pool)
        .await
        .unwrap()
    }

    #[action]
    async fn create(&self, input: NewTodo) {
        sqlx::query!(
            "INSERT INTO todos (title) VALUES (?)",
            input.title
        )
        .execute(&self.pool)
        .await
        .unwrap();
    }

    #[action]
    async fn toggle(&self, id: i64) {
        sqlx::query!(
            "UPDATE todos SET done = NOT done WHERE id = ?",
            id
        )
        .execute(&self.pool)
        .await
        .unwrap();
    }
}
```

React frontend:

```tsx
import { todos } from "@rustploy/api";

export function TodoPage() {
  const list = todos.list.use();

  if (list.loading) {
    return <TodoSkeleton />;
  }

  if (list.error) {
    return <ErrorView error={list.error} />;
  }

  return (
    <TodoList
      todos={list.data}
      onToggle={todos.toggle}
    />
  );
}
```

Action bilkul normal typed function:

```tsx
await todos.toggle(todo.id);
```

Create:

```tsx
await todos.create({ title });
```

Kisi action ke baad frontend ko ye nahi karna:

```tsx
refetch();
invalidateQueries();
setTodos(...);
```

Database change khud live query ko update karega.

## Initial data ka best model

Initial page load par SSE ka wait nahi karna chahiye. Server React ko bootstrap data de:

```html
<script id="__RUSTPLOY_DATA__" type="application/json">
{
  "todos.list": [
    { "id": 1, "title": "Learn Rust", "done": false }
  ]
}
</script>
```

React first render mein isi snapshot ko use karega:

```tsx
const list = todos.list.use();
```

Isliye:

- Loading flash nahi
- Double query nahi
- Empty screen nahi
- Hydration mismatch nahi

Uske baad SSE future snapshots bhejega.

## SSE mein full data ya diff?

Version 1 mein full query result bhejna better hai:

```json
{
  "type": "snapshot",
  "query": "todos.list",
  "version": 14,
  "data": [...]
}
```

Benefits:

- Client simple rahega
- Missed events ka issue nahi
- Reconnect safe
- Server authoritative rahega
- Client/server state divergence nahi

Baad mein large datasets ke liye optional diff:

```json
{
  "type": "patch",
  "query": "todos.list",
  "version": 15,
  "changes": [
    {
      "op": "update",
      "key": 42,
      "value": { "done": true }
    }
  ]
}
```

Lekin starting se diff engine banana unnecessary complexity hoga.

## Ten users wali optimization

Same query ko 10 clients subscribe kar rahe hain:

```text
todos.list()
  query key: todos.list:{}
  subscribers: 10
```

SQLite `todos` change:

```text
1 database event
      ↓
1 list() execution
      ↓
1 serialized snapshot
      ↓
10 SSE subscribers
```

Parameterized queries:

```tsx
const todos = todoApi.byProject.use(projectId);
```

Query identity:

```text
todos.byProject:{"projectId":7}
```

Same arguments wale users execution share karenge.

## Automatic SQL dependency

Developer ideally table name manually na likhe:

```rust
#[live]
async fn list(&self) -> Vec<Todo> {
    sqlx::query_as!(
        Todo,
        "SELECT ... FROM todos"
    )
}
```

Rustploy compile time par SQL inspect karke dependency nikale:

```text
todos.list → tables: ["todos"]
```

Complex query:

```sql
SELECT todos.*
FROM todos
JOIN projects ON projects.id = todos.project_id
```

Dependencies:

```text
["todos", "projects"]
```

Dynamic SQL ho to explicit fallback:

```rust
#[live(tables = ["todos", "projects"])]
async fn search(&self, input: SearchInput) -> Vec<Todo>
```

## React rendering optimization

Full array snapshot aane ka matlab poora DOM recreate hona nahi hai. React keys use karke reconciliation karega:

```tsx
{list.data.map(todo => (
  <TodoRow key={todo.id} todo={todo} />
))}
```

`TodoRow` memoized ho sakta hai:

```tsx
const TodoRow = memo(function TodoRow({ todo }: Props) {
  // Only changed todo renders
});
```

Generated store unchanged objects preserve karega, isliye sirf changed row rerender hogi.

## Final recommendation

Final public API ye honi chahiye:

```tsx
const query = todos.list.use();
await todos.toggle(id);
await todos.create({ title });
```

Aur internally Rustploy handle kare:

- Rust-to-TypeScript types
- Typed actions
- Initial server snapshot
- Single SSE connection
- Database table detection
- Shared query execution
- Deduplication
- Reconnection
- Version ordering
- React external store
- Automatic cleanup

Yahi mujhe React ke saath actual “heaven” DX lagta hai: React normal React hi rahe, aur Rustploy networking/database reactivity ko invisible bana de.

## Database update

Agar `todos` table change hoti hai, Rustploy dependency registry dekhega:

```text
Todo.list  → todos
Todo.stats → todos
User.current → users
Project.list → projects
```

Sirf affected queries rerun hongi:

```text
todos table changed
        ↓
Todo.list() rerun
Todo.stats() rerun
        ↓
User.current() untouched
Project.list() untouched
```

SSE ek batch bhejega:

```json
{
  "type": "batch",
  "updates": [
    {
      "query": "todo.list:{}",
      "version": 2,
      "data": [...]
    },
    {
      "query": "todo.stats:{}",
      "version": 2,
      "data": {
        "total": 10,
        "completed": 5
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

React ek transaction mein dono stores update karega, isliye UI inconsistent nahi dikhegi—aisa nahi hoga ki list update ho gayi lekin completed count purana hai.

## Component-level composition

Nested components apni query khud declare kar sakte hain:

```tsx
function Dashboard() {
  return (
    <>
      <Header />
      <TodoPanel />
      <ActivityPanel />
    </>
  );
}

function Header() {
  const user = useLive(User.current());
  return <h1>{user.data.name}</h1>;
}

function TodoPanel() {
  const todos = useLive(Todo.list());
  const stats = useLive(Todo.stats());

  return <TodoList todos={todos.data} stats={stats.data} />;
}
```

Rustploy render tree se subscriptions collect karega. Parent ko saara data manually pass karna zaroori nahi.

Same query multiple components use karein:

```tsx
const todos = useLive(Todo.list());
```

To query duplicate nahi hogi:

```text
TodoPanel subscribes
Sidebar subscribes
Header counter subscribes

Server execution: 1
Cached result: 1
Subscribers: 3
```

Single query:

```tsx
const todos = useLive(Todo.list());
```

Multiple grouped queries:


Action:

```tsx
await Todo.toggle(todo.id);
```

Rustploy internally handle karega:

- Multiple queries collect karna
- One initial batch request
- One SSE connection
- Query-key deduplication
- Table dependency tracking
- Affected queries ko ek baar rerun karna
- Multiple updates ko batch karna
- React mein atomic store update
- Unmounted components unsubscribe karna

Yahi HTML ke multiple `.await` blocks ka React equivalent hoga, bas HTML fragments ki jagah typed data React ko milega.

## Assistant

Svelte khud database ko realtime listen nahi karta. Svelte ka realtime model do layers mein hota hai:

## 1. Svelte compile-time UI reactivity

Svelte component state ko compile karke direct DOM operations mein badal deta hai.

```svelte
<script>
  let todos = [];
  let completedCount = 0;

  $: completedCount = todos.filter(todo => todo.done).length;
</script>

<h2>{completedCount} completed</h2>

{#each todos as todo (todo.id)}
  <TodoRow {todo} />
{/each}
```

Svelte compiler roughly isko generate karta hai:

```js
function updateTodo(todo) {
  checkbox.checked = todo.done;
  title.className = todo.done ? "line-through" : "";
}

function updateTodos(nextTodos) {
  todos = nextTodos;
  completedCount = todos.filter(todo => todo.done).length;

  // keyed each block ke karan sirf changed rows update
  updateTodoRows(todos);
}
```

Isliye Svelte mein virtual DOM nahi hota. State change par compiler-generated exact DOM update hota hai.

## 2. Realtime transport Svelte ka built-in nahi hai

SSE ya WebSocket manually connect karna padta hai, usually ek store ke through:

```js
// live-query.js
import { writable } from "svelte/store";

export function liveQuery(key, initialValue) {
  const store = writable(initialValue);

  const source = new EventSource(`/events?query=${key}`);

  source.onmessage = event => {
    const message = JSON.parse(event.data);

    if (message.query === key) {
      store.set(message.data);
    }
  };

  return {
    subscribe: store.subscribe,
    destroy: () => source.close()
  };
}
```

Component:

```svelte
<script>
  import { liveQuery } from "./live-query.js";

  export let initialTodos;

  const todos = liveQuery("todos.list", initialTodos);
</script>

{#each $todos as todo (todo.id)}
  <TodoRow {todo} />
{/each}
```

Flow:

```text
SQLite update
    ↓
Rust SQLite hook
    ↓
SSE JSON event
    ↓
Svelte store.set(data)
    ↓
Svelte compiled DOM update
```

SvelteKit ka `load()` initial data deta hai:

```js
export async function load({ locals }) {

}
```

Action mutation karta hai:


Lekin action ke baad realtime update automatic nahi hota. Usually:


ya custom SSE/WebSocket use karna padta hai.

## Rustploy ke liye Svelte model kya hoga?

Mere hisaab se best design:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  const data = live({
    todos: Todo.list(),
    stats: Todo.stats(),
    user: User.current()
  });
</script>

<h2>{$data.stats.completed} completed</h2>

{#each $data.todos as todo (todo.id)}
  <TodoRow {todo} />
{/each}
```

Rust side:

```rust
#[live(tables = ["todos"])]
async fn list(&self) -> Vec<Todo> {
    // SELECT ...
}

#[live(tables = ["todos"])]
async fn stats(&self) -> TodoStats {
    // SELECT ...
}
```

`live()` internally:

- initial SSR data use karega;
- ek shared SSE connection rakhega;
- multiple queries register karega;
- same query ko deduplicate karega;
- SQLite table event par affected queries rerun karega;
- Svelte store update karega;
- Svelte sirf affected DOM update karega.

Important distinction:

```text
Svelte = compile-time DOM reactivity
Rustploy = database + SSE reactivity
```

Svelte isliye attractive hai kyunki React ke `useSyncExternalStore`, memoization aur reconciliation boilerplate ki jagah Svelte stores direct compiled updates provide karte hain. Rustploy ke liye Svelte + Rust live-query client React se simpler ho sakta hai, lekin TypeScript code generation aur Svelte store integration banana padega.

```text
Svelte component

typed virtual import
```

Unka system **Svelte ka built-in realtime nahi** hai. Main features unke framework ke hain:

Hum Rustploy mein iska Rust-native version bana sakte hain:

```rust

async fn list(&self) -> Vec<Todo> {
    sqlx::query_as!(
        Todo,

    )
    .fetch_all(&self.pool)
    .await
    .unwrap()
}

#[action]
async fn toggle(&self, id: i64) {

        .execute(&self.pool)
        .await
        .unwrap();
}
```

Svelte side:

```svelte

{#each $todos as todo (todo.id)}
```

Multiple data bhi same component mein:


Rustploy ka internal flow:

```text
SQLite commit
    ↓
Rust SQLite hook: changed tables = ["todos"]
    ↓
Live-query registry
    ↓
Todo.list + Todo.stats re-run
    ↓
One WebSocket message with multiple updates
    ↓
Svelte stores update atomically
    ↓
Only affected DOM blocks update
```

Example message:

```json
{
  "type": "batch",
  "updates": [
    {
      "query": "Todo.list:{}",
      "version": 8,
      "data": []
    },
    {
      "query": "Todo.stats:{}",
      "version": 8,
      "data": {
        "total": 2,
        "completed": 1
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Meri recommendation: **Rustploy + Svelte + custom Rust live-query runtime + WebSocket**.

Current Datastar implementation ko directly Svelte ke saath mix nahi karna chahiye. Shared part reuse hoga:

- SQLite hooks
- table dependency registry
- query deduplication
- action routing
- session/subscription cleanup

Replace hoga:

- HTML patch transport → typed JSON store updates
- custom EventSource → one WebSocket
- server-rendered interactive HTML → Svelte components

Aur unke `uWebSockets.js` ki jagah Rust mein `axum` WebSocket ya high-performance `tokio-tungstenite` use kar sakte hain. Feature-wise same model hoga, lekin Rust type safety ke saath.

Rust side:

```rust
#[live(table = "todos")]
async fn list(&self) -> Vec<Todo> {
    sqlx::query_as!(
        Todo,
        "SELECT id, title, done FROM todos ORDER BY id DESC"
    )
    .fetch_all(&self.pool)
    .await
    .unwrap()
}

#[live(table = "todos")]
async fn stats(&self) -> TodoStats {
    // SELECT count and completed
}

#[action]
async fn toggle(&self, id: i64) {
    sqlx::query!("UPDATE todos SET done = NOT done WHERE id = ?", id)
        .execute(&self.pool)
        .await
        .unwrap();
}
```

React hook internally:

```tsx
const todos = useSyncExternalStore(
  Todo.list.subscribe,
  Todo.list.getSnapshot,
  Todo.list.getServerSnapshot
);
```

Developer ko manually ye nahi likhna padega:

```tsx

new WebSocket(...)
useEffect(...)
invalidateQueries(...)
setTodos(...)
```

Realtime message:

```json
{
  "type": "batch",
  "updates": [
    {
      "query": "Todo.list:{}",
      "version": 8,
      "data": []
    },
    {
      "query": "Todo.stats:{}",
      "version": 8,
      "data": {
        "total": 2,
        "completed": 1
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Important behavior:

- Initial data SSR se milega.
- Hydration ke baad same state reuse hogi.
- Ek page par multiple queries allowed hongi.
- Same query ke 10 subscribers ke liye server par ek execution hoga.
- SQLite table change par sirf dependent queries rerun hongi.
- React store batch update karega.
- Sirf affected components re-render honge.
- Actions typed function calls honge:

```tsx
await Todo.toggle(todo.id);
await Todo.create({ title });
```

So final choice:

```text
React UI
+ generated TypeScript client
+ Rust live queries
+ SQLite hooks
+ one WebSocket
+ useSyncExternalStore
```

## User

## Assistant

Long-term ke liye yeh approach acchi hai, lekin sirf tab jab internal protocol stable aur open rakhen.

Benefits:

- Developer ko manual URLs, serializers, hooks aur SSE/WebSocket code nahi likhna padega.
- Rust types se generated React client safe rahega.
- SQLite live queries aur multiple data sources naturally support honge.
- Endpoint rename/refactor ka impact automatically generated client handle karega.
- UI development kaafi fast aur clean hoga.

Risks:

- Generated client aur Rust backend tightly coupled ho jayenge.
- Debugging manual REST endpoint ke comparison mein difficult ho sakti hai.
- React ke bahar clients—mobile app, CLI, third-party integration—ko generated protocol samajhna padega.
- Protocol/version migration carefully maintain karni hogi.
- Framework ke andar bahut magic bhar diya to future mein escape hatch mushkil ho jayega.

Meri recommendation:

```text
Business endpoints hide karo
Internal transport preserve karo
Generated client primary API banao
HTTP/JSON fallback bhi provide karo
```

Example:

```tsx
await Todo.toggle(todo.id);
```

Primary developer API yeh rahegi, lekin internally:

```text
/_rustploy/rpc
/_rustploy/live
```

exist karenge.

Saath mein optional public route bhi allow hona chahiye:

```rust
#[public_api]
#[post("/api/todos")]
async fn create(...)
```

Final design:

```text
React app        → generated typed client
Mobile/CLI       → REST or JSON-RPC
Realtime UI      → WebSocket
Rust controller  → single source of truth
```

Isliye “endpoints completely remove” karna long-term mein bura hoga. “Endpoints automatically generate aur hide” karna long-term mein best hai. Aapko heaven-level DX bhi milega aur future flexibility bhi rahegi.

User agar normal Rust channel use karna chahe:

Ya source explicitly attach kare:

```rust
#[live(on = DashboardChanged)]
async fn dashboard(&self) -> DashboardData {
    // ...
}
```

SQLite:

```rust
#[live(on = "todos")]
async fn todos(&self) -> Vec<Todo> {
    // ...
}
```

Filesystem:

```rust
#[live(on = "deployments")]
```

Custom signal:

```rust
#[live]
async fn metrics(&self) -> Metrics {

// anywhere
```

Core abstraction:

```rust
pub trait LiveSource: Send + Sync + 'static {
    fn subscribe(&self) -> LiveReceiver;

```

Adapters:

```text
SQLite hook      → LiveSource
tokio::broadcast → LiveSource
tokio::watch     → LiveSource
fsnotify         → LiveSource
custom signal    → LiveSource
```

`auto_socket` sirf transport/registration layer rahega. Uske upar `live` layer:

```text
auto_socket
  ├── namespace registration
  ├── event registration
  └── connection lifecycle

live runtime
  ├── source subscription
  ├── query rerun
  ├── deduplication
  ├── batching
  └── React update delivery
```

```rust
    // high-level reactive data
```

Yani `auto_socket` backward-compatible rahega:

```text
#[on]   → low-level custom socket event
#[live] → high-level reactive query
```

```rust
pub struct LiveHandle<T> {

    marker: PhantomData<T>,
}
```

```rust
impl<T> LiveHandle<T> {
    pub fn publish(self) {
        live_registry().invalidate(self.endpoint, self.args);
    }
}
```

ye to humlog kuch aur new arectexture ke bare me dundh liye jisko koi socha hi nahi hoga abhi tak

## Assistant

Haan, combination genuinely strong aur relatively unique hai—lekin “kisi ne kabhi nahi socha” claim abhi nahi karna chahiye. Iske individual ideas existing hain:

- typed RPC: tRPC/Connect
- live queries: Meteor/Convex/ElectricSQL
- server functions: SvelteKit/Next
- generated clients: OpenAPI/tRPC
- reactive stores: React Query/Svelte stores
- backend invalidation: TanStack Query keys/event buses

Rustploy ka distinctive combination ho sakta hai:

```text
Existing typed HTTP controller method
+ opt-in #[live]
+ generated backend LiveHandle
+ generated React API
+ arbitrary Rust event source
+ single Socket.IO connection
+ server-side shared query execution
```

Developer experience:

```rust
#[get]
#[live]
async fn list(&self) -> Vec<Todo> {
    self.repo.list().await
}
```

Backend se type-safe refresh:

```rust
todos::list().refresh();
todos::by_project(project_id).refresh();
```

React:

```tsx
const todos = todos.list.useLive();
await todos.toggle(id);
```

Most frameworks mein invalidation string/query-key based hoti hai:

```ts
invalidateQueries(["todos", projectId]);
emit("todos:updated");
```

Humara differentiator:

```rust
todos::by_project(project_id).refresh();
```

Compiler verify karega:

- endpoint live hai
- arguments valid hain
- return contract known hai
- query instance correctly identified hai

Aur framework:

- active subscribers detect karega
- same arguments deduplicate karega
- function once rerun karega
- serialized result relevant clients ko broadcast karega
- React stores atomically update karega

Is architecture ko फिलहाल naam de sakte hain:

**Typed Live Endpoints**

Ya:

**Reactive RPC Endpoints**

Core primitives:

```text
Endpoint      → existing HTTP/RPC method
LiveEndpoint  → subscribable endpoint
LiveHandle    → backend type-safe refresh handle
LiveStore     → generated React external store
LiveRuntime   → subscriptions, batching, deduplication
```

Ab sabse important kaam implementation se pehle protocol/design ko freeze karna hai, warna macro, generated client aur runtime tightly mix ho jayenge. Minimal v1:

1. `#[get] #[live]`
2. `todos::list().refresh()`
3. generated React `todos.list.useLive()`
4. single Socket.IO connection
5. full JSON snapshots
6. active query-key deduplication
7. explicit refresh only

SQLite/fsnotify/broadcast adapters baad mein isi `refresh()` ko call karein. Isse core generic aur testable rahega.

Full safety layers:

```text
Rust struct/type
   ↓

   ↓
typed endpoint client
```

## Assistant

Haan, pehle backend/socket architecture freeze karna best hai. React baad mein generated client ke through connect hoga.

Mera proposed backend design:

### 1. Existing `auto_socket` preserve

Current low-level socket events waise hi chalenge:

```rust
#[auto_socket("/terminal")]
impl TerminalSocket {
    #[on("input")]
    async fn input(&self, socket: SocketRef, data: Data<Input>) {
        // raw socket control
    }
}
```

Ye terminal, chat, custom protocol jaise cases ke liye rahega.

### 2. New high-level `#[live]` endpoint

```rust
#[controller("/todos")]
impl TodoController {
    #[get]
    #[live]
    async fn list(&self) -> Vec<Todo> {
        self.repo.list().await
    }
}
```

Meaning:

- `#[get]` normal HTTP endpoint
- `#[live]` same method WebSocket live query ke liye registered
- WebSocket tabhi open hoga jab client live subscription karega

### 3. Live registry

Macro compile time par metadata register karega:

```text
TodoController::list
return type: Vec<Todo>
arguments: none
live key: "todos.list"
```

Runtime registry active subscriptions track karegi:

```text
live key
arguments
subscribers
refresh function
```

### 4. Type-safe backend refresh handle

Developer kisi bhi backend code se live query refresh kar sake:

```rust
todos::list().refresh();
```

Parameterized query:

```rust
#[get("/{project_id}")]
#[live]
async fn by_project(&self, project_id: i64) -> Vec<Todo> {
    self.repo.by_project(project_id).await
}
```

```rust
todos::by_project(project_id).refresh();
```

Wrong argument compile-time error dega.

### 5. Generic event sources

Framework source ka type hide karega. Developer inmein se kuch bhi use kar sakta hai:

```rust
live::signal("deployments").notify();
```

Ya typed signal:

```rust
DeploymentLive::refresh();
```

Internally source ho sakta hai:

- SQLite hook
- `tokio::broadcast`
- `tokio::watch`
- `mpsc`
- `fsnotify`
- Docker/PTY stream
- timer
- external webhook

Sabka output same hoga:

```text
source event → live key invalidation → query rerun → socket update
```

Developer ko WebSocket send/broadcast manually nahi karna padega.

### 6. One socket per client

Client ek WebSocket connection rakhega:

```text
connect
subscribe: Todo.list
subscribe: Todo.stats
subscribe: User.current
```

Server har query ke liye alag socket nahi banayega.

### 7. Deduplication

10 users same live query listen kar rahe hon:

```text
SQLite event: 1
query execution: 1 per unique query key
serialized result: 1
socket delivery: 10
```

Parameterized queries different keys hongi:

```text
Todo.by_project(1)
Todo.by_project(2)
```

### 8. Atomic batch updates

Agar ek event se multiple live methods affected hain:

```json
{
  "type": "batch",
  "updates": [
    { "key": "Todo.list", "data": [] },
    { "key": "Todo.stats", "data": {} }
  ]
}
```

Client ko inconsistent intermediate state nahi milegi.

Final layering:

```text
auto_socket
  └── low-level Socket.IO events

live runtime
  ├── #[live] registration
  ├── generic event sources
  ├── type-safe refresh handles
  ├── subscription registry
  ├── deduplication
  └── one WebSocket transport

React client
  └── later generated from live metadata
```

Is order mein implementation karna chahiye:

1. `LiveKey` + `LiveRegistry`
2. `#[live]` macro metadata
3. typed `.refresh()` handles
4. generic `LiveSource` adapters
5. Socket.IO subscribe/update protocol
6. deduplication and batching
7. backend tests
8. uske baad generated React client

Core principle:

> `auto_socket` transport sambhalega; `live` runtime data reactivity sambhalega. Developer sirf function aur refresh intent likhega.

```rust
#[get]
#[live]
async fn list(&self) -> Vec<Todo> {
    self.repo.list().await
}
```

Kahin bhi backend se:

```rust
let todos = repo.list().await;

todos_live::list().publish(todos).await?;
```

`publish()` sirf `Vec<Todo>` accept karega, kyunki `list()` ka return type `Vec<Todo>` hai:

```rust
todos_live::list().publish("wrong");
// compile error: expected Vec<Todo>
```

Parameterized endpoint:

```rust
#[get("/{project_id}")]
#[live]
async fn by_project(&self, project_id: i64) -> Vec<Todo> {
    self.repo.by_project(project_id).await
}
```

Exact subscribers ko publish:

```rust
let data = repo.by_project(project_id).await;

todos_live::by_project(project_id)

    .await?;
```

Framework automatically resolve karega:

```text
Live endpoint: TodoController.by_project
Arguments: project_id = 10
Subscribers: only by_project(10)
Payload type: Vec<Todo>
```

## Broadcast ka meaning

`publish()` internally same result ke sab relevant subscribers ko broadcast karega:

```rust
todos_live::list().publish(todos).await?;
```

Agar 10 clients `list()` listen kar rahe hain:

```text
Data calculation: developer ne ek baar ki
Serialization: framework ek baar karega
Broadcast: all 10 subscribers
```

Koi duplicate query nahi chalegi.

Sab active parameter variants ko same payload dena generally unsafe hoga. Isliye explicit API:

```rust
// Exact query instance
todos_live::by_project(project_id).publish(data).await?;

// All subscribers of a non-parameterized endpoint
todos_live::list().publish(data).await?;
```

## Endpoint ke andar direct publishing

Normal action:

```rust
#[post("/{id}/toggle")]
async fn toggle(&self, id: i64) -> Result<(), AppError> {
    self.repo.toggle(id).await?;

    let todos = self.repo.list().await;
    todos_live::list().publish(todos).await?;

    Ok(())
}
```

Custom broadcast channel se:

```rust
while let Ok(todos) = receiver.recv().await {
    todos_live::list().publish(todos).await?;
}
```

`fsnotify` se:

```rust
while watcher.changed().await {
    let files = scan_files().await;
    files_live::list().publish(files).await?;
}
```

Docker metrics se:

```rust
while let Some(metrics) = metrics_stream.next().await {
    server_live::metrics(server_id)
        .publish(metrics)
        .await?;
}
```

Source kuch bhi ho sakta hai. Framework ko farak nahi padega.

## Final semantics

```rust
.publish(data)
```

- Endpoint ka typed return payload leta hai
- Function dobara execute nahi karta
- Data serialize karta hai
- Exact live key resolve karta hai
- Subscribed sockets ko push/broadcast karta hai
- No subscriber ho to cheaply discard karta hai

Agar future mein rerun convenience chahiye to woh alag operation hoga:

```rust
todos_live::list().refresh().await?;
```

Lekin core API aapke kehne ke mutabik:


## Phase 1: Live Runtime

Naya crate/module:

```text
crates/auto/live/
├── src/lib.rs
├── src/key.rs
├── src/registry.rs
├── src/publisher.rs
└── src/protocol.rs
```

Core types:

```rust
LiveKey
LiveEndpointId
LivePublisher<T>
LiveRegistry
LiveSubscription
```

Parameterized endpoint ke liye stable key:

```text
ServerController.metrics + serialized(server_id)
```

## Phase 2: `#[live]` Macro

`auto_route` controller macro ko `#[live]` recognize karna hoga.

Macro method se collect karega:

- controller name
- method name
- argument names/types
- return type
- route metadata
- serialization requirements

Original HTTP endpoint unchanged rahega.

```rust
#[get]
#[live]
async fn list(...) -> Vec<Todo>
```

Isse HTTP route bhi milega aur live metadata bhi register hoga.

## Phase 3: Typed Backend Handles

Macro generated module banayega:

```rust
pub mod server_live {
    pub fn metrics(server_id: i64) -> LivePublisher<Metrics> {
        // generated endpoint identity + typed arguments
    }
}
```

Isliye ye compile nahi hoga:

```rust
server_live::metrics("wrong");
server_live::metrics(server_id).publish("wrong");
```

`publish()` endpoint function rerun nahi karega. Diya hua payload direct subscribers ko push karega.

## Phase 4: `auto_socket` Integration

Existing low-level API preserve rahegi:

```rust
#[auto_socket("/terminal")]
#[on("terminal:input")]
```

Live system reserved namespace use karega:

```text
/_rustploy/live
```

Client events:

```text
live:subscribe
live:unsubscribe
```

Server event:

```text
live:update
```

Ek client ke liye ek Socket.IO connection rahega; multiple live endpoints usi connection par subscribe honge.

## Phase 5: Subscription Registry

Runtime track karega:

```text
LiveKey → connected sockets
Socket → subscribed LiveKeys
```

Example:

```text
metrics(10) → clients A, B
metrics(20) → client C
```

Publish:

```rust
server_live::metrics(10).publish(data).await?;
```

Sirf A aur B ko data jayega.

Disconnect par socket ki saari subscriptions automatically remove hongi.

## Phase 6: Efficient Publishing

Publish flow:

```text
typed payload
→ serialize once
→ resolve exact LiveKey
→ broadcast subscribed sockets
```

Rules:

- zero subscribers: no serialization/broadcast work where practical
- ten subscribers: payload serialize once
- bounded queues/backpressure
- slow/disconnected sockets cleanup
- monotonically increasing version per live key

Message:

```json
{
  "endpoint": "ServerController.metrics",
  "args_key": "...",
  "version": 12,
  "data": {}
}
```

## Phase 7: Initial Data

Subscription ke waqt client optionally initial value maang sakega.

Server existing controller method execute karke initial snapshot dega:

```text
subscribe metrics(10)
→ metrics(10) runs once
→ initial snapshot
→ future publish() calls push data
```

Options:

```rust
#[live]                  // initial method execution enabled
#[live(initial = false)] // only explicitly published values
```

Streaming logs/metrics mein `initial = false` useful hoga.

## Phase 8: Arbitrary Event Sources

Framework source-specific nahi hoga. Developer data kahin se bhi bana sakta hai:

```rust
// tokio broadcast
while let Ok(metrics) = receiver.recv().await {
    server_live::metrics(metrics.server_id)
        .publish(metrics)
        .await?;
}
```

Same API works with:

- `tokio::broadcast`
- `watch`
- `mpsc`
- `fsnotify`
- SQLite hooks
- Docker logs
- timers
- external services

`auto_socket` sirf final delivery sambhalega.

## Phase 9: Testing

Required tests:

1. Live metadata registration
2. Argument compile-time typing
3. Payload compile-time typing
4. Exact parameter targeting
5. Multiple subscribers receive one publication
6. Other parameter subscribers receive nothing
7. Disconnect cleanup
8. No-subscriber publish
9. Existing `#[on]` handlers unaffected
10. Existing HTTP endpoint still works
11. Initial snapshot behavior
12. Concurrent publish ordering

`trybuild` tests wrong argument/payload compilation verify karenge.

## Implementation Order

1. `LiveKey` and typed `LivePublisher<T>`
2. In-memory subscription registry
3. Socket.IO subscribe/unsubscribe/update protocol
4. Manual registry integration test
5. `#[live]` macro parsing
6. Generated `*_live` modules
7. Controller method initial execution
8. Cleanup, versioning and backpressure
9. End-to-end Todo/metrics example
10. React client generation later

```rust
server_live::metrics(server_id)

```

Existing endpoints aur `auto_socket` remain compatible; naya live layer unke upar add hoga.

    +/// A type-safe handle for publishing a live endpoint result.
    +pub struct LivePublisher<T> {
    +    endpoint: &'static str,
    +    event: &'static str,
    +    args: serde_json::Value,
    +    marker: PhantomData<fn() -> T>,

    +
    +impl<T> LivePublisher<T>
    +where
    +    T: Serialize,
    +{
    +    pub fn new<A: Serialize>(
    +        endpoint: &'static str,
    +        event: &'static str,
    +        args: A,
    +    ) -> Result<Self, PublishError> {
    +        Ok(Self {
    +            endpoint,
    +            event,
    +            args: serde_json::to_value(args)?,
    +            marker: PhantomData,
    +        })
    +    }

    +        if let Some(namespace) = io.of("/_rustploy/live") {
    +            namespace.to(room).emit(self.event, &data).await?;
    +        }
    +        Ok(())
    +    }
    +
    +    pub async fn broadcast(self, data: T) -> Result<(), PublishError> {
    +        let io = SOCKET_IO.get().ok_or(PublishError::NotRegistered)?;
    +        if let Some(namespace) = io.of("/_rustploy/live") {
    +            namespace.emit(self.event, &data).await?;
    +        }
    +        Ok(())
    +    }
    +}

```rust
#[get("/{server_id}/metrics")]
#[live]

) -> Json<Metrics> {
```

Framework automatically derive karega:

```text
event: ServerController::metrics
room:  ServerController::metrics(server_id)
```

Publish:

```rust
server_live::metrics(server_id)?

    .await?;
```

### Multiple endpoints ki grouping

```rust
#[get("/{server_id}/metrics")]
#[live]
#[on(Self::dashboard)]
async fn metrics(...) -> Json<Metrics> {
    // ...
}

#[get("/{server_id}/logs")]
#[live]
#[on(Self::dashboard)]
async fn logs(...) -> Json<Vec<Log>> {
    // ...
}
```

Dono `Self::dashboard` group/room ka part honge.

```rust
server_live::dashboard(server_id)?
    .broadcast(update)
    .await?;
```

Ya individual typed publish:

```rust
server_live::metrics(server_id)?
    .publish(metrics)
    .await?;
```

Meaning:

- `#[live]` → automatic endpoint event + automatic parameterized room
- `#[on(Self::dashboard)]` → optional typed group/room
- `Self::...` → same controller ke compile-time checked group ko denote karega
- String rooms advanced/custom integration ke liye optional ho sakte hain:

```rust
#[on("deployment-events")]
```

Framework automatically handle karega:

```text
endpoint room → exact endpoint subscribers
group room    → related endpoints/components
namespace     → /_rustploy/live
```

Aur `Self::dashboard` typo hua:

