```

to compile-time error milna chahiye. Event/room strings manually maintain karna normal developer ke liye zaroori nahi hoga.

Current implementation mein `#[on]` mandatory hai; isko correct model ke according change karna hai: **`#[live]` standalone valid, `#[on]` optional typed grouping.**

## Aap jo keh rahe ho, uska correct model

`#[live]` standalone ho to framework automatic endpoint room banaye:

```rust
#[get("/{server_id}/metrics")]

Automatic:

```text

room  = ServerController::metrics + serialized arguments

### `#[on]` ho to grouping/room override

async fn metrics(...) -> Json<Metrics>

```text
endpoint event = ServerController::metrics
group room     = ServerController::dashboard(server_id)
```

Another endpoint:

#[get("/{server_id}/logs")]

#[on(Self::dashboard(server_id))]
async fn logs(...) -> Json<Vec<Log>>

Dono same dashboard room mein honge:

ServerController::dashboard(server_id)
```

Individual publish:

```rust
server_live::metrics(server_id)?

Group broadcast:

```rust
server_live::dashboard(server_id)?

`Self` current controller grouping namespace denote kare:

```rust
#[on(Self::dashboard)]

Macro compile-time par expand kare:

Self::dashboard

Parameterized:

#[on(Self::dashboard(server_id))]

```text
ServerController::dashboard:[server_id]

Isse strings nahi likhni padengi aur grouping controller-scoped rahegi.

Yahan `#[on]` grouping room hai because context `#[controller] + #[live]` hai.

Context clear hai, conflict nahi hoga.

Current `src/websocket` ke hisaab se final separation:

```text
TerminalSocket
  SocketRef.emit()       → one client/session

Live endpoint publish()
  room.emit()            → exact endpoint subscribers

Live group broadcast()
  group room.emit()      → related subscribers
```

akela valid hona chahiye. Abhi implementation `#[on]` mandatory karta hai, jo correct final model nahi hai.

#[get("/{server_id}/metrics")]

## Missing pieces

### 1. Typed room/group declarations

`Self::dashboard` kahaan declare hoga, ye define karna zaroori hai.

Clean option:

```rust
#[room]
fn dashboard(server_id: i64);
```

Use:

```rust
#[live]
#[on(Self::dashboard(server_id))]
async fn metrics(...) -> Json<Metrics> {}
```

Generated handle:

```rust
server_live::dashboard(server_id)
```

Compiler argument type verify karega.

### 2. Endpoint event aur room separate hone chahiye

Event payload ka type endpoint return type hai:

```rust
server_live::metrics(server_id)
    .publish(metrics);
```

Room sirf targeting hai:

```text
room: ServerController::metrics(10)
event: ServerController::metrics
payload: Metrics
```

Group room mein multiple return types ho sakte hain. Isliye generic:

```rust
server_live::dashboard(server_id).broadcast(data)
```

type-safe nahi ho sakta, kyunki dashboard room mein `Metrics`, `Logs`, `Status` alag types hain.

Better:

```rust
server_live::metrics(server_id)
    .to(server_live::dashboard(server_id))
    .publish(metrics);
```

Ya group invalidation envelope:

```rust
server_live::dashboard(server_id).notify();
```

### 3. Initial snapshot behavior

Client subscribe karte waqt first data kaise milega?

Options:

```rust
#[live] // method automatically runs once on subscribe
```

Then future updates:

```rust
server_live::metrics(id).publish(data)
```

Without initial execution, new client blank rahega until next publish.

### 4. Authorization

Client arbitrary room subscribe na kar sake:

```json
{
  "endpoint": "ServerController::metrics",
  "args": [999]
}
```

Subscription ke waqt same auth/permissions run hone chahiye jo HTTP endpoint par hain.

Otherwise user server `999` ka private data listen kar sakta hai.

### 5. Argument canonicalization

Room key currently serialized JSON arguments se banti hai.

Problems:

```json
{"a":1,"b":2}
{"b":2,"a":1}
```

Same logical arguments different room bana sakte hain.

Generated tuple arguments best hain:

```text
[server_id, project_id]
```

Stable canonical serialization + hash use hona chahiye:

```text
live:ServerController::metrics:sha256(args)
```

### 6. Payload envelope

Raw `Metrics` directly event par bhejne ke bajaye metadata useful hai:

```json
{
  "endpoint": "ServerController::metrics",
  "version": 12,
  "data": {}
}
```

Required for:

- stale update rejection
- reconnect
- debugging
- batching
- future protocol migrations

### 7. Last-value/replay cache

New subscriber ko endpoint rerun karna expensive ho sakta hai. Optional latest-value cache useful hai:

```rust
#[live(cache = "latest")]
```

Subscribe:

```text
cached snapshot available → immediately send
otherwise → endpoint execute
```

### 8. Backpressure

Metrics/log streams rapidly publish karenge. Slow browser ke liye strategy chahiye:

```rust
#[live(mode = "latest")] // old metrics drop, latest preserve
#[live(mode = "stream")] // logs ordered, bounded buffer
```

Metrics aur logs same delivery semantics nahi rakhte.

### 9. Publish/broadcast naming

Clear semantics freeze karna hoga:

```rust
.publish(data)
```

Exact parameterized endpoint subscribers.

```rust
.broadcast(data)
```

Kisko? Entire endpoint across all arguments ya optional group?

Meri recommendation:

```rust
.publish(data)      // exact endpoint + args
.publish_all(data)  // all active argument variants; rarely useful
.to(group).publish(data)
```

“broadcast” ambiguous hai.

### 10. Error handling

This is slightly cluttered:

```rust
server_live::metrics(id)?
    .publish(data)
    .await?;
```

Arguments generated by macro should nearly always serialize successfully. Better:

```rust
server_live::metrics(id)
    .publish(data)
    .await?;
```

Handle construction infallible ban sakti hai if args serialize only during publish, or serialization failure stored internally.

### 11. Return wrapper support

Currently only `Json<T>` unwrap ho raha hai. Support eventually needed:

```rust
Result<Json<T>, AppError>
Result<T, AppError>
Arc<T>
Option<T>
```

Live payload type extraction:

```text
Result<Json<Metrics>, Error> → Metrics
```

### 12. Multi-instance deployment

Current global `SocketIo` only same Rust process ke clients ko emit karega.

Multiple Rustploy replicas:

```text
instance A receives publish
client connected to instance B
```

Client update miss karega.

Later adapter needed:

- Redis adapter
- NATS
- PostgreSQL pub/sub

Single-machine v1 mein okay, but protocol should not assume one process forever.

## Recommended minimal v1

Pehle sirf ye freeze karo:

```rust
#[get("/{server_id}/metrics")]
#[live]
async fn metrics(...) -> Json<Metrics>
```

```rust
server_live::metrics(server_id)
    .publish(metrics)
    .await?;
```

V1 behavior:

- automatic event name
- exact typed argument room
- initial method execution on subscribe
- subscription authorization
- versioned envelope
- disconnect cleanup
- `Result<Json<T>, E>` unwrapping
- one Socket.IO namespace

Optional grouping ko uske baad add karo:

```rust
#[room]
fn dashboard(server_id: i64);

#[on(Self::dashboard(server_id))]
```

Sabse dangerous missing part authorization hai; sabse important DX correction `#[live]` standalone support hai; sabse unresolved design group rooms mein mixed payload types hain.

weboscket terminame bana to diya tha auto_soket se group and uske under on likha to automatic user agar puchna nahi pucha khud dekhlo na pub mod helpers;
pub mod local;
pub mod remote;
pub mod types;

use std::sync::Arc;

use auto_di::singleton;
#[allow(unused_imports)]
use auto_socket::{auto_socket, on};
use dashmap::DashMap;
use socketioxide::{
    extract::{Data, SocketRef},
    socket::DisconnectReason,
};
use sqlx::SqlitePool;
use tokio::{io::AsyncWriteExt, process::Command};

use helpers::{emit_error, socket_key};
use local::{spawn_docker_terminal, spawn_local_terminal};
use remote::spawn_remote_terminal;
pub use types::{
    DockerTerminalStart, ServerTerminalStart, TerminalInput, TerminalResize, TerminalSession,
};

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct TerminalSocket {
    sessions: Arc<DashMap<String, TerminalSession>>,
    db: Arc<SqlitePool>,
}

#[singleton]
#[auto_socket("/terminal")]
impl TerminalSocket {
    fn new(db: Arc<SqlitePool>) -> Self {
        Self {
            sessions: Arc::new(DashMap::new()),
            db,
        }
    }

    async fn stop_socket_session(&self, socket: &SocketRef) {
        let key = socket_key(socket);
        if let Some((_, session)) = self.sessions.remove(&key) {
            match session {
                TerminalSession::Pty { .. } => {}
                TerminalSession::Local { child, .. } => {
                    let _ = child.lock().await.kill().await;
                }
                TerminalSession::Remote { cancel, .. } => {
                    cancel.cancel();
                }
            }
        }
    }

    fn bind_disconnect_cleanup(&self, socket: &SocketRef, key: String) {
        let sessions = self.sessions.clone();
        socket.on_disconnect(move |_socket: SocketRef, _reason: DisconnectReason| {
            let sessions = sessions.clone();
            let key = key.clone();
            async move {
                if let Some((_, session)) = sessions.remove(&key) {
                    match session {
                        TerminalSession::Pty { .. } => {}
                        TerminalSession::Local { child, .. } => {
                            let _ = child.lock().await.kill().await;
                        }
                        TerminalSession::Remote { cancel, .. } => {
                            cancel.cancel();
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        });
    }

    #[on("docker:start")]
    async fn docker_start(&self, socket: SocketRef, Data(payload): Data<serde_json::Value>) {
        self.stop_socket_session(&socket).await;
        self.bind_disconnect_cleanup(&socket, socket_key(&socket));

        let container = payload
            .get("container")
            .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
            .unwrap_or("app")
            .to_string();
        let shell = payload
            .get("shell")
            .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
            .map(|s| s.to_string());
        let server_id = payload
            .get("server_id")
            .and_then(|v| v.as_i64())
            .or_else(|| payload.get("serverId").and_then(|v| v.as_i64()));

        let input = DockerTerminalStart {
            container,
            shell,
            server_id,
        };
        spawn_docker_terminal(socket, &self.sessions, input).await;
    }

    #[on("server:start")]
    async fn server_start(&self, socket: SocketRef, Data(payload): Data<serde_json::Value>) {
        self.stop_socket_session(&socket).await;
        self.bind_disconnect_cleanup(&socket, socket_key(&socket));

        let server_id = payload
            .get("server_id")
            .and_then(|v| v.as_i64())
            .or_else(|| payload.get("serverId").and_then(|v| v.as_i64()));
        let shell = payload
            .get("shell")
            .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
            .or_else(|| payload.get("command").and_then(|v| v.as_str()))
            .map(|s| s.to_string());

        let input = ServerTerminalStart { shell, server_id };

        if let Some(server_id) = input.server_id {
            spawn_remote_terminal(socket, &self.sessions, self.db.as_ref(), server_id, input).await;
            return;
        }

        let shell_cmd = input
            .shell
            .unwrap_or_else(|| std::env::var("SHELL").unwrap_or_else(|_| "/bin/sh".into()));
        let mut command = Command::new(shell_cmd);
        command
            .stdin(std::process::Stdio::piped())
            .stdout(std::process::Stdio::piped())
            .stderr(std::process::Stdio::piped());

        spawn_local_terminal(socket, &self.sessions, "server", command).await;
    }

    #[on("input")]
    async fn input(&self, socket: SocketRef, Data(payload): Data<serde_json::Value>) {
        let key = socket_key(&socket);
        let data = if let Some(s) = payload.as_str() {
            s.to_string()
        } else if let Some(s) = payload.get("data").and_then(|v| v.as_str()) {
            s.to_string()
        } else {
            return;
        };

        let Some(session) = self.sessions.get(&key).map(|entry| entry.clone()) else {
            tracing::warn!("Input received for session {key} but session is not found");
            emit_error(&socket, "terminal session is not running");
            return;
        };

        match session {
            TerminalSession::Pty { writer, .. } => {
                let mut w = writer.lock().await;
                if let Err(error) = w.write_all(data.as_bytes()).await {
                    tracing::warn!("PTY write_all failed: {error}");
                    emit_error(&socket, format!("could not write PTY input: {error}"));
                }
            }
            TerminalSession::Local { stdin, .. } => {
                let mut s = stdin.lock().await;
                if let Err(error) = s.write_all(data.as_bytes()).await {
                    tracing::warn!("Local terminal write_all failed: {error}");
                    emit_error(&socket, format!("could not write terminal input: {error}"));
                } else {
                    let _ = s.flush().await;
                }
            }
            TerminalSession::Remote { input: tx, .. } => {
                if tx.send(data.into_bytes()).await.is_err() {
                    emit_error(&socket, "remote terminal input channel is closed");
                }
            }
        }
    }

    #[on("resize")]
    async fn resize(&self, socket: SocketRef, Data(payload): Data<serde_json::Value>) {
        let key = socket_key(&socket);
        let Some(session) = self.sessions.get(&key).map(|entry| entry.clone()) else {
            return;
        };

        let cols = payload
            .get("cols")
            .and_then(|v| v.as_u64())
            .map(|v| v as u16)
            .unwrap_or(80);
        let rows = payload
            .get("rows")
            .and_then(|v| v.as_u64())
            .map(|v| v as u16)
            .unwrap_or(24);

        match session {
            TerminalSession::Pty { writer, .. } => {
                let w = writer.lock().await;
                if let Err(error) = w.resize(pty_process::Size::new(rows, cols)) {
                    tracing::warn!("PTY resize failed: {error}");
                }
            }
            TerminalSession::Remote { resize, .. } => {
                let _ = resize.send((rows, cols)).await;
            }
            TerminalSession::Local { .. } => {}
        }
    }

    #[on("stop")]
    async fn stop(&self, socket: SocketRef) {
        self.stop_socket_session(&socket).await;
    }
}

## Current terminal code mein actual improvements

### 1. Raw JSON payload hata sakte hain

Abhi:

```rust
Data(payload): Data<serde_json::Value>
```

Phir manually fields read ho rahe hain. `auto_socket` already typed arguments support karta hai, isliye direct:

```rust
#[on("docker:start")]
async fn docker_start(
    &self,
    socket: SocketRef,
    Data(input): Data<DockerTerminalStart>,
) {
    // input.container
    // input.shell
    // input.server_id
}
```

Same:

```rust
#[on("input")]
async fn input(
    &self,
    socket: SocketRef,
    Data(input): Data<TerminalInput>,
) {}
```

```rust
#[on("resize")]
async fn resize(
    &self,
    socket: SocketRef,
    Data(input): Data<TerminalResize>,
) {}
```

Isse frontend payload compile/runtime validation clean hogi.

### 2. Disconnect handler multiple times register ho raha hai

Har `docker:start` aur `server:start` par:

```rust
self.bind_disconnect_cleanup(...)
```

call ho raha hai. Same socket multiple terminal starts kare to multiple disconnect callbacks register honge.

Cleanup ideally socket connect hote hi sirf once bind hona chahiye. `auto_socket` mein lifecycle hook add ho sakta hai:

```rust
#[connect]
async fn connected(&self, socket: SocketRef) {
    self.bind_disconnect_cleanup(&socket);
}

#[disconnect]
async fn disconnected(&self, socket: SocketRef) {
    self.stop_socket_session(&socket).await;
}
```

### 3. PTY stop actual process ko kill nahi karta

Current session:

```rust
TerminalSession::Pty {
    writer,
}
```

`stop_socket_session()` mein:

```rust
TerminalSession::Pty { .. } => {}
```

Matlab session map se remove hoti hai, lekin Docker/local SSH PTY child necessarily terminate nahi hota.

PTY session mein cancellation/child control store hona chahiye:

```rust
TerminalSession::Pty {
    writer,
    cancel: CancellationToken,
}
```

Ya child handle:

```rust
TerminalSession::Pty {
    writer,
    child: Arc<Mutex<Child>>,
}
```

Phir stop/disconnect actual process terminate kare.

### 4. Remote variant practically use nahi ho rahi

`TerminalSession::Remote` defined hai:

```rust
Remote {
    input,
    resize,
    cancel,
}
```

Lekin `spawn_remote_terminal()` currently session map mein:

```rust
TerminalSession::Pty { writer }
```

insert karta hai.

Isliye `input()` aur `resize()` ke `Remote` branches remote SSH path ke liye hit nahi honge. Remote SSH bhi PTY branch use karega. Either:

- `Remote` variant remove karo, or
- remote implementation ko actual `Remote` channels ke through connect karo.

### 5. `test_data()` production module mein nahi rehna chahiye

```rust
#[test]
fn test_data() {
    // prints zeroized secret
}
```

Iska terminal socket se relation nahi. Isko remove ya dedicated unit-test module mein shift karna better hai.

### 6. Errors silently ignore ho rahe hain

Kaafi places:

```rust
let _ = socket.emit(...);
```

Disconnect expected ho sakta hai, lekin unexpected serialization/send failure logging useful hogi:

```rust
if let Err(error) = socket.emit("output", &payload) {
    tracing::debug!("terminal output emit failed: {error}");
}
```

## Live architecture ka corrected model

Existing design ko follow karte hue:

```rust
#[auto_socket("/dashboard")]
impl DashboardSocket {
    #[live]
    async fn metrics(&self, server_id: i64) -> Metrics {
        // initial value
    }

    #[live]
    async fn alerts(&self, server_id: i64) -> Vec<Alert> {
        // initial value
    }
}
```

Backend:

```rust
dashboard_live::metrics(server_id)
    .publish(metrics)
    .await?;
```

Meaning:

```text
group/namespace = /dashboard
event           = metrics
target          = metrics(server_id)
payload         = Metrics
```

Custom event name chahiye tab optional:

```rust
#[live]
#[on("server:metrics")]
async fn metrics(...) -> Metrics {}
```

Final rule:

- `#[auto_socket("/dashboard")]` → grouping automatically.
- `#[live]` → publishable typed output.
- Function name → default event name.
- Function arguments → exact room/subscription identity.
- Return type → `publish()` payload type.
- `#[on("...")]` → optional custom event name.
- `SocketRef`/`Data<T>` → low-level interactive events ke liye.

Aapka existing `auto_socket` design fundamentally sahi hai. Naya live system isi ke andar extend hona chahiye, controller macros mein separate room architecture invent nahi karni chahiye.

## Assistant

Haan, ab final model clear hai. `#[auto_socket("/group")]` ke andar developer `#[live]` ya `#[on("specific:name")]`—dono mein se kuch bhi use kare, macro automatically handle karega.

```rust
#[auto_socket("/dashboard")]
impl DashboardSocket {
    // Function name se event automatically: "metrics"
    #[live]
    async fn metrics(&self, server_id: i64) -> Metrics {
        self.service.metrics(server_id).await
    }

    // Developer ka exact event name: "alerts:update"
    #[on("alerts:update")]
    async fn alerts(&self, server_id: i64) -> Vec<Alert> {
        self.service.alerts(server_id).await
    }
}
```

Dono generated typed publishers denge:

```rust
dashboard_live::metrics(server_id)
    .publish(metrics)
    .await?;

dashboard_live::alerts(server_id)
    .publish(alerts)
    .await?;
```

Resolution:

```text
#[live]
namespace = /dashboard
event     = metrics
room      = metrics(server_id)
payload   = Metrics

#[on("alerts:update")]
namespace = /dashboard
event     = alerts:update
room      = alerts(server_id)
payload   = Vec<Alert>
```

Difference sirf event naming ka hoga:

- `#[live]` → method name automatically event name
- `#[on("...")]` → developer ka exact event name
- arguments → typed room identity
- return type → typed publish payload
- `auto_socket` → namespace/group registration

Low-level interactive handler bhi supported rehna chahiye:

```rust
#[on("input")]
async fn input(
    &self,
    socket: SocketRef,
    Data(input): Data<TerminalInput>,
) {
    // inbound event because it consumes SocketRef/Data
}
```

Macro signature se intent identify karega:

```text
SocketRef/Data<T> parameters present
→ inbound socket handler

normal typed arguments + serializable return value
→ publishable live endpoint
```

Isliye same `#[on]` naturally dono cases handle kar sakta hai:

```rust
#[on("input")]
async fn input(SocketRef, Data<T>)      // inbound event

#[on("alerts:update")]
async fn alerts(server_id) -> Vec<T>    // typed live output
```

Final public rule:

> `#[auto_socket]` group banata hai. `#[live]` automatic-name live output hai. `#[on("name")]` exact-name event hai. Macro function signature dekhkar inbound handler ya typed publish endpoint automatically decide karega.

    +fn is_socket_argument(ty: &Type) -> bool {
    +    let Type::Path(path) = ty else { return false; };
    +    path.path.segments.last().is_some_and(|segment| {
    +        matches!(segment.ident.to_string().as_str(), "SocketRef" | "Data")
    +    })
    +}
    +
    +fn live_return_type(output: &ReturnType) -> syn::Result<Type> {
    +    let ReturnType::Type(_, ty) = output else {
    +        return Err(syn::Error::new_spanned(output, "#[live] methods must return a value"));
    +    };
    +    Ok(wrapper_inner_type(ty, &["Json", "Result", "Option"])
    +        .unwrap_or_else(|| (**ty).clone()))
    +}
    +
    +fn wrapper_inner_type(ty: &Type, wrappers: &[&str]) -> Option<Type> {
    +    let Type::Path(path) = ty else { return None; };
    +    let segment = path.path.segments.last()?;
    +    let PathArguments::AngleBracketed(arguments) = &segment.arguments else { return None; };
    +    if !wrappers.iter().any(|wrapper| segment.ident == *wrapper) { return None; }
    +    arguments.args.iter().find_map(|argument| match argument {
    +        GenericArgument::Type(inner) => Some((**inner).clone()),
    +        _ => None,
    +    })
    +}

### Ek specific user/socket ko

```rust
dashboard_live::metrics(server_id)?
    .emit(&socket, metrics)?;

dashboard_live::metrics(server_id)?

Lekin `emit`/`broadcast` ke liye arguments nahi chahiye. Rust function overloading support nahi karta, isliye same `metrics()` ko zero aur multiple arguments dono tarah call nahi kar sakte.

Best API:

```rust
// Parameter-room publish
dashboard_live::metrics(server_id, region)
    .publish(metrics)
    .await?;

// Specific socket
dashboard_live::metrics_to(&socket)
    .emit(metrics)?;

// Whole namespace
dashboard_live::metrics_all()
    .broadcast(metrics)

dashboard_live::metrics(server_id, region).publish(metrics);
dashboard_live::metrics().emit(&socket, metrics); // Rust mein overload impossible

dashboard_live::metrics(server_id, region)
    .publish(metrics);

dashboard_live::metrics_event()

dashboard_live::metrics_event()
    .broadcast(metrics);

## Assistant

Actual flow simple hai:

```rust
#[auto_socket("/dashboard")]
impl DashboardSocket {
    #[live]
    async fn metrics(&self, server_id: i64, region: String) -> Metrics {
        self.service.metrics(server_id, region).await
    }
}
```

Macro compile time par roughly ye API generate karta hai:

```rust
mod dashboard_live {
    pub fn metrics(
        server_id: i64,
        region: String,
    ) -> Result<LivePublisher<Metrics>, PublishError> {
        LivePublisher::new(
            "/dashboard",
            "DashboardSocket::metrics",
            "metrics",
        )
        .room((server_id, region))
    }

    pub fn metrics_event() -> LivePublisher<Metrics> {
        LivePublisher::new(
            "/dashboard",
            "DashboardSocket::metrics",
            "metrics",
        )
    }
}
```

## 1. Client room subscribe karta hai

Frontend jab live metrics use karega, generated client code internally ye subscription bhejega:

```json
{
  "endpoint": "DashboardSocket::metrics",
  "args": [42, "india"]
}
```

Backend automatically room key banata hai:

```text
DashboardSocket::metrics:[42,"india"]
```

Socket us room mein join ho jata hai.

Developer ko `socket.join()` ya room name manually nahi likhna.

## 2. Parameter-room publish

```rust
dashboard_live::metrics(42, "india".to_string())?
    .publish(metrics)
    .await?;
```

Iska flow:

```text
metrics(42, "india")
        ↓
Arguments JSON mein serialize
        ↓
Room = DashboardSocket::metrics:[42,"india"]
        ↓
publish(metrics)
        ↓
Us room ke sab clients ko `metrics` event
```

Agar 10 clients same params se subscribed hain:

```text
Room DashboardSocket::metrics:[42,"india"]
├── Client 1
├── Client 2
├── Client 3
└── ... Client 10
```

Ek `publish(metrics)` call sab 10 clients ko same payload bhejega. Publish khud koi DB query execute nahi karta.

Important distinction: agar har client separately `metrics()` function call kar raha hai, tab query deduplication alag caching/shared-loader feature maangegi. Current room publish delivery ek hi broadcast hai, lekin initial data-loading automatically one-query guarantee nahi karta.

## 3. Specific socket emit

```rust
dashboard_live::metrics_event()
    .emit(&socket, metrics)?;
```

Flow:

```text
Given SocketRef
      ↓
"metrics" event
      ↓
Sirf wahi socket
```

Ismein `server_id` aur `region` nahi chahiye, kyunki destination already `socket` se determined hai.

Useful for:

- Request ka private response
- User-specific error
- Initial snapshot
- Acknowledgement

## 4. Namespace-wide broadcast

```rust
dashboard_live::metrics_event()
    .broadcast(metrics)
    .await?;
```

Flow:

```text
/dashboard namespace
        ↓
Connected sab sockets
        ↓
"metrics" event + typed Metrics payload
```

Ismein room filtering nahi hoti.

## Compile-time safety

Suppose return type hai:

```rust
async fn metrics(...) -> Metrics
```

To generated publisher sirf `Metrics` accept karega:

```rust
.publish(metrics)       // ✅
.publish(alerts)        // ❌ compile error
```

Parameters bhi original function signature se generate hote hain:

```rust
dashboard_live::metrics(42, "india".to_string()) // ✅
dashboard_live::metrics("wrong", 42)             // ❌ compile error
```

Overall mapping:

| Call | Destination |
|---|---|
| `metrics(params)?.publish(data)` | Same params wala room |
| `metrics_event().emit(&socket, data)` | Ek specific socket |
| `metrics_event().broadcast(data)` | Pura `/dashboard` namespace |

Macro/generated output conceptually:

```rust
pub mod dashboard_live {
    pub const METRICS_EVENT: &str = "metrics";
    pub const METRICS_ENDPOINT: &str = "DashboardSocket::metrics";

    pub fn metrics(server_id: i64, region: String)
        -> MetricsSubscription
    {
        MetricsSubscription {
            server_id,
            region,
        }
    }

    pub struct MetricsSubscription {
        pub server_id: i64,
        pub region: String,
    }

    impl MetricsSubscription {
        pub async fn subscribe(
            &self,
            client: &LiveClient,
        ) -> Result<LiveHandle<Metrics>, ClientError> {
            client.subscribe(
                METRICS_ENDPOINT,
                serde_json::json!([self.server_id, self.region]),
                METRICS_EVENT,
            ).await
        }
    }
}
```

Developer-facing usage:

```rust
let metrics = dashboard_live::metrics(server_id, region)
    .subscribe(&client)
    .await?;
```

Ya UI macro ke andar:

```rust

}
```

Generated client automatically handle karega:

- Typed payload deserialization: JSON → `Metrics`
- Typed subscription parameters
- Event name and endpoint identity
- Room subscribe/unsubscribe
- Reconnect ke baad resubscribe
- Duplicate subscription reuse
- Parameter change par old room leave, new room join
- Component unmount par cleanup
- Multiple live subscriptions on one connection
- Invalid payload/error reporting

Client transport generic rahega:

```rust
pub trait LiveTransport {
    async fn subscribe<P, T>(
        &self,
        endpoint: &'static str,
        args: P,
    ) -> Result<LiveHandle<T>, ClientError>;
}
```

Generated type-specific layer sirf metadata aur types provide karega.

Important design decision: server macro se browser JavaScript directly generate karna ideal nahi hai. Better hai shared/generated client crate:

```text
dashboard/
├── server.rs
├── client.rs
└── types.rs
```

Rust/WASM client ho to true compile-time safety milegi. Agar normal JavaScript frontend ho, to same Rust definitions se TypeScript types + runtime validators generate karne honge.

Final target API:

```rust
dashboard_live::metrics(server_id, region)
    .subscribe(&client)
    .on_update(|metrics: Metrics| {
        // typed update
    });
```

Aur server side:

```rust
dashboard_live::metrics(server_id, region)?
    .publish(metrics)
    .await?;
```

Dono same generated endpoint metadata aur same payload type use karenge—isi se end-to-end type safety milegi.

## Assistant

Haan, kaafi optimize kar sakte hain. Current implementation typed metadata deta hai, lekin developer-facing client API abhi bhi verbose hai:

```rust
metrics_subscription(...)
transport.emit(...)
transport.on(...)
subscription.decode(...)
```

Ideal DX ye hona chahiye:

```rust
let metrics = dashboard_live::metrics(server_id, region)
    .subscribe(|metrics| {
        state.set(metrics);
    });
```

Server side wahi natural rahe:

```rust
dashboard_live::metrics(server_id, region)?
    .publish(metrics)
    .await?;
```

Main ye optimizations recommend karunga:

1. `_subscription()` function hatao

Same generated `metrics(...)` descriptor ko client aur server dono context mein use karna:

```rust
// Backend
dashboard_live::metrics(server_id, region)?
    .publish(metrics)
    .await?;

// Client
dashboard_live::metrics(server_id, region)?
    .subscribe(|metrics| state.set(metrics));
```

2. Transport globally managed ho

Developer `transport.emit()` aur `transport.on()` na likhe:

```rust
dashboard_live::metrics(server_id, region)?
    .subscribe(|metrics| {
        // Metrics already typed
    });
```

Runtime internally:

- one connection maintain kare
- reconnect kare
- subscribe message bheje
- payload deserialize kare
- unmount/drop par unsubscribe kare

3. Duplicate subscriptions deduplicate hon

Agar page ke 5 components ye use karein:

```rust
dashboard_live::metrics(10, "india")?
```

To network par ek subscription ho:

```text
DashboardSocket::metrics:[10,"india"]
    ├── Component A
    ├── Component B
    ├── Component C
    ├── Component D
    └── Component E
```

Runtime reference count maintain kare:

```text
first subscriber  → server subscribe
next subscribers  → local listener only
last subscriber dropped → server unsubscribe
```

4. Stable room identity

Abhi room JSON string se banta hai:

```text
DashboardSocket::metrics:[10,"india"]
```

Isko canonical key/hash banana better hoga:

```text
live:a21f947c...
```

Benefits:

- Long JSON room names nahi
- Object property ordering issue nahi
- Sensitive arguments room name mein visible nahi
- Server/client guaranteed same identity

5. Event collision fix

Sirf `"metrics"` event risky ho sakta hai agar multiple groups same naam use karein. Internally complete identity use ho:

```text
DashboardSocket::metrics
```

Developer ko phir bhi sirf:

```rust
dashboard_live::metrics(...)
```

dikhai dega.

6. Actual TypeScript/React generation

Current code Rust typed descriptor generate karta hai. React client ke liye build time par ye generate hona chahiye:

```ts
export type Metrics = {
  cpu: number;
  memory: number;
};

export function useMetrics(
  serverId: number,
  region: string,
): LiveResult<Metrics> {
  return useLive({
    endpoint: "DashboardSocket::metrics",
    args: [serverId, region],
  });
}
```

Usage:

```tsx
function MetricsCard({ serverId, region }: Props) {
  const { data, loading, error } =
    useMetrics(serverId, region);

  if (loading) return <Skeleton />;
  if (error) return <ErrorView error={error} />;

  return <div>{data.cpu}%</div>;
}
```

7. Snapshot + updates properly define hon

Subscription ke turant baad client ko initial data kaise milega, ye important hai. Best behavior:

```text
subscribe
   ↓
server method executes once
   ↓
initial typed snapshot
   ↓
future publish updates
```

Developer ko separately initial API fetch nahi karni pade:

```tsx
const { data, loading } = useMetrics(serverId, region);
```

8. Versioning and stale-update protection

Params change:

```text
metrics(10, "india")
        ↓
metrics(11, "india")
```

Old response late aaye to ignore hona chahiye. Har subscription ko generation/version ID mile.

Final “heaven” API:

Backend:

```rust
#[live]
async fn metrics(
    &self,
    server_id: i64,
    region: String,
) -> Metrics {
    self.service.metrics(server_id, region).await
}
```

Publish:

```rust
dashboard_live::metrics(server_id, region)?
    .publish(metrics)
    .await?;
```

React:

```tsx
const { data, loading, error } =
  useMetrics(serverId, region);
```

Mere hisaab se next implementation priority honi chahiye:

1. Unified descriptor API
2. Stable room identity
3. Shared connection + subscription deduplication
4. Initial snapshot
5. TypeScript models and React hook generation

Ye complete hone ke baad developer ko socket, rooms, event names, JSON decoding, reconnect aur cleanup ka pata bhi nahi chalega.

  enabled: serverId !== undefined,
});
```

Options:

```tsx
const metrics = useLive.metrics(serverId, region, {
  initialData: emptyMetrics,
  keepPreviousData: true,
  retry: 3,
});
```

Manual control:

```tsx
const metrics = useLive.metrics(serverId, region);

metrics.refresh();
metrics.pause();
metrics.resume();
```

Lekin normal developer ko mostly sirf ye chahiye:

```tsx
const metrics = useLive.metrics(serverId, region);
```

## Return shape

Har generated hook consistent result return kare:

```ts
type LiveResult<T> = {
  data: T | undefined;
  loading: boolean;
  error: LiveError | undefined;
  connected: boolean;
  refresh(): void;
};
```

Usage:

```tsx
const { data, loading, error, connected, refresh } =
  useLive.metrics(serverId, region);
```

## Better namespace grouping

Agar multiple socket groups hon:

```rust
#[auto_socket("/dashboard")]
impl DashboardSocket {
    #[live]
    async fn metrics(...) -> Metrics {}
}
```

Generated React API:

```tsx
const metrics =
  live.dashboard.metrics.use(serverId, region);
```

Lekin ye thoda unnatural hai. Cleaner:

```tsx
const metrics =
  dashboardLive.useMetrics(serverId, region);
```

Generated imports:

```tsx
import { dashboardLive } from "@/generated/live";

const { data, loading, error } =
  dashboardLive.useMetrics(serverId, region);
```

Ye naming collisions bhi avoid karega:

```tsx
dashboardLive.useMetrics(...)
serverLive.useMetrics(...)
billingLive.useMetrics(...)
```

## Events without room parameters

Backend:

```rust
#[live]
async fn systemStatus(&self) -> SystemStatus {}
```

Frontend:

```tsx
const status = dashboardLive.useSystemStatus();
```

## Mutation ke baad manual wiring nahi

```tsx
const restart = useAction.restartServer();

await restart({ serverId });
```

Backend publish karega:

```rust
dashboard_live::metrics(server_id, region)?
    .publish(metrics)
    .await?;
```

Subscribed React hook automatically update ho jayega.

## List rendering

```tsx
function TodoList({ userId }: Props) {
  const {
    data: todos = [],
    loading,
  } = todoLive.useTodos(userId);

  if (loading) return <TodoSkeleton />;

  return todos.map(todo => (
    <TodoItem key={todo.id} todo={todo} />
  ));
}
```

## Multiple subscriptions together

Optional generated composition API:

```tsx
const dashboard = dashboardLive.use({
  metrics: [serverId, region],
  alerts: [serverId],
  containers: [serverId],
});
```

Then:

```tsx
dashboard.metrics.data
dashboard.alerts.data
dashboard.containers.data
dashboard.loading
```

Useful hai, lekin primary API individual hooks hi rehna chahiye.

Final recommended client syntax:

```tsx
import { dashboardLive } from "@/generated/live";

function Dashboard({ serverId, region }: Props) {
  const { data, loading, error } =
    dashboardLive.useMetrics(serverId, region);

  if (loading) return <Skeleton />;
  if (error) return <ErrorView error={error} />;
  if (!data) return null;

  return <MetricsView metrics={data} />;
}
```

Developer sirf generated hook use karega. Runtime internally single connection, typed decoding, room subscription, deduplication, reconnect, stale update protection aur cleanup manage karega.

    import {useEffect, useMemo, useState} from 'react';
    import {subscribeLive, type LiveEndpoint} from './runtime';
    
    export type LiveResult<T> = {
    	data: T | undefined;
    	loading: boolean;
    	error: Error | undefined;
    };
    
    export function useLive<TArgs extends readonly unknown[], TData>(
    	createEndpoint: (...args: TArgs) => LiveEndpoint<TArgs, TData>,
    	...args: TArgs
    ): LiveResult<TData> {
    	const argsKey = JSON.stringify(args);
    	const endpoint = useMemo(() => createEndpoint(...args), [createEndpoint, argsKey]);
    	const [result, setResult] = useState<LiveResult<TData>>({data: undefined, loading: true, error: undefined});
    
    	useEffect(() => {
    		setResult({data: undefined, loading: true, error: undefined});
    		try {
    			return subscribeLive(endpoint, (data) => setResult({data, loading: false, error: undefined}));
    		} catch (error) {
    			setResult({data: undefined, loading: false, error: error instanceof Error ? error : new Error(String(error))});
    		}
    	}, [endpoint]);
    
    	return result;
    }
    
    export function createLiveHook<TArgs extends readonly unknown[], TData>(
    	endpoint: Omit<LiveEndpoint<TArgs, TData>, 'args'>,
    ) {
    	const createEndpoint = (...args: TArgs): LiveEndpoint<TArgs, TData> => ({...endpoint, args});
    	return (...args: TArgs) => useLive(createEndpoint, ...args);
    }

    import {io, type Socket} from 'socket.io-client';
    
    export type LiveEndpoint<TArgs extends readonly unknown[], TData> = {
    	namespace: string;
    	endpoint: string;
    	event: string;
    	args: TArgs;
    	parse?: (value: unknown) => TData;
    };
    
    type Listener<T> = (value: T) => void;
    type Entry = {
    	endpoint: LiveEndpoint<readonly unknown[], unknown>;
    	listeners: Set<Listener<unknown>>;
    	value?: unknown;
    	hasValue: boolean;
    	version: number;
    };
    
    const sockets = new Map<string, Socket>();
    const entries = new Map<string, Entry>();
    
    function roomKey(endpoint: LiveEndpoint<readonly unknown[], unknown>) {
    	return `${endpoint.namespace}:${endpoint.endpoint}:${JSON.stringify(endpoint.args)}`;
    }
    
    function socketFor(namespace: string) {
    	let socket = sockets.get(namespace);
    	if (socket) return socket;
    
    	socket = io(namespace, {path: '/socket.io', transports: ['websocket', 'polling']});
    	sockets.set(namespace, socket);
    	return socket;
    }
    
    function subscribeMessage(endpoint: LiveEndpoint<readonly unknown[], unknown>) {
    	return {endpoint: endpoint.endpoint, args: endpoint.args};
    }
    
    export function subscribeLive<T>(endpoint: LiveEndpoint<readonly unknown[], T>, listener: Listener<T>) {
    	const key = roomKey(endpoint);
    	let entry = entries.get(key);
    	if (!entry) {
    		const socket = socketFor(endpoint.namespace);
    		entry = {endpoint, listeners: new Set(), hasValue: false, version: 0};
    		entries.set(key, entry);
    
    		const current = entry;
    		const receive = (payload: unknown) => {
    			const value = endpoint.parse ? endpoint.parse(payload) : (payload as T);
    			current.value = value;
    			current.hasValue = true;
    			current.version++;
    			for (const notify of current.listeners) notify(value);
    		};
    		socket.on(endpoint.event, receive);
    		socket.emit('live:subscribe', subscribeMessage(endpoint));
    	}
    
    	entry.listeners.add(listener as Listener<unknown>);
    	if (entry.hasValue) listener(entry.value as T);
    
    	return () => {
    		const current = entries.get(key);
    		if (!current) return;
    		current.listeners.delete(listener as Listener<unknown>);
    		if (current.listeners.size !== 0) return;
    
    		const socket = socketFor(endpoint.namespace);
    		socket.emit('live:unsubscribe', subscribeMessage(endpoint));
    		socket.off(endpoint.event);
    		entries.delete(key);
    	};
    }

```

    use crate::{models::{NewTodo, Todo}, socket::publish_todos};
    use auto_route::controller;
    use axum::{Json, extract::Path, http::StatusCode};
    use sqlx::SqlitePool;
    
    pub struct TodoController {
        pool: SqlitePool,
    }
    
    #[controller("/api/todos")]
    impl TodoController {
        fn new() -> Self {
            Self { pool: crate::POOL.get().expect("database is initialized").clone() }
        }
    
        #[get]
        async fn list(&self) -> Json<Vec<Todo>> {
            Json(load_todos(&self.pool).await)
        }
    
        #[post]
        async fn create(&self, Json(todo): Json<NewTodo>) -> StatusCode {
            let title = todo.title.trim();
            if title.is_empty() { return StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST; }
            if sqlx::query("INSERT INTO todos(title) VALUES (?)")
                .bind(title).execute(&self.pool).await.is_err() {
                return StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR;
            }
            publish_todos(&self.pool).await;
            StatusCode::CREATED
        }
    
        #[post("/{id}/toggle")]
        async fn toggle(&self, Path(id): Path<i64>) -> StatusCode {
            if sqlx::query("UPDATE todos SET done = NOT done WHERE id = ?")
                .bind(id).execute(&self.pool).await.is_err() {
                return StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR;

            StatusCode::NO_CONTENT
        }
    
        #[delete("/{id}")]
        async fn delete(&self, Path(id): Path<i64>) -> StatusCode {
            if sqlx::query("DELETE FROM todos WHERE id = ?")
                .bind(id).execute(&self.pool).await.is_err() {
                return StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR;
            }
            publish_todos(&self.pool).await;
            StatusCode::NO_CONTENT
        }
    }
    
    pub async fn load_todos(pool: &SqlitePool) -> Vec<Todo> {
        sqlx::query_as("SELECT id, title, done FROM todos ORDER BY id DESC")
            .fetch_all(pool).await.unwrap_or_default()
    }

    import {FormEvent, useEffect, useState} from 'react';
    import {type Todo, useTodos} from './live';
    
    async function mutate(path: string, method = 'POST', body?: unknown) {
      const response = await fetch(path, {method, headers: body ? {'content-type': 'application/json'} : undefined, body: body ? JSON.stringify(body) : undefined});
      if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`Request failed: ${response.status}`);
    }
    
    export function App() {
      const [initial, setInitial] = useState<Todo[] | null>(null);
      const [title, setTitle] = useState('');
    
      useEffect(() => { fetch('/api/todos').then((r) => r.json()).then(setInitial); }, []);
      if (!initial) return <main className="shell"><p>Loading todos…</p></main>;
      return <TodoApp initial={initial} title={title} setTitle={setTitle} />;
    }
    
    function TodoApp({initial, title, setTitle}: {initial: Todo[]; title: string; setTitle: (value: string) => void}) {
      const {todos, connected} = useTodos(initial);
      const submit = async (event: FormEvent) => {
        event.preventDefault();
        if (!title.trim()) return;
        await mutate('/api/todos', 'POST', {title});
        setTitle('');
      };
    
      return <main className="shell">
        <header><div><h1>Realtime Todos</h1><p>Open two tabs and edit either one.</p></div><span className={connected ? 'status online' : 'status'}>{connected ? 'Live' : 'Offline'}</span></header>
        <form onSubmit={submit}><input value={title} onChange={(e) => setTitle(e.target.value)} placeholder="What needs doing?"/><button>Add</button></form>
        <section>{todos.length === 0 ? <p className="empty">No todos yet.</p> : todos.map((todo) =>
          <article key={todo.id}>
            <input type="checkbox" checked={todo.done} onChange={() => mutate(`/api/todos/${todo.id}/toggle`)}/>
            <span className={todo.done ? 'done' : ''}>{todo.title}</span>
            <button className="delete" onClick={() => mutate(`/api/todos/${todo.id}`, 'DELETE')}>Delete</button>
          </article>
        )}</section>
        <footer>{todos.filter((todo) => !todo.done).length} remaining · {todos.filter((todo) => todo.done).length} completed</footer>
      </main>;
    }
    Add: /run/media/das/SSD/Devloper/rustploy/crates/todo-test/react/src/live.ts
    import {useEffect, useState} from 'react';
    import {io} from 'socket.io-client';
    
    export type Todo = {id: number; title: string; done: boolean};
    type Update<T> = {endpoint: string; args: unknown[]; data: T};
    
    const socket = io('/todo', {path: '/socket.io'});
    const subscription = {endpoint: 'TodoSocket::todos', args: []};
    
    export function useTodos(initial: Todo[]) {
      const [todos, setTodos] = useState(initial);
      const [connected, setConnected] = useState(socket.connected);
    
      useEffect(() => {
        const subscribe = () => {
          setConnected(true);
          socket.emit('live:subscribe', subscription);
        };
        const disconnect = () => setConnected(false);
        const update = (message: Update<Todo[]>) => {
          if (message.endpoint === subscription.endpoint && JSON.stringify(message.args) === '[]') setTodos(message.data);
        };
        socket.on('connect', subscribe);
        socket.on('disconnect', disconnect);
        socket.on('live:update', update);
        if (socket.connected) subscribe();
        return () => {
          socket.emit('live:unsubscribe', subscription);
          socket.off('connect', subscribe);
          socket.off('disconnect', disconnect);
          socket.off('live:update', update);
        };
      }, []);
    
      return {todos, connected};
    }

    #[auto_route::get("/_rustploy/html/events/{session}")]
    pub async fn events(Path(session): Path<String>) -> Response {
        let Some(receiver) = html_rt::take_session(&session) else {
            return StatusCode::NOT_FOUND.into_response();
        };
        let stream = futures::stream::unfold(receiver, |mut receiver| async move {
            receiver.recv().await.map(|patch| {
                let data = serde_json::json!({"slot": patch.slot, "html": patch.html});
                (
                    Ok::<Event, Infallible>(Event::default().data(data.to_string())),
                    receiver,
                )
            })
        });
        Sse::new(stream).into_response()
    }

    import {useEffect, useMemo, useState} from 'react';
    import {io, type Socket} from 'socket.io-client';
    
    type Endpoint<A extends unknown[], T> = {namespace: string; endpoint: string; event: string; args: A};
    type Update<T> = {endpoint: string; args: unknown[]; data: T};
    const sockets = new Map<string, Socket>();
    
    export function createLiveHook<A extends unknown[], T>(metadata: Omit<Endpoint<A, T>, 'args'>) {
      return (...args: A) => {
        const key = JSON.stringify(args);
        const endpoint = useMemo(() => ({...metadata, args}), [key]);
        const [data, setData] = useState<T>();
        const [connected, setConnected] = useState(false);
        useEffect(() => {
          let socket = sockets.get(endpoint.namespace);
          if (!socket) {
            socket = io(endpoint.namespace, {path: '/socket.io'});
            sockets.set(endpoint.namespace, socket);
          }
          const subscription = {endpoint: endpoint.endpoint, args: endpoint.args};
          const subscribe = () => { setConnected(true); socket!.emit('live:subscribe', subscription); };
          const update = (message: Update<T>) => {
            if (message.endpoint === endpoint.endpoint && JSON.stringify(message.args) === key) setData(message.data);
          };
          socket.on('connect', subscribe);
          socket.on('disconnect', () => setConnected(false));
          socket.on('live:update', update);
          if (socket.connected) subscribe();
          return () => { socket!.emit('live:unsubscribe', subscription); socket!.off('live:update', update); };
        }, [endpoint, key]);
        return {data, connected};
      };
    }

    import {execFileSync} from 'node:child_process';
    import {existsSync} from 'node:fs';
    import {dirname, resolve} from 'node:path';
    
    const VIRTUAL_ID = 'virtual:rustploy-live';
    const RESOLVED_ID = `\0${VIRTUAL_ID}`;
    
    function findManifest(start) {
      let current = start;
      while (current !== dirname(current)) {
        const candidate = resolve(current, 'Cargo.toml');
        if (existsSync(candidate)) return candidate;
        current = dirname(current);
      }
      throw new Error('[rustploy] Cargo.toml not found above Vite root');
    }
    
    function loadManifest(root) {
      const cargo = findManifest(root);
      const stdout = execFileSync('cargo', ['run', '--quiet', '--manifest-path', cargo, '--bin', 'rustploy-live-manifest'], {encoding: 'utf8'});
      return JSON.parse(stdout);
    }
    
    function runtimeSource(manifest) {
      const endpoints = manifest.endpoints.map((endpoint) => `
    export const ${endpoint.hook} = createLiveHook(${JSON.stringify(endpoint)});`).join('');
      const types = manifest.types.map((type) => `export type ${type.name} = ${type.definition};`).join('\n');
      return `
    import {useEffect, useMemo, useState} from 'react';
    import {io} from 'socket.io-client';
    ${types}
    const sockets = new Map();
    function createLiveHook(metadata) {
      return (...args) => {
        const key = JSON.stringify(args);
        const endpoint = useMemo(() => ({...metadata, args}), [key]);
        const [data, setData] = useState();
        const [connected, setConnected] = useState(false);
        useEffect(() => {
          let socket = sockets.get(endpoint.namespace);
          if (!socket) { socket = io(endpoint.namespace, {path: '/socket.io'}); sockets.set(endpoint.namespace, socket); }
          const subscription = {endpoint: endpoint.endpoint, args};
          const subscribe = () => { setConnected(true); socket.emit('live:subscribe', subscription); };
          const disconnect = () => setConnected(false);
          const update = (message) => {
            if (message.endpoint === endpoint.endpoint && JSON.stringify(message.args) === key) setData(message.data);
          };
          socket.on('connect', subscribe); socket.on('disconnect', disconnect); socket.on('live:update', update);
          if (socket.connected) subscribe();
          return () => { if (socket.connected) socket.emit('live:unsubscribe', subscription); socket.off('connect', subscribe); socket.off('disconnect', disconnect); socket.off('live:update', update); };
        }, [endpoint, key]);
        return {data, connected, loading: data === undefined};
      };
    }
    ${endpoints}
    `;
    }
    
    export function rustploy() {
      let source;
      return {
        name: 'rustploy-live',
        enforce: 'pre',
        configResolved(config) { source = runtimeSource(loadManifest(config.root)); },
        resolveId(id) { if (id === VIRTUAL_ID) return RESOLVED_ID; },
        load(id) { if (id === RESOLVED_ID) return source; },
      };
    }

    import {useEffect, useMemo, useState} from 'react';
    import {io, type Socket} from 'socket.io-client';
    
    type Endpoint<A extends unknown[], T> = {namespace: string; endpoint: string; event: string; args: A};
    type Update<T> = {endpoint: string; args: unknown[]; data: T};
    const sockets = new Map<string, Socket>();
    
    export function createLiveHook<A extends unknown[], T>(metadata: Omit<Endpoint<A, T>, 'args'>) {
      return (...args: A) => {
        const key = JSON.stringify(args);
        const endpoint = useMemo(() => ({...metadata, args}), [key]);
        const [data, setData] = useState<T>();
        const [connected, setConnected] = useState(false);
        useEffect(() => {
          let socket = sockets.get(endpoint.namespace);
          if (!socket) {
            socket = io(endpoint.namespace, {path: '/socket.io'});
            sockets.set(endpoint.namespace, socket);
          }
          const subscription = {endpoint: endpoint.endpoint, args: endpoint.args};
          const subscribe = () => { setConnected(true); socket!.emit('live:subscribe', subscription); };
          const update = (message: Update<T>) => {
            if (message.endpoint === endpoint.endpoint && JSON.stringify(message.args) === key) setData(message.data);
          };
          socket.on('connect', subscribe);
          socket.on('disconnect', () => setConnected(false));
          socket.on('live:update', update);
          if (socket.connected) subscribe();
          return () => { socket!.emit('live:unsubscribe', subscription); socket!.off('live:update', update); };
        }, [endpoint, key]);
        return {data, connected};
      };
    }

## User

ye to custom rpc ho gaya na

## Assistant

Haan—current Vite plugin approach technically custom typed RPC/live protocol ban gaya hai.

Ismein:

```text
Rust route metadata
   ↓
Manifest binary
   ↓
Vite plugin
   ↓
Generated React hook
   ↓
Socket.IO subscribe/publish protocol
```

Custom pieces:

- `rustploy-live-manifest` binary
- `virtual:rustploy-live`
- `live:subscribe`
- `live:unsubscribe`
- `live:update`
- Endpoint identity such as `TodoController::list`
- Room argument serialization
- Generated React hooks

Lekin normal RPC se thoda different hai:

```text
Normal RPC:
client calls function → server responds once

Rustploy live:
client subscribes to function identity + arguments
server publishes multiple future results
```

Isko “typed reactive RPC” ya “live query RPC” kehna zyada accurate hoga.

Developer experience:

```rust
#[get("")]
#[live]
async fn list(&self) -> Json<Vec<Todo>>
```

```tsx
const {data} = useTodos();
```

Framework internally isko roughly treat karta hai:

```text
subscribe TodoController::list([])
receive Vec<Todo>
receive Vec<Todo>
receive Vec<Todo>
...
```

Concern valid hai: agar hum khud transport protocol, schema generator, React runtime, caching, reconnect aur RPC identity sab maintain karenge, architecture ka scope kaafi bada ho jayega.

Better boundary:

- HTTP routes remain standard HTTP.
- Socket.IO remains standard transport.
- OpenAPI/JSON Schema types remain existing contract.
- Rustploy plugin only generates live subscription wrappers.
- Custom business-level RPC invocation introduce na karein.

Meaning client mutations standard API se:

```tsx
await api.POST('/api/todos', {body});
```

Live data generated hook se:

```tsx
const {data} = useTodos();
```

Server mutation standard route hai:

```rust
#[post("")]
async fn create(...) { ... }
```

Server update typed publisher hai:

```rust
todo_live::list()?
    .publish(todos)
    .await?;
```

So yes, custom live-query RPC layer ban raha hai—but full application RPC framework nahi. Agar client se Rust functions directly invoke karna bhi add karenge, tab woh definitely full custom RPC framework ho jayega. Current boundary ko live subscriptions tak limited rakhna maintainable rahega.

## User

how it acutally works samjooge

## Assistant

Haan. Actual system ko end-to-end dekhte hain.

Backend mein developer ye likhta hai:

```rust
#[get("")]
#[live]
async fn list(&self) -> Json<Vec<Todo>> {
    Json(load_todos(&self.pool).await)
}
```

Is single function ke do roles hain:

```text
GET /api/todos  → initial HTTP response
#[live]          → realtime subscription definition
```

### 1. Compile time par Rust macro

`#[controller]` macro route ko inspect karta hai aur metadata nikalta hai:

```text
Controller: TodoController
Method:     list
HTTP:       GET /api/todos
Arguments:  []
Return:     Vec<Todo>
Live event: list
Namespace:  /_rustploy/live
```

Macro server-side typed publisher generate karta hai:

```rust
todo_live::list()?
    .publish(todos)
    .await?;
```

Conceptually:

```rust
pub fn list() -> Result<LivePublisher<Vec<Todo>>, PublishError> {
    LivePublisher::new(
        "/_rustploy/live",
        "TodoController::list",
        "list",
    )
    .room([])
}
```

It also generates subscription metadata:

```rust
todo_live::list_subscription()
```

### 2. Vite plugin startup

Vite config:

```ts
plugins: [
  react(),
  rustploy(),
]
```

Plugin runs:

```bash
cargo run --bin rustploy-live-manifest
```

Manifest binary macro-generated subscription ko read karta hai:

```rust
let subscription =
    todo_live::list_subscription()?;
```

It prints JSON:

```json
{
  "endpoints": [
    {
      "hook": "useTodos",
      "namespace": "/_rustploy/live",
      "endpoint": "TodoController::list",
      "event": "list",
      "parameters": "",
      "result": "Todo[]"
    }
  ]
}
```

### 3. Vite virtual module

Plugin manifest se memory mein module banata hai:

```ts
virtual:rustploy-live
```

React app import karta hai:

```tsx
import {
  useTodos,
  type Todo,
} from "virtual:rustploy-live";
```

Disk par `useTodos.ts` file nahi hoti. Vite import resolve karke generated JavaScript provide karta hai.

Conceptually generated hook:

```ts
export const useTodos = createLiveHook({
  namespace: "/_rustploy/live",
  endpoint: "TodoController::list",
});
```

Plugin TypeScript ke liye declaration generate karta hai:

```ts
declare module "virtual:rustploy-live" {
  export type Todo = {
    id: number;
    title: string;
    done: boolean;
  };

  export function useTodos(): {
    data: Todo[] | undefined;
    loading: boolean;
    connected: boolean;
  };
}
```

### 4. React component mounts

```tsx
const live = useTodos();
```

Hook Socket.IO connection create/reuse karta hai:

```ts
io("/_rustploy/live")
```

Phir subscription message send karta hai:

```json
{
  "endpoint": "TodoController::list",
  "args": []
}
```

Event name:

```text
live:subscribe
```

### 5. Server room join

`auto_socket` server automatically receive karta hai:

```rust
socket.on("live:subscribe", ...)
```

Room key banti hai:

```text
TodoController::list:[]
```

Socket room join karta hai:

```text
/_rustploy/live
└── TodoController::list:[]
    ├── Browser tab 1
    └── Browser tab 2
```

### 6. Mutation normal HTTP se hoti hai

React create request bhejta hai:

```ts
fetch("/api/todos", {
  method: "POST",
  body: JSON.stringify({title}),
});
```

Backend standard endpoint execute karta hai:

```rust
#[post("")]
async fn create(...) {
    sqlx::query("INSERT ...").execute(...).await;

    self.publish_todos().await;
}
```

No client-side RPC function invocation hua. Mutation normal HTTP hai.

### 7. Server publish karta hai

```rust
todo_live::list()?
    .publish(todos)
    .await?;
```

Publisher room identity already jaanta hai:

```text
namespace = /_rustploy/live
endpoint  = TodoController::list
args      = []
room      = TodoController::list:[]
```

Server one Socket.IO room emission karta hai:

```json
{
  "endpoint": "TodoController::list",
  "args": [],
  "data": [
    {
      "id": 1,
      "title": "Test",
      "done": false
    }
  ]
}
```

Transport event:

```text
live:update
```

### 8. React state updates

Hook message verify karta hai:

```ts
message.endpoint === "TodoController::list"
JSON.stringify(message.args) === "[]"
```

Match hua to:

```ts
setData(message.data);
```

React sirf subscribed components rerender karta hai. Pura page reload ya refetch nahi hota.

Complete flow:

```text
#[get + live] Rust method
          │
          ├── GET /api/todos
          ├── typed publisher
          └── manifest metadata
                    │
                    ▼
              Vite plugin
                    │
                    ▼
              generated useTodos()
                    │
                    ▼
React mounts → live:subscribe → room join
                                    │
HTTP mutation → DB write → publish()
                                    │
                                    ▼
                     live:update to matching room
                                    │
                                    ▼
                             React setData()
```

Important limitation: `#[live] list()` currently subscription par method automatically execute karke initial snapshot nahi bhejta. Initial data abhi separate HTTP GET se aata hai:

```tsx
fetch("/api/todos")
```

Uske baad future updates Socket.IO se aate hain. True live-query behavior mein subscription ke samay backend same `list()` method execute karke initial snapshot bhi emit karega.

## Assistant

Samajh gaya. `#[live("name")]` ka naam server publisher/event ke liye nahi, specifically generated client hook ka naam hoga.

Example:

```rust
#[get("")]
#[live("todos")]
async fn list(&self) -> Json<Vec<Todo>> {
    Json(load_todos(&self.pool).await)
}
```

Server-side API method-based hi rahegi:

```rust
todo_live::list()?
    .publish(todos)
    .await?;
```

Internal endpoint/event bhi stable rahega:

```text
TodoController::list
```

Sirf React generation change hogi:

```tsx
import {
    useTodos,
    type Todo,
} from "virtual:openoxide-live";

const {data} = useTodos();
```

Another example:

```rust
#[get("/{server_id}/metrics")]
#[live("server_metrics")]
async fn metrics(
    &self,
    Path(server_id): Path<i64>,
) -> Json<Metrics> {
    // ...
}
```

Generated React hook:

```tsx
const metrics = useServerMetrics(serverId);
```

Rules:

```text
#[live]                   → useList()
#[live("todos")]          → useTodos()
#[live("server_metrics")] → useServerMetrics()
```

`#[on("event")]` agar kabhi use ho to woh transport event override rahega. `#[live("name")]` sirf client-facing generated hook alias hoga. Ye separation sahi hai.

    +        .map(|part| {

{

Vite plugin is manifest ko read karke TypeScript hook generate karta hai, roughly:

```tsx
export function useTodos() {
  const [data, setData] = useState<Todo[] | null>(null);
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true);
  const [connected, setConnected] = useState(false);

  useEffect(() => {
    const socket = openoxideLive("/_openoxide/live");

    socket.on("connect", () => {
      setConnected(true);

      socket.emit("live:subscribe", {
        endpoint: "TodoController::list",
        event: "list",
        args: [],
      });
    });

    socket.on("live:update", (payload) => {
      if (
        payload.endpoint === "TodoController::list" &&
        payload.event === "list"
      ) {
        setData(decodeTodoArray(payload.data));
        setLoading(false);
      }
    });

    socket.on("disconnect", () => {
      setConnected(false);
    });

    return () => socket.close();
  }, []);

  return { data, loading, connected };
}
```

Developer sirf itna likhega:

```tsx

  const { data: todos, loading, connected } = useTodos();

  if (loading) return <TodoSkeleton />;

        <li key={todo.id}>{todo.title}</li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  );
}
```

1. `useTodos()` mount hota hai.
2. Hook generated endpoint identity ke saath live socket subscribe karta hai.
3. Backend initial `todos` data publish karta hai.
4. Hook payload ko generated `Todo[]` type mein decode karta hai.
5. `setData()` sirf todo state update karta hai.
6. React component re-render hota hai; poora page manually reload nahi hota.
7. Cleanup par subscription/socket close ho jata hai.

## Assistant

Ho gaya. Automatic SQLite realtime bridge implement kar diya.

Ab Todo controller:

```rust
#[get("")]
#[live("todos", table = "todos")]
async fn list(&self) -> Json<Vec<Todo>> {
    // query
}
```

Create/toggle/delete mein manual publish nahi hai:

```rust
sqlx::query("UPDATE todos SET done = NOT done WHERE id = ?")
    .bind(id)
    .execute(&self.pool)
    .await?;
```

Runtime flow:

```text
SQLite INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE
        ↓
preupdate + commit hook
        ↓
table = "todos"
        ↓
generated live resolver
        ↓
one SELECT query
        ↓
one TodoController::todos() publish
        ↓
all subscribed clients update
```

Optimizations:

- Same endpoint ke 10 clients → one refresh query
- Same table ke rapid commits → in-flight refresh deduplicate
- Latest state publish hoti hai
- Rollback changes notify nahi karta
- Room args canonicalized hain (`[]` zero-arg endpoint ke liye)
- DB layer live socket ko notify karta hai; controller ko manual publish nahi karna

Macro ab `#[live("name", table = "table_name")]` support karta hai. Table-backed automatic resolver currently zero-argument live methods ke liye enabled hai; parameterized room endpoints ke liye explicit publish path safe rahega jab tak argument-aware resolver add nahi hota.

#[get("")]

```text
todos change    ─┐
users change    ─┼─→ one dashboard refresh → all subscribers
projects change ─┘
```

Single table ke liye shorthand:

```rust
#[live("todos", table = "todos")]
```

Multiple ke liye:

```rust
#[live("dashboard", tables = ["todos", "users"])]
```

Agar ek transaction dono tables update kare:

```sql
BEGIN;
UPDATE users ...;
INSERT INTO todos ...;
COMMIT;
```

to dashboard query sirf **ek baar** execute honi chahiye, do baar nahi.

Abhi implemented parser only single `table = "todos"` support karta hai. `tables = [...]` support abhi add nahi hua hai; yahi next correct extension hai.

BEGIN;
UPDATE users SET ...;

COMMIT;

To endpoint refresh sirf ek baar hoga, do ya teen baar nahi.

Multiple clients ke case mein bhi:

1 endpoint refresh query

    Add: /run/media/das/SSD/Devloper/rustploy/docs/realtime.md
    # Typed realtime endpoints
    
    OpenOxide can expose an Axum controller method as a typed HTTP route and a React live data source at the same time. SQLite-backed endpoints can refresh automatically after committed writes, without calling `publish` from every mutation handler.
    
    ## Basic endpoint
    
    ```rust
    use auto_route::controller;
    use axum::Json;
    
    #[controller("/api/todos")]
    impl TodoController {
        #[get("")]
        #[live("todos", table = "todos")]
        async fn list(&self) -> Json<Vec<Todo>> {
            Json(
                sqlx::query_as("SELECT id, title, done FROM todos ORDER BY id DESC")
                    .fetch_all(&self.pool)
                    .await
                    .unwrap_or_default(),
            )
        }
    }
    ```
    
    This declaration generates:
    
    - the normal `GET /api/todos` route;
    - the live endpoint identity `TodoController::list`;
    - the server publisher `TodoController::todos()`;
    - the typed subscription descriptor `TodoController::todos_subscription()`;
    - the React hook name `useTodos` in the generated client manifest;
    - an automatic refresh resolver associated with the `todos` SQLite table.
    
    ## Mutation handlers
    
    Mutation handlers only write to SQLite:
    
    ```rust
    #[post("")]
    async fn create(&self, Json(input): Json<NewTodo>) -> StatusCode {
        sqlx::query("INSERT INTO todos(title) VALUES (?)")
            .bind(input.title)
            .execute(&self.pool)
            .await
            .expect("insert todo");
    
        StatusCode::CREATED
    }
    ```
    
    Do not query the list again or call `publish` after the write. The SQLite commit hook performs the refresh.
    
    ## Multiple tables
    
    Use `tables` when the result depends on more than one table:
    
    ```rust
    #[get("")]
    #[live(
        "dashboard",
        tables = ["users", "projects", "deployments"]
    )]
    async fn dashboard(&self) -> Json<Dashboard> {
        Json(self.service.dashboard().await)
    }
    ```
    
    A committed change to any listed table schedules the endpoint resolver. If one transaction changes several listed tables, the endpoint still appears once in the refresh registry for each notification cycle and its in-flight guard prevents parallel duplicate refreshes.
    
    The single-table shorthand remains supported:
    
    ```rust
    #[live("todos", table = "todos")]
    ```
    
    ## Runtime flow
    
    ```text
    SQLite INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE
                  │
                  ▼
           pre-update hook records
           table and row metadata
                  │
                  ▼
           successful commit hook
                  │
                  ▼
           DbEventBus publishes the
           committed table names
                  │
                  ▼
           matching live resolver
           executes the route once
                  │
                  ▼
           one typed payload is sent
           to the endpoint room
                  │
                  ▼
           every subscribed client
           receives the same update
    ```
    
    Rollback clears pending changes and does not refresh endpoints. A short post-commit delay ensures the new rows are visible to SQLx readers.
    
    ## Query and connection behavior
    
    Subscriber count does not control query count. Ten clients subscribed to the same zero-argument endpoint share one server refresh:
    
    ```text
    1 committed database change
    1 endpoint resolver execution
    1 SELECT query
    1 serialized live payload
    10 socket deliveries
    ```
    
    Each browser namespace also reuses a shared Socket.IO connection. Multiple generated React hooks create separate logical subscriptions, not separate connections.
    
    Rapid commits are guarded per endpoint. If a resolver is already running, another notification marks it pending instead of starting a parallel query. After the active resolver completes, one more refresh reads the latest state.
    
    ## React usage
    
    The Vite plugin reads the generated live manifest and creates a typed hook:
    
    ```tsx
    function TodoList() {
      const {data: todos, loading, connected} = useTodos();
    
      if (loading) return <p>Loading…</p>;
    
      return (
        <ul>
          {todos?.map(todo => <li key={todo.id}>{todo.title}</li>)}
        </ul>
      );
    }
    ```
    
    The hook subscribes with the compile-time endpoint identity and decodes updates as `Todo[]`. Endpoint strings and payload types do not need to be duplicated in application code.
    
    ## Explicit publishing
    
    Explicit publishing remains available for data that is not driven by SQLite, such as filesystem notifications, metrics, jobs, or broadcast channels:
    
    ```rust
    TodoController::todos()?
        .publish(todos)
        .await?;
    ```
    
    Target one socket:
    
    ```rust
    dashboard_live::metrics_event().emit(&socket, metrics)?;
    ```
    
    Broadcast to the namespace:
    
    ```rust
    dashboard_live::metrics_event()
        .broadcast(metrics)
        .await?;
    ```
    
    ## Current constraints
    
    - Automatic `table`/`tables` refresh currently supports zero-argument controller methods returning `Json<T>`.
    - Parameterized endpoints can still use generated typed rooms and explicit `publish` calls.
    - Writes performed through the configured SQLite connections are observed. A separate process writing the database file does not pass through the in-process SQLx hooks.
    - Table names are explicit metadata. OpenOxide does not attempt to parse arbitrary SQL or infer dependencies from service code.
    - SQLite `SELECT` statements do not trigger the write hooks, so refresh queries do not create a reactive loop.
    
    ## Server setup
    
    SQLx must enable SQLite pre-update hooks:
    
    ```toml
    sqlx = {
      version = "0.9",
      default-features = false,
      features = ["runtime-tokio", "sqlite", "sqlite-preupdate-hook"]
    }
    ```
    
    Create Socket.IO and register generated handlers before serving the app:
    
    ```rust
    let app = auto_route::routes().await?;
    let (socket_layer, io) = socketioxide::SocketIo::new_layer();
    auto_socket::register_global(&io).await?;
    let app = app.layer(socket_layer);
    ```
    
    The application SQLite pool installs `crate::db::reactive::install_hooks` in `after_connect`, ensuring every pooled connection participates in committed-change detection.

## User

publish karte waqat block bhi karta hai kya

## Assistant

`publish(...).await` **OS thread block nahi karta**, kyunki async hai:

```rust
TodoController::todos()?
    .publish(todos)
    .await?;
```

Lekin current refresh task publish complete hone ka wait karta hai:

```text
query complete
→ payload serialize
→ Socket.IO room emit await
→ refresh complete
```

Is duration mein:

- Tokio thread free rehta hai; dusre tasks chal sakte hain.
- Same endpoint ka parallel refresh start nahi hota.
- Beech mein SQLite change aaye to `pending = true` hota hai.
- Current publish complete hote hi latest state ek baar phir refresh hoti hai.

```text
refresh running
   ├── another change → pending
   ├── another change → still pending
   ↓
publish complete
   ↓
one latest refresh
```

Slow/disconnected client normally poore server ko block nahi karta; Socket.IO apne transport buffers/tasks manage karta hai. Lekin payload serialization aur room emission complete hone tak endpoint refresher logically waiting state mein rehta hai.

Ye deliberate backpressure hai—unlimited parallel publishes aur stale out-of-order updates rokta hai. Bahut high-frequency metrics/logs ke liye DB resolver ke bajaye dedicated bounded channel/watch stream better rahega.

    +### Vite generation setup
    +
    +Install and configure the plugin:
    +
    +```ts
    +// vite.config.ts
    +import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react';
    +import {defineConfig} from 'vite';
    +import {openoxide} from '@openoxide/vite';
    +
    +export default defineConfig({
    +  plugins: [
    +    react(),
    +    openoxide({
    +      manifestPath: '../Cargo.toml',
    +      manifestBin: 'openoxide-live-manifest',
    +      declarations: 'src/openoxide-live.generated.d.ts',
    +    }),
    +  ],
    +});
    +```
    +
    +All options are optional. Without `manifestPath`, the plugin walks upward from the Vite root and uses the nearest `Cargo.toml`.
    +
    +The paths mean:
    +
    +| Option | Purpose | Default |
    +| --- | --- | --- |
    +| `manifestPath` | Cargo manifest containing the generator binary; relative to the Vite root | nearest parent `Cargo.toml` |
    +| `manifestBin` | Rust binary that prints the live JSON manifest to stdout | `openoxide-live-manifest` |
    +| `declarations` | Generated TypeScript declaration path, relative to the Vite root | `src/openoxide-live.generated.d.ts` |
    +
    +At Vite startup the plugin executes:
    +
    +```text
    +cargo run --quiet --manifest-path <manifestPath> --bin <manifestBin>
    +```
    +
    +The binary must print a JSON manifest. The plugin then creates two client outputs:
    +
    +```text
    +virtual:openoxide-live
    +    generated runtime module held in Vite memory
    +
    +src/openoxide-live.generated.d.ts
    +    generated TypeScript types written to disk
    +```
    +
    +There is intentionally no generated `live.ts` runtime file. Application code imports the virtual module:
    +
    +```tsx
    +import {type Todo, useTodos} from 'virtual:openoxide-live';
    +```
    +
    +The declaration file should be included by the application's `tsconfig.json` through its normal `src` include. Do not edit it manually.
    +
    +Example generator binary:
    +
    +```rust
    +// src/bin/openoxide-live-manifest.rs
    +use crate::{controller::TodoController, models::Todo};
    +
    +fn main() {
    +    let subscription = TodoController::todos_subscription()
    +        .expect("generate todos subscription");
    +
    +    println!("{}", serde_json::json!({
    +        "types": [{
    +            "name": "Todo",
    +            "definition": Todo::TYPESCRIPT
    +        }],
    +        "endpoints": [{
    +            "hook": "useTodos",
    +            "namespace": subscription.namespace(),
    +            "endpoint": subscription.endpoint(),
    +            "event": subscription.event(),
    +            "parameters": "",
    +            "result": "Todo[]"
    +        }]
    +    }));
    +}
    +```
    +

## User

type bhi lelo pubsub jasa hai ya option batoo kya hoga type nahi stratiges batoo taki fast work kare apna

## Assistant

Haan, `tables` ke saath ek `strategy` option lena useful hoga. Isse framework ko pata chalega realtime update ka source aur refresh behavior kya hai.

Recommended syntax:

```rust
#[live(
    "dashboard",
    strategy = "sqlite",
    tables = ["servers", "deployments"]
)]
```

Lekin strings ke bajaye compile-time identifiers cleaner rahenge:

```rust
#[live(
    "dashboard",
    strategy = sqlite,
    tables = ["servers", "deployments"]
)]
```

Main ye strategies suggest karunga:

### `sqlite`

DB commit par endpoint function dobara execute hoga:

```rust
#[live("todos", strategy = sqlite, table = "todos")]
```

Flow:

```text
SQLite commit → one query refresh → publish
```

Best for CRUD lists/dashboard data.

### `publish`

Framework automatic refresh nahi karega. Developer ready payload push karega:

```rust
#[live("metrics", strategy = publish)]
```

```rust
DashboardController::metrics()?
    .publish(metrics)
    .await?;
```

Best for metrics, filesystem events aur external APIs.

### `latest`

High-frequency data ke liye `tokio::sync::watch` style—sirf latest value important:

```rust
#[live("cpu", strategy = latest)]
```

Behavior:

```text
10 rapid updates → intermediate values dropped → latest value delivered
```

Best for CPU, RAM, progress aur status.

### `stream`

Har event preserve karna ho:

```rust
#[live("logs", strategy = stream, capacity = 512)]
```

Behavior:

```text
event 1 → event 2 → event 3 → all delivered
```

Best for logs, terminal output aur deployment events. Bounded capacity compulsory honi chahiye.

### `signal`

Payload event ke andar available nahi; event sirf refresh trigger karta hai:

```rust
#[live("files", strategy = signal, debounce = 100)]
```

`fsnotify`, broadcast channel ya job completion endpoint ko re-run karega.

Recommended defaults:

```rust
#[live("todos", table = "todos")]
```

Automatically equivalent ho:

```rust
strategy = sqlite
```

Aur bina table:

```rust
#[live("metrics")]
```

Equivalent:

```rust
strategy = publish
```

Final strategy table:

| Strategy | Query repeat | Drops updates | Best use |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `sqlite` | Yes, once per burst | Coalesces | CRUD/data |
| `publish` | No | No | Ready payload |
| `latest` | No | Yes, keeps latest | Metrics/status |
| `stream` | No | No, bounded | Logs/terminal |
| `signal` | Endpoint dependent | Debounced | fsnotify/jobs |

Mere hisaab se initial implementation mein teen rakho:

```rust
sqlite
latest
stream
```

`publish` implicit manual mode ho aur `signal` baad mein add ho sakta hai. Isse API simple bhi rahegi aur major realtime workloads cover ho jayenge.
